> AGENT

Here's how I'd think about this before writing any code:

**The hard part isn't the UI — it's the content pipeline.** A three-column reader (Gurmukhi / romanized / English) with hover-popovers and click-to-speak is a weekend's worth of React. What's actually hard is producing *good* word-by-word morphological annotations and aligning them to clean source texts. Punjabi has Sanskrit-derived (तत्सम) vocabulary like *parmatma* where root decomposition is meaningful, plus Perso-Arabic loans where it isn't — and an LLM-generated breakdown will sometimes confidently invent etymologies. I'd treat the annotation layer as the core IP and design around the assumption that it needs human review for anything you publish.

**My recommendation for v0:** pick *one* short Janamsakhi episode (a Sakhi from the Puratan or Bhai Bala tradition — they're public domain and many are already digitized in Unicode Gurmukhi). Get it end-to-end: clean source → English translation (DeepL/Claude as draft, you verify) → Anvaad/ISO 15919 romanization → per-word morphological gloss generated by Claude with citations → audio via a TTS that actually handles Punjabi (Google Cloud TTS has `pa-IN`; ElevenLabs doesn't really). One Sakhi, fully polished, tells you whether the experience is worth scaling. Trying to build the CMS + ingestion pipeline first is the classic trap.

**Main tradeoff to decide now:** do you want this as a *reader* (curated, slow-growing library, high quality per text) or a *tool* (paste any Punjabi text and it annotates it)? They imply very different architectures — the reader is a content product, the tool is an NLP product. Your description sounds like the reader, but the etymology-drilldown feature you're most excited about is reusable across both.

Want me to spin up a scratch repo and prototype the three-pane reader on one hand-curated Sakhi so you can feel the interaction? Or would you rather sketch the data model for annotations first?

> AGENT

Good call — this is the part that won't just fall out of an LLM prompt cleanly, so it's the right thing to derisk first.

The core challenge: Punjabi words come from at least three etymological streams (Sanskrit-derived tatsama like *parmātmā*, evolved tadbhava forms, and Perso-Arabic loans like *zindagī* or *kitāb*), and each decomposes by different rules. A naive "ask Claude to break this down" will produce confident, wrong answers — especially for the Perso-Arabic side, where the model tends to invent Sanskrit roots. So the real question isn't "can we decompose words" but "how do we ground the decompositions in something verifiable."

The realistic shape I'd build: a small tool where you paste a Punjabi word and get back a tree (param → ātmā → each with their own Sanskrit/Persian/Arabic source + meaning, recursively expandable), where each node cites *where* the claim came from (Wiktionary entry, dictionary reference, or "LLM inference — unverified"). That provenance flag is what saves you from learning hallucinated etymologies. Wiktionary actually has structured etymology data for a surprising amount of Punjabi/Hindi/Sanskrit vocabulary that we can pull as ground truth, and fall back to LLM only for gaps.

Before I sketch the data model and start building, two quick scoping questions:

> AGENT

Your existing projects are mostly Python/Streamlit or Docker-orchestrated services — nothing Next-ish to copy from. For a hover-rich reading UI, Streamlit is the wrong tool (no good word-level interactivity), so I'd reach for a real web stack here.

**Proposed v0 — root decomposition, wired into a one-Sakhi reader:**

Stack:
- **Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind** (App Router, server actions for the lookup API)
- **SQLite** (via `better-sqlite3`) for caching Wiktionary lookups and storing the curated decomposition tree — etymology lookups are slow and rate-limited, you want them cached forever once verified
- **Claude API** (Sonnet 4.6) for two narrow jobs: (1) parsing unstructured Wiktionary etymology prose into structured morpheme nodes, (2) gap-filling with an `unverified: true` flag when Wiktionary has no entry
- **Google Cloud TTS** (`pa-IN` voice) for the click-to-speak — punt on this until decomposition works

Data model (the important part):
```
Morpheme {
  id, surface_gurmukhi, romanized (ISO 15919), gloss_en,
  source_language: 'sanskrit' | 'persian' | 'arabic' | 'punjabi' | 'unknown',
  source_form,           // e.g. परम for param
  provenance: {
    source: 'wiktionary' | 'llm' | 'manual',
    url?, fetched_at?, confidence: 'verified' | 'unverified'
  },
  components: Morpheme[]  // recursive — param + atma, each may decompose further
}
```

UX:
- Single page: one Janamsakhi (Bhai Bala or Puratan tradition, public domain text from Punjabi Wikisource)
- Three columns: Gurmukhi / ISO 15919 romanization / English translation, aligned at the sentence level
- Hover any word → popover shows the Morpheme tree with `verified`/`unverified` badges
- Click a child morpheme inside the popover → drills into *its* tree
- Bottom of popover: "Wrong? Edit." → opens a form that overwrites the cached entry with provenance: 'manual'. This is your slow accumulation of ground truth.

What I'd *not* build in v0: user accounts, multiple texts, TTS, spaced repetition, mobile polish.

Two things to confirm before I scaffold:

1	---
2	title: How to upgrade to version 16
3	nav_title: Version 16
4	description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.
5	---
6	
7	{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
8	
9	## Upgrading from 15 to 16
10	
11	### Using AI Agents with Next.js DevTools MCP
12	
13	If you're using an AI coding assistant that supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), you can use the **Next.js DevTools MCP** to automate the upgrade process and migration tasks.
14	
15	#### Setup
16	
17	Add the following configuration to your MCP client, for each coding agent you can read [this section](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp#mcp-client-configuration) for configuration details.
18	
19	**example:**
20	
21	```json filename=".mcp.json"
22	{
23	  "mcpServers": {
24	    "next-devtools": {
25	      "command": "npx",
26	      "args": ["-y", "next-devtools-mcp@latest"]
27	    }
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	For more information, visit the [`next-devtools-mcp`](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp) documentation to configure with your MCP client.
33	
34	> **Note:** Using `next-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Next.js DevTools MCP server.
35	
36	#### Example Prompts
37	
38	Once configured, you can use natural language prompts to upgrade your Next.js app:
39	
40	**To upgrade to Next.js 16:**
41	
42	Connect to your coding agent and then prompt:
43	
44	```txt
45	Next Devtools, help me upgrade my Next.js app to version 16
46	```
47	
48	**To migrate to Cache Components (after upgrading to v16):**
49	
50	Connect to your coding agent and then prompt:
51	
52	```txt
53	Next Devtools, migrate my Next.js app to cache components
54	```
55	
56	Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/guides/mcp).
57	
58	### Using the Codemod
59	
60	To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160):
61	
62	```bash package="pnpm"
63	pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
64	```
65	
66	```bash package="npm"
67	npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
68	```
69	
70	```bash package="yarn"
71	yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
72	```
73	
74	```bash package="bun"
75	bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
76	```
77	
78	The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to:
79	
80	- Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration
81	- Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI
82	- Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy`
83	- Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs
84	- Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts
85	
86	If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions:
87	
88	```bash package="pnpm"
89	pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
90	```
91	
92	```bash package="npm"
93	npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
94	```
95	
96	```bash package="yarn"
97	yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
98	```
99	
100	```bash package="bun"
101	bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
102	```
103	
104	If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions.
105	
106	## Node.js runtime and browser support
107	
108	| Requirement   | Change / Details                                                   |
109	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
110	| Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported |
111	| TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0`                                        |
112	| Browsers      | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+                 |
113	
114	## Turbopack by default
115	
116	Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build`
117	
118	Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`.
119	
120	```json filename="package.json"
121	{
122	  "scripts": {
123	    "dev": "next dev --turbopack",
124	    "build": "next build --turbopack",
125	    "start": "next start"
126	  }
127	}
128	```
129	
130	This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts:
131	
132	```json filename="package.json"
133	{
134	  "scripts": {
135	    "dev": "next dev",
136	    "build": "next build",
137	    "start": "next start"
138	  }
139	}
140	```
141	
142	If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues.
143	
144	You have a few different ways to address this:
145	
146	- **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config.
147	- **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options.
148	- **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack.
149	
150	> **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option
151	
152	### Opting out of Turbopack
153	
154	If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds:
155	
156	```json filename="package.json"
157	{
158	  "scripts": {
159	    "dev": "next dev",
160	    "build": "next build --webpack",
161	    "start": "next start"
162	  }
163	}
164	```
165	
166	We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack.
167	
168	### Turbopack configuration location
169	
170	The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental.
171	
172	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
173	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
174	
175	// Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack
176	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
177	  experimental: {
178	    turbopack: {
179	      // options
180	    },
181	  },
182	}
183	
184	export default nextConfig
185	```
186	
187	You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option:
188	
189	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
190	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
191	
192	// Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig
193	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
194	  turbopack: {
195	    // options
196	  },
197	}
198	
199	export default nextConfig
200	```
201	
202	Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example:
203	
204	- [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions)
205	- [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids)
206	
207	### Resolve alias fallback
208	
209	In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors.
210	
211	When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules.
212	
213	However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser.
214	
215	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
216	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
217	
218	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
219	  turbopack: {
220	    resolveAlias: {
221	      fs: {
222	        browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method
223	      },
224	    },
225	  },
226	}
227	
228	export default nextConfig
229	```
230	
231	It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules.
232	
233	### Sass node_modules imports
234	
235	Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax.
236	
237	In Webpack:
238	
239	```scss filename="styles/globals.scss"
240	@import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
241	```
242	
243	In Turbopack:
244	
245	```scss filename="styles/globals.scss"
246	@import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
247	```
248	
249	If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example:
250	
251	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
252	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
253	
254	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
255	  turbopack: {
256	    resolveAlias: {
257	      '~*': '*',
258	    },
259	  },
260	}
261	
262	export default nextConfig
263	```
264	
265	### Turbopack File System Caching (beta)
266	
267	Turbopack now supports filesystem caching in development, storing compiler artifacts on disk between runs for significantly faster compile times across restarts.
268	
269	Enable filesystem caching in your configuration:
270	
271	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
272	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
273	
274	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
275	  experimental: {
276	    turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true,
277	  },
278	}
279	
280	export default nextConfig
281	```
282	
283	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
284	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
285	const nextConfig = {
286	  experimental: {
287	    turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true,
288	  },
289	}
290	
291	module.exports = nextConfig
292	```
293	
294	## Async Request APIs (Breaking change)
295	
296	Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility.
297	
298	Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously.
299	
300	- [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies)
301	- [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers)
302	- [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode)
303	- `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon).
304	- `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page)
305	
306	Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs.
307	
308	### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs
309	
310	To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers:
311	
312	- [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper)
313	- [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper)
314	- [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper)
315	
316	> **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5
317	
318	This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example:
319	
320	```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx"
321	export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) {
322	  const { slug } = await props.params
323	  const query = await props.searchParams
324	  return <h1>Blog Post: {slug}</h1>
325	}
326	```
327	
328	This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page.
329	
330	## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change)
331	
332	> The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises.
333	
334	In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function.
335	
336	```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js"
337	// Next.js 15 - synchronous params access
338	export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) {
339	  const { slug } = params
340	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }]
341	}
342	
343	// Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access
344	export default function Image({ params, id }) {
345	  const slug = params.slug
346	  const imageId = id // string
347	  // ...
348	}
349	```
350	
351	Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`.
352	
353	```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js"
354	export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) {
355	  const { slug } = params
356	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }]
357	}
358	
359	// Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access
360	export default async function Image({ params, id }) {
361	  const { slug } = await params // params now async
362	  const imageId = await id // id is now Promise<string> when using generateImageMetadata
363	  // ...
364	}
365	```
366	
367	## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change)
368	
369	Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function.
370	
371	```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js"
372	export async function generateSitemaps() {
373	  return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }]
374	}
375	
376	// Next.js 15 - synchronous id access
377	export default async function sitemap({ id }) {
378	  const start = id * 50000 // id is a number
379	  // ...
380	}
381	```
382	
383	Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise.
384	
385	```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js"
386	export async function generateSitemaps() {
387	  return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }]
388	}
389	
390	// Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access
391	export default async function sitemap({ id }) {
392	  const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise<string>
393	  const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000
394	  // ...
395	}
396	```
397	
398	## React 19.2
399	
400	The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include:
401	
402	- **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation
403	- **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions
404	- **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects
405	
406	Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2).
407	
408	## React Compiler Support
409	
410	Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes.
411	
412	The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types.
413	
414	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
415	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
416	
417	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
418	  reactCompiler: true,
419	}
420	
421	export default nextConfig
422	```
423	
424	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
425	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
426	const nextConfig = {
427	  reactCompiler: true,
428	}
429	
430	module.exports = nextConfig
431	```
432	
433	Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin:
434	
435	```bash package="pnpm"
436	pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler
437	```
438	
439	```bash package="npm"
440	npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler
441	```
442	
443	```bash package="yarn"
444	yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler
445	```
446	
447	```bash package="bun"
448	bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler
449	```
450	
451	> **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel.
452	
453	## Caching APIs
454	
455	### revalidateTag
456	
457	[`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error.
458	
459	```ts
460	// Before
461	revalidateTag('posts')
462	
463	// After
464	revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
465	```
466	
467	If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead.
468	
469	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
470	'use server'
471	
472	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
473	
474	export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) {
475	  // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates
476	  revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max')
477	}
478	```
479	
480	```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
481	'use server'
482	
483	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
484	
485	export async function updateArticle(articleId) {
486	  // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates
487	  revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max')
488	}
489	```
490	
491	Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background.
492	
493	### updateTag
494	
495	[`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
496	
497	It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request.
498	
499	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
500	'use server'
501	
502	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
503	
504	export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) {
505	  await db.users.update(userId, profile)
506	
507	  // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away
508	  updateTag(`user-${userId}`)
509	}
510	```
511	
512	```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
513	'use server'
514	
515	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
516	
517	export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) {
518	  await db.users.update(userId, profile)
519	
520	  // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away
521	  updateTag(`user-${userId}`)
522	}
523	```
524	
525	This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly.
526	
527	Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag).
528	
529	### refresh
530	
531	[`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action.
532	
533	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
534	'use server'
535	
536	import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
537	
538	export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) {
539	  // Update the notification in the database
540	  await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId)
541	
542	  // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header
543	  refresh()
544	}
545	```
546	
547	```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
548	'use server'
549	
550	import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
551	
552	export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) {
553	  // Update the notification in the database
554	  await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId)
555	
556	  // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header
557	  refresh()
558	}
559	```
560	
561	Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action.
562	
563	### cacheLife and cacheTag
564	
565	[`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed.
566	
567	Wherever you had aliased imports like:
568	
569	```ts
570	import {
571	  unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife,
572	  unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag,
573	} from 'next/cache'
574	```
575	
576	You can update your imports to:
577	
578	```ts
579	import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
580	```
581	
582	## Enhanced Routing and Navigation
583	
584	**Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data:
585	
586	- **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once.
587	- **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages.
588	
589	These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps.
590	
591	However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications.
592	
593	If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item.
594	
595	## Partial Prerendering (PPR)
596	
597	**Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`.
598	
599	Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration.
600	
601	```js filename="next.config.js"
602	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
603	const nextConfig = {
604	  cacheComponents: true,
605	}
606	
607	module.exports = nextConfig
608	```
609	
610	PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns.
611	
612	```js filename="next.config.js"
613	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
614	const nextConfig = {
615	  // If you are using PPR today
616	  // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary
617	  experimental: {
618	    ppr: true,
619	  },
620	}
621	
622	module.exports = nextConfig
623	```
624	
625	## `middleware` to `proxy`
626	
627	The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus.
628	
629	The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions.
630	
631	```bash filename="Terminal"
632	# Rename your middleware file
633	mv middleware.ts proxy.ts
634	# or
635	mv middleware.js proxy.js
636	```
637	
638	The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`.
639	
640	```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
641	export function proxy(request: Request) {}
642	```
643	
644	```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
645	export function proxy(request) {}
646	```
647	
648	We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export.
649	
650	Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize`
651	
652	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
653	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
654	
655	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
656	  skipProxyUrlNormalize: true,
657	}
658	
659	export default nextConfig
660	```
661	
662	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
663	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
664	const nextConfig = {
665	  skipProxyUrlNormalize: true,
666	}
667	
668	module.exports = nextConfig
669	```
670	
671	The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too.
672	
673	## `next/image` changes
674	
675	### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change)
676	
677	Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks.
678	
679	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
680	import Image from 'next/image'
681	
682	export default function Page() {
683	  return <Image src="/assets/photo?v=1" alt="Photo" width="100" height="100" />
684	}
685	```
686	
687	If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration:
688	
689	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
690	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
691	
692	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
693	  images: {
694	    localPatterns: [
695	      {
696	        pathname: '/assets/**',
697	        search: '?v=1',
698	      },
699	    ],
700	  },
701	}
702	
703	export default nextConfig
704	```
705	
706	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
707	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
708	const nextConfig = {
709	  images: {
710	    localPatterns: [
711	      {
712	        pathname: '/assets/**',
713	        search: '?v=1',
714	      },
715	    ],
716	  },
717	}
718	
719	module.exports = nextConfig
720	```
721	
722	### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change)
723	
724	The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers.
725	
726	For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost.
727	
728	Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed.
729	
730	If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds:
731	
732	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
733	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
734	
735	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
736	  images: {
737	    minimumCacheTTL: 60,
738	  },
739	}
740	
741	export default nextConfig
742	```
743	
744	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
745	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
746	const nextConfig = {
747	  images: {
748	    minimumCacheTTL: 60,
749	  },
750	}
751	
752	module.exports = nextConfig
753	```
754	
755	### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change)
756	
757	The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array.
758	
759	We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`.
760	
761	If you need to support 16px images:
762	
763	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
764	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
765	
766	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
767	  images: {
768	    imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384],
769	  },
770	}
771	
772	export default nextConfig
773	```
774	
775	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
776	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
777	const nextConfig = {
778	  images: {
779	    imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384],
780	  },
781	}
782	
783	module.exports = nextConfig
784	```
785	
786	Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays.
787	
788	### `qualities` Default (Breaking change)
789	
790	The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`.
791	
792	If you need to support multiple quality levels:
793	
794	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
795	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
796	
797	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
798	  images: {
799	    qualities: [50, 75, 100],
800	  },
801	}
802	
803	export default nextConfig
804	```
805	
806	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
807	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
808	const nextConfig = {
809	  images: {
810	    qualities: [50, 75, 100],
811	  },
812	}
813	
814	module.exports = nextConfig
815	```
816	
817	If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75.
818	
819	### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change)
820	
821	A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks.
822	
823	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
824	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
825	
826	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
827	  images: {
828	    dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks
829	  },
830	}
831	
832	export default nextConfig
833	```
834	
835	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
836	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
837	const nextConfig = {
838	  images: {
839	    dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks
840	  },
841	}
842	
843	module.exports = nextConfig
844	```
845	
846	### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change)
847	
848	The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum.
849	
850	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
851	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
852	
853	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
854	  images: {
855	    maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects
856	    // or
857	    maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases
858	  },
859	}
860	
861	export default nextConfig
862	```
863	
864	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
865	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
866	const nextConfig = {
867	  images: {
868	    maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects
869	    // or
870	    maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases
871	  },
872	}
873	
874	module.exports = nextConfig
875	```
876	
877	### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated)
878	
879	The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead:
880	
881	```tsx
882	// Before
883	import Image from 'next/legacy/image'
884	
885	// After
886	import Image from 'next/image'
887	```
888	
889	### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated)
890	
891	The `images.domains` config is deprecated.
892	
893	```js filename="next.config.js"
894	// image.domains is deprecated
895	module.exports = {
896	  images: {
897	    domains: ['example.com'],
898	  },
899	}
900	```
901	
902	Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security:
903	
904	```js filename="next.config.js"
905	// Use image.remotePatterns instead
906	module.exports = {
907	  images: {
908	    remotePatterns: [
909	      {
910	        protocol: 'https',
911	        hostname: 'example.com',
912	      },
913	    ],
914	  },
915	}
916	```

918	## Concurrent `dev` and `build`
919	
920	`next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`.
921	
922	Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project.
923	
924	Since the development server outputs to `.next/dev`, the [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be:
925	
926	```bash package="pnpm"
927	pnpm next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack
928	```
929	
930	```bash package="npm"
931	npx next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack
932	```
933	
934	```bash package="yarn"
935	yarn next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack
936	```
937	
938	```bash package="bun"
939	bunx next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack
940	```
941	
942	## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement
943	
944	All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them.
945	
946	To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`.
947	
948	```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx"
949	import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
950	
951	export default function Default() {
952	  notFound()
953	}
954	```
955	
956	Or return `null`:
957	
958	```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx"
959	export default function Default() {
960	  return null
961	}
962	```
963	
964	## ESLint Flat Config
965	
966	`@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support.
967	
968	Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin.
969	
970	If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details.
971	
972	## Scroll Behavior Override
973	
974	In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `<html>` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows:
975	
976	1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto`
977	2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top)
978	3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value
979	
980	This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation.
981	
982	In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation.
983	
984	**If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `<html>` element:
985	
986	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
987	export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
988	  return (
989	    <html lang="en" data-scroll-behavior="smooth">
990	      <body>{children}</body>
991	    </html>
992	  )
993	}
994	```
995	
996	## Performance Improvements
997	
998	Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics.
999	
1000	**Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload.
1001	
1002	The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes.
1003	
1004	### `next dev` config load
1005	
1006	In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development:
1007	
1008	- When running the `next dev` command
1009	- When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server
1010	
1011	This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server.
1012	
1013	A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`.
1014	
1015	> **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`.
1016	
1017	This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`.
1018	
1019	```js filename="next.config.js"
1020	import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server'
1021	
1022	const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'
1023	
1024	if (isDev) {
1025	  startServer()
1026	}
1027	
1028	const nextConfig = {
1029	  /* Your config options */
1030	}
1031	
1032	module.exports = nextConfig
1033	```
1034	
1035	Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded.
1036	
1037	## Build Adapters API (alpha)
1038	
1039	Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available.
1040	
1041	Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output.
1042	
1043	```js filename="next.config.js"
1044	const nextConfig = {
1045	  experimental: {
1046	    adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'),
1047	  },
1048	}
1049	
1050	module.exports = nextConfig
1051	```
1052	
1053	`adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference.
1054	
1055	## Modern Sass API
1056	
1057	`sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features.
1058	
1059	## Removals
1060	
1061	These features were previously deprecated and are now removed:
1062	
1063	### AMP Support
1064	
1065	AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed:
1066	
1067	- `amp` configuration from your Next config file
1068	- `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`)
1069	
1070	```tsx
1071	// Removed
1072	import { useAmp } from 'next/amp'
1073	
1074	// Removed
1075	export const config = { amp: true }
1076	```
1077	
1078	- `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages
1079	
1080	```js filename="next.config.js"
1081	const nextConfig = {
1082	  // Removed
1083	  amp: {
1084	    canonicalBase: 'https://example.com',
1085	  },
1086	}
1087	
1088	export default nextConfig
1089	```
1090	
1091	Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards.
1092	
1093	### `next lint` Command
1094	
1095	The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting.
1096	
1097	A codemod is available to automate migration:
1098	
1099	```bash package="pnpm"
1100	pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
1101	```
1102	
1103	```bash package="npm"
1104	npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
1105	```
1106	
1107	```bash package="yarn"
1108	yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
1109	```
1110	
1111	```bash package="bun"
1112	bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
1113	```
1114	
1115	The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed.
1116	
1117	```js filename="next.config.mjs"
1118	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
1119	const nextConfig = {
1120	  // No longer supported
1121	  // eslint: {},
1122	}
1123	
1124	export default nextConfig
1125	```
1126	
1127	### Runtime Configuration
1128	
1129	`serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead.
1130	
1131	**Before (Next.js 15):**
1132	
1133	```js filename="next.config.js"
1134	module.exports = {
1135	  serverRuntimeConfig: {
1136	    dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
1137	  },
1138	  publicRuntimeConfig: {
1139	    apiUrl: '/api',
1140	  },
1141	}
1142	```
1143	
1144	```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx"
1145	import getConfig from 'next/config'
1146	
1147	export default function Page() {
1148	  const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig()
1149	  return <p>API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}</p>
1150	}
1151	```
1152	
1153	**After (Next.js 16):**
1154	
1155	For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components:
1156	
1157	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1158	async function fetchData() {
1159	  const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL
1160	  // Use for server-side operations only
1161	  return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users')
1162	}
1163	
1164	export default async function Page() {
1165	  const data = await fetchData()
1166	  return <div>{/* render data */}</div>
1167	}
1168	```
1169	
1170	> **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components.
1171	
1172	For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix:
1173	
1174	```bash filename=".env.local"
1175	NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api"
1176	```
1177	
1178	```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx"
1179	'use client'
1180	
1181	export default function ClientComponent() {
1182	  const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
1183	  return <p>API URL: {apiUrl}</p>
1184	}
1185	```
1186	
1187	To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`:
1188	
1189	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1190	import { connection } from 'next/server'
1191	
1192	export default async function Page() {
1193	  await connection()
1194	  const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG
1195	  return <p>{config}</p>
1196	}
1197	```
1198	
1199	Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables).
1200	
1201	### `devIndicators` Options
1202	
1203	The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators):
1204	
1205	- `appIsrStatus`
1206	- `buildActivity`
1207	- `buildActivityPosition`
1208	
1209	The indicator itself remains available.
1210	
1211	### `experimental.dynamicIO`
1212	
1213	The `experimental.dynamicIO` flag has been renamed to `cacheComponents`:
1214	
1215	Update your Next config file, by removing the `dynamicIO` flag.
1216	
1217	```js filename="next.config.js"
1218	// Next.js 15 - experimental.dynamicIO is now removed
1219	module.exports = {
1220	  experimental: {
1221	    dynamicIO: true,
1222	  },
1223	}
1224	```
1225	
1226	Add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag set to true.
1227	
1228	```js filename="next.config.js"
1229	// Next.js 16 - use cacheComponents instead
1230	module.exports = {
1231	  cacheComponents: true,
1232	}
1233	```
1234	
1235	### `unstable_rootParams`
1236	
1237	The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. We are working on an alternative API that we will ship in an upcoming minor release.
1238	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/lib/db.ts",
  "content": "import Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"./types\";\n\nlet _db: Database.Database | null = null;\n\nexport function db(): Database.Database {\n  if (_db) return _db;\n  const file = path.join(process.cwd(), \"lipi.db\");\n  _db = new Database(file);\n  _db.pragma(\"journal_mode = WAL\");\n  _db.exec(`\n    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS morpheme_cache (\n      script TEXT NOT NULL,\n      surface TEXT NOT NULL,\n      morpheme_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n      updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n      PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)\n    );\n  `);\n  return _db;\n}\n\nexport function getCached(script: string, surface: string): Morpheme | null {\n  const row = db()\n    .prepare(\n      \"SELECT morpheme_json FROM morpheme_cache WHERE script = ? AND surface = ?\",\n    )\n    .get(script, surface) as { morpheme_json: string } | undefined;\n  if (!row) return null;\n  return JSON.parse(row.morpheme_json) as Morpheme;\n}\n\nexport function putCached(morpheme: Morpheme): void {\n  db()\n    .prepare(\n      `INSERT INTO morpheme_cache (script, surface, morpheme_json, updated_at)\n       VALUES (?, ?, ?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\n       ON CONFLICT(script, surface) DO UPDATE SET\n         morpheme_json = excluded.morpheme_json,\n         updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`,\n    )\n    .run(morpheme.script, morpheme.surface, JSON.stringify(morpheme));\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/lib/wiktionary.ts",
  "content": "import { gurmukhiToDevanagari } from \"./transliterate\";\n\nexport interface WiktionaryHit {\n  page: string;\n  url: string;\n  wikitext: string;\n  matched_script: \"gurmukhi\" | \"devanagari\";\n}\n\nconst API = \"https://en.wiktionary.org/w/api.php\";\n\nasync function fetchWikitext(page: string): Promise<string | null> {\n  const url = new URL(API);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"action\", \"parse\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"format\", \"json\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"prop\", \"wikitext\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"page\", page);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"origin\", \"*\");\n  const res = await fetch(url, {\n    headers: { \"User-Agent\": \"Lipi/0.1 (Punjabi reading tool; dev)\" },\n    cache: \"force-cache\",\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) return null;\n  const json = (await res.json()) as {\n    parse?: { wikitext?: { \"*\": string } };\n    error?: unknown;\n  };\n  if (json.error || !json.parse?.wikitext?.[\"*\"]) return null;\n  return json.parse.wikitext[\"*\"];\n}\n\nexport async function lookupWiktionary(\n  gurmukhi: string,\n): Promise<WiktionaryHit | null> {\n  const gurmukhiHit = await fetchWikitext(gurmukhi);\n  if (gurmukhiHit) {\n    return {\n      page: gurmukhi,\n      url: `https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/${encodeURIComponent(gurmukhi)}`,\n      wikitext: gurmukhiHit,\n      matched_script: \"gurmukhi\",\n    };\n  }\n  const devanagari = gurmukhiToDevanagari(gurmukhi);\n  if (devanagari !== gurmukhi) {\n    const devHit = await fetchWikitext(devanagari);\n    if (devHit) {\n      return {\n        page: devanagari,\n        url: `https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/${encodeURIComponent(devanagari)}`,\n        wikitext: devHit,\n        matched_script: \"devanagari\",\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Trim the raw wikitext to sections most relevant to etymology, to keep\n * the LLM prompt tight. Returns the entire wikitext if no anchors are found.\n */\nexport function extractRelevantSections(wikitext: string): string {\n  const langOrder = [\"Punjabi\", \"Hindi\", \"Sanskrit\", \"Urdu\", \"Persian\", \"Arabic\"];\n  const sections: string[] = [];\n  for (const lang of langOrder) {\n    const re = new RegExp(`==\\\\s*${lang}\\\\s*==([\\\\s\\\\S]*?)(?=\\\\n==[^=]|$)`, \"i\");\n    const m = wikitext.match(re);\n    if (m) sections.push(`== ${lang} ==\\n${m[1].trim()}`);\n  }\n  if (sections.length === 0) return wikitext.slice(0, 8000);\n  return sections.join(\"\\n\\n\").slice(0, 8000);\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import Anthropic from \"@anthropic-ai/sdk\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"./types\";\nimport { gurmukhiToIso15919 } from \"./transliterate\";\n\nlet _client: Anthropic | null = null;\nfunction client(): Anthropic {\n  if (!_client) _client = new Anthropic();\n  return _client;\n}\n\nconst ETYMOLOGY_INSTRUCTIONS = `You are a Punjabi etymologist. Given a Punjabi word (in Gurmukhi) and optional grounding from Wiktionary, produce a structured morphological decomposition.\n\nCRITICAL RULES:\n1. Punjabi vocabulary comes from multiple streams. Identify which applies before decomposing:\n   - Tatsama (direct from Sanskrit): e.g. ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ parmātmā = ਪਰਮ param (\"supreme\") + ਆਤਮਾ ātmā (\"soul\"). Sanskrit-style root decomposition is meaningful.\n   - Tadbhava (evolved from Sanskrit/Prakrit): decomposition is historical, often a single morpheme synchronically.\n   - Perso-Arabic loans (via Mughal influence): e.g. ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ zindagī = Persian zinda (\"alive\") + -gī (abstract suffix). DO NOT force a Sanskrit decomposition on these.\n   - Native Indo-Aryan: may not decompose further.\n2. If you are uncertain about etymology, mark provenance.confidence = \"unverified\". Better to admit uncertainty than to fabricate roots.\n3. Only decompose when the components are real, identifiable morphemes — not arbitrary syllable splits.\n4. For ground truth: prefer the supplied Wiktionary context. If it conflicts with what you \"remember,\" trust Wiktionary.\n\nOUTPUT: a single JSON object matching the Morpheme schema. No prose, no markdown fences.\n\nMorpheme schema:\n{\n  \"surface\": string (Gurmukhi),\n  \"script\": \"gurmukhi\",\n  \"romanized\": string (ISO 15919),\n  \"gloss_en\": string (concise English meaning),\n  \"source_language\": \"sanskrit\" | \"prakrit\" | \"old-punjabi\" | \"punjabi\" | \"persian\" | \"arabic\" | \"turkic\" | \"portuguese\" | \"english\" | \"unknown\",\n  \"source_form\": string | null (the parent-language form, e.g. \"परम\" for Sanskrit param),\n  \"source_form_script\": \"devanagari\" | \"perso-arabic\" | \"latin\" | null,\n  \"provenance\": {\n    \"source\": \"wiktionary\" | \"llm\",\n    \"url\": string | null,\n    \"confidence\": \"verified\" | \"unverified\",\n    \"note\": string | null (optional 1-line explanation of decomposition or uncertainty)\n  },\n  \"components\": Morpheme[] (recursive; empty array if atomic)\n}`;\n\nexport interface DecomposeArgs {\n  surface: string;\n  wiktionaryUrl?: string;\n  wiktionaryExcerpt?: string;\n}\n\nexport async function decomposeWithClaude(\n  args: DecomposeArgs,\n): Promise<Morpheme> {\n  const grounding = args.wiktionaryExcerpt\n    ? `Wiktionary entry (${args.wiktionaryUrl}):\\n\\n${args.wiktionaryExcerpt}`\n    : \"No Wiktionary entry was found for this word. Use your knowledge but mark provenance.confidence as 'unverified'.\";\n\n  const response = await client().messages.create({\n    model: \"claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    max_tokens: 4096,\n    system: [\n      {\n        type: \"text\",\n        text: ETYMOLOGY_INSTRUCTIONS,\n        cache_control: { type: \"ephemeral\" },\n      },\n    ],\n    messages: [\n      {\n        role: \"user\",\n        content: `Word: ${args.surface}\\nRomanized (ISO 15919 hint): ${gurmukhiToIso15919(args.surface)}\\n\\n${grounding}\\n\\nReturn the JSON now.`,\n      },\n    ],\n  });\n\n  const text = response.content\n    .filter((b): b is Anthropic.TextBlock => b.type === \"text\")\n    .map((b) => b.text)\n    .join(\"\")\n    .trim();\n\n  const jsonText = stripCodeFences(text);\n  const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonText) as Morpheme;\n  return parsed;\n}\n\nfunction stripCodeFences(text: string): string {\n  const fenced = text.match(/```(?:json)?\\s*([\\s\\S]*?)```/);\n  if (fenced) return fenced[1].trim();\n  return text;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/lib/morpheme-service.ts",
  "content": "import { getCached, putCached } from \"./db\";\nimport { lookupWiktionary, extractRelevantSections } from \"./wiktionary\";\nimport { decomposeWithClaude } from \"./claude\";\nimport { gurmukhiToIso15919 } from \"./transliterate\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"./types\";\n\n/**\n * Resolve a Punjabi word to a structured morpheme tree.\n * Order: SQLite cache → Wiktionary + Claude → Claude alone.\n */\nexport async function getMorpheme(surface: string): Promise<Morpheme> {\n  const cached = getCached(\"gurmukhi\", surface);\n  if (cached) return cached;\n\n  const wikt = await lookupWiktionary(surface);\n  const morpheme = await decomposeWithClaude({\n    surface,\n    wiktionaryUrl: wikt?.url,\n    wiktionaryExcerpt: wikt ? extractRelevantSections(wikt.wikitext) : undefined,\n  });\n\n  if (wikt && morpheme.provenance) {\n    morpheme.provenance.url ??= wikt.url;\n    morpheme.provenance.source = morpheme.provenance.source ?? \"wiktionary\";\n  }\n  morpheme.surface = morpheme.surface || surface;\n  morpheme.script = \"gurmukhi\";\n  morpheme.romanized = morpheme.romanized || gurmukhiToIso15919(surface);\n\n  putCached(morpheme);\n  return morpheme;\n}\n\nexport function overrideMorpheme(morpheme: Morpheme): Morpheme {\n  const stamped: Morpheme = {\n    ...morpheme,\n    provenance: {\n      ...morpheme.provenance,\n      source: \"manual\",\n      confidence: \"verified\",\n      fetched_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n    },\n  };\n  putCached(stamped);\n  return stamped;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import type { Sakhi } from \"@/lib/types\";\nimport { gurmukhiToIso15919 } from \"@/lib/transliterate\";\n\n/**\n * v0 seed content. Three short, well-known sentences about Guru Nanak that\n * exercise the decomposition pipeline (Sanskrit compounds, native verbs,\n * abstract nouns).\n *\n * Replace with a sourced Janamsakhi excerpt + verified human translation.\n */\nconst RAW: { gurmukhi: string; english: string }[] = [\n  {\n    gurmukhi: \"ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਨ।\",\n    english: \"Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Guru of Punjab.\",\n  },\n  {\n    gurmukhi: \"ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੀ ਏਕਤਾ ਦਾ ਸੁਨੇਹਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ।\",\n    english: \"He delivered the message of God's oneness.\",\n  },\n  {\n    gurmukhi: \"ਸੱਚ ਹੀ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਧਰਮ ਹੈ।\",\n    english: \"Truth alone is the highest dharma.\",\n  },\n];\n\nconst SENTENCE_TERMINATORS = /[।॥.?!]/;\n\nfunction tokenize(gurmukhi: string): string[] {\n  return gurmukhi\n    .split(/\\s+/)\n    .map((w) => w.replace(SENTENCE_TERMINATORS, \"\"))\n    .filter((w) => w.length > 0);\n}\n\nexport const SAKHI: Sakhi = {\n  id: \"seed-guru-nanak\",\n  title_gurmukhi: \"ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ\",\n  title_en: \"Guru Nanak Dev Ji\",\n  source: \"Editorial placeholder — replace with sourced Janamsakhi excerpt.\",\n  sentences: RAW.map((s, i) => ({\n    id: `s${i}`,\n    gurmukhi: s.gurmukhi,\n    romanized: gurmukhiToIso15919(s.gurmukhi),\n    english: s.english,\n    words: tokenize(s.gurmukhi),\n  })),\n};\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/app/api/morpheme/route.ts",
  "content": "import { getMorpheme, overrideMorpheme } from \"@/lib/morpheme-service\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"@/lib/types\";\n\nexport const runtime = \"nodejs\";\n\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);\n  const word = searchParams.get(\"word\");\n  if (!word) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing 'word' query param\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  try {\n    const morpheme = await getMorpheme(word);\n    return Response.json(morpheme);\n  } catch (err) {\n    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n    return Response.json({ error: message }, { status: 500 });\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\n  const body = (await request.json()) as { morpheme: Morpheme };\n  if (!body?.morpheme?.surface) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing morpheme.surface\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  const stamped = overrideMorpheme(body.morpheme);\n  return Response.json(stamped);\n}\n"
}

}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/components/HoverWord.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\nimport { useEffect, useState } from \"react\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"@/lib/types\";\nimport MorphemePopover from \"./MorphemePopover\";\n\ninterface Props {\n  word: string;\n  isActive: boolean;\n  onOpen: () => void;\n  onClose: () => void;\n}\n\nexport default function HoverWord({ word, isActive, onOpen, onClose }: Props) {\n  const [morpheme, setMorpheme] = useState<Morpheme | null>(null);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);\n  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!isActive || morpheme || loading) return;\n    setLoading(true);\n    setError(null);\n    fetch(`/api/morpheme?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`)\n      .then(async (r) => {\n        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);\n        return r.json();\n      })\n      .then((m: Morpheme) => setMorpheme(m))\n      .catch((e: unknown) => setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)))\n      .finally(() => setLoading(false));\n  }, [isActive, word, morpheme, loading]);\n\n  return (\n    <span className=\"relative inline-block\">\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        onClick={() => (isActive ? onClose() : onOpen())}\n        className={`mx-1 cursor-pointer rounded px-1 transition-colors ${\n          isActive\n            ? \"bg-amber-200 dark:bg-amber-900\"\n            : \"hover:bg-amber-100 dark:hover:bg-amber-950\"\n        }`}\n      >\n        {word}\n      </button>\n      {isActive && (\n        <MorphemePopover\n          word={word}\n          morpheme={morpheme}\n          loading={loading}\n          error={error}\n          onClose={onClose}\n          onUpdate={(m) => setMorpheme(m)}\n        />\n      )}\n    </span>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "\"use client\";\nimport { useState } from \"react\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"@/lib/types\";\n\ninterface Props {\n  word: string;\n  morpheme: Morpheme | null;\n  loading: boolean;\n  error: string | null;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  onUpdate: (m: Morpheme) => void;\n}\n\nexport default function MorphemePopover({\n  word,\n  morpheme,\n  loading,\n  error,\n  onClose,\n  onUpdate,\n}: Props) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"absolute left-1/2 top-full z-50 mt-2 w-96 -translate-x-1/2 rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 bg-white p-4 shadow-xl dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900\">\n      <div className=\"mb-2 flex items-center justify-between\">\n        <div className=\"text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {word}\n        </div>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={onClose}\n          className=\"text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-700 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n          aria-label=\"Close\"\n        >\n          ✕\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      {loading && <div className=\"text-sm text-zinc-500\">Decomposing…</div>}\n      {error && (\n        <div className=\"text-sm text-red-600 dark:text-red-400\">\n          Error: {error}\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {morpheme && (\n        <MorphemeNode morpheme={morpheme} depth={0} onUpdate={onUpdate} />\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction MorphemeNode({\n  morpheme,\n  depth,\n  onUpdate,\n}: {\n  morpheme: Morpheme;\n  depth: number;\n  onUpdate: (m: Morpheme) => void;\n}) {\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(depth === 0);\n  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);\n\n  const hasChildren = morpheme.components && morpheme.components.length > 0;\n  const indentClass = depth > 0 ? \"ml-3 border-l border-zinc-200 pl-3 dark:border-zinc-800\" : \"\";\n\n  return (\n    <div className={indentClass}>\n      <div className=\"flex items-baseline gap-2 py-1\">\n        {hasChildren && (\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            onClick={() => setExpanded((e) => !e)}\n            className=\"text-xs text-zinc-400\"\n          >\n            {expanded ? \"▾\" : \"▸\"}\n          </button>\n        )}\n        <span className=\"font-serif text-base text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {morpheme.surface}\n        </span>\n        <span className=\"font-mono text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n          {morpheme.romanized}\n        </span>\n        <ConfidenceBadge confidence={morpheme.provenance.confidence} />\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"ml-5 text-sm text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n        {morpheme.gloss_en}\n      </div>\n      {morpheme.source_form && (\n        <div className=\"ml-5 text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n          ← {morpheme.source_language} {morpheme.source_form}\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {morpheme.provenance.note && (\n        <div className=\"ml-5 mt-1 text-xs italic text-zinc-500\">\n          {morpheme.provenance.note}\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {depth === 0 && (\n        <div className=\"ml-5 mt-2 flex items-center gap-3 text-xs\">\n          {morpheme.provenance.url && (\n            <a\n              href={morpheme.provenance.url}\n              target=\"_blank\"\n              rel=\"noreferrer\"\n              className=\"text-blue-600 hover:underline dark:text-blue-400\"\n            >\n              Source ↗\n            </a>\n          )}\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            onClick={() => setEditing((e) => !e)}\n            className=\"text-zinc-500 hover:text-zinc-800 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n          >\n            {editing ? \"Cancel\" : \"Wrong? Edit\"}\n          </button>\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {editing && depth === 0 && (\n        <EditForm\n          morpheme={morpheme}\n          onSave={(m) => {\n            onUpdate(m);\n            setEditing(false);\n          }}\n          onCancel={() => setEditing(false)}\n        />\n      )}\n      {expanded && hasChildren && (\n        <div className=\"mt-1\">\n          {morpheme.components.map((c, i) => (\n            <MorphemeNode\n              key={`${c.surface}-${i}`}\n              morpheme={c}\n              depth={depth + 1}\n              onUpdate={onUpdate}\n            />\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConfidenceBadge({\n  confidence,\n}: {\n  confidence: \"verified\" | \"unverified\";\n}) {\n  const verified = confidence === \"verified\";\n  return (\n    <span\n      className={`rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-medium uppercase ${\n        verified\n          ? \"bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700 dark:bg-emerald-950 dark:text-emerald-300\"\n          : \"bg-amber-100 text-amber-700 dark:bg-amber-950 dark:text-amber-300\"\n      }`}\n    >\n      {confidence}\n    </span>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction EditForm({\n  morpheme,\n  onSave,\n  onCancel,\n}: {\n  morpheme: Morpheme;\n  onSave: (m: Morpheme) => void;\n  onCancel: () => void;\n}) {\n  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(JSON.stringify(morpheme, null, 2));\n  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);\n  const [err, setErr] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  async function handleSave() {\n    setSaving(true);\n    setErr(null);\n    try {\n      const parsed = JSON.parse(draft) as Morpheme;\n      const res = await fetch(\"/api/morpheme\", {\n        method: \"POST\",\n        headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n        body: JSON.stringify({ morpheme: parsed }),\n      });\n      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n      onSave((await res.json()) as Morpheme);\n    } catch (e) {\n      setErr(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));\n    } finally {\n      setSaving(false);\n    }\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mt-2\">\n      <textarea\n        value={draft}\n        onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}\n        className=\"h-64 w-full rounded border border-zinc-300 bg-zinc-50 p-2 font-mono text-xs dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n      />\n      {err && <div className=\"mt-1 text-xs text-red-600\">{err}</div>}\n      <div className=\"mt-2 flex gap-2\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={handleSave}\n          disabled={saving}\n          className=\"rounded bg-zinc-900 px-3 py-1 text-xs text-white disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-100 dark:text-zinc-900\"\n        >\n          {saving ? \"Saving…\" : \"Save (overrides cache)\"}\n        </button>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={onCancel}\n          className=\"text-xs text-zinc-500\"\n        >\n          Cancel\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

v0 is built and verified end-to-end at `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi`. Page renders, hover triggers a fetch, the API hits Wiktionary → Claude → SQLite cache, and the only thing missing is your `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

**To run it:**
```sh
cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi
echo 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...' > .env.local
npm run dev
```
Open `http://localhost:3000` and hover any Gurmukhi word.

**What's there:**
- `lib/types.ts` — `Morpheme` tree with `provenance.confidence: 'verified'|'unverified'`
- `lib/db.ts` — SQLite cache keyed by `(script, surface)`, persisted to `lipi.db`
- `lib/transliterate.ts` — Gurmukhi → Devanagari (for Wiktionary fallback) + ISO 15919 romanization
- `lib/wiktionary.ts` — fetches English Wiktionary; tries Gurmukhi page, falls back to Devanagari; trims to relevant language sections to keep the LLM prompt tight
- `lib/claude.ts` — Sonnet 4.6 + cached system prompt that explains tatsama vs. Perso-Arabic decomposition rules and demands an `unverified` flag when guessing
- `lib/morpheme-service.ts` — orchestrator: cache → Wiktionary+Claude → cache
- `app/api/morpheme/route.ts` — `GET ?word=X` for lookups, `POST` for manual overrides (stamped `provenance.source: "manual"`, `confidence: "verified"`)
- `components/Reader.tsx` + `HoverWord.tsx` + `MorphemePopover.tsx` — three-column reader, hoverable words, recursive expandable tree, color-coded confidence badges, and a "Wrong? Edit" JSON editor that overwrites the cache

**v0 caveats to know before you use it:**
- The seed text in `data/sakhi.ts` is editorial placeholder, not a real Janamsakhi excerpt — swap in real sourced content as soon as you trust the pipeline.
- The romanizer is a hand-rolled ISO 15919 approximation; it'll be wrong on edge cases (nasals, geminates, Perso-Arabic-origin sounds). Fine for v0.
- No TTS yet (deferred per the original plan).
- Wiktionary often has *no* entry for the Punjabi page, so most lookups fall back to LLM-only and will show `unverified`. That's the design — the edit flow is how you accumulate ground truth over time.

> DEVELOPER

Why do I need the anthropic key?

> AGENT

Because the Lipi app calls Claude from its own backend (Next.js server, `lib/claude.ts`) — that's a separate process billed against an API key, not your Claude Code subscription. Claude Code doesn't expose a shared credential to other apps on your machine.

Three options:

1. **Get an API key** — fastest. Go to `https://console.anthropic.com/`, create a key, drop it in `.env.local`. You'd pay per-token for decomposition calls (cheap — each lookup is ~1K input + ~500 output tokens with Sonnet 4.6, so fractions of a cent per word, and they're cached forever after the first hit).

2. **Skip the LLM, use Wiktionary only** — I can change `morpheme-service.ts` to return raw Wiktionary etymology as plain text when found, and "no data" otherwise. Free but you lose the structured tree decomposition for the majority of words where Wiktionary has no Punjabi entry.

3. **Local model** — swap the Claude call for a local Ollama instance running something like Llama 3.1 or Qwen. Free, but quality on Indic etymology will be noticeably worse and Punjabi-specific tatsama vs. Perso-Arabic distinctions will likely degrade.

For a learning tool you'll actually use, option 1 is by far the best — the cost is genuinely trivial (your entire library of pre-decomposed words probably stays under a dollar), and the quality gap matters because you're trying to learn from these decompositions, not just see plausible-looking ones. Want me to set up anything differently?

> DEVELOPER

no but why do we need this?

> AGENT

Honestly? We don't strictly need it. I reached for Claude because it does two things that would otherwise be slow:

1. **Parses unstructured Wiktionary wikitext into a clean tree** — Wiktionary's etymology sections are prose like *"From Sanskrit परम (parama, 'highest') + आत्मन् (ātman, 'self')"*. Something has to turn that into the structured `Morpheme` shape with components, source language, etc. An LLM is the path-of-least-resistance parser.

2. **Fills gaps when Wiktionary has nothing** — most Punjabi words don't have full Wiktionary entries, especially the literary vocabulary you care about. Without an LLM, you get "no data" most of the time.

But for a personal learning tool that you'll use slowly over months, there's a cleaner alternative I steered past: **build the dictionary by hand as you read.** Look each new word up yourself (Wiktionary + Platts dictionary online + ask someone for the hard ones), type the decomposition into the edit form once, and it's cached forever. A few hundred high-frequency words covers most Janamsakhi vocabulary, after which new content mostly reuses what's already there. Slower to bootstrap, but you actually *learn* the etymology by entering it instead of accepting an LLM's guess — which is the whole point of the app.

If you want, I can rip out the Claude dependency entirely and make it pure Wiktionary-fetch + manual-entry, so you only ever see verified decompositions. The trade is: empty popovers (with a "look this up" link to Wiktionary) for words you haven't entered yet, instead of confident-but-maybe-wrong LLM output.

> DEVELOPER

I can give you my nano-gpt.com key? do you wanna do some tests with it first??

> AGENT

Yes, smart move — let's validate quality before wiring it in. nano-gpt's API is OpenAI-compatible and proxies a bunch of models, so the test will tell us two things at once: does the key work, and which model gives decent Punjabi etymology.

To test, I need:
1. The key (paste it here, or drop it in `~/.lipi-test-key` and I'll read it from there — your call)
2. Which models you want me to try

For a tool where the etymologies need to be *accurate enough to learn from*, I'd want to test 2-3 models head-to-head on the same word and let you eyeball which one is least wrong. nano-gpt typically routes to all the big names — my picks for the test panel:

- **`claude-sonnet-4-6`** (Anthropic) — what I'd default to
- **`gpt-5`** or **`gpt-4o`** (OpenAI) — sanity check that the answer isn't model-specific
- **`deepseek-chat`** or **`qwen-2.5-72b`** — the cheap-and-cheerful tier, in case quality is close enough that cost wins

I'll write a tiny standalone script that takes 3-4 Punjabi test words (one obvious Sanskrit compound like ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ, one Perso-Arabic loan like ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ, one tricky tadbhava, one verb), runs them through each model, and dumps the side-by-side output for you to judge. That way we're not committing to a stack change based on vibes.

return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef main():\n    key = os.environ.get(\"NANO_GPT_KEY\")\n    if not key:\n        if len(sys.argv) > 1:\n            key = sys.argv[1]\n        else:\n            sys.exit(\"Set NANO_GPT_KEY env var or pass key as first arg.\")\n\n    results = {}\n    total = len(MODELS) * len(TEST_WORDS)\n    n = 0\n    for word, _note in TEST_WORDS:\n        for model in MODELS:\n            n += 1\n            print(f\"[{n}/{total}] {model} ← {word} ...\", end=\" \", flush=True)\n            r = call_model(key, model, word)\n            results[(model, word)] = r\n            status = \"ok\" if r.get(\"ok\") else f\"FAIL ({r.get('error', r.get('parse_error', 'unknown'))[:80]})\"\n            print(f\"{r['latency_ms']}ms  {status}\")\n\n    out_path = Path(__file__).parent / \"test-results.md\"\n    out_path.write_text(render_markdown(results))\n    print(f\"\\nReport written to {out_path}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
