  "new_string": "function tokenizeGurmukhi(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    const t = m[0];\n    if (!seen.has(t)) {\n      seen.add(t);\n      out.push(t);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\n// Split a sakhi body into sentence-sized chunks for sentence-level TTS.\n// Mirrors SakhiReader's splitPa: terminator-aware (। ? !), one entry per\n// sentence, dedup'd so repeated sentences are synth'd once.\nfunction splitSentences(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[^।?!]+[।?!]+[\"'”’)\\]]*|[^।?!]+$/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    const s = m[0].trim();\n    if (s && !seen.has(s)) {\n      seen.add(s);\n      out.push(s);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}"
}

Pronunciation audio\n\nEach word also has a cached MP3 in `audio_cache(word, mp3, fetched_at)`.\n\n**Pipeline** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):\n- Voice: `pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar` (Google Cloud Chirp 3 HD — same family\n  that powers Gemini's voice mode; older Wavenet voices clipped word-final\n  stops, e.g. ਪਿੰਡ came out as \"pin\" without the retroflex ḍ).\n- Input: word + ASCII period (`.`). Without a terminator Chirp 3 picks a\n  question-like rising intonation; daanda `।` causes the engine to clip the\n  output to a tiny stub; ASCII period gives reliable declarative falling tone.\n- Best-of-5: each fetch calls the GCP synth API 5x in parallel and keeps the\n  longest MP3. Chirp 3 is generative and occasionally returns a short clipped\n  sample (~1.3KB instead of 4–7KB); picking the longest reliably filters that\n  out. Cost is ~5 chars × 5 calls × $30/Mchar ≈ $0.0008 per unique word, paid\n  once.\n- Cache key includes the voice name (`pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar:<word>`) so\n  swapping voices automatically invalidates without manual cleanup.\n\n**Requires** `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` in `.env.local` pointing at a\nservice account with the Cloud Text-to-Speech API enabled on its project.",
  "new_string": "## 1b. Pronunciation audio\n\nBoth individual words AND full sentences have cached MP3s in\n`audio_cache(word, mp3, fetched_at)`. The \"word\" column is misnamed — it holds\nany text input (word, sentence, etc.); the route uses the same endpoint and\ncache for both.\n\n**Pipeline** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):\n- Voice: `pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar` (Google Cloud Chirp 3 HD — same family\n  that powers Gemini's voice mode; older Wavenet voices clipped word-final\n  stops, e.g. ਪਿੰਡ came out as \"pin\" without the retroflex ḍ).\n- Input: text + ASCII period (`.`). Without a terminator Chirp 3 picks a\n  question-like rising intonation; daanda `।` causes the engine to clip the\n  output to a tiny stub; ASCII period gives reliable declarative falling tone.\n- Best-of-5: each fetch calls the GCP synth API 5x in parallel and keeps the\n  longest MP3. Chirp 3 is generative and occasionally returns a short clipped\n  sample (~1.3KB instead of 4–7KB); picking the longest reliably filters that\n  out.\n- **Silent-word fallback**: if best-of-5 still comes back under ~2000B (Chirp\n  3 sometimes renders short common particles like ਜੀ, ਦਾ, ਨੇ as ~0.3s of\n  near-silence regardless of how many candidates we generate), the route\n  retries with the input *doubled* (`${w}. ${w}.`). The user hears the word\n  twice but it's audible. Sentences are long enough to avoid this entirely.\n- **Quota backoff**: GCP per-minute quota (~1000 req/min) is easy to trip\n  during bulk prewarms. The route retries per-call on `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`\n  with 2s/5s/12s/30s backoff so a partial batch still contributes to the\n  best-of-5.\n- Cache key includes the voice name (`pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar:<text>`) so\n  swapping voices automatically invalidates without manual cleanup.\n- Cost: ~5 chars × 5 calls × $30/Mchar ≈ $0.0008 per unique word; sentences\n  are proportionally larger but still pennies per sakhi.\n\nThe prewarm script runs *two* TTS passes: `tts-words` (one entry per unique\nGurmukhi token) then `tts-sentences` (one per unique `।`/`?`/`!`-terminated\nsentence in the body). The reader uses both: hover popover plays the word,\nthe speaker icon next to each sentence plays the whole line.\n\n**Requires** `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` in `.env.local` pointing at a\nservice account with the Cloud Text-to-Speech API enabled on its project."
}

> AGENT

Congrats! Here's the cheapest path that scales sanely. I'll recommend a stack, then explain what changes in your current code.

## Recommended stack: Vercel + Supabase + Cloudflare R2

| Layer | Service | Free tier | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hosting** | Vercel | Hobby plan free; 100GB bandwidth/mo | Zero-config for Next.js 16, instant GitHub deploys |
| **Database + Auth** | Supabase | 500MB Postgres + 50k monthly active users + 1GB file storage | One signup gives you DB + accounts + email/Google login |
| **Audio storage** | Cloudflare R2 | 10GB storage + **no egress fees** | Audio streaming bandwidth is what kills you at scale on S3/Supabase; R2 has zero egress charge — critical for this app |
| **TTS / OCR** | Your existing GCP project | Chirp 3 HD: 100k chars/month free | Cached per-word forever, so it stays near-free |
| **Domain + DNS + CDN** | Cloudflare (already!) | Free | Point akhar.io at Vercel |

**Total monthly cost at zero traffic: $0.** Even at a few thousand readers a month: still likely $0. When you outgrow Supabase free, it's $25/mo, Vercel Pro $20/mo — that's roughly when you'd be ready to think about revenue.

## What changes in your current code

You've built almost everything in a way that ports cleanly. The work splits into 4 chunks:

1. **`lipi.db` (SQLite, local) → Supabase Postgres.** Same schema, just different driver. Replace `better-sqlite3` with `pg` or `@supabase/supabase-js`. The `morpheme_cache` and `audio_cache` tables move 1:1. The read-only `data/sakhis.db` (the corpus) is interesting — that's static archival data, could stay as a bundled SQLite file in the Vercel deploy (read-only), or move to Postgres too.

2. **`audio_cache` BLOBs → R2 objects.** Don't store MP3s in Postgres at scale — bandwidth is the killer. Each cached audio becomes a key in R2 (`audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3`); the DB just records "exists, generated at X." R2 streams them with zero egress cost.

3. **Add Supabase Auth.** Drop in `@supabase/ssr` — gives you `signUp`, `signIn`, magic links, Google OAuth in maybe 50 lines. Wrap protected routes (your reader could be public; bookmarks/notes/progress would be per-user).

4. **Deploy: connect your GitHub repo to Vercel, set env vars, point akhar.io DNS.** ~15 minutes.

## What to do first (a concrete first day)

If you want me to start, the order I'd go:

1. Push the current code to a GitHub repo (private is fine — Vercel hobby supports it)
2. Create a Supabase project, get the Postgres URL + service key
3. Migrate the schema (`morpheme_cache`, `audio_cache`) to Postgres
4. Create a Cloudflare R2 bucket, get an API token
5. Move `audio_cache` from BLOB-in-DB to "key in R2, metadata in Postgres"
6. Add a minimal Supabase Auth login page
7. Deploy to Vercel, point akhar.io at it

Want me to start with step 1 (initializing the repo + dependencies) or do you want to talk through any of these choices first? If you'd rather go full-Cloudflare (Pages + D1 + R2) for ideological consistency with the domain registrar, that's a viable alternative — slightly cheaper at huge scale, slightly more friction for Next.js right now.

> DEVELOPER

just a question could I get in trouble for charging for this app?

> AGENT

Short answer: **probably fine for the core idea, but specific content sources matter, and there's a separate community-perception risk that's worth thinking about even when there's no legal one.**

The actual risk areas:

**1. Bhai Vir Singh's Punjabi originals** — He died in 1957. Under Indian copyright (life + 60 years), his works entered public domain on Jan 1, 2018. So the Punjabi text is fine to use commercially in India. Western countries use life + 70, so they're protected in the UK/US/EU until ~2027–28. In practice his works are reprinted everywhere without enforcement and the foundation that manages his estate (Bhai Vir Singh Sahitya Sadan) is mission-driven, not litigious — but technically there's a window where US users could be a legal grey area.

**2. The English translations** — This is the bigger one. If you OCR'd English translations from sikhbookclub.com or similar, those translators/publishers hold separate copyright on the translation even when the original is PD. The safe play: rewrite the English yourself (which you're already doing in body_en hand-cleanup) or commission/generate your own. Don't ship verbatim someone else's translation behind a paywall.

**3. Punjabipedia** — You're scraping their entries into your popovers. Check their TOS; most wiki-style projects are CC-BY-SA which requires attribution AND that derivatives stay openly licensed. You already show ਸਰੋਤ markers in the popup which is most of the attribution work; the share-alike clause could complicate selling the dataset itself, but probably doesn't affect selling app access.

**4. Google Cloud TTS audio** — GCP's TOS explicitly allow commercial use of outputs. No issue.

**5. Trademark on "akhar"** — Common Punjabi word, unlikely to be trademarked but worth a 10-min USPTO/IPO search before printing merch.

**The non-legal risk** worth flagging: Sikh community norms around free access to spiritual content are strong (seva, langar). Every major Sikh app — SikhNet, SikhiToTheMax, Gurbani Now — is donation-based, not paid. Charging for sakhi access (vs. e.g., charging for *user features* like cross-device bookmarks, downloadable audio, personal notes, progress tracking) tends to get blowback. The common pattern is: **core reading free, "pro" features paid.** This sidesteps both the "you're selling sacred content" criticism and most of the copyright grey-area pressure.

If you go that route, you're effectively only monetizing your *engineering*, not the texts — which is on much firmer ground both legally and reputationally. And it lets you grow the user base faster, because free is the lowest-friction onboarding.

**Bottom line:** Won't get sued at small scale. Get a lawyer before raising money or hitting US scale. And consider the freemium model regardless of legal risk — it's a better fit for the space.

> DEVELOPER

Okay but these are sakhi, not sacred text and also you can buy sakhis as books right...

> AGENT

You're right — I conflated two things. Let me correct that:

- **Gurbani** (the scripture in SGGS) has strong "must be free" norms. That's why SikhiToTheMax / SikhNet / Gurbani Now don't charge — they ship scripture.
- **Sakhis** are narrative literature *about* the Gurus, written by authors. They've been commercially published as books for over a century. Bhai Vir Singh himself made his living from publishing and selling these. Singh Brothers Amritsar, Bhai Vir Singh Sahitya Sadan, Sikh Book Club, Amazon — all sell sakhi books at full retail.

So **selling akhar.io is the digital equivalent of selling a sakhi book — totally normal and well-established commercial territory.** No different from a Penguin Classics paid ebook of, say, the Mahabharata translations.

The actual legal points I raised still stand:
1. Bhai Vir Singh's Punjabi text — PD in India since 2018, grey in US/UK until ~2027 (low practical risk)
2. Don't ship someone else's verbatim English translation — write your own (you're already doing this)
3. Punjabipedia attribution per their license (you already display ਸਰੋਤ markers)

But the "community will object to monetization" concern I raised was overblown for sakhi content specifically. Apologies for the overcorrection — your instinct is right. A paid akhar.io is a normal product, not a transgression.

Freemium is still a *good* business choice (lower friction, bigger top of funnel, lets you charge for engineering features like cross-device sync, audio downloads, bookmarks), but for product/growth reasons — not because charging would be wrong.

> DEVELOPER

The idea is to make this a pubjabi learning platform which I don't think exists at a good scale yet and at least not one that's premium

> AGENT

Big opportunity — and there's a real gap. Quick market scan:

**No premium Punjabi learning app exists at scale.** Duolingo has 40+ languages but still no Punjabi (~100M+ speakers globally — by speaker count it's bigger than Korean, Italian, Polish — but underserved because it's "ethnic" not "tourist"). Pimsleur has audio-only Punjabi at $15/mo. The rest is YouTube + low-quality Indian apps. The diaspora demand (UK / Canada / US / Australia Sikh families wanting kids to keep the language) is high-willingness-to-pay and currently un-monetized.

**Your existing build is already 70% of a premium learning platform**, you just haven't framed it that way:
- Parallel text reader = LingQ / Beelinguapp model (narrative-driven learning, currently in vogue vs. Duolingo-style drills)
- Hover popover with romanization + etymology + Punjabipedia = best-in-class lookup
- Sentence-level Chirp 3 audio = built-in shadowing/listening practice
- Bhai Vir Singh sakhis = differentiated content (cultural+religious vs. generic textbook material — and parents/kids both engage with it)

**What you'd add to position as "learning platform" v1:**
1. **Accounts** (already in the plan — Supabase Auth)
2. **SRS deck**: clicking any word during reading adds it to a personal Anki-style spaced-repetition deck. Free tier = 50 words, paid = unlimited. Huge perceived value.
3. **Progress tracking**: "you've read 12 sakhis, know 340 words, listened to 2.1 hours." The dashboard is what justifies subscription pricing.
4. **Difficulty curve**: tag content by level (simple folk tales → Bhai Vir Singh's literary register). Start beginners gently.
5. **Mobile-first PWA**: most learners read on phones. Next.js PWA is straightforward.
6. **Listening mode**: shuffle through sentences with audio + show meaning after delay (passive practice).

**Pricing benchmark**: $8–12/mo, $60–80/year is the niche-language-learning sweet spot. Diaspora parents pay $30+/mo for kids' heritage-language tutoring on iTalki / OutSchool — so $10/mo for an app is easy.

**Freemium structure that works for this market:**
- Free forever: read the whole corpus, basic hover lookups, listen to audio
- Premium ($10/mo): SRS deck unlimited, progress tracking, sentence-level "shadow this" exercises, offline downloads, advanced grammar notes

The architecture we just started (Vercel + Supabase + R2) handles all of this with zero changes. Accounts → Supabase Auth. SRS state → Postgres table. Audio → R2.

---
title: How to implement authentication in Next.js
nav_title: Authentication
description: Learn how to implement authentication in your Next.js application.
---

Understanding authentication is crucial for protecting your application's data. This page will guide you through what React and Next.js features to use to implement auth.

Before starting, it helps to break down the process into three concepts:

1. **[Authentication](#authentication)**: Verifies if the user is who they say they are. It requires the user to prove their identity with something they have, such as a username and password.
2. **[Session Management](#session-management)**: Tracks the user's auth state across requests.
3. **[Authorization](#authorization)**: Decides what routes and data the user can access.

This diagram shows the authentication flow using React and Next.js features:

<Image
  alt="Diagram showing the authentication flow with React and Next.js features"
  srcLight="/docs/light/authentication-overview.png"
  srcDark="/docs/dark/authentication-overview.png"
  width="1600"
  height="1383"
/>

The examples on this page walk through basic username and password auth for educational purposes. While you can implement a custom auth solution, for increased security and simplicity, we recommend using an authentication library. These offer built-in solutions for authentication, session management, and authorization, as well as additional features such as social logins, multi-factor authentication, and role-based access control. You can find a list in the [Auth Libraries](#auth-libraries) section.

## Authentication

<AppOnly>

### Sign-up and login functionality

You can use the [`<form>`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/form) element with React's [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) and `useActionState` to capture user credentials, validate form fields, and call your Authentication Provider's API or database.

Since Server Actions always execute on the server, they provide a secure environment for handling authentication logic.

Here are the steps to implement signup/login functionality:

#### 1. Capture user credentials

To capture user credentials, create a form that invokes a Server Action on submission. For example, a signup form that accepts the user's name, email, and password:

```tsx filename="app/ui/signup-form.tsx" switcher
import { signup } from '@/app/actions/auth'

export function SignupForm() {
  return (
    <form action={signup}>
      <div>
        <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
        <input id="name" name="name" placeholder="Name" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
        <input id="email" name="email" type="email" placeholder="Email" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <label htmlFor="password">Password</label>
        <input id="password" name="password" type="password" />
      </div>
      <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/ui/signup-form.js" switcher
import { signup } from '@/app/actions/auth'

export function SignupForm() {
  return (
    <form action={signup}>
      <div>
        <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
        <input id="name" name="name" placeholder="Name" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
        <input id="email" name="email" type="email" placeholder="Email" />
      </div>
===cookies===
---
title: cookies
description: API Reference for the cookies function.
---

`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

## Reference

### Methods

The following methods are available:

| Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
| `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
| `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
| `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
| `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
| `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |

### Options

When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:

| Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
| `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
| `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
| `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
| `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
| `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/lipi/supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql",
  "content": "-- akhar.io — initial schema.\n--\n-- Two layers:\n--\n--   1. SHARED CACHES (no user_id) — derived data we generate from external\n--      sources, identical for everyone, paid for once.\n--        - morpheme_cache: per-word dictionary entry (PA word → JSON with\n--          romanization, gloss, etymology, Punjabipedia entries)\n--        - audio_meta: per-text TTS metadata (the MP3 itself lives in R2)\n--\n--   2. PER-USER LEARNING STATE — every row scoped to auth.users.id with RLS,\n--      so a user can only ever read/write their own data.\n--        - sakhi_progress: read/in-progress/done per sakhi\n--        - bookmarks: arbitrary saved positions\n--        - srs_cards: spaced-repetition deck\n--        - srs_reviews: review history\n--        - word_encounters: every PA word the user has ever hovered\n--        - profiles: account-level info (display name, level, plan tier)\n\n-- ============================================================\n-- Shared caches\n-- ============================================================\n\nCREATE TABLE morpheme_cache (\n  script        TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- 'gurmukhi' for now\n  surface       TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- the word as it appears\n  morpheme_json JSONB NOT NULL,                 -- full Morpheme object\n  processed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, -- manual verification gate\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)\n);\n\n-- TTS audio: the MP3 BLOB lives in Cloudflare R2 (bandwidth = main scaling\n-- cost, R2 has no egress fees). Here we only track what's been generated.\n-- The R2 object key is derived deterministically: audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3\nCREATE TABLE audio_meta (\n  voice        TEXT NOT NULL,        -- e.g. 'pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar'\n  text         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- the actual text fed to TTS\n  r2_key       TEXT NOT NULL,        -- object key in R2 bucket\n  bytes        INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- for diagnostics + cost tracking\n  fetched_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (voice, text)\n);\n\n-- ============================================================\n-- Per-user learning state\n-- ============================================================\n-- auth.users is owned by Supabase Auth. We add profile fields here.\n\nCREATE TABLE profiles (\n  user_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  display_name  TEXT,\n  level         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'beginner',  -- beginner|intermediate|advanced\n  plan          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',      -- free|premium\n  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Auto-create a profile row when a new auth user is created\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, display_name)\n  VALUES (NEW.id, COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'display_name', SPLIT_PART(NEW.email, '@', 1)));\n  RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;\n\nCREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created\n  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();\n\nCREATE TABLE sakhi_progress (\n  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  sakhi_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_progress', -- in_progress | done\n  last_para    INTEGER,                              -- paragraph index of last position\n  last_sentence INTEGER,                             -- sentence index within that para\n  started_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, sakhi_id)\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE bookmarks (\n  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  sakhi_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  para_index   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  sentence_index INTEGER,\n  note         TEXT,\n  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\nCREATE INDEX bookmarks_user_sakhi ON bookmarks (user_id, sakhi_id);\n\n-- Spaced-repetition deck. Schedule fields target the FSRS algorithm\n-- (https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki) but the columns\n-- work for SM-2 too — we can ship SM-2 first and migrate to FSRS later.\nCREATE TABLE srs_cards (\n  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  surface       TEXT NOT NULL,         -- PA word, joins to morpheme_cache.surface\n  added_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  -- Scheduling state\n  due_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  stability     REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- FSRS stability\n  difficulty    REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- FSRS difficulty\n  reps          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  lapses        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  state         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', -- new | learning | review | relearning\n  UNIQUE (user_id, surface)\n);\nCREATE INDEX srs_cards_due ON srs_cards (user_id, due_at);\n\nCREATE TABLE srs_reviews (\n  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n  card_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES srs_cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  rating       SMALLINT NOT NULL,    -- 1=again 2=hard 3=good 4=easy\n  reviewed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  elapsed_days REAL,                 -- time since last review\n  ms_thinking  INTEGER               -- how long the user took\n);\nCREATE INDEX srs_reviews_card ON srs_reviews (card_id, reviewed_at);\n\n-- Every time a user hovers a word, record it. Lets us show \"encountered N\n-- times\" badges, build a personal vocab corpus, drive auto-add-to-SRS, etc.\nCREATE TABLE word_encounters (\n  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  surface      TEXT NOT NULL,\n  count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n  first_seen   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  last_seen    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, surface)\n);\n\n-- ============================================================\n-- Row-Level Security — per-user tables are owner-only\n-- ============================================================\nALTER TABLE profiles         ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE sakhi_progress   ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE bookmarks        ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE srs_cards        ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE srs_reviews      ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE word_encounters  ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\n\n-- Same shape policy applied to each per-user table: row.user_id = auth.uid()\nCREATE POLICY \"own profile\" ON profiles\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\nCREATE POLICY \"own sakhi progress\" ON sakhi_progress\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\nCREATE POLICY \"own bookmarks\" ON bookmarks\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\nCREATE POLICY \"own srs cards\" ON srs_cards\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\nCREATE POLICY \"own srs reviews\" ON srs_reviews\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\nCREATE POLICY \"own word encounters\" ON word_encounters\n  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\n-- Shared caches: readable by everyone (incl. anon), writable only by the\n-- service role (server-side routes using SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY).\nALTER TABLE morpheme_cache ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE audio_meta     ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nCREATE POLICY \"read morphemes\" ON morpheme_cache FOR SELECT USING (true);\nCREATE POLICY \"read audio_meta\" ON audio_meta    FOR SELECT USING (true);\n-- (No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies → only service_role bypasses RLS)\n"
}
```

  "content": "// Supabase clients for server-side use (Server Components, Server Actions,\n// Route Handlers). Two flavors:\n//\n//   - serverClient(): authed as the current user (RLS-enforced). Use for\n//     anything user-scoped: their SRS deck, their bookmarks, etc.\n//   - serviceClient(): bypasses RLS. Use for shared-cache writes (morpheme\n//     cache, audio metadata) where the server is acting on behalf of all\n//     users, not one. NEVER expose the service role key to the browser.\n//\n// Next.js 16: `cookies()` is async — must `await cookies()` before reading\n// or writing the cookie store.\nimport { createServerClient } from \"@supabase/ssr\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\nexport async function serverClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => {\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options);\n            });\n          } catch {\n            // Reading from a Server Component — set is a no-op there. Safe.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}\n\nlet _serviceClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient> | null = null;\nexport function serviceClient() {\n  if (_serviceClient) return _serviceClient;\n  _serviceClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false },\n    },\n  );\n  return _serviceClient;\n}\n"
}

## 3. Add the new account to your `gh` CLI

So you can run `gh` commands as `reliq-digital` (creating PRs, repos, etc.) without juggling browser logins. `gh` supports multiple accounts:

```
gh auth login             # walk through it, choose GitHub.com → HTTPS or SSH → login via browser → sign in as reliq-digital

gh auth switch            # toggle between them
```

For day-to-day on this repo, since the remote is SSH (`git@github.com:...`), it'll work regardless of which gh account is "active" — SSH uses your `~/.ssh` keys, not `gh`. So as long as your SSH key is added to **either** GitHub account, push/pull just works.

> AGENT

Here's exactly where to click in the Supabase dashboard:

## 1. Project URL + anon key + service_role key

**Project Settings → API** (left sidebar → ⚙️ icon → "API" tab)

You'll see three things on that page:
- **Project URL** — a box at the top, looks like `https://abcdefghij.supabase.co` — **copy this**
- **Project API keys** section, two rows:
  - `anon` `public` — long JWT starting `eyJ...` — **copy this** (safe for browser, will become `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`)
  - `service_role` `secret` — also `eyJ...` but click "Reveal" first — **copy this** (server-only, will become `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`)

## 2. Database connection string

**Project Settings → Database** (left sidebar → ⚙️ → "Database" tab)

Scroll down to **"Connection string"**. There are tabs: PSQL, URI, .NET, JDBC, Golang… **stay on "URI"**.

Above the connection strings there's a dropdown labeled **"Connection mode"** with three options:
- ❌ Direct connection (don't use — Vercel can't reach it)
- ❌ Transaction pooler (limited, no prepared statements)
- ✅ **Session pooler** — use this one

Copy the string. It'll look like:
```
postgresql://postgres.abcdefghij:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@aws-0-eu-west-2.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
```

The `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` is a literal placeholder — **replace it** with the database password you set when creating the project. (If you didn't save it, you can reset it under Database → "Reset database password" — but that'll invalidate any existing connections.)

-- akhar.io — initial schema.
--
-- Two layers:
--
--   1. SHARED CACHES (no user_id) — derived data we generate from external
--      sources, identical for everyone, paid for once.
--        - morpheme_cache: per-word dictionary entry (PA word → JSON with
--          romanization, gloss, etymology, Punjabipedia entries)
--        - audio_meta: per-text TTS metadata (the MP3 itself lives in R2)
--
--   2. PER-USER LEARNING STATE — every row scoped to auth.users.id with RLS,
--      so a user can only ever read/write their own data.
--        - sakhi_progress: read/in-progress/done per sakhi
--        - bookmarks: arbitrary saved positions
--        - srs_cards: spaced-repetition deck
--        - srs_reviews: review history
--        - word_encounters: every PA word the user has ever hovered
--        - profiles: account-level info (display name, level, plan tier)

-- ============================================================
-- Shared caches
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE morpheme_cache (
  script        TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- 'gurmukhi' for now
  surface       TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- the word as it appears
  morpheme_json JSONB NOT NULL,                 -- full Morpheme object
  processed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, -- manual verification gate
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)
);

-- TTS audio: the MP3 BLOB lives in Cloudflare R2 (bandwidth = main scaling
-- cost, R2 has no egress fees). Here we only track what's been generated.
-- The R2 object key is derived deterministically: audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3
CREATE TABLE audio_meta (
  voice        TEXT NOT NULL,        -- e.g. 'pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar'
  text         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- the actual text fed to TTS
  r2_key       TEXT NOT NULL,        -- object key in R2 bucket
  bytes        INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- for diagnostics + cost tracking
  fetched_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (voice, text)
);

-- ============================================================
-- Per-user learning state
-- ============================================================
-- auth.users is owned by Supabase Auth. We add profile fields here.

CREATE TABLE profiles (
  user_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  display_name  TEXT,
  level         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'beginner',  -- beginner|intermediate|advanced
  plan          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',      -- free|premium
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Auto-create a profile row when a new auth user is created
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, display_name)
  VALUES (NEW.id, COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'display_name', SPLIT_PART(NEW.email, '@', 1)));
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created
  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();

CREATE TABLE sakhi_progress (
  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sakhi_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_progress', -- in_progress | done
  last_para    INTEGER,                              -- paragraph index of last position
  last_sentence INTEGER,                             -- sentence index within that para
  started_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, sakhi_id)
);

CREATE TABLE bookmarks (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sakhi_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  para_index   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sentence_index INTEGER,
  note         TEXT,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX bookmarks_user_sakhi ON bookmarks (user_id, sakhi_id);

-- Spaced-repetition deck. Schedule fields target the FSRS algorithm
-- (https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki) but the columns
-- work for SM-2 too — we can ship SM-2 first and migrate to FSRS later.
CREATE TABLE srs_cards (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  surface       TEXT NOT NULL,         -- PA word, joins to morpheme_cache.surface
  added_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  -- Scheduling state
  due_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  stability     REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- FSRS stability
  difficulty    REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- FSRS difficulty
  reps          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  lapses        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  state         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new', -- new | learning | review | relearning
  UNIQUE (user_id, surface)
);
CREATE INDEX srs_cards_due ON srs_cards (user_id, due_at);

CREATE TABLE srs_reviews (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  card_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES srs_cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  rating       SMALLINT NOT NULL,    -- 1=again 2=hard 3=good 4=easy
  reviewed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  elapsed_days REAL,                 -- time since last review
  ms_thinking  INTEGER               -- how long the user took
);
CREATE INDEX srs_reviews_card ON srs_reviews (card_id, reviewed_at);

-- Every time a user hovers a word, record it. Lets us show "encountered N
-- times" badges, build a personal vocab corpus, drive auto-add-to-SRS, etc.
CREATE TABLE word_encounters (
  user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  surface      TEXT NOT NULL,
  count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_seen   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_seen    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, surface)
);

-- ============================================================
-- Row-Level Security — per-user tables are owner-only
-- ============================================================
ALTER TABLE profiles         ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE sakhi_progress   ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE bookmarks        ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE srs_cards        ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE srs_reviews      ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE word_encounters  ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Same shape policy applied to each per-user table: row.user_id = auth.uid()
CREATE POLICY "own profile" ON profiles
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
CREATE POLICY "own sakhi progress" ON sakhi_progress
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
CREATE POLICY "own bookmarks" ON bookmarks
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
CREATE POLICY "own srs cards" ON srs_cards
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
CREATE POLICY "own srs reviews" ON srs_reviews
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
CREATE POLICY "own word encounters" ON word_encounters
  FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);

-- Shared caches: readable by everyone (incl. anon), writable only by the
-- service role (server-side routes using SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY).
ALTER TABLE morpheme_cache ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE audio_meta     ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "read morphemes" ON morpheme_cache FOR SELECT USING (true);
CREATE POLICY "read audio_meta" ON audio_meta    FOR SELECT USING (true);
-- (No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies → only service_role bypasses RLS)
```

  "name": "0002_lock_down_handle_new_user",
  "query": "-- Lock down the auth trigger function flagged by security advisors:\n-- 1. Set search_path explicitly so a malicious user can't shadow public\n--    objects via a hostile search path.\n-- 2. Revoke EXECUTE from anon + authenticated. The function is only meant\n--    to be called by the on_auth_user_created trigger; nobody should be\n--    able to invoke it directly via /rest/v1/rpc.\n\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()\nRETURNS TRIGGER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nSECURITY DEFINER\nSET search_path = public, pg_temp\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, display_name)\n  VALUES (NEW.id, COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'display_name', SPLIT_PART(NEW.email, '@', 1)));\n  RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$;\n\nREVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.handle_new_user() FROM PUBLIC;\nREVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.handle_new_user() FROM anon;\nREVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.handle_new_user() FROM authenticated;"
}

New API Keys and Asymmetric Authentication","href":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/self-hosted-auth-keys","content":"# New API Keys and Asymmetric Authentication\n\nConfigure new API keys and ES256 asymmetric authentication for self-hosted Supabase.\n\nYou can configure self-hosted Supabase to use the [new API keys](/docs/guides/api/api-keys) alongside the legacy API keys (`ANON_KEY` and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` HS256-signed JWTs).\n\n\n## Before you begin\n\n*   Complete the [Docker setup guide](/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker), including running `generate-keys.sh` so that `JWT_SECRET`, `ANON_KEY`, and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are set in your `.env` file.\n*   Ensure `openssl` and `node` version 16 or newer are available on the machine where you will generate new keys.\n*   If you are upgrading an existing self-hosted Supabase environment, make sure to check the [changelog](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/docker/CHANGELOG.md) and add/update the following files:\n    *   `.env.example` (merge new sections into your `.env` file)\n    *   `docker-compose.yml`\n    *   `utils/add-new-auth-keys.sh`\n    *   `utils/rotate-new-api-keys.sh`\n    *   `volumes/api/kong-entrypoint.sh`\n    *   `volumes/api/kong.yml`\n\n\n## Adding the new keys\n\nFrom your project directory where you have `docker-compose.yml`:\n\n```sh\nsh utils/add-new-auth-keys.sh --update-env\n```\n\nThis generates new configuration environment variables and writes them to `.env`. Without `--update-env`, the script prints the values and prompts you interactively.\n\n<Admonition type=\"caution\">\n  The script reads `JWT_SECRET` from `.env` and includes it as a symmetric key inside both `JWT_KEYS` and `JWT_JWKS`. If you later change `JWT_SECRET`, you must regenerate the JWKS as well.\n</Admonition>\n\nAfter updating `.env`, enable new authentication by uncommenting these lines in `docker-compose.yml`:\n\n```yaml\nauth:\n  environment:\n    # JSON array of signing JWKs (EC private + legacy symmetric)\n    GOTRUE_JWT_KEYS: ${JWT_KEYS:-[]}\n\nrealtime:\n  environment:\n    # JWKS for token verification (EC public + legacy symmetric)\n    API_JWT_JWKS: ${JWT_JWKS:-{\"keys\":[]}}\n\nstorage:\n  environment:\n    # JWKS for token verification (EC public + legacy symmetric)\n    JWT_JWKS: ${JWT_JWKS:-{\"keys\":[]}}\n```\n\nPostgREST does not need uncommenting - it already uses `PGRST_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_JWKS:-${JWT_SECRET}}` which automatically picks up `JWT_JWKS` when set.\n\nThen restart all services:\n\n```sh\ndocker compose down && docker compose up -d\n```\n\n\n### New API keys format\n\nThe new API keys use the [same format](/docs/guides/api/api-keys) as the Supabase platform:\n\n```\nsb_publishable_<22-char-random>_<8-char-checksum>\nsb_secret_<22-char-random>_<8-char-checksum>\n```\n\n\n### Verifying the setup\n\nTest with the new publishable key:\n\n```\ncurl http://<your-domain>/rest/v1/ \\\n-H \"apikey=[REDACTED]\"\n```\n\nYou should receive a valid response from PostgREST. Then verify that the legacy key still works:\n\n```\ncurl http://<your-domain>/rest/v1/ \\\n-H \"apikey: your-anon-key\"\n```\n\nBoth should work and return the same result.\n\nYou can also verify the public JWKS endpoint:\n\n```\ncurl http://<your-domain>/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json\n```\n\nThis should return the EC public key (the symmetric key is excluded). Third-party services can use this endpoint to obtain the public key and verify asymmetric user session JWTs without needing the private key.\n\n\n### Environment variables configuration\n\nNew variables default to empty values in `.env.example`. When empty, the API gateway and all services operate in legacy-only mode: `sb_publishable` and `sb_secret` API keys are not configured.\n\n| Environment variable (existing and new) | Type             | Description                                                                                                                           |\n| --------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `JWT_SECRET`                            | Symmetric secret | **Existing:** Shared secret for signing and verifying HS256 JWTs. Used by multiple services.                                          |\n| `ANON_KEY`                              | HS256 JWT        | **Existing:** Legacy client-side API key. Embedded JWT with `role: \"anon\"`.                                                           |\n| `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`                      | HS256 JWT        | **Existing:** Legacy server-side API key. Embedded JWT with `role: \"service_role\"`.                                                   |\n| `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`              | Opaque           | **New:** Short random key with checksum. > AGENT

Good catch — Supabase migrated to a new API key system. The new ones are:

- **`sb_publishable_<random>_<checksum>`** — replaces the old `anon` key (client-side, safe to ship in browser)
- **`sb_secret_<random>_<checksum>`** — replaces the old `service_role` key (server-only)

Benefits: opaque format with built-in checksum (faster leak detection), better key rotation, and the platform supports multiple publishable keys per project (so you can revoke just one without taking down everything).

13	import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

Safe.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}\n\nlet _serviceClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient> | null = null;\nexport function serviceClient() {\n  if (_serviceClient) return _serviceClient;\n  _serviceClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false },\n    },\n  );\n  return _serviceClient;\n}",
  "new_string": "// Supabase clients for server-side use (Server Components, Server Actions,\n// Route Handlers). Two flavors:\n//\n//   - serverClient(): authed as the current user (RLS-enforced). Use for\n//     anything user-scoped: their SRS deck, their bookmarks, etc.\n//   - serviceClient(): bypasses RLS. Use for shared-cache writes (morpheme\n//     cache, audio metadata) where the server is acting on behalf of all\n//     users, not one. NEVER expose the secret key to the browser.\n//\n// Uses the new Supabase API key system:\n//   sb_publishable_*  → browser-safe, replaces legacy anon JWT\n//   sb_secret_*       → server-only, replaces legacy service_role JWT\n//\n// Next.js 16: `cookies()` is async — must `await cookies()` before reading\n// or writing the cookie store.\nimport { createServerClient } from \"@supabase/ssr\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\nexport async function serverClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => {\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options);\n            });\n          } catch {\n            // Reading from a Server Component — set is a no-op there. Safe.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}\n\nlet _serviceClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient> | null = null;\nexport function serviceClient() {\n  if (_serviceClient) return _serviceClient;\n  _serviceClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY!,\n    {\n      auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false },\n    },\n  );\n  return _serviceClient;\n}"
}

You're right — localhost:3000 is just dev. For prod the plan is **Vercel** (the original step 7), but there's a blocker: the current code writes to local SQLite files (`lipi.db`) which **won't work on Vercel** because serverless functions have read-only filesystems.

So the deploy order is:

1. **Migrate `morpheme_cache` from SQLite → Supabase** (~30 min) — so hover lookups work in prod
2. **Handle audio** — either migrate `audio_cache` to Supabase Storage / R2, or accept that prod only plays the pre-warmed sakhi 1 audio for now
3. **Handle GCP credentials** — your vision-key.json is a *file path* on your Mac. Vercel has no filesystem, so we move the JSON contents into an env var (`GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON`) and parse it in code
4. **Push to GitHub → Connect Vercel** (~5 min in browser) — Vercel auto-builds Next.js, sets up preview deploys per branch, gives you a `*.vercel.app` URL
5. **Point akhar.io DNS** at Vercel — since you bought via Cloudflare you just add a CNAME / A record in Cloudflare DNS

The "fully working in production" path is steps 1→2→3→4→5. That gets you `https://akhar.io` working end-to-end with hover + audio.

**Two paths from here:**

**A. Fast & dirty (an hour):** I migrate just `morpheme_cache` to Supabase, hardcode the GCP creds-as-env-var pattern, push to GitHub, you click "Import" in Vercel and add env vars. End result: `akhar.io` live with hover lookups working, but **audio only works for words already cached in prod** (which would be zero in a fresh deploy). Sakhi reader text + hover popovers are fully functional.

**B. Real & complete (~3 hours total):** Same as A, plus migrate `audio_cache` to R2, plus run the prewarm against the prod DB so sakhi 1 has all word + sentence audio in prod from day one.

Which do you want? Both end at `akhar.io` live publicly — A just has a known "audio doesn't generate on first hover for new words" gap until we do B later.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/google-tts.ts",
  "content": "// Google Cloud Text-to-Speech wrapper.\n//\n// Credentials: works in two environments —\n//   - Local dev: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/key.json (file path)\n//   - Vercel: GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON=<entire contents of key.json> (env var)\n// The GCP Node SDKs auto-pick-up GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, but Vercel\n// has no persistent filesystem so we feed the credentials directly.\n//\n// Voice picked by ear from the full pa-IN Chirp 3 HD lineup. Chirp 3 voices\n// do not accept SSML or speakingRate — only plain text.\nimport textToSpeech from \"@google-cloud/text-to-speech\";\n\nexport const VOICE_NAME = \"pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar\";\n// Below this byte count, Chirp 3 produced a clipped/silent stub. Triggers\n// the doubled-input fallback.\nconst MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES = 2000;\nconst CANDIDATES = 5;\nconst RETRY_DELAYS = [2000, 5000, 12000, 30000];\n\nlet _client: ReturnType<typeof textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient> | null = null;\nfunction client() {\n  if (_client) return _client;\n  const json = process.env.GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON;\n  if (json) {\n    const credentials = JSON.parse(json);\n    _client = new textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient({ credentials });\n  } else {\n    // Falls back to GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS file path\n    _client = new textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient();\n  }\n  return _client;\n}\n\nfunction toBuf(c: unknown): Buffer | null {\n  if (c == null) return null;\n  if (Buffer.isBuffer(c)) return c;\n  if (typeof c === \"string\") return Buffer.from(c, \"base64\");\n  if (c instanceof Uint8Array) return Buffer.from(c);\n  return null;\n}\n\nasync function synthOne(text: string): Promise<Buffer | null> {\n  let lastErr: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= RETRY_DELAYS.length; attempt++) {\n    try {\n      const [r] = await client().synthesizeSpeech({\n        input: { text },\n        voice: { languageCode: \"pa-IN\", name: VOICE_NAME },\n        audioConfig: { audioEncoding: \"MP3\" },\n      });\n      return toBuf(r.audioContent);\n    } catch (err) {\n      lastErr = err;\n      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (!/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|429|UNAVAILABLE/i.test(msg)) throw err;\n      if (attempt === RETRY_DELAYS.length) throw err;\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, RETRY_DELAYS[attempt]));\n    }\n  }\n  throw lastErr;\n}\n\nasync function bestOf(text: string, n: number): Promise<Buffer | null> {\n  const results = await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: n }, () => synthOne(text)));\n  const bufs = results.filter((b): b is Buffer => b != null);\n  if (bufs.length === 0) return null;\n  return bufs.reduce((best, cur) => (cur.length > best.length ? cur : best));\n}\n\n/**\n * Synthesize a Punjabi word or sentence to MP3.\n *\n * Two tricks baked in:\n *   - Appends `.` to the input for declarative falling intonation (without\n *     it, Chirp 3 reads isolated words with question-like rising contour).\n *   - Best-of-5 + silent-word fallback (`${w}. ${w}.`) for short particles\n *     like ਜੀ/ਦਾ/ਨੇ where the engine sometimes returns ~0.3s of silence.\n */\nexport async function synthesize(text: string): Promise<Buffer> {\n  const primary = `${text}.`;\n  let buf = await bestOf(primary, CANDIDATES);\n  if (!buf) throw new Error(\"TTS returned no audio for: \" + text);\n  if (buf.length < MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES) {\n    const doubled = await bestOf(`${text}. ${text}.`, CANDIDATES);\n    if (doubled && doubled.length > buf.length) buf = doubled;\n  }\n  return buf;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/morpheme-cache.ts",
  "content": "// Postgres-backed morpheme cache (lives in Supabase `morpheme_cache` table).\n// Replaces the SQLite functions that used to live in lib/db.ts.\n//\n// Reads are public via the publishable key (RLS policy \"read morphemes\").\n// Writes require the service role — only the server-side morpheme route\n// calls these.\nimport { serviceClient } from \"./supabase/server\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"./types\";\n\nexport interface CachedMorpheme {\n  morpheme: Morpheme;\n  processed: boolean;\n}\n\n// Anon client for reads (so this code works in scripts too, where there's no\n// Next.js request context). The publishable key + RLS policy \"read morphemes\"\n// lets anyone read morpheme_cache rows.\nlet _readClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient> | null = null;\nfunction readClient() {\n  if (_readClient) return _readClient;\n  _readClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    { auth: { persistSession: false } },\n  );\n  return _readClient;\n}\n\nexport async function getCachedMorpheme(\n  script: string,\n  surface: string,\n): Promise<CachedMorpheme | null> {\n  const { data, error } = await readClient()\n    .from(\"morpheme_cache\")\n    .select(\"morpheme_json, processed\")\n    .eq(\"script\", script)\n    .eq(\"surface\", surface)\n    .maybeSingle();\n  if (error) throw new Error(\"getCachedMorpheme: \" + error.message);\n  if (!data) return null;\n  return {\n    morpheme: data.morpheme_json as Morpheme,\n    processed: data.processed === true,\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function putCachedMorpheme(\n  morpheme: Morpheme,\n  opts: { processed?: boolean } = {},\n): Promise<void> {\n  const { error } = await serviceClient()\n    .from(\"morpheme_cache\")\n    .upsert(\n      {\n        script: morpheme.script,\n        surface: morpheme.surface,\n        morpheme_json: morpheme,\n        processed: opts.processed ?? false,\n        updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n      },\n      { onConflict: \"script,surface\" },\n    );\n  if (error) throw new Error(\"putCachedMorpheme: \" + error.message);\n}\n\nexport async function markMorphemeProcessed(\n  script: string,\n  surface: string,\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const { data, error } = await serviceClient()\n    .from(\"morpheme_cache\")\n    .update({ processed: true, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() })\n    .eq(\"script\", script)\n    .eq(\"surface\", surface)\n    .select(\"script\");\n  if (error) throw new Error(\"markMorphemeProcessed: \" + error.message);\n  return (data?.length ?? 0) > 0;\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/audio-cache.ts",
  "content": "// Audio cache: metadata in Supabase (`audio_meta` table), MP3 blobs in\n// Cloudflare R2.\n//\n// Why split: bandwidth is the dominant scaling cost for audio. R2 has zero\n// egress fees and explicit pricing for storage; Postgres bandwidth is more\n// expensive and counts against Supabase's egress quota.\n//\n// R2 keys are derived deterministically from (voice, text) so the same input\n// always maps to the same object:\n//   audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3\n//\n// Reads from cache: anyone can fetch (the route streams R2 through itself).\n// Writes: server-only (service role for Supabase metadata, R2 creds for blob).\nimport { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\nimport {\n  S3Client,\n  GetObjectCommand,\n  PutObjectCommand,\n} from \"@aws-sdk/client-s3\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport { serviceClient } from \"./supabase/server\";\n\nlet _readClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient> | null = null;\nfunction readClient() {\n  if (_readClient) return _readClient;\n  _readClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    { auth: { persistSession: false } },\n  );\n  return _readClient;\n}\n\nlet _r2: S3Client | null = null;\nfunction r2() {\n  if (_r2) return _r2;\n  _r2 = new S3Client({\n    region: \"auto\",\n    endpoint: process.env.R2_ENDPOINT!,\n    credentials: {\n      accessKeyId: process.env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,\n      secretAccessKey: process.env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,\n    },\n  });\n  return _r2;\n}\n\nexport function r2KeyFor(voice: string, text: string): string {\n  const hash = createHash(\"sha1\").update(text, \"utf8\").digest(\"hex\");\n  return `audio/${voice}/${hash}.mp3`;\n}\n\nexport interface CachedAudio {\n  buffer: Buffer;\n  bytes: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Look up cached audio. Returns null if no row exists in audio_meta — i.e.\n * the audio has never been synthesized for this (voice, text).\n *\n * On miss, the route returns 404 — there is no on-demand synthesis. Audio is\n * pre-generated via scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts (or any other server-side flow).\n */\nexport async function getCachedAudio(\n  voice: string,\n  text: string,\n): Promise<CachedAudio | null> {\n  const { data, error } = await readClient()\n    .from(\"audio_meta\")\n    .select(\"r2_key, bytes\")\n    .eq(\"voice\", voice)\n    .eq(\"text\", text)\n    .maybeSingle();\n  if (error) throw new Error(\"getCachedAudio (meta): \" + error.message);\n  if (!data) return null;\n\n  const obj = await r2().send(\n    new GetObjectCommand({\n      Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!,\n      Key: data.r2_key as string,\n    }),\n  );\n  if (!obj.Body) throw new Error(\"getCachedAudio: R2 returned no Body\");\n  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];\n  for await (const chunk of obj.Body as AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>) {\n    chunks.push(chunk);\n  }\n  const buffer = Buffer.concat(chunks);\n  return { buffer, bytes: buffer.length };\n}\n\n/**\n * Upload the MP3 to R2 and record the metadata in Postgres. Idempotent —\n * re-running with the same (voice, text) overwrites both the object and\n * the row.\n */\nexport async function putCachedAudio(\n  voice: string,\n  text: string,\n  mp3: Buffer,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);\n  await r2().send(\n    new PutObjectCommand({\n      Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!,\n      Key: key,\n      Body: mp3,\n      ContentType: \"audio/mpeg\",\n    }),\n  );\n  const { error } = await serviceClient()\n    .from(\"audio_meta\")\n    .upsert(\n      {\n        voice,\n        text,\n        r2_key: key,\n        bytes: mp3.length,\n        fetched_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n      },\n      { onConflict: \"voice,text\" },\n    );\n  if (error) throw new Error(\"putCachedAudio (meta): \" + error.message);\n}\n"
}

6	// Google Cloud Text-to-Speech using Chirp 3 HD — Google's latest generative
7	// TTS (the same family that powers Gemini's voice mode). Unlike Wavenet, it
8	// handles Gurmukhi natively and articulates word-final stops correctly
9	// (ਪਿੰਡ comes out as "pind" with the retroflex ḍ properly released).
10	//
11	// Voice picked by ear from auditioning the full pa-IN Chirp3 HD lineup.
12	// Chirp3 voices do NOT accept speakingRate or SSML — only plain text.
13	const VOICE_NAME = "pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar";
14	
15	let _client: ReturnType<typeof textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient> | null = null;
16	function client() {
17	  if (_client) return _client;
18	  _client = new textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient();
19	  return _client;
20	}

22	export async function GET(request: Request) {
23	  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
24	  const word = searchParams.get("word");
25	  if (!word) {
26	    return Response.json({ error: "missing 'word' query param" }, { status: 400 });
27	  }
28	
29	  // Cache key includes the voice name so swapping the voice invalidates.
30	  const cacheKey = `${VOICE_NAME}:${word}`;
31	  const cached = getCachedAudio(cacheKey);
32	  if (cached) {
33	    return new Response(new Uint8Array(cached), {
34	      headers: {
35	        "Content-Type": "audio/mpeg",
36	        "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
37	        "X-Lipi-Cache": "HIT",
38	      },
39	    });
40	  }
41	
42	  try {
43	    // Chirp 3 is generative — same input yields different outputs each call,
44	    // and occasional samples come out clipped/too short (e.g. ~2.8KB for ਪਿੰਡ
45	    // when normal is ~5-7KB). Generate N candidates in parallel and keep the
46	    // longest one. Each word is cached forever, so the extra spend (~3x) is
47	    // a one-time cost per unique word.
48	    const CANDIDATES = 5;
49	    // Below this byte size the output is effectively silence/clipped — Chirp
50	    // 3 sometimes returns a ~1.3KB stub for short inputs even with best-of-5.
51	    // When that happens, retry with the word doubled (`${w}. ${w}.`) which
52	    // forces the engine to articulate. The user hears the word twice but at
53	    // least it's audible — common short particles like ਜੀ, ਦਾ, ਨੇ all need
54	    // this. Each word is cached forever, so the extra cost is paid once.
55	    const MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES = 2000;
56	    // Per-call retry on GCP per-minute quota exhaustion. Easy to trip during
57	    // bulk prewarms (5 candidates × N concurrent words). Retry per-call so
58	    // even a partial success still contributes to best-of-5.
59	    async function synthOne(text: string) {
60	      let lastErr: unknown;
61	      const delays = [2000, 5000, 12000, 30000];
62	      for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= delays.length; attempt++) {
63	        try {
64	          return await client().synthesizeSpeech({
65	            input: { text },
66	            voice: { languageCode: "pa-IN", name: VOICE_NAME },
67	            audioConfig: { audioEncoding: "MP3" },
68	          });
69	        } catch (err) {
70	          lastErr = err;
71	          const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
72	          if (!/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|429|UNAVAILABLE/i.test(msg)) throw err;
73	          if (attempt === delays.length) throw err;
74	          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delays[attempt]));
75	        }
76	      }
77	      throw lastErr;
78	    }
79	    function toBuf(c: Buffer | Uint8Array | string | null | undefined): Buffer | null {
80	      if (c == null) return null;
81	      if (Buffer.isBuffer(c)) return c;
82	      if (typeof c === "string") return Buffer.from(c, "base64");
83	      return Buffer.from(c as Uint8Array);
84	    }
85	    async function bestOf(text: string): Promise<Buffer | null> {
86	      const responses = await Promise.all(
87	        Array.from({ length: CANDIDATES }, () => synthOne(text)),
88	      );
89	      const bufs = responses
90	        .map(([r]) => toBuf(r.audioContent))
91	        .filter((b): b is Buffer => b != null);
92	      if (bufs.length === 0) return null;
93	      return bufs.reduce((best, cur) => (cur.length > best.length ? cur : best));
94	    }
95	    // Append "." so Chirp 3 picks a declarative falling intonation. Without
96	    // a sentence terminator the model reads isolated words with a rising
97	    // (question-like) contour. ASCII period gives consistent statement prosody.
98	    let buf = await bestOf(`${word}.`);
99	    if (!buf) {
100	      return Response.json({ error: "no audio returned" }, { status: 502 });
101	    }
102	    if (buf.length < MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES) {
103	      const doubled = await bestOf(`${word}. ${word}.`);
104	      if (doubled && doubled.length > buf.length) buf = doubled;
105	    }
106	    putCachedAudio(cacheKey, buf);
107	    return new Response(new Uint8Array(buf), {
108	      headers: {
109	        "Content-Type": "audio/mpeg",
110	        "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
111	        "X-Lipi-Cache": "MISS",
112	      },
113	    });
114	  } catch (err) {
115	    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
116	    return Response.json({ error: message }, { status: 502 });
117	  }
118	}
119

22	// POST with { morpheme: ... }  → save the edited morpheme + mark processed
23	// POST with { verify: "<word>" } → just flip the processed flag for that word
24	export async function POST(request: Request) {
25	  const body = (await request.json()) as
26	    | { morpheme: Morpheme }
27	    | { verify: string };
28	  if ("verify" in body && body.verify) {
29	    // Enforce the processed=true criteria server-side:
30	    //   - romanized populated
31	    //   - gloss_en populated (and not the placeholder)
32	    //   - at least one Punjabipedia dictionary entry
33	    const cached = await getMorpheme(body.verify);
34	    const reasons: string[] = [];
35	    if (!cached.romanized) reasons.push("missing romanization");
36	    if (
37	      !cached.gloss_en ||
38	      cached.gloss_en.startsWith("(no ")
39	    ) {
40	      reasons.push("missing English gloss");
41	    }
42	    if (!cached.dictionary_entries || cached.dictionary_entries.length === 0) {
43	      reasons.push("no Punjabipedia dictionary entries");
44	    }
45	    if (reasons.length) {
46	      return Response.json(
47	        { error: `cannot verify ${body.verify}: ${reasons.join(", ")}` },
48	        { status: 409 },
49	      );
50	    }
51	    const ok = markProcessed("gurmukhi", body.verify);
52	    if (!ok) {
53	      return Response.json(
54	        { error: `word not in cache: ${body.verify}` },
55	        { status: 404 },
56	      );
57	    }
58	    return Response.json({ verified: body.verify });
59	  }
60	  if ("morpheme" in body && body.morpheme?.surface) {
61	    // Manual edits are implicitly verified
62	    const stamped = overrideMorpheme(body.morpheme);
63	    markProcessed("gurmukhi", body.morpheme.surface);
64	    return Response.json(stamped);
65	  }
66	  return Response.json(
67	    { error: "expected { morpheme } or { verify }" },

70	}

26	/**
27	 * Resolve a Punjabi word to a Morpheme.
28	 *
29	 * Per request:
30	 *   1. SQLite cache → instant hit.
31	 *   2. Live Punjabipedia lookup. If hits, store dictionary entries.
32	 *   3. Always call nano-gpt for the English gloss (Punjabipedia is all
33	 *      Punjabi, the user needs an English meaning). Punjabipedia entries
34	 *      are passed as grounding so the gloss reflects real dictionary data.
35	 *   4. If both fail, return a minimal placeholder so the popover degrades
36	 *      instead of 500-ing.
37	 *
38	 * Romanization is computed locally (transliterate.ts, ISO 15919) for every
39	 * word — no LLM needed.
40	 */
41	export async function getMorpheme(surface: string): Promise<Morpheme> {
42	  const cached = getCached("gurmukhi", surface);
43	  if (cached) {
44	    // Annotate the morpheme with its processed-state so the UI knows
45	    // whether to show a "verified" badge.
46	    return { ...cached.morpheme, processed: cached.processed } as Morpheme;
47	  }
48	
49	  const romanized = gurmukhiToIso15919(surface);
50	  // Step 2: direct Punjabipedia lookup
51	  const pp = await lookupPunjabipedia(surface);
52	  let dictionaryEntries = pp?.entries ?? [];
53	  let dictionaryUrl = pp?.url;
54	  let lemmaUsedForDictionary: string | null = null;
55	
56	  // Always try to get an English gloss
57	  let glossEn = "";
58	  let sourceLanguage: Morpheme["source_language"] = "unknown";
59	  let note: string | undefined;
60	  let components: Morpheme[] = [];
61	  let senses: Morpheme["senses"];
62	  let llmError: string | null = null;
63	
64	  let lemmaPa: string | null = null;
65	  try {
66	    const gloss = await getEnglishGloss(surface, dictionaryEntries);
67	    glossEn = gloss.gloss_en;
68	    sourceLanguage = gloss.source_language;
69	    lemmaPa = gloss.lemma_pa;
70	    senses = (gloss.senses ?? []).map((s) => ({
71	      gloss_en: s.gloss_en,
72	      lemma_pa: s.lemma_pa,
73	      lemma_en: s.lemma_en,
74	      form: s.form,
75	    }));
76	    if (gloss.lemma_pa && gloss.lemma_pa !== surface) {
77	      note = `Lemma: ${gloss.lemma_pa}${gloss.lemma_en ? ` (${gloss.lemma_en})` : ""}${gloss.note ? `. ${gloss.note}` : ""}`;
78	    } else if (gloss.note) {
79	      note = gloss.note;
80	    }
81	    // Map compound decomposition into nested Morphemes
82	    components = (gloss.components ?? []).map((c) => ({
83	      surface: c.surface,
84	      script: "gurmukhi",
85	      romanized: c.romanized || gurmukhiToIso15919(c.surface),
86	      gloss_en: c.gloss_en,
87	      source_language: normalizeSourceLang(c.source_language),
88	      provenance: {
89	        source: "llm",
90	        confidence: "unverified",
91	      },
92	      components: [],
93	    }));
94	  } catch (err) {
95	    llmError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
96	  }
97	
98	  // Step 2b: if Punjabipedia missed the surface form AND the LLM gave us a
99	  // lemma (e.g. ਘੱਲਿਆ → ਘੱਲਣਾ), try the lemma. Many inflected/archaic
100	  // forms aren't indexed but their lemma is. Attribute the entries to the
101	  // lemma so the popover can show which form was actually consulted.
102	  if (
103	    dictionaryEntries.length === 0 &&
104	    lemmaPa &&
105	    lemmaPa !== surface
106	  ) {
107	    const ppLemma = await lookupPunjabipedia(lemmaPa);
108	    if (ppLemma && ppLemma.entries.length > 0) {
109	      dictionaryEntries = ppLemma.entries;
110	      dictionaryUrl = ppLemma.url;
111	      lemmaUsedForDictionary = lemmaPa;
112	    }
113	  }
114	
115	  // If we found entries via the lemma fallback, surface that fact in the note
116	  const finalNote = (() => {
117	    const bits: string[] = [];
118	    if (note) bits.push(note);
119	    if (lemmaUsedForDictionary) {
120	      bits.push(`Dictionary entries shown are for the lemma ${lemmaUsedForDictionary}.`);
121	    }
122	    if (!bits.length && llmError) bits.push(`LLM gloss failed: ${llmError}`);
123	    return bits.length ? bits.join(" ") : undefined;
124	  })();
125	
126	  const provenance: Provenance = {
127	    source: dictionaryEntries.length > 0 ? "punjabipedia" : "llm",
128	    url: dictionaryUrl,
129	    fetched_at: new Date().toISOString(),
130	    confidence:
131	      dictionaryEntries.length > 0 ? "verified" : "unverified",
132	    note: finalNote,
133	  };
134	
135	  const morpheme: Morpheme = {
136	    surface,
137	    script: "gurmukhi",
138	    romanized,
139	    gloss_en: glossEn || "(no English gloss available)",
140	    senses: senses && senses.length > 0 ? senses : undefined,
141	    source_language: sourceLanguage,
142	    provenance,
143	    components,
144	    dictionary_entries:
145	      dictionaryEntries.length > 0 ? dictionaryEntries : undefined,
146	  };
147	
148	  // Only cache if we got something useful (either entries OR a gloss)
149	  if (dictionaryEntries.length > 0 || (glossEn && !llmError)) {
150	    putCached(morpheme);
151	  }
152	  return morpheme;
153	}
154	
155	export function overrideMorpheme(morpheme: Morpheme): Morpheme {
156	  const stamped: Morpheme = {
157	    ...morpheme,
158	    provenance: {
159	      ...morpheme.provenance,
160	      source: "manual",
161	      confidence: "verified",
162	      fetched_at: new Date().toISOString(),
163	    },
164	  };
165	  putCached(stamped);
166	  return stamped;
167	}

7	let _db: Database.Database | null = null;

10	// The lipi-dict-rip build pipeline rewrites this DB out-of-band. If the file
11	// gets replaced (different inode) under a long-lived dev process, the cached
12	// SQLite handle ends up pointing at a deleted/swapped file and reads come
13	// back as "database disk image is malformed". Re-open whenever the inode
14	// changes so the dev server stays consistent without manual restarts.
15	export function sakhiDb(): Database.Database {
16	  const inode = statSync(DB_PATH).ino;
17	  if (_db && _dbInode === inode) return _db;
18	  if (_db) _db.close();
19	  _db = new Database(DB_PATH, { readonly: true });
20	  _dbInode = inode;
21	  return _db;

125	export function sakhiNeighbors(id: number): { prev: number | null; next: number | null } {
126	  const cur = sakhiDb().prepare("SELECT book_id, seq_in_book FROM sakhis WHERE id = ?")
127	    .get(id) as { book_id: number; seq_in_book: number } | undefined;
128	  if (!cur) return { prev: null, next: null };
129	  const prev = sakhiDb().prepare(
130	    "SELECT id FROM sakhis WHERE book_id = ? AND seq_in_book < ? ORDER BY seq_in_book DESC LIMIT 1"
131	  ).get(cur.book_id, cur.seq_in_book) as { id: number } | undefined;
132	  const next = sakhiDb().prepare(
133	    "SELECT id FROM sakhis WHERE book_id = ? AND seq_in_book > ? ORDER BY seq_in_book ASC LIMIT 1"
134	  ).get(cur.book_id, cur.seq_in_book) as { id: number } | undefined;
135	  return { prev: prev?.id ?? null, next: next?.id ?? null };
136	}

Here's the full walkthrough — should take ~5 minutes:

## 1. Open R2 in Cloudflare

Go to **https://dash.cloudflare.com** → in the left sidebar look for **"R2 Object Storage"** (might just say "R2"). Click it.

If you've never used R2 before, you'll see a "Purchase R2" or "Subscribe to R2" screen first:
- Click through to enable it
- You'll need to add a payment method (debit/credit card)
- **Free tier**: 10 GB storage + zero egress fees + 1M class-A ops/mo + 10M class-B ops/mo. We're nowhere near these limits — won't get charged.

## 2. Create the bucket

Once R2 is enabled, you'll be on the R2 overview page. 

- Click **"Create bucket"** (top right)
- **Bucket name**: `akhar-audio`
- **Location**: leave on "Automatic" (Cloudflare picks closest)
- **Storage class**: Standard
- Click **"Create bucket"**

## 3. Grab the Account ID

On the R2 overview page, look at the **right sidebar** — there's a section labeled **"Account details"** with **"Account ID"** below it. It's a hex string like `abc123def456...`. **Copy this** — that's value 1 of 4.

## 4. Create API token

From the R2 page, click **"Manage R2 API Tokens"** (top right, near "Create bucket"). Then:

- Click **"Create API Token"**
- **Token name**: `akhar-prod`
- **Permissions**: select **"Object Read & Write"**
- **Specify bucket(s)**: pick **"Apply to specific buckets only"** → select `akhar-audio`
- **TTL**: "Forever"
- Click **"Create API Token"**

## 5. Copy the credentials (IMPORTANT — only shown once)

After creating, you'll see a screen with:
- **Access Key ID** → copy this (value 2)
- **Secret Access Key** → copy this (value 3) — this is the **last time you'll ever see it**, save it now
- **Use jurisdiction-specific endpoints for S3 clients** section, which shows:
  - **Endpoint**: `https://<your-account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` → copy this (value 4)

If you close that page without copying, the secret is gone forever and you'll have to create a new token.
