> AGENT

Honestly, you're right to push back on this. Let me think out loud about it.

**What actually needs to be cloud vs what doesn't:**

| Thing | Needs cloud? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| User accounts | **Yes** | Auth, multi-device persistence |
| User's SRS cards / bookmarks / progress | **Yes** | Same — they switch devices |
| Sakhi corpus (the texts) | **No** | Static, ~4.4MB, doesn't change at runtime |
| Morpheme cache (gloss/dictionary entries) | **No** | You author this on your machine, prod is read-only |
| Audio MP3s | **Yes-ish** | Will hit ~700MB at full corpus — too big to ship in deploy bundle. Needs R2. |

**The crucial insight: production is INHERENTLY read-only for caches.** You explicitly said audio shouldn't generate on first hover for new words. Same logic applies to morphemes — new words shouldn't trigger Punjabipedia + nano-gpt calls on user hover. So why migrate them to a DB Postgres can write to? Just ship them as bundled data.

## Simpler architecture (your instinct)

1. **`data/sakhis.db`** — keep as SQLite, commit to repo. Vercel reads it via `better-sqlite3` (Vercel supports it). 4.4MB.
2. **`data/morphemes.db` (or `morphemes.json`)** — same. Commit your local cache to the repo. ~5-10MB at full corpus. Prewarming pushes new words to your local file → git commit → deploy. Prod can't add new words but doesn't need to.
3. **Audio in R2** — only because of size. ~2KB per word, will grow to ~700MB total. Too big to bundle.
4. **Supabase** — only for the things that genuinely need it: user accounts + SRS + bookmarks + progress.

**Pros over what I was building:**
- Drops the morpheme_cache + audio_meta Postgres migration entirely
- Hover lookups in prod = zero DB calls, instant (read from bundled file)
- Prewarm workflow stays simple: local SQLite, git commit
- Reproducible: same `git checkout` = same exact cache state
- Easier to version, diff, audit

**Cons:**
- Each `git commit` after prewarming adds DB diffs (binary diff is messy for SQLite, but JSON would be diffable)
- Vercel bundle gets a bit larger with each deploy (negligible)
- New words still need R2 setup before deploy

## Trade-off question

R2 for audio is unavoidable if you ever process all 405 sakhis (~700MB). But for **right now** (sakhi 1 = ~1.8MB of audio), you could even ship audio bundled too — `public/audio/<voice>/<hash>.mp3` as static assets — and add R2 later when corpus grows.

**My revised recommendation:**
- Keep morpheme_cache + sakhi corpus as bundled SQLite (no migration)
- For now, ship audio as `public/audio/...` static files too (no R2 needed yet)
- Supabase ONLY for user accounts + learning state
- Add R2 later when audio bundle gets > ~50MB

This means **you can deploy today without R2** and don't pay anything extra. Want me to pivot to this?

> DEVELOPER

but do you think It's better to have the audio offline or maybe it's a feature we can add for later or something?

> AGENT

Two separate things — let me untangle them:

**Where the audio LIVES on the server** ≠ **whether USERS can download it for offline use**.

For users:
- **Offline playback (downloadable) is a great premium feature.** Every comparable app gates it behind paid — Pimsleur, Spotify, Duolingo Super, Apple Music, Netflix all do this. Big diaspora use case: parents playing sakhis during car rides / school runs / walks where data is spotty.
- **Implementation later**: it's a Service Worker / PWA feature — a "Download this sakhi" button that pre-caches the MP3s in the browser's Cache API. Doesn't change the server-side architecture at all; it's just a frontend feature that pre-fetches and stores.
- **Don't build it now** — ship free streaming first, add downloads when you have paying users asking for it.

For the server architecture (current decision):
- **Free users get streaming from server.** Tap play → fetch MP3 → play.
- **Where the MP3 lives** is the question: bundled in `/public` or in R2.

So the question becomes: where do MP3s live on the server today?

**My recommendation: ship in `/public/audio/<voice>/<hash>.mp3` for now, migrate to R2 only when needed.**

Numbers:
- Sakhi 1 fully cached audio = 1.8 MB
- All 405 sakhis estimated = ~700 MB
- Vercel deploy size limits: 100 MB per static asset (none of our files hit that), but **total deploy size** practically maxes around 500 MB before deploys get slow/painful
- So bundled `/public` works fine for the first ~100 sakhis or so

This means:
- **Today**: bundle audio in `/public/audio/...`, deploy to Vercel. Zero R2 needed. Zero new accounts. `akhar.io` lives today.
- **When `/public/audio` hits ~100 MB** (~50–80 sakhis processed): migrate to R2. Single config change in `lib/audio-cache.ts`. ~10 min of work + R2 setup. Trivial future cost.
- **When users ask for offline**: build the PWA download button as a premium feature.

**Bottom line: skip R2 for now.** Way faster to ship. We'll add it when there's actually a reason to.

Want me to proceed on this path? It means:
1. Cache stays local SQLite (no Supabase migration for caches)
2. Audio files get moved from SQLite BLOBs → `public/audio/<voice>/<hash>.mp3` (so they're served as Vercel static assets, CDN-cached automatically)
3. Supabase only for user accounts + SRS + bookmarks
4. Push + Vercel deploy + DNS

Way fewer moving parts.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/audio-cache.ts",
  "content": "// Audio cache backed by Cloudflare R2.\n//\n// R2 is the single source of truth — no metadata DB. The key is derived\n// deterministically from (voice, text):\n//   audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3\n// so checking \"is this cached?\" is just an R2 HeadObject. Cheap (class B\n// op, 10M free per month) and removes a Postgres roundtrip from the hover\n// hot path.\nimport { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\nimport {\n  S3Client,\n  GetObjectCommand,\n  PutObjectCommand,\n  HeadObjectCommand,\n  NoSuchKey,\n  NotFound,\n} from \"@aws-sdk/client-s3\";\n\nlet _client: S3Client | null = null;\nfunction client() {\n  if (_client) return _client;\n  _client = new S3Client({\n    region: \"auto\",\n    endpoint: process.env.R2_ENDPOINT!,\n    credentials: {\n      accessKeyId: process.env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,\n      secretAccessKey: process.env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,\n    },\n  });\n  return _client;\n}\n\nexport function r2KeyFor(voice: string, text: string): string {\n  const hash = createHash(\"sha1\").update(text, \"utf8\").digest(\"hex\");\n  return `audio/${voice}/${hash}.mp3`;\n}\n\nexport interface CachedAudio {\n  buffer: Buffer;\n  bytes: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fetch cached audio. Returns null if no object exists for this (voice, text)\n * — the route returns 404, the UI hides the play button. No on-demand\n * synthesis.\n */\nexport async function getCachedAudio(\n  voice: string,\n  text: string,\n): Promise<CachedAudio | null> {\n  const Key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);\n  try {\n    const obj = await client().send(\n      new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!, Key }),\n    );\n    if (!obj.Body) return null;\n    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];\n    for await (const chunk of obj.Body as AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>) {\n      chunks.push(chunk);\n    }\n    const buffer = Buffer.concat(chunks);\n    return { buffer, bytes: buffer.length };\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof NoSuchKey || err instanceof NotFound) return null;\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Cheap existence check — used by the prewarm script to skip already-cached\n * words without paying for a full GET. Class B op, free tier covers >10M/mo.\n */\nexport async function audioCacheHas(voice: string, text: string): Promise<boolean> {\n  const Key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);\n  try {\n    await client().send(\n      new HeadObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!, Key }),\n    );\n    return true;\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof NoSuchKey || err instanceof NotFound) return false;\n    // Some SDK versions throw a generic error with $metadata.httpStatusCode = 404\n    if (typeof err === \"object\" && err && \"$metadata\" in err) {\n      const meta = (err as { $metadata?: { httpStatusCode?: number } }).$metadata;\n      if (meta?.httpStatusCode === 404) return false;\n    }\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function putCachedAudio(\n  voice: string,\n  text: string,\n  mp3: Buffer,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const Key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);\n  await client().send(\n    new PutObjectCommand({\n      Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!,\n      Key,\n      Body: mp3,\n      ContentType: \"audio/mpeg\",\n    }),\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/morpheme-cache.ts",
  "content": "// SQLite-backed morpheme cache. Lives in `lipi.db` at the project root.\n// Authored on dev machines via the prewarm script + popover verification,\n// then committed to git so production reads the same data.\n//\n// Production is read-only — Vercel's filesystem is read-only. Writes\n// (popover \"Mark verified\", prewarm) only work in local dev. New cache\n// entries flow into production via `git commit && git push`.\nimport Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"./types\";\n\nlet _db: Database.Database | null = null;\n\nfunction db(): Database.Database {\n  if (_db) return _db;\n  _db = new Database(path.join(process.cwd(), \"lipi.db\"));\n  _db.pragma(\"journal_mode = WAL\");\n  _db.exec(`\n    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS morpheme_cache (\n      script TEXT NOT NULL,\n      surface TEXT NOT NULL,\n      morpheme_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n      processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n      updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n      PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)\n    );\n  `);\n  // Schema migration for legacy DBs that pre-date the processed column\n  const cols = _db\n    .prepare(`PRAGMA table_info(morpheme_cache)`)\n    .all() as { name: string }[];\n  if (!cols.some((c) => c.name === \"processed\")) {\n    _db.exec(\n      `ALTER TABLE morpheme_cache ADD COLUMN processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,\n    );\n  }\n  return _db;\n}\n\nexport interface CachedMorpheme {\n  morpheme: Morpheme;\n  processed: boolean;\n}\n\nexport function getCachedMorpheme(\n  script: string,\n  surface: string,\n): CachedMorpheme | null {\n  const row = db()\n    .prepare(\n      \"SELECT morpheme_json, processed FROM morpheme_cache WHERE script = ? AND surface = ?\",\n    )\n    .get(script, surface) as\n    | { morpheme_json: string; processed: number }\n    | undefined;\n  if (!row) return null;\n  return {\n    morpheme: JSON.parse(row.morpheme_json) as Morpheme,\n    processed: row.processed === 1,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function putCachedMorpheme(\n  morpheme: Morpheme,\n  opts: { processed?: boolean } = {},\n): void {\n  db()\n    .prepare(\n      `INSERT INTO morpheme_cache (script, surface, morpheme_json, processed, updated_at)\n       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\n       ON CONFLICT(script, surface) DO UPDATE SET\n         morpheme_json = excluded.morpheme_json,\n         processed = excluded.processed,\n         updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`,\n    )\n    .run(\n      morpheme.script,\n      morpheme.surface,\n      JSON.stringify(morpheme),\n      opts.processed ? 1 : 0,\n    );\n}\n\nexport function markMorphemeProcessed(script: string, surface: string): boolean {\n  const r = db()\n    .prepare(\n      `UPDATE morpheme_cache SET processed = 1, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n       WHERE script = ? AND surface = ?`,\n    )\n    .run(script, surface);\n  return r.changes > 0;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/migrate-audio-to-r2.ts",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env tsx\n/**\n * One-shot migration: copy every cached MP3 out of the local SQLite\n * `audio_cache` table into Cloudflare R2.\n *\n * The legacy `word` column was actually `<voice>:<text>` (we keyed it that\n * way so re-voicing would invalidate). We parse it back into voice + text\n * here and use the same r2KeyFor() helper the route uses so cache lookups\n * after migration find the same key.\n *\n * Re-runnable: existing R2 objects are skipped via HEAD check (cheap).\n *\n * Usage: tsx scripts/migrate-audio-to-r2.ts\n */\nimport Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { audioCacheHas, putCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\n// Load .env.local manually (this isn't a Next.js context)\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\ninterface Row {\n  word: string;\n  mp3: Buffer;\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const dbPath = path.join(process.cwd(), \"lipi.db\");\n  const db = new Database(dbPath, { readonly: true });\n  const rows = db\n    .prepare(\"SELECT word, mp3 FROM audio_cache ORDER BY word\")\n    .all() as Row[];\n  db.close();\n\n  console.log(`Found ${rows.length} cached audio entries in ${dbPath}\\n`);\n\n  let migrated = 0,\n    skipped = 0,\n    failed = 0,\n    parseFailed = 0;\n  const t0 = Date.now();\n  for (let i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {\n    const row = rows[i];\n    // Legacy key format: \"pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar:ਸਕਾਰ\"\n    const colon = row.word.indexOf(\":\");\n    if (colon === -1) {\n      parseFailed++;\n      console.warn(`  [${i + 1}/${rows.length}] ?? unparseable key: ${row.word}`);\n      continue;\n    }\n    const voice = row.word.slice(0, colon);\n    const text = row.word.slice(colon + 1);\n    try {\n      if (await audioCacheHas(voice, text)) {\n        skipped++;\n        continue;\n      }\n      await putCachedAudio(voice, text, row.mp3);\n      migrated++;\n      const preview = text.length > 30 ? text.slice(0, 30) + \"…\" : text;\n      console.log(\n        `  [${i + 1}/${rows.length}] uploaded (${row.mp3.length}B): ${preview}`,\n      );\n    } catch (err) {\n      failed++;\n      console.error(\n        `  [${i + 1}/${rows.length}] FAILED for \"${text.slice(0, 40)}\": ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`,\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  const wall = ((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1);\n  console.log(\n    `\\nDone in ${wall}s. migrated=${migrated} skipped=${skipped} failed=${failed} unparseable=${parseFailed}`,\n  );\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

2	/**
3	 * Pre-warm caches for a sakhi.
4	 *
5	 * Two passes:
6	 *   1. /api/morpheme — romanization + gloss + Punjabipedia entries
7	 *   2. /api/tts      — Chirp 3 HD audio (best-of-5 per word)
8	 *
9	 * Usage:
10	 *   tsx scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts <sakhi-id>
11	 *   tsx scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts <sakhi-id> --concurrency 4

22	const BASE = process.env.LIPI_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000";

24	function tokenizeGurmukhi(text: string): string[] {
25	  const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;
26	  const seen = new Set<string>();
27	  const out: string[] = [];
28	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
29	  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {
30	    const t = m[0];
31	    if (!seen.has(t)) {
32	      seen.add(t);
33	      out.push(t);
34	    }
35	  }
36	  return out;
37	}
38	
39	// Split a sakhi body into sentence-sized chunks for sentence-level TTS.
40	// Mirrors SakhiReader's splitPa: terminator-aware (। ? !), one entry per
41	// sentence, dedup'd so repeated sentences are synth'd once.
42	function splitSentences(text: string): string[] {
43	  const re = /[^।?!]+[।?!]+["'”’)\]]*|[^।?!]+$/g;
44	  const seen = new Set<string>();
45	  const out: string[] = [];
46	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
47	  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {
48	    const s = m[0].trim();
49	    if (s && !seen.has(s)) {
50	      seen.add(s);
51	      out.push(s);
52	    }
53	  }
54	  return out;
55	}
56	
57	async function lookupMorpheme(word: string): Promise<{
58	  ok: boolean;
59	  cached: boolean;
60	  ms: number;
61	  gloss?: string;
62	  err?: string;
63	}> {
64	  const t0 = Date.now();
65	  try {
66	    const res = await fetch(
67	      `${BASE}/api/morpheme?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`,
68	    );
69	    const ms = Date.now() - t0;
70	    if (!res.ok) {
71	      return { ok: false, cached: false, ms, err: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
72	    }
73	    const j = (await res.json()) as { gloss_en?: string };
74	    return { ok: true, cached: ms < 50, ms, gloss: j.gloss_en };
75	  } catch (err) {
76	    return {
77	      ok: false,
78	      cached: false,
79	      ms: Date.now() - t0,
80	      err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
81	    };
82	  }
83	}
84	
85	async function lookupTts(word: string): Promise<{
86	  ok: boolean;
87	  cached: boolean;
88	  ms: number;
89	  bytes?: number;
90	  err?: string;
91	}> {
92	  const t0 = Date.now();
93	  try {
94	    const res = await fetch(
95	      `${BASE}/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`,
96	    );

99	      return { ok: false, cached: false, ms, err: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
100	    }
101	    const buf = await res.arrayBuffer();
102	    const cacheHdr = res.headers.get("x-lipi-cache");
103	    return {
104	      ok: true,
105	      cached: cacheHdr === "HIT",
106	      ms,
107	      bytes: buf.byteLength,
108	    };
109	  } catch (err) {

112	      cached: false,
113	      ms: Date.now() - t0,
114	      err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
115	    };
116	  }
117	}

119	interface PassResult {

121	  fetched: number;
122	  failed: number;
123	  wallMs: number;
124	}
125	
126	async function runPass(
127	  name: string,
128	  tokens: string[],
129	  concurrency: number,
130	  lookup: (word: string) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; cached: boolean; ms: number; err?: string }>,
131	  describe: (r: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof lookup>>) => string,
132	): Promise<PassResult> {
133	  console.log(`=== ${name} pass (concurrency=${concurrency}) ===`);
134	  let done = 0, cached = 0, fetched = 0, failed = 0;
135	  const t0 = Date.now();
136	  let cursor = 0;
137	  async function worker() {
138	    while (cursor < tokens.length) {
139	      const i = cursor++;
140	      const word = tokens[i];
141	      const r = await lookup(word);
142	      done++;
143	      if (r.ok) {
144	        if (r.cached) cached++;
145	        else fetched++;
146	        if (!r.cached) {
147	          console.log(
148	            `  [${done}/${tokens.length}] ${word.padEnd(14)} ${r.ms.toString().padStart(5)}ms  ${describe(r)}`,
149	          );
150	        }
151	      } else {
152	        failed++;
153	        console.warn(`  [${done}/${tokens.length}] ${word} FAILED: ${r.err}`);
154	      }
155	    }
156	  }
157	  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: concurrency }, worker));
158	  const wallMs = Date.now() - t0;
159	  console.log(
160	    `  ${name} done in ${(wallMs / 1000).toFixed(1)}s. cached-hits=${cached}  fetched=${fetched}  failed=${failed}\n`,
161	  );
162	  return { cached, fetched, failed, wallMs };
163	}
164	
165	async function main() {
166	  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
167	  const sakhiId = Number(args[0]);
168	  const concIdx = args.indexOf("--concurrency");
169	  const concurrency = concIdx >= 0 ? Number(args[concIdx + 1] ?? 2) : 2;
170	  const skipMorpheme = args.includes("--skip-morpheme");
171	  const skipTts = args.includes("--skip-tts");
172	  if (!sakhiId) {
173	    console.error(
174	      "usage: tsx scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts <sakhi-id> [--concurrency N] [--skip-morpheme] [--skip-tts]",
175	    );
176	    process.exit(2);
177	  }
178	
179	  const db = new Database(path.join(process.cwd(), "data", "sakhis.db"), {
180	    readonly: true,
181	  });
182	  const row = db
183	    .prepare(`SELECT title_pa, body_pa FROM sakhis WHERE id = ?`)
184	    .get(sakhiId) as { title_pa: string; body_pa: string } | undefined;
185	  db.close();
186	  if (!row) {
187	    console.error(`sakhi id=${sakhiId} not found`);
188	    process.exit(1);
189	  }
190	
191	  const allText = `${row.title_pa}\n\n${row.body_pa}`;
192	  const tokens = tokenizeGurmukhi(allText);
193	  const sentences = splitSentences(row.body_pa);
194	  console.log(`sakhi ${sakhiId}: "${row.title_pa}"`);
195	  console.log(`  ${tokens.length} unique words, ${sentences.length} unique sentences\n`);
196	
197	  if (!skipMorpheme) {
198	    await runPass(
199	      "morpheme",
200	      tokens,
201	      concurrency,
202	      lookupMorpheme,
203	      (r) => (r as { gloss?: string }).gloss?.slice(0, 60) ?? "",
204	    );
205	  }
206	
207	  if (!skipTts) {
208	    // TTS = best-of-5 GCP calls per word. Default GCP per-minute quota is
209	    // tight (~1000 req/min) and we trip it easily — keep concurrency low.
210	    // Route has per-call backoff/retry so transient quota errors recover,
211	    // but staying under the limit avoids those long backoff stalls.
212	    const ttsConc = 2;
213	    await runPass(
214	      "tts-words",
215	      tokens,
216	      ttsConc,
217	      lookupTts,
218	      (r) => `${(r as { bytes?: number }).bytes ?? 0}B`,
219	    );
220	    await runPass(
221	      "tts-sentences",
222	      sentences,
223	      ttsConc,
224	      lookupTts,
225	      (r) => `${(r as { bytes?: number }).bytes ?? 0}B`,
226	    );
227	  }
228	}
229	
230	main().catch((e) => {
231	  console.error(e);
232	  process.exit(1);
233	});

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/components/MorphemePopover.tsx",
  "old_string": "// Server-side TTS: hits /api/tts which proxies Google Translate's free TTS\n// endpoint, caches the MP3 in SQLite, and streams audio back. This works\n// regardless of whether the user has a Punjabi voice installed locally.\nfunction SpeakButton({ text }: { text: string }) {\n  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n\n  function play() {\n    // Reuse one Audio element so we can stop a previous play before starting\n    if (audioRef.current) {\n      audioRef.current.pause();\n      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;\n    }\n    const audio = new Audio(`/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n    setPlaying(true);\n    audio.onended = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.onerror = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.play().catch(() => setPlaying(false));\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={play}\n      disabled={playing}\n      className=\"text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-40 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n      title=\"Pronounce\"\n      aria-label={`Pronounce ${text}`}\n    >\n      {playing ? \"🔉\" : \"🔊\"}\n    </button>\n  );\n}",
  "new_string": "// /api/tts is cache-only: returns 200 with MP3 if cached, 404 if not. We\n// HEAD the URL once to know whether audio exists, then either render a\n// playable icon or hide the button entirely (no broken UI for uncached words).\nfunction SpeakButton({ text }: { text: string }) {\n  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);\n  const [available, setAvailable] = useState<boolean | null>(null);\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`;\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    fetch(url, { method: \"HEAD\" })\n      .then((r) => !cancelled && setAvailable(r.ok))\n      .catch(() => !cancelled && setAvailable(false));\n    return () => { cancelled = true; };\n  }, [url]);\n\n  function play() {\n    if (audioRef.current) {\n      audioRef.current.pause();\n      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;\n    }\n    const audio = new Audio(url);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n    setPlaying(true);\n    audio.onended = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.onerror = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.play().catch(() => setPlaying(false));\n  }\n\n  if (available === false) return null;\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={play}\n      disabled={playing || available !== true}\n      className=\"text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-40 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n      title=\"Pronounce\"\n      aria-label={`Pronounce ${text}`}\n    >\n      {playing ? \"🔉\" : \"🔊\"}\n    </button>\n  );\n}"
}

## Vercel setup

1. Go to **https://vercel.com/signup** → **"Continue with GitHub"** → log in as `reliq-digital` (it'll need permission to access the org's repos)
2. From the Vercel dashboard, click **"Add New… → Project"**
3. Find `reliq-digital/akhar` in the list → click **"Import"**
4. **Framework Preset**: Next.js (auto-detected)
5. **Root Directory**: leave as `.`
6. **Build & Output Settings**: leave defaults
7. **Environment Variables** — this is the important part. Click **"Add"** and paste in each of these (copy from the `.env.local` on your Mac):

| Name | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `https://fsahapmiupwfljajyngw.supabase.co` | safe in browser |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | `sb_publishable_...` | safe in browser |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | `sb_secret_...` | server only |
| `R2_ENDPOINT` | `https://9967...r2.cloudflarestorage.com` | server only |
| `R2_BUCKET` | `akhar-audio` | server only |
| `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | (your key id) | server only |
| `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | (your secret) | server only |
| `NANOGPT_API_KEY` | `sk-nano-...` | server only (only used in dev prewarm currently) |
| `GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON` | **paste the entire contents** of `~/.config/lipi/vision-key.json` as one line (Vercel handles long values) | server only |

For `GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON`: open the file, copy ALL of it (the entire JSON including braces), paste as the value. Vercel will store it as one env var.

8. Click **"Deploy"**. Build takes ~3 min.

Once it finishes, Vercel gives you a `*.vercel.app` URL. Try it — should show the same reader as localhost. Tell me when:
- The build completed (success or fails — paste errors if it fails)
- You have the `*.vercel.app` URL

Then I'll walk you through pointing `akhar.io` DNS at Vercel via Cloudflare.

Now: point **akhar.io** at Vercel via Cloudflare DNS.

## 1. Add the domain in Vercel

1. In your Vercel project dashboard → **Settings → Domains**
2. Type `akhar.io` → click **Add**
3. Vercel will show you a record to add. It will be **one** of:
   - **CNAME** → `cname.vercel-dns.com`, OR
   - **A record** → `76.76.21.21` (Vercel's anycast IP)

For an apex domain like `akhar.io`, Vercel usually asks for the **A record `76.76.21.21`**. Note exactly what it tells you — copy the value verbatim.

Also add `www.akhar.io` while you're at it (so both work).

## 2. Add the DNS records in Cloudflare

1. **https://dash.cloudflare.com** → click on `akhar.io`
2. Left sidebar → **DNS → Records**
3. Click **Add record**:
   - **Type**: `A`
   - **Name**: `@` (means the apex, akhar.io itself)
   - **IPv4 address**: `76.76.21.21` (or whatever Vercel told you)
   - **Proxy status**: **DNS only** ⚠️ (the orange cloud OFF — Vercel manages CDN itself, Cloudflare proxy in front breaks SSL handshake)
   - **TTL**: Auto
   - Save
4. Add another record:
   - **Type**: `CNAME`
   - **Name**: `www`
   - **Target**: `cname.vercel-dns.com`
   - **Proxy status**: **DNS only**
   - Save

## 3. Wait + verify

DNS propagation: usually 1–5 minutes through Cloudflare. Vercel polls automatically and will turn the domain status green once it sees the records. SSL cert (via Let's Encrypt) provisions automatically right after — another minute or two.

Tell me when:
- `akhar.io` shows as **Valid Configuration** ✅ in Vercel, AND
- Hitting **https://akhar.io** in a browser loads the reader

**Email for socials — fast & free path:**

Use **Cloudflare Email Routing** (free, set up in 2 min). Since you bought akhar.io via Cloudflare, it's already integrated. You won't send from @akhar.io yet, but you'll **receive** everything forwarded to your existing inbox — which is all you need for social-account verification emails.

### Setup (do this in parallel with what I'm coding):

1. **dash.cloudflare.com → click on akhar.io → Email → Email Routing** (left sidebar)
2. Click **"Get started"** → Cloudflare will offer to add the MX + TXT records automatically. **Click "Add records and enable"**.
3. Once enabled, click **"Routes"** tab → **Create address**:
   - Custom address: `hello@akhar.io` → forward to your personal inbox (sumeet@sumeetsaini.com)
   - Repeat for: `support@akhar.io`, and a **Catch-all** rule (anything-else@akhar.io → your inbox)
4. **Catch-all**: also in Routes tab → enable it → forward to your personal inbox. This means typos like `helo@akhar.io` still reach you.

That gives you working @akhar.io email in ~5 min, completely free, forever.

**For sending later** (when you want `hello@akhar.io` to be the actual From address on outbound emails): pair Cloudflare Email Routing with Resend (the transactional service I mentioned earlier). Resend will let you send from `noreply@akhar.io`. Free tier 3000/mo. Setup later.

### Which social handles to grab (priority order for Punjabi learning audience)

1. **Instagram @akhar** ⭐ — biggest priority. Punjabi diaspora lives on IG, especially the parent demographic.
2. **TikTok @akhar** ⭐ — short-form Punjabi content has massive growth right now
3. **X/Twitter @akhar** — less important but free
4. **YouTube @akhar** — for longer-form content later (sakhi readings, etc.)
5. **Threads @akhar** — auto-created with IG
6. **Bluesky @akhar.bsky.social** — emerging, cheap to hold

Fallback if `@akhar` is taken: `@akharapp`, `@akharlearning`, `@akhar_io`.

7	export async function GET(request: Request) {
8	  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
9	  const word = searchParams.get("word");
10	  if (!word) {
11	    return Response.json({ error: "missing 'word' query param" }, { status: 400 });
12	  }
13	  try {
14	    const morpheme = await getMorpheme(word);
15	    return Response.json(morpheme);
16	  } catch (err) {
17	    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
18	    return Response.json({ error: message }, { status: 500 });
19	  }
20	}
21	
22	// POST with { morpheme: ... }  → save the edited morpheme + mark processed
23	// POST with { verify: "<word>" } → just flip the processed flag for that word
24	export async function POST(request: Request) {
25	  const body = (await request.json()) as
26	    | { morpheme: Morpheme }
27	    | { verify: string };
28	  if ("verify" in body && body.verify) {
29	    // Enforce the processed=true criteria server-side:
30	    //   - romanized populated
31	    //   - gloss_en populated (and not the placeholder)
32	    //   - at least one Punjabipedia dictionary entry
33	    const cached = await getMorpheme(body.verify);
34	    const reasons: string[] = [];
35	    if (!cached.romanized) reasons.push("missing romanization");
36	    if (
37	      !cached.gloss_en ||
38	      cached.gloss_en.startsWith("(no ")
39	    ) {
40	      reasons.push("missing English gloss");
41	    }
42	    if (!cached.dictionary_entries || cached.dictionary_entries.length === 0) {
43	      reasons.push("no Punjabipedia dictionary entries");
44	    }
45	    if (reasons.length) {
46	      return Response.json(
47	        { error: `cannot verify ${body.verify}: ${reasons.join(", ")}` },
48	        { status: 409 },
49	      );
50	    }
51	    const ok = markMorphemeProcessed("gurmukhi", body.verify);
52	    if (!ok) {
53	      return Response.json(
54	        { error: `word not in cache: ${body.verify}` },
55	        { status: 404 },
56	      );
57	    }
58	    return Response.json({ verified: body.verify });
59	  }
60	  if ("morpheme" in body && body.morpheme?.surface) {
61	    // Manual edits are implicitly verified
62	    const stamped = overrideMorpheme(body.morpheme);
63	    markMorphemeProcessed("gurmukhi", body.morpheme.surface);
64	    return Response.json(stamped);
65	  }
66	  return Response.json(

69	  );
70	}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/middleware.ts",
  "content": "// Refresh Supabase session cookies on every server request.\n//\n// Why this exists: Supabase Auth stores session JWTs in cookies. Once an\n// access token expires (default 1 hour), the next request needs to swap it\n// for a fresh one using the refresh token. Without middleware that does\n// this proactively, Server Components see stale/expired sessions and treat\n// the user as logged out. This middleware just calls `getUser()` once per\n// request, which under the hood refreshes when needed and rewrites cookies.\nimport { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport { createServerClient } from \"@supabase/ssr\";\n\nexport async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\n  let response = NextResponse.next({ request });\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          response = NextResponse.next({ request });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>\n            response.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n  // Touching getUser() triggers the auto-refresh of cookies if needed.\n  await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  return response;\n}\n\nexport const config = {\n  // Skip static assets + image optimization for perf — we only need session\n  // refresh on real routes.\n  matcher: [\n    \"/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|api/tts|.*\\\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|mp3)$).*)\",\n  ],\n};\n"
}

We exchange the `code` query param for a real\n// session (sets the auth cookies) and then send them to wherever they were\n// trying to go (?next=).\nimport { NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\n\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\";\n\n  if (!code) {\n    return NextResponse.redirect(\n      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(\"Missing code in callback URL\")}`,\n    );\n  }\n\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n  if (error) {\n    return NextResponse.redirect(\n      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`,\n    );\n  }\n  return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}${next}`);\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/deck/actions.ts",
  "content": "\"use server\";\n\n// Per-user SRS deck actions. Reads from the authed Supabase client so RLS\n// enforces ownership — even if the surface or user_id is tampered with,\n// the database refuses the write unless auth.uid() matches user_id.\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\n\nexport async function addToDeck(\n  surface: string,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  if (!surface || surface.length > 60) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"invalid surface\" };\n  }\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) return { ok: false, error: \"not signed in\" };\n\n  // Upsert by (user_id, surface) — adding a word that's already in the\n  // deck is a no-op rather than an error.\n  const { error } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .upsert(\n      { user_id: user.id, surface },\n      { onConflict: \"user_id,surface\", ignoreDuplicates: true },\n    );\n  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n"
}

1	"use client";
2	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
3	import type { Morpheme } from "@/lib/types";
4	import MorphemePopover from "./MorphemePopover";
5	
6	interface Props {
7	  word: string;
8	  isActive: boolean;
9	  onOpen: () => void;
10	  onClose: () => void;
11	}
12	
13	const HOVER_OPEN_MS = 200;
14	const HOVER_CLOSE_MS = 250;
15	
16	export default function HoverWord({ word, isActive, onOpen, onClose }: Props) {
17	  const [morpheme, setMorpheme] = useState<Morpheme | null>(null);
18	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
19	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
20	  // "sticky" = popover was opened by click and should stay open until another
21	  // explicit close (click outside or click trigger again). Hover-opens are
22	  // not sticky and auto-close when the pointer leaves both trigger + popover.
23	  const [sticky, setSticky] = useState(false);
24	  const openTimer = useRef<number | null>(null);
25	  const closeTimer = useRef<number | null>(null);
26	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
27	
28	  useEffect(() => {
29	    if (!isActive || morpheme || loading) return;
30	    setLoading(true);
31	    setError(null);
32	    fetch(`/api/morpheme?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`)
33	      .then(async (r) => {
34	        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
35	        return r.json();
36	      })
37	      .then((m: Morpheme) => setMorpheme(m))
38	      .catch((e: unknown) => setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)))
39	      .finally(() => setLoading(false));
40	  }, [isActive, word, morpheme, loading]);
41	
42	  // Clear any in-flight timers when this component unmounts so we don't try
43	  // to open/close on a stale parent.
44	  useEffect(
45	    () => () => {
46	      if (openTimer.current) window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
47	      if (closeTimer.current) window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
48	    },
49	    [],
50	  );
51	
52	  function scheduleOpen() {
53	    if (closeTimer.current) {
54	      window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
55	      closeTimer.current = null;
56	    }
57	    if (isActive) return;
58	    openTimer.current = window.setTimeout(() => {
59	      onOpen();
60	      openTimer.current = null;
61	    }, HOVER_OPEN_MS);
62	  }
63	
64	  function scheduleClose() {
65	    if (sticky) return;
66	    if (openTimer.current) {
67	      window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
68	      openTimer.current = null;
69	    }
70	    if (!isActive) return;
71	    closeTimer.current = window.setTimeout(() => {
72	      onClose();
73	      closeTimer.current = null;
74	    }, HOVER_CLOSE_MS);
75	  }
76	
77	  function handleClick() {
78	    // Clicking pins (or unpins) the popover. If currently closed, open it
79	    // immediately and make it sticky; if open and sticky, unpin + close;
80	    // if open via hover (not sticky), just pin it.
81	    if (openTimer.current) {
82	      window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
83	      openTimer.current = null;
84	    }
85	    if (closeTimer.current) {
86	      window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
87	      closeTimer.current = null;
88	    }
89	    if (!isActive) {
90	      setSticky(true);
91	      onOpen();
92	    } else if (sticky) {
93	      setSticky(false);
94	      onClose();
95	    } else {
96	      setSticky(true);
97	    }
98	  }
99	
100	  // When the popover gets closed (e.g. by the parent because another word
101	  // was opened), reset sticky so the next interaction starts fresh AND
102	  // cancel any pending timers so they don't fire stale onClose/onOpen.
103	  useEffect(() => {
104	    if (!isActive) {
105	      if (sticky) setSticky(false);
106	      if (closeTimer.current) {
107	        window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
108	        closeTimer.current = null;
109	      }
110	    } else {
111	      // Becoming active cancels any in-flight close
112	      if (closeTimer.current) {
113	        window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
114	        closeTimer.current = null;
115	      }
116	    }
117	  }, [isActive, sticky]);
118	
119	  return (
120	    <span className="relative inline-block">
121	      <button
122	        ref={triggerRef}
123	        type="button"
124	        onClick={handleClick}
125	        onMouseEnter={scheduleOpen}
126	        onMouseLeave={scheduleClose}
127	        className={`cursor-pointer rounded transition-colors ${
128	          isActive
129	            ? "bg-amber-200 dark:bg-amber-900"
130	            : "hover:bg-amber-100 dark:hover:bg-amber-950"
131	        }`}
132	      >
133	        {word}
134	      </button>
135	      {isActive && (
136	        <MorphemePopover
137	          word={word}
138	          morpheme={morpheme}
139	          loading={loading}
140	          error={error}
141	          sticky={sticky}
142	          triggerEl={triggerRef.current}
143	          onClose={() => {
144	            setSticky(false);
145	            onClose();
146	          }}
147	          onHoverIn={() => {
148	            // Keep popover open while pointer is over it
149	            if (closeTimer.current) {
150	              window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
151	              closeTimer.current = null;
152	            }
153	          }}
154	          onHoverOut={scheduleClose}
155	          onUpdate={(m) => setMorpheme(m)}
156	        />
157	      )}
158	    </span>
159	  );
160	}
161

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/middleware.ts",
  "content": "// Refresh Supabase session cookies on every server request AND enforce\n// \"must be signed in\" for app routes. Public routes:\n//   /            (landing page — the pitch)\n//   /login       (sign-in form)\n//   /auth/*      (magic-link callback)\n//   /api/*       (handlers do their own auth where needed)\n//   static assets\n// Everything else (sakhi, guru, deck, etc.) redirects to /login?next=...\nimport { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport { createServerClient } from \"@supabase/ssr\";\n\nconst PUBLIC_PATHS = new Set([\"/\", \"/login\"]);\nconst PUBLIC_PREFIXES = [\"/auth/\", \"/api/\"];\n\nfunction isPublic(pathname: string): boolean {\n  if (PUBLIC_PATHS.has(pathname)) return true;\n  return PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p));\n}\n\nexport async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\n  let response = NextResponse.next({ request });\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          response = NextResponse.next({ request });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>\n            response.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n  // Touching getUser() triggers the auto-refresh of cookies if needed.\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl;\n  if (!user && !isPublic(pathname)) {\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/login\";\n    url.search = `?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname + search)}`;\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  return response;\n}\n\nexport const config = {\n  matcher: [\n    \"/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|mp3)$).*)\",\n  ],\n};\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/DEV.md",
  "content": "# Development workflow\n\n## Branches\n\n- **`main`** — production. Deploys to akhar.io.\n- **`dev`** — staging. Deploys to a Vercel preview URL (auto-generated, looks\n  like `akhar-git-dev-reliq-digital.vercel.app`). Use this for any change\n  you want to see live before users do.\n\n**Default branch for new work: `dev`.** Never push directly to `main`.\n\n## Day-to-day loop\n\n```sh\n# Start on dev\ngit checkout dev\ngit pull\n\n# Make changes, test locally\nnpm run dev   # http://localhost:3000\n\n# Commit + push when ready to see it on the staging URL\ngit add -A && git commit -m \"...\"\ngit push      # Vercel auto-builds the dev preview in ~2 min\n\n# When the preview looks good, ship it to prod\ngit checkout main\ngit merge dev\ngit push      # Vercel auto-builds prod akhar.io\ngit checkout dev   # back to dev for next batch\n```\n\n## Local environment\n\n`.env.local` has all the production secrets — local dev hits the **same\nSupabase project and R2 bucket as production**. This means:\n\n- Sign-in cookies you create locally will be valid on akhar.io too (same\n  Supabase auth instance).\n- \"Save to deck\" writes from localhost land in the real user's deck.\n- TTS audio uploads from `tsx scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts` go straight to\n  production R2 — convenient (prewarms benefit prod), risky (you can\n  pollute real data).\n\nIf you ever need true isolation, spin up a second Supabase project\n(\"akhar-dev\"), put its keys in `.env.local.dev`, and use a separate R2\nbucket. Don't need this yet.\n\n## What's local-only vs cloud\n\n| Data | Where | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Morpheme cache (`lipi.db`) | Local SQLite, committed to git | Production reads the bundled file (read-only). `git commit && git push` ships new entries. |\n| Sakhi corpus (`data/sakhis.db`) | Local SQLite, committed to git | Same — bundled into deploy. |\n| Audio MP3s | Cloudflare R2 (`akhar-audio` bucket) | Shared across all environments. |\n| User accounts + decks + bookmarks | Supabase Postgres | Shared. |\n\n## Tests / smoke\n\n- `npx tsx scripts/smoke-supabase.ts` — verifies the Supabase keys + RLS\n  policies still work end-to-end.\n- `npx tsc --noEmit` — typecheck. Run before pushing.\n- `npm run build` — full Next.js production build. Run if you've changed\n  middleware, config, or anything that might break the prod build path.\n\n## Auth gate\n\nMiddleware (`middleware.ts`) requires sign-in for every route except `/`,\n`/login`, `/auth/*`, `/api/*`. If you add a new public page (e.g. /about,\n/pricing), add it to `PUBLIC_PATHS` in `middleware.ts`.\n\n## Vercel env vars\n\nWhen you add a new env var to `.env.local`, also add it to Vercel:\n\n- Project Settings → Environment Variables\n- Add for all three environments: **Production**, **Preview**, **Development**\n- Trigger a new deploy (Vercel only picks up new env vars on rebuild)\n"
}

git merge dev
git push

import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}

## Exports

### Proxy function

The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

```js filename="proxy.js"
// Example of default export
export default function proxy(request) {
  // Proxy logic
}
```
--
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  // Proxy logic goes here
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
export function proxy(request) {
  // Proxy logic goes here
}
```

If you prefer a shorthand, you can use the `NextProxy` type. It infers the parameter types for both `request` (`NextRequest`) and `event` (`NextFetchEvent`) automatically:

```tsx filename="proxy.ts"
import type { NextProxy } from 'next/server'
```

1	// Refresh Supabase session cookies on every server request AND enforce
2	// "must be signed in" for app routes. Public routes:
3	//   /            (landing page — the pitch)
4	//   /login       (sign-in form)
5	//   /auth/*      (magic-link callback)
6	//   /api/*       (handlers do their own auth where needed)
7	//   static assets
8	// Everything else (sakhi, guru, deck, etc.) redirects to /login?next=...
9	import { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
10	import { createServerClient } from "@supabase/ssr";
11	
12	const PUBLIC_PATHS = new Set(["/", "/login"]);
13	const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ["/auth/", "/api/"];
14	
15	function isPublic(pathname: string): boolean {
16	  if (PUBLIC_PATHS.has(pathname)) return true;
17	  return PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p));
18	}
19	
20	export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
21	  let response = NextResponse.next({ request });
22	  const supabase = createServerClient(
23	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
24	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,
25	    {
26	      cookies: {
27	        getAll() {
28	          return request.cookies.getAll();
29	        },
30	        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
31	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>
32	            request.cookies.set(name, value),
33	          );
34	          response = NextResponse.next({ request });
35	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
36	            response.cookies.set(name, value, options),
37	          );
38	        },
39	      },
40	    },
41	  );
42	  // Touching getUser() triggers the auto-refresh of cookies if needed.
43	  const {
44	    data: { user },
45	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
46	
47	  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl;
48	  if (!user && !isPublic(pathname)) {
49	    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
50	    url.pathname = "/login";
51	    url.search = `?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname + search)}`;
52	    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
53	  }
54	
55	  return response;
56	}
57	
58	export const config = {
59	  matcher: [
60	    "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|mp3)$).*)",
61	  ],
62	};
63

```sh
rm -rf .next && npm run dev
```

A panic in Turbopack's HMR is usually cache corruption — nuking `.next/` rebuilds it from scratch and resolves it.

> DEVELOPER

so what I think is really important is to hae a a punjabi alphabet learning section. Let's talk aboyt this and how we could do it

> AGENT

Great instinct — for a Punjabi learning app, the alphabet is the literal first thing 90% of learners need. Let me think through this carefully.

## Why this is a strategic feature, not just a feature

1. **It's the funnel top.** Most people searching "learn Punjabi" don't know the alphabet. Without it they bounce. Duolingo's whole onboarding starts with the alphabet for every new script.
2. **It's the SEO play.** "Punjabi alphabet", "Gurmukhi letters", "paintee akhar" — high-volume keywords with weak existing content.
3. **It naturally cross-promotes the reader.** Every example word in the alphabet section can link to a sakhi where the word appears in real classical context. No other app does this.

## What's in scope (Gurmukhi script)

- **35 base letters** (paintee akhar) — the canonical alphabet
- **6 nukta letters** (ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ ਲ਼) for borrowed sounds
- **10 vowel signs (matras)** that attach to consonants
- **Special symbols** — tippi (ੰ), bindi (ਂ), addhak (ੱ), halant (੍), bihari (ੀ), etc.
- **Numerals** (੦–੯)

## The thing nobody else does

**Use sakhi vocabulary as the example words.** Most apps teach "ਘ = ਘੋੜਾ (horse)" — generic textbook content. We'd teach "ਘ = ਘੱਲਿਆ (sent), from sakhi 12, where Guru Nanak says..." Every letter becomes a doorway into the corpus, not a flashcard in isolation.

## What I'd build (phased)

### Phase 1: Reference (1 day) — `/alphabet`

- Grid of 35 letters, click any → detail page
- Detail page per letter:
  - The character (large, calligraphic)
  - Its name in Gurmukhi + romanized ("ਜੱਜਾ jajja")
  - Phonetic value (IPA + romanized: /dʒə/, "ja")
  - Audio: play the letter name (Chirp 3, cached in R2)
  - 3-5 example words from sakhis we've processed, each linking to where it appears
  - Optional: stroke order / origin (Brahmi → Sharada → Gurmukhi)

Just *reading content* — no quizzes. Already shippable, already SEO-valuable.

### Phase 2: Recognition practice (2-3 days) — `/alphabet/practice`

- Flashcards: shows letter, you say name in your head, click reveal, mark "knew it / didn't"
- Audio mode: plays letter name, you pick the right letter from 4 options
- Tracks per-user "letters known" via Supabase (`alphabet_progress` table)

### Phase 3: Integration with reader

- Hover any word in a sakhi → popover gains a "letter breakdown" line showing each character with link to its page
- Reading view has a "show letter names" toggle that overlays small romanized letter names above each Gurmukhi character

### Phase 4 (later): Writing practice — `/alphabet/write`

- Touch/mouse trace the letter with correct stroke order
- Premium feature candidate

## Questions for you (architecture)

Before we get started, something that needs to happeb is that we gotta talk about movile. I want tehse to be proper mobile apps. Is tehre a way we can do the web veriosn and movile apss as well>

> AGENT

Yes — multiple paths, with different tradeoffs. Let me lay them out.

## The three real options

### Option A: PWA (Progressive Web App)
Add a manifest + service worker to the existing Next.js app. Users get an "Add to Home Screen" prompt, the app installs like a native app, runs in fullscreen, can work offline, can send push notifications (Android freely, iOS more limited).

- **Cost**: $0 (no app store fees)
- **Time**: ~1-2 days
- **Codebase**: same as web (zero extra code beyond the manifest)
- **Distribution**: people install from akhar.io, NOT from App Store
- **Limitation**: NOT in App Store / Play Store → lower trust, lower discoverability, no "search for Punjabi app" findability

### Option B: Capacitor (web wrapped as native) ⭐ **What I'd recommend**
Capacitor wraps your existing Next.js web app in a native shell (WebView) and ships to both App Store and Play Store. Same codebase as web — no rewrite. Plus native APIs for push notifications, offline downloads, app badges, biometric auth, etc.

- **Cost**: $99/yr (Apple Dev) + $25 one-time (Google Play)
- **Time**: ~1 week first time, hours per update after
- **Codebase**: same as web (one repo, one product)
- **Distribution**: real apps in both stores, akhar.io still serves the web
- **Native features**: progressively add as needed (push for SRS reminders, offline sakhis for premium, etc.)
- **Used by**: Discord (early days), Microsoft Teams, Sworkit, Spotify Lite

### Option C: Expo / React Native (truly native)
Separate native app codebase, share types/logic with web via packages. Real native performance, real native components. This is what you'd build if you were Notion or Linear — eventually they all end up here.

- **Cost**: store fees + significant dev time
- **Time**: ~3-4 weeks to reach web parity, then ongoing parallel development
- **Codebase**: two render targets (web + native), most logic shared
- **When it's right**: when you have users telling you the WebView is too slow

## My honest recommendation: **B (Capacitor)**

For akhar.io specifically:

1. **You already have a Next.js web app that's nearly launch-ready.** Capacitor reuses 100% of it. Option C would mean rebuilding it.
2. **The performance penalty of WebView is invisible for a reading app.** Akhar is text + audio playback + hover popovers — none of these need native rendering speed. (If we were building a Punjabi *video chat* app, different story.)
3. **The store presence is real value.** "Punjabi learning app" → if you're not in App Store/Play Store, you're invisible. Diaspora parents searching for kids' learning apps look in the App Store first, Google second.
4. **You can escape later.** If years from now you want to rewrite specific screens in true native, Capacitor lets you mix WebView screens with native React Native screens in the same app. No lock-in.

## The path I'd actually take

1. **Now → next 1–2 weeks** — make the web responsive and touch-friendly. This benefits desktop AND mobile web AND future native apps. Concretely:
   - Hover popovers → tap-and-hold or tap-to-open on touch devices
   - Sentence play buttons sized for fingers
   - Reader layout works on phone widths (320px+)
   - Bottom-nav pattern on mobile (Home / Library / Deck / Profile)
   - This is needed regardless of native or not

2. **PWA basics** (~1 day after that)
   - manifest.json, app icons, splash screen
   - Service worker for offline caching of read sakhis
   - "Install akhar" prompt on mobile

3. **When ready to launch in stores** (~1 week)
   - Add Capacitor
   - Build for iOS + Android
   - Submit to both stores (1-3 day review)
   - Same web codebase keeps updating both

4. **Later** (post-launch, only if needed) — rewrite hot paths in React Native if WebView feels slow.

## Decision

Yes, Capacitor is the right call for both of your goals. Let me address them specifically:

## "Will the app be accepted on the App Stores?"

**Yes, with one caveat that's easy to satisfy.**

The historical concern: Apple Guideline 4.2 — "apps must include features that go beyond a repackaged website." A bare WebView wrapping akhar.io would get rejected as "just a website."

The fix: add native features that justify the app's existence. For akhar specifically, we'd add:

1. **Push notifications** — "Time to review your Punjabi flashcards" (SRS reminders)
2. **Offline sakhi downloads** — read on flights, on the subway (also a premium tier hook)
3. **Native Sign in with Apple** — mandatory on iOS if you offer any other auth method (we do — email magic links)
4. **Native audio session** — proper background audio playback (continues when phone is locked, integrates with iOS lock-screen controls)
5. **Native share sheet** — "Share this sakhi with a friend"

Each is one Capacitor plugin (`@capacitor/push-notifications`, `@capacitor/filesystem`, `@capacitor/share`, etc.). Apple accepts apps doing this all day. Real examples: Burger King (US), Southwest Airlines, Sworkit, MarketWatch — all Capacitor apps in the App Store.

## "Will the website work mirror perfectly on the mobile app?"

**Yes, that's literally Capacitor's whole point.**

The mobile app *is* the web app — rendered inside a WebView. Two flavors:

- **Bundled mode**: web app is shipped inside the .ipa/.apk. Offline-first. Need a store release to ship new features.
- **Live mode** (recommended for akhar): app loads `https://akhar.io` at runtime. Every web deploy → mobile app updates instantly with no store submission. Store updates only needed when you change native plugins.

For akhar, **live mode is the sweet spot**:
- Update the reader UI → users see it next time they open the app
- Add a new sakhi → in the app immediately
- Change copy on the landing page → live
- Add a new native plugin → THAT needs a store release

This is exactly the workflow you described — "work we do in the website mirrored perfectly on the app store."

**Caveat**: live mode has tradeoffs. If the user is offline, the app shows a blank screen. Solution: cache a basic offline shell + the user's saved sakhis. Capacitor + service worker handles this.

## What this means concretely for the order of work

1. ✅ Now: build the alphabet feature (web only)
2. ✅ Soon: finish auth polish, save-to-deck UI, /deck review page
3. Next: **responsive/touch UX pass** across the whole web app (mobile-friendly first)
4. Then: **PWA basics** (manifest, icons, service worker for offline shell)
5. Then: **Capacitor wrap + store submissions** (App Store + Play Store)
6. Then: **native plugins as needed** (push, downloads, share, Sign in with Apple)

You're approving this path. Now back to the alphabet — you picked:
- **Signed-in only** (gates SEO opportunity but you said you want everyone signed in anyway, consistent with the rest of the app)
- **Both textbook + sakhi examples** (beginner-friendly + the corpus-integration angle)
- **Reference page first, no practice** (ship in a day, validate before adding interactive)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/alphabet-corpus.ts",
  "content": "// Find example words from the sakhi corpus that contain a given Gurmukhi\n// letter. Walks every sakhi's body_pa once (fast — the corpus is 4 MB),\n// tokenises into Gurmukhi runs, counts occurrences, and returns the most\n// frequent unique words containing the target character.\n//\n// Why frequency-weighted: rare or one-off words aren't great teaching\n// examples. \"ਨਾਮ\" is more useful than a hapax legomenon.\nimport { sakhiDb } from \"./sakhi-db\";\n\nconst GURMUKHI_WORD_RE = /[਀-੿]+/g;\n\nexport interface SakhiWordExample {\n  word: string;\n  count: number;\n  sakhi_id: number;          // first sakhi the word appears in\n  sakhi_title: string;       // its title (PA)\n}\n\ninterface Row {\n  id: number;\n  title_pa: string;\n  body_pa: string;\n}\n\nlet _wordIndex: Map<string, { count: number; first: { id: number; title: string } }> | null = null;\n\n// Build a single in-memory index of every distinct Gurmukhi word in the\n// corpus → frequency + first appearance. Built lazily on first call,\n// reused for every subsequent lookup. ~80k unique tokens total when full\n// corpus is processed; ~5 MB RAM. Fine for serverless cold starts.\nfunction ensureIndex(): NonNullable<typeof _wordIndex> {\n  if (_wordIndex) return _wordIndex;\n  const rows = sakhiDb()\n    .prepare(\"SELECT id, title_pa, body_pa FROM sakhis\")\n    .all() as Row[];\n  const idx = new Map<string, { count: number; first: { id: number; title: string } }>();\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    const text = `${row.title_pa}\\n${row.body_pa}`;\n    let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n    GURMUKHI_WORD_RE.lastIndex = 0;\n    while ((m = GURMUKHI_WORD_RE.exec(text)) !== null) {\n      const word = m[0];\n      const cur = idx.get(word);\n      if (cur) {\n        cur.count++;\n      } else {\n        idx.set(word, {\n          count: 1,\n          first: { id: row.id, title: row.title_pa },\n        });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  _wordIndex = idx;\n  return idx;\n}\n\n/**\n * Return up to `limit` real corpus words that contain `letter`, ranked by\n * frequency. Skips trivially-short words (≤1 char — they're letter forms,\n * not lexical examples).\n */\nexport function corpusExamplesFor(\n  letter: string,\n  limit = 5,\n): SakhiWordExample[] {\n  const idx = ensureIndex();\n  const matches: SakhiWordExample[] = [];\n  for (const [word, info] of idx) {\n    if (word.length < 2) continue;\n    if (!word.includes(letter)) continue;\n    matches.push({\n      word,\n      count: info.count,\n      sakhi_id: info.first.id,\n      sakhi_title: info.first.title,\n    });\n  }\n  matches.sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count);\n  return matches.slice(0, limit);\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/components/LetterAudio.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\n// Plays a cached audio clip from /api/tts. Same as the popover/sentence\n// speakers: HEADs the URL once, hides itself if no cache exists, plays\n// the MP3 from R2 on tap.\nexport default function LetterAudio({\n  text,\n  label,\n}: {\n  text: string;\n  label: string;\n}) {\n  const [available, setAvailable] = useState<boolean | null>(null);\n  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`;\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    fetch(url, { method: \"HEAD\" })\n      .then((r) => !cancelled && setAvailable(r.ok))\n      .catch(() => !cancelled && setAvailable(false));\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n  }, [url]);\n\n  function play() {\n    if (audioRef.current) {\n      audioRef.current.pause();\n      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;\n    }\n    const audio = new Audio(url);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n    setPlaying(true);\n    audio.onended = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.onerror = () => setPlaying(false);\n    audio.play().catch(() => setPlaying(false));\n  }\n\n  if (available === false) return null;\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={play}\n      disabled={playing || available !== true}\n      className=\"mt-4 inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-zinc-700 transition hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 disabled:opacity-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\"\n    >\n      <span>{playing ? \"🔉\" : \"🔊\"}</span>\n      <span>{label}</span>\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/prewarm-alphabet.ts",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env tsx\n/**\n * Synth + upload audio for every letter in data/alphabet.ts.\n *\n * Two clips per letter:\n *   - the letter's full Punjabi name (e.g. ਜੱਜਾ)\n *   - the example word (e.g. ਜੀਵਨ)\n *\n * Skips entries already in R2. Re-runnable.\n *\n *   tsx scripts/prewarm-alphabet.ts\n */\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\n// .env.local loader — same pattern as the other scripts\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { ALL_LETTERS } from \"@/data/alphabet\";\nimport { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { audioCacheHas, putCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\nasync function ensureClip(text: string): Promise<{\n  status: \"cached\" | \"synthed\" | \"failed\";\n  bytes?: number;\n  err?: string;\n}> {\n  try {\n    if (await audioCacheHas(VOICE_NAME, text)) {\n      return { status: \"cached\" };\n    }\n    const mp3 = await synthesize(text);\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text, mp3);\n    return { status: \"synthed\", bytes: mp3.length };\n  } catch (err) {\n    return {\n      status: \"failed\",\n      err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),\n    };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const targets: { kind: \"name\" | \"example\"; text: string }[] = [];\n  for (const l of ALL_LETTERS) {\n    targets.push({ kind: \"name\", text: l.name_pa });\n    targets.push({ kind: \"example\", text: l.example_pa });\n  }\n\n  console.log(`Synthing ${targets.length} clips (${ALL_LETTERS.length} letters × 2)\\n`);\n\n  let cached = 0, synthed = 0, failed = 0;\n  // Concurrency 2 to stay under GCP per-minute quota during fresh runs.\n  const conc = 2;\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker(id: number) {\n    while (cursor < targets.length) {\n      const i = cursor++;\n      const t = targets[i];\n      const r = await ensureClip(t.text);\n      if (r.status === \"cached\") {\n        cached++;\n        console.log(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${targets.length}] cached  (${t.kind}) ${t.text}`);\n      } else if (r.status === \"synthed\") {\n        synthed++;\n        console.log(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${targets.length}] synthed (${t.kind}) ${t.text} → ${r.bytes}B`);\n      } else {\n        failed++;\n        console.warn(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${targets.length}] FAILED  (${t.kind}) ${t.text}: ${r.err}`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: conc }, (_, i) => worker(i + 1)));\n  console.log(`\\ncached=${cached} synthed=${synthed} failed=${failed}`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

I've read the whole book. Here's what makes it work pedagogically and how I'd map it to akhar:

## The book's actual methodology (49 pages, distilled)

It's a **sequential curriculum**, not a reference. Every page introduces ONE concept, shows examples, then has a reading exercise.

| Section | Pages | What's taught |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Pronunciation primer** | 5–7 | The 10 vowel sounds with English equivalents (u/ū/o, a/ā/æ/ɔ, i/ī/e), diacritic conventions (bar = long, dot = retroflex, h = aspirated), tongue-position diagrams (dental vs retroflex t/d) |
| **2. Letter flashcards** | 8–21 | One letter per page in a big frame: large character + name + 1–2 illustrated example words with romanization + English. NOT a grid — every letter gets its own dedicated page. |
| **3. Letter chart** | 22–23 | All 35 letters in one reference grid + the 5 nukta letters |
| **4. Recognition test** | 24 | Same letters shuffled — "Can you identify these now?" |
| **5. Mukta** (inherent 'a') | 25–26 | Words with NO vowel sign + reading sentences |
| **6. Vowel signs (matras)** | 27–37 | One lesson per matra: Kannā ā, Sihārī i, Bihārī ī, Aunkaṛ u, Dulæṅkaṛ ū, Lāvāṅ e, Dulāvāṅ æ, Hoṛā o, Kanɔṛā ɔ. Each shows construction (ਕ + ਾ = ਕਾ), 15–25 example words, then sentences using them. |
| **7. Gemination** | 38–39 | Adhikk ੱ — doubles the next consonant |
| **8. Nasalization** | 40–43 | Tippī ੰ (above-the-line) and Bindī ਂ (above-the-curve) |
| **9. Subscript Rārā** | 44 | Pairī Rārā ੍ਰ — conjuncts |
| **10. H at end/foot** | 45 | Tone marks, subscript h |
| **11. Glossary** | 46–49 | Every word from every lesson, with page refs |

**The structural insight**: every lesson teaches one thing, then **immediately uses it in real sentences**. By page 26 the learner is already reading sentences like "ਬਸ ਫੜ ਘਰ ਵੱਲ ਚੱਲ" (catch the bus, go home). Confidence-building through reading practice from day one.

## What's wrong with my current `/alphabet`

It's a reference grid. The book is a curriculum. Two completely different things.

A reference page is for someone who already knows the alphabet and needs to look one up. A curriculum is for someone learning from scratch — which is our actual user.

## How I'd restructure

**Restructure `/alphabet` from "grid" to "lesson path":**

```
/alphabet                       — Lesson index (1, 2, 3... with progress dots)
/alphabet/pronunciation         — Lesson 0: vowel/consonant system overview
/alphabet/letters/ੳ             — Lesson 1: letter ੳ (Ūṛā) — single letter, big, examples, audio
/alphabet/letters/ਅ             — Lesson 2: letter ਅ
...
/alphabet/letters/ੜ             — Lesson 35: letter ੜ
/alphabet/nukta                 — Lesson 36: the 5 nukta letters as a group
/alphabet/chart                 — Reference: all letters in one grid (the page you wanted to scrap, but as a separate reference, not the entry point)
/alphabet/recognition           — Exercise: shuffled letters, click to name
/alphabet/mukta                 — Lesson: inherent 'a' (reading words without vowel signs)
/alphabet/matras/kanna          — Lesson: vowel sign ਾ (ā)
/alphabet/matras/sihari         — Lesson: vowel sign ਿ (i)
...
/alphabet/adhikk                — Lesson: gemination ੱ
/alphabet/tippi                 — Lesson: nasalization ੰ
/alphabet/bindi                 — Lesson: nasalization ਂ
/alphabet/pairin-rara           — Lesson: subscript ਰ
/alphabet/tone-h                — Lesson: tone-marking h
```

Each lesson is a focused, single-concept page with:
- Big visual of the new concept
- Audio for the concept and the examples
- 5–15 real Punjabi example words from the book's wordlists (manually curated, you wanted this)
- A short reading-practice section: 3–5 sentences using only what's been taught so far
- "Mark complete" button → writes to a new `alphabet_progress` per-user table (so you can resume + see overall completion %)
- Prev / next lesson nav

Total: ~50 lessons (35 letters + 5 nukta-as-group + 10 matras + 5 other concepts). Roughly the full book translated into the medium.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/components/lessons/RecognitionExerciseView.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Recognition exercise — book page 24: \"Can you identify these letters now?\"\n// Shows letters in shuffled order. Tap one to reveal its name (and the link\n// to its lesson). Re-shuffle button for a fresh round.\n//\n// Future: track per-user correctness, randomize stable per-day, etc.\nimport { useMemo, useState } from \"react\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { CURRICULUM, type LetterLesson, type NuktaGroupLesson } from \"@/data/curriculum\";\n\ninterface ChartItem {\n  char: string;\n  name_iso: string;\n  slug: string;\n}\n\nfunction buildPool(): ChartItem[] {\n  const items: ChartItem[] = [];\n  for (const l of CURRICULUM) {\n    if (l.kind === \"letter\") {\n      const ll = l as LetterLesson;\n      items.push({ char: ll.char, name_iso: ll.name_iso, slug: ll.slug });\n    } else if (l.kind === \"nukta-group\") {\n      const ng = l as NuktaGroupLesson;\n      for (const n of ng.letters) {\n        items.push({ char: n.char, name_iso: n.name_iso, slug: ng.slug });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return items;\n}\n\nfunction shuffle<T>(arr: T[], seed: number): T[] {\n  // Deterministic shuffle so SSR/CSR agree until the user re-shuffles.\n  const out = [...arr];\n  let s = seed;\n  for (let i = out.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {\n    s = (s * 9301 + 49297) % 233280;\n    const j = Math.floor((s / 233280) * (i + 1));\n    [out[i], out[j]] = [out[j], out[i]];\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport default function RecognitionExerciseView() {\n  const pool = useMemo(buildPool, []);\n  const [seed, setSeed] = useState(42);\n  const [revealed, setRevealed] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});\n  const items = useMemo(() => shuffle(pool, seed), [pool, seed]);\n\n  function reshuffle() {\n    setSeed(Math.floor(Math.random() * 1_000_000));\n    setRevealed({});\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <article>\n      <header className=\"text-center\">\n        <h1 className=\"text-3xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          Can you identify these letters now?\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-2 text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n          Tap any letter to reveal its name. When you can name them all\n          without revealing, you&apos;re ready for the next section.\n        </p>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={reshuffle}\n          className=\"mt-4 inline-flex items-center rounded-md border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-zinc-700 hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\"\n        >\n          ↻ Shuffle\n        </button>\n      </header>\n\n      <div className=\"mt-8 grid grid-cols-5 gap-2 sm:grid-cols-5\">\n        {items.map((item, i) => {\n          const key = `${seed}-${i}-${item.char}`;\n          const isRevealed = revealed[key];\n          return (\n            <div key={key} className=\"aspect-square\">\n              {isRevealed ? (\n                <Link\n                  href={`/alphabet/${encodeURIComponent(item.slug)}`}\n                  className=\"flex h-full flex-col items-center justify-center rounded-md border border-emerald-300 bg-emerald-50 text-center dark:border-emerald-800 dark:bg-emerald-950\"\n                  title=\"Open lesson\"\n                >\n                  <span className=\"font-serif text-2xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n                    {item.char}\n                  </span>\n                  <span className=\"mt-0.5 font-mono text-[10px] text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n                    {item.name_iso}\n                  </span>\n                </Link>\n              ) : (\n                <button\n                  type=\"button\"\n                  onClick={() => setRevealed((r) => ({ ...r, [key]: true }))}\n                  className=\"flex h-full w-full items-center justify-center rounded-md border border-zinc-200 bg-white text-3xl text-zinc-900 transition hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-amber-50 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-50 dark:hover:bg-amber-950\"\n                >\n                  <span className=\"font-serif\">{item.char}</span>\n                </button>\n              )}\n            </div>\n          );\n        })}\n      </div>\n    </article>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/prewarm-alphabet.ts",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env tsx\n/**\n * Synth + upload audio for every clip the alphabet curriculum needs:\n *   - every letter's name (e.g. ਜੱਜਾ)\n *   - every example word in every lesson\n *\n * Walks the CURRICULUM tree so any new lesson added to data/curriculum.ts\n * is automatically covered next run. Skips entries already in R2.\n *\n *   tsx scripts/prewarm-alphabet.ts\n */\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { CURRICULUM } from \"@/data/curriculum\";\nimport { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { audioCacheHas, putCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\nfunction collectClips(): { kind: string; text: string }[] {\n  const out: { kind: string; text: string }[] = [];\n  for (const l of CURRICULUM) {\n    if (l.kind === \"letter\") {\n      out.push({ kind: \"letter-name\", text: l.name_pa });\n      for (const ex of l.examples) out.push({ kind: \"letter-example\", text: ex.pa });\n    } else if (l.kind === \"nukta-group\") {\n      for (const n of l.letters) {\n        out.push({ kind: \"nukta-name\", text: n.name_pa });\n        for (const ex of n.examples) out.push({ kind: \"nukta-example\", text: ex.pa });\n      }\n    } else if (l.kind === \"matra\") {\n      out.push({ kind: \"matra-name\", text: l.name_pa });\n      for (const ex of l.examples) out.push({ kind: \"matra-example\", text: ex.pa });\n      for (const s of l.reading) out.push({ kind: \"matra-reading\", text: s });\n    } else if (l.kind === \"mukta\") {\n      for (const ex of l.examples) out.push({ kind: \"mukta-example\", text: ex.pa });\n      for (const s of l.reading) out.push({ kind: \"mukta-reading\", text: s });\n    } else if (l.kind === \"concept\") {\n      out.push({ kind: \"concept-name\", text: l.name_pa });\n      for (const ex of l.examples) out.push({ kind: \"concept-example\", text: ex.pa });\n      if (l.reading) for (const s of l.reading) out.push({ kind: \"concept-reading\", text: s });\n    }\n  }\n  // De-dup by text — many words appear across lessons\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  return out.filter((c) => {\n    if (seen.has(c.text)) return false;\n    seen.add(c.text);\n    return true;\n  });\n}\n\nasync function ensureClip(text: string): Promise<{\n  status: \"cached\" | \"synthed\" | \"failed\";\n  bytes?: number;\n  err?: string;\n}> {\n  try {\n    if (await audioCacheHas(VOICE_NAME, text)) {\n      return { status: \"cached\" };\n    }\n    const mp3 = await synthesize(text);\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text, mp3);\n    return { status: \"synthed\", bytes: mp3.length };\n  } catch (err) {\n    return {\n      status: \"failed\",\n      err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),\n    };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const clips = collectClips();\n  console.log(`Synthing ${clips.length} unique clips from curriculum\\n`);\n\n  let cached = 0, synthed = 0, failed = 0;\n  const conc = 2; // stay under GCP per-minute quota\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker(id: number) {\n    while (cursor < clips.length) {\n      const i = cursor++;\n      const c = clips[i];\n      const r = await ensureClip(c.text);\n      if (r.status === \"cached\") {\n        cached++;\n        if ((i + 1) % 25 === 0)\n          console.log(`  [${i + 1}/${clips.length}] (mostly cached)`);\n      } else if (r.status === \"synthed\") {\n        synthed++;\n        console.log(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${clips.length}] synthed ${c.kind.padEnd(16)} ${c.text} → ${r.bytes}B`);\n      } else {\n        failed++;\n        console.warn(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${clips.length}] FAILED ${c.kind} ${c.text}: ${r.err}`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: conc }, (_, i) => worker(i + 1)));\n  console.log(`\\ncached=${cached} synthed=${synthed} failed=${failed}`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}
