## Updated MVP Pro — £8/mo or £80/yr

- All 50+ processed sakhis
- **Remaining 8 matras + diacritics + stories + glossary** (the rest of the alphabet curriculum)
- Daily SRS review session
- Custom decks
- Audio downloads (PWA offline cache)
- Deck analytics

## What about the 5 free sakhis if matras are paid?

Important consequence: someone who uses *only* the free tier (just letters, no matras) can't actually read those 5 sakhis from scratch — they don't know the vowel signs. Two ways to handle:

**A. Generous hover lookup as the bridge.** The hover popover already shows romanization + meaning for every word. So a learner who knows letters but not matras can still navigate a sakhi by hover-translating each word. They don't fully decode it, but they understand it. This is genuinely useful and might be enough for many heritage learners.

**B. Pick the 5 free sakhis carefully.** We curate 5 that are short, narratively rich, and have the most consistent vocabulary — so the hover-only experience feels rewarding even without full reading skill. The other 400+ are gated.

I'd do both. The 5 freebies are the "fall in love with reading even before you can read" moment.

## Bottom line

You were right. **Gate the second half of the alphabet behind Pro.** Free becomes "letters + a taste of vowel signs + 5 sakhis with hover help" — a real product, but with an obvious upgrade path to "actually read Punjabi."

Two genuinely important questions. Let me answer each properly.

## How we gather metrics

### Recommended stack

| Tool | What it does | Cost | Why this one |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PostHog** (cloud free tier) | Product analytics — events, funnels, retention cohorts, session replay | Free up to 1M events/mo | Open-source, self-hostable if we ever care, excellent free tier, GDPR-friendly defaults |
| **Sentry** | Errors + performance monitoring | Free up to 5k errors/mo | Industry standard, catches the bugs we don't catch |
| **Stripe** | Revenue, MRR, churn, refunds | Free (built-in dashboard) | Already in the plan |
| **Supabase logs** | DB query slowness, auth errors | Free | Already in the plan |
| **First-party events table** in Supabase | The 10–20 business-critical events we always want to query ourselves | Pennies | Lets us write SQL against our own data without depending on a third-party |

**Don't add Google Analytics.** GA4 is bloated, tracks more than we need, makes us look like every other surveillance-ad-tech site, and we'd be hated by privacy-conscious heritage learners (who, anecdotally, are getting more wary every year).

### The events that actually matter

Don't track everything. ~20 events tell you everything:

**Acquisition**
- `page_viewed` (with referrer + path)
- `signup_started` / `signup_completed` (with source)

**Activation** — *did they "get it" in first session?*
- `first_alphabet_lesson_completed`
- `first_sakhi_opened`
- `first_word_saved`
- `first_audio_played`

**Engagement** — *do they come back?*
- `lesson_completed` (which lesson, time spent)
- `sakhi_completed` (which sakhi)
- `srs_review_session_finished` (cards reviewed, accuracy)
- `audio_played` (rough engagement proxy)
- `streak_milestone_hit` (7-day, 30-day, etc.)

**Monetization**
- `paywall_seen` (which paywall — alphabet matra vs sakhi 6 vs deck review)
- `pricing_page_viewed`
- `checkout_started` / `checkout_completed`
- `trial_started` / `trial_converted` / `trial_canceled`
- `subscription_canceled` (with optional reason)

**Drop-off** — *where do they leave?*
- `session_ended` (auto)
- `alphabet_abandoned_at_lesson_N`
- `sakhi_abandoned_at_paragraph_N`

That's the whole list. PostHog handles all of it via a single `posthog.capture()` call.

### What we actually do with the data

The metrics question only matters if we *use* the data. Realistic cadence:

- **Weekly review** (15 min, every Monday): funnel from signup → first sakhi → save → review → paywall → checkout. Look for the biggest drop-off; that's next week's priority.
- **Monthly cohort review**: are day-30 retention numbers improving as we ship features?
- **Per-feature ship**: define one metric before shipping. "If this AI-marking feature is working, the percentage of GCSE-tier trial users who convert should rise from X% to Y%." If it doesn't, kill the feature.

The temptation is to track everything and analyse none of it. Resist that.

---

## How we don't appear scammy

This is genuinely more important than the metrics question, and the things below are decisions we should commit to in writing now — not figure out later.

### Where scammy comes from

Apps feel scammy because of specific dark patterns:

1. **"Free trial" that requires a credit card with hidden auto-renewal**
2. **"Cancellation" flows that take 7 clicks with manipulative copy** ("Are you SURE? You'll lose your streak!")
3. **Fake urgency** ("50% off — 48 hours only!" when the price is always that)
4. **Aggressive paywalls** popping up every 30 seconds mid-lesson
5. **Selling user data** to third parties
6. **Email spam** after signup
7. **Push notification harassment** ("You've abandoned your streak! Come back!")
8. **Bait-and-switch** (free becomes paid after content addiction)
9. **Hidden costs / surprise charges**

### Concrete commitments akhar makes

**On free trials and pricing:**
- **Free tier without sign-up wall** — you can try the alphabet curriculum first 3 lessons without an account. Sign-up is for saving progress, not for evaluation.
- **Free trial without credit card** when possible. Industry says we lose 22% conversion vs requiring card; we accept that for trust.
- **One pricing page, all tiers visible, monthly and annual side by side.** No "contact us for pricing." No bundles requiring 3-year commitments.
- **Annual plans clearly marked as annual** with renewal date shown at every billing event.
- **Email 7 days before renewal** for annual plans so nobody is surprised.
- **No fake-urgency anywhere.** No "limited time offers" unless they're actually limited time. No countdown timers.

**On cancellation:**
- **One-click cancel from account settings.** No "are you sure?" loops with retention copy.
- **Refunds within 14 days for any reason.** UK law requires this for digital products bought online (Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013). Be visible about it.
- **Data export on cancel** — they can take their saved words + reading history with them in JSON or CSV.

**On notifications:**
- **All notifications opt-in.** Default OFF after signup; user chooses what they want.
- **Configurable times.** Heritage parents reading at 8pm not 8am.
- **Max one email per week** as marketing. Transactional emails (receipts, password resets) excepted.
- **No guilt-trip notifications.** No "You've abandoned your streak!" — just "Your daily review is ready when you are."

**On privacy:**
- **GDPR-compliant** by default — cookie consent that actually works, data deletion on request honoured within 30 days.
- **No selling data to third parties.** Ever. State it prominently.
- **No third-party trackers** beyond PostHog (privacy-friendly) and Sentry (error tracking only). No Facebook Pixel, no Google Ads, no TikTok.
- **Cookie banner** with a real "Reject all" button (not buried).

**On trust signals:**
- **Real "About" page** with the founders' names and faces. Sumeet Saini, who built this because his own kids deserved better. Honesty is the moat.
- **Public changelog** showing what we shipped each week.
- **Public roadmap** so users can see what's coming and vote.
- **Open-source core** consideration — the alphabet curriculum data + the sakhi reader UI could plausibly be open source. Builds trust + lets the community contribute corrections.
- **Real customer support** — a `hello@akhar.io` that a human replies to within 24 hours.
- **A "Sikh community statement"** addressing the elephant in the room: "We are not a religious organisation. We're not affiliated with any Gurdwara, school, or Sikh institution. We built this because the diaspora needs better tools. We treat the sakhi content with respect: we don't paywall reading the texts themselves — we charge for engineering features (cross-device, audio downloads, SRS, AI marking). The texts are our shared cultural inheritance."

### The specific worry for a Punjabi/Sikh learning product

The diaspora community is tight-knit and reputation spreads fast — in Gurdwara WhatsApp groups, in supplementary-school staff rooms, on Sikh subreddits. **One scammy interaction will sink us within weeks.** One genuinely good interaction will get us recommended for years.

This means the right strategy is **be visibly more ethical than we need to be**, not "ethical enough." The cost of going slow and trustworthy is paid in conversion percentages. The cost of going fast and scammy is paid in total addressable market we can never reach.

### What's NOT scammy

To be clear, none of these are scammy and we shouldn't worry about them:

- **Charging £8/mo** for a quality product is not scammy. It's fair value.
- **Paywalling content behind a tier** is not scammy if the tier is clearly priced and the gate is visible upfront.
- **Marketing the product** via email/social is not scammy if frequency is reasonable.
- **Asking for reviews** in-app after a positive moment is not scammy.
- **A/B testing** copy or pricing is not scammy (but be ethical: don't test dark patterns).
- **Showing "X people signed up this week"** is not scammy if it's true.

Yes, all of it works on mobile — but there are some specific mobile considerations worth knowing upfront.

## Metrics: clean carryover

**PostHog** has a JavaScript SDK that runs natively inside Capacitor's WebView. Since our Capacitor app is essentially the web app wrapped in a native shell, **the same `posthog.capture()` calls fire on web and mobile** — no separate tracking code, no two-code-paths-to-maintain problem.

Better still: because users sign in with the same Supabase Auth on web and mobile, **events from both surfaces attribute to the same user.** A user who reads sakhi 1 on mobile and saves a word on web shows up in PostHog as one journey. This is the cleanest possible setup.

**Sentry** works the same way — JS SDK in WebView covers everything we care about. There's an additional Capacitor-native Sentry plugin for catching crashes that happen at the native shell level (rare but worth having for the store submission).

**Mobile-specific events** to add on top of the web event list:
- `app_installed` (first launch detection)
- `push_notification_permission_granted`
- `push_notification_opened` (tracks re-engagement)
- `offline_mode_used` (did they read while no internet?)
- `native_share_used` (system share sheet — "share this sakhi to WhatsApp")
- `app_store_review_prompted` / `_completed`

PostHog handles all these via the same JS SDK calls.

## Stripe + the 30% problem

Here's the wrinkle nobody warns you about: **Apple and Google take 30% of any digital subscription purchased through their in-app billing systems.** It drops to 15% in year 2, or 15% from day one if you're under $1M/yr revenue, but it's still significant compared to Stripe's ~3%.

Three ways to handle it:

### Option A: Web-only purchases (recommended for launch)

- Mobile app: free tier fully usable, sign-in works
- "Upgrade to Pro" button → opens system browser → `akhar.io/pricing` → Stripe Checkout → user pays via Stripe → returns to app, now logged in as Pro
- **Cost: 3% to Stripe, 0% to Apple/Google**
- **Cost: ~10-15% conversion friction** (some users abandon at the browser handoff)

This is what Spotify, Netflix, YouTube, and the Kindle app all do. Apple's 2026 rules (post-*Epic v Apple* ruling) explicitly allow linking out to external purchase pages with disclosure copy. We're allowed.

### Option B: Native In-App Purchase (IAP)

- Pro/GCSE subs purchasable inside the mobile app via Apple/Google billing
- Smoother UX, much higher mobile conversion
- **Cost: 30% (year 1) / 15% (year 2+) to Apple/Google**
- Need to keep Stripe for web purchases simultaneously
- Sub state has to be synced between Stripe + RevenueCat (or equivalent) + Supabase — annoying but standard

### Option C: Hybrid (probably year-2 move)

- Free tier: full access on web + mobile
- Pro purchase: both options available
  - Default CTA → web checkout (cheaper for us)
  - Secondary "Subscribe in App" button → IAP (smoother for them)

### My recommendation

**Launch with Option A (web-only).** Reasons:
- Heritage parents researching a £8/mo subscription will use a laptop anyway, not a phone
- The 30% Apple tax on a £8/mo sub = £2.88 lost per user per month. At our small scale that compounds fast
- Avoids the engineering complexity of RevenueCat/IAP wiring at MVP stage
- Can add IAP later when we have data showing how many mobile users would have converted with a native flow

Switch to Option C in year 2 if metrics show mobile users dropping off at the browser handoff.

## Trust principles: identical, with mobile-specific additions

All the not-scammy commitments carry over. **Plus** the app stores impose their own compliance requirements:

### iOS App Store

- **Privacy nutrition labels** (mandatory) — explicit declaration of what data you collect, linked to your privacy policy. PostHog events fall under "Usage Data" and "Diagnostics."
- **Sign in with Apple** (required) if you offer any other auth method. We use magic links → we must add Sign in with Apple. Apple gives users an option to hide their real email; we honour the relay.
- **App Tracking Transparency (ATT)** if we ever track users across other apps/websites. PostHog by default doesn't do this — we're fine.
- **No bait-and-switch on subscriptions** — pricing must be clear in the app, charges must match what's displayed, renewals must be honoured per Apple's rules.

### Google Play Store

- **Data safety section** — equivalent to Apple's privacy labels. Same declarations.
- **Refund policy** — clearly disclosed.
- **No deceptive ads** — same standard as everywhere.

### What this means in practice

Three additions to the trust commitments doc, just for mobile:

1. **Add Sign in with Apple** alongside email magic links, before iOS submission
2. **Privacy nutrition labels match privacy policy match PostHog reality** — these three documents stay in sync, audited at every release
3. **Push notifications strictly opt-in** with system prompt — never request permission until the user has already decided they want them (after they enable "daily review reminder" in settings, for example, not at first launch)

## Updated takeaway

Yes, our analytics + trust stack works on mobile with minimal extra work. The one real decision is **payment routing**: web-only Stripe (cheap, lower mobile conversion) vs native IAP (expensive, higher conversion). Launch with web-only, layer IAP in when data justifies it.

The one thing to **do early** that I haven't called out: **submit to App Store + Play Store sooner than you think**. Approval can take 1-2 weeks the first time; subsequent updates are usually <24h. If we want the apps live on launch day, we need to start the submission cycle ~3 weeks before. Capacitor wrap + minimal native features (push notifications, native share, Sign in with Apple) is enough for first approval.

Find the biggest drop-off; that\n  becomes next week's priority.\n- **Monthly cohort review**: are day-30 retention numbers improving as\n  we ship features?\n- **Per-feature ship**: define ONE success metric before shipping. If it\n  doesn't move, the feature is killed.\n\nThe temptation is to track everything and analyse none of it. Set a\nweekly calendar reminder; the metrics matter only if we use them.\n\n---\n\n## Payment routing: web vs mobile\n\nThe unavoidable wrinkle. Apple and Google take **30% of in-app digital\nsubscriptions** (15% in year 2 or for small businesses), vs Stripe's\n~3% for web purchases. Three options:\n\n### Option A: Web-only purchases (Recommended for launch)\n- Mobile app: free tier fully usable, sign-in works\n- \"Upgrade to Pro\" → opens system browser → `akhar.io/pricing` → Stripe\n  Checkout → returns to app, now Pro\n- **Cost:** ~3% Stripe fees\n- **Friction:** ~10–15% mobile conversion drop at browser handoff\n- **Used by:** Spotify, Netflix, YouTube, Kindle\n\n### Option B: Native IAP everywhere\n- Subscribe inside the app via Apple/Google billing\n- Smoother UX\n- **Cost:** 30% (year 1) / 15% (year 2+)\n- **Infra:** add RevenueCat or equivalent to keep Stripe + IAP +\n  Supabase subscription state in sync\n\n### Option C: Hybrid (likely year-2 move)\n- Free tier same everywhere\n- Pro purchase: web checkout (default) + IAP as secondary in-app option\n- Data-driven: deploy only if metrics show mobile users dropping off at\n  the browser handoff\n\n**Launch decision: Option A.** Heritage parents researching £8/mo\nsubscriptions tend to be on laptops anyway. Avoid the 30% tax at MVP.\nRevisit at first signs of friction.\n\n---\n\n## Trust commitments\n\nThe default that scammy apps have, that we won't.\n\n### Free tier and trials\n- **Free experience without a sign-up wall** for the first lesson — you\n  can try the alphabet curriculum's first 3 lessons before any account is\n  required. Sign-up is for saving progress, not for evaluation.\n- **Free trials of paid tiers don't require a credit card.** Industry\n  benchmark is 22% trial→paid loss vs requiring a card; we accept it.\n- **One pricing page, all tiers visible, monthly + annual side by\n  side.** No \"contact us for pricing,\" no enterprise mystery bundle.\n\n### Renewals and cancellation\n- **Annual plans clearly labelled as annual** with the next renewal date\n  shown in account settings and on every billing email.\n- **Renewal reminder email 7 days before charge** for annual plans.\n- **One-click cancel from account settings.** No \"are you sure\" loops.\n  No retention copy designed to manipulate.\n- **14-day refund for any reason** on any first-time purchase. UK\n  Consumer Contracts Regulations require this for digital products\n  bought online; we surface it visibly.\n- **Data export on cancel.** Users can download saved words, reading\n  history, and SRS data in JSON or CSV. Their learning belongs to them.\n\n### Notifications\n- **All notifications opt-in.** Default OFF after signup; user picks\n  what they want, when.\n- **Configurable times.** Heritage parents reading at 8pm not 8am.\n- **Maximum one marketing email per week.** Transactional emails\n  (receipts, password resets, renewal warnings) excepted.\n- **No guilt-trip copy.** \"Your daily review is ready when you are\" —\n  not \"You've abandoned your streak!\"\n- **Push notifications, where supported, follow the same rules.**\n  Opt-in only, configurable, no urgency manipulation.\n\n### Privacy\n- **GDPR + UK GDPR compliant by default.** Real cookie consent with a\n  visible \"Reject all\" button (not buried). Data deletion on request\n  honoured within 30 days.\n- **No selling user data to anyone.** Stated prominently in privacy\n  policy.\n- **No third-party trackers** beyond PostHog (privacy-friendly) and\n  Sentry (error tracking only). No Facebook Pixel, no Google Ads\n  conversion tracking, no TikTok pixel.\n- **PostHog configured for privacy**: no autocapture of form contents,\n  no session replay for free users, IP addresses anonymised, EU data\n  residency.\n- **Privacy policy that reads like a human wrote it.** No 14-page\n  legalese; a short, honest document.\n\n### Pricing fairness\n- **No fake urgency.** No \"48 hours left at 50% off!\" when the price is\n  always that. No countdown timers designed to pressure.\n- **Same price for everyone.** No price tests where unlucky users pay\n  more. (A/B testing UI copy is fine; A/B testing the price someone is\n  charged is not.)\n- **Annual discount is real and stable.** £80/yr vs £8/mo = 16% off.\n  Always available.\n- **Student discount (50%) on GCSE/A-Level tiers** with proof of\n  enrolment, applied transparently.\n\n### Identity and accountability\n- **Real \"About\" page** with founder names and faces. People want to\n  know who built this.\n- **Real customer support inbox** (`hello@akhar.io`) checked daily by\n  a human, responses within 24 hours.\n- **In-app feedback widget** so issues can be reported without leaving\n  the app.\n- **Public changelog** showing what shipped each week.\n- **Public roadmap** so users can see what's coming.\n- **Sikh community statement** addressing the cultural sensitivity:\n  > akhar is not a religious organisation and is not affiliated with\n  > any Gurdwara, school, or Sikh institution. We built it because the\n  > diaspora needs better tools. We treat the sakhi content with\n  > respect: reading the texts is always free. We charge for\n  > engineering features — cross-device sync, audio downloads, SRS\n  > review, AI marking. The texts themselves are our shared cultural\n  > inheritance and are never gated.\n\n### Specific mobile additions (App Store / Play Store)\n\nMobile compliance is partly about not being scammy and partly about\nsatisfying Apple and Google's rules.\n\n- **Sign in with Apple** alongside any other auth method (Apple\n  requires this on iOS if you offer other social/email sign-in). Honour\n  the \"hide my real email\" relay.\n- **iOS Privacy Nutrition Labels** must match our actual data\n  collection. PostHog events go under \"Usage Data\" + \"Diagnostics\".\n  Audited at every App Store submission.\n- **Android Data Safety** declarations same as above.\n- **App Tracking Transparency (iOS):** we don't track across apps —\n  declare it accurately, don't trigger the ATT prompt unnecessarily.\n- **Push notification permission requested late.** Never on first\n  launch. Only after the user has explicitly enabled a notification\n  type (\"daily review reminder\") in settings.\n- **No deceptive ads inside the app.** Easy because we don't show ads.\n- **Submission cadence:** start the App Store / Play Store review\n  pipeline 3 weeks before any intended public launch. First reviews\n  take 1–2 weeks; subsequent updates are usually under 24 hours.\n\n---\n\n## What \"not scammy\" doesn't mean\n\nTo be clear, none of these are scammy and we shouldn't worry about them:\n\n- **Charging £8/mo** for a quality product. Fair value.\n- **Paywalling content behind a tier.** Fine if the tier is clearly\n  priced and the gate is visible upfront.\n- **Marketing via email and social.** Fine at reasonable frequency.\n- **Asking for an in-app review** after a positive moment (completed\n  sakhi, finished review session). Apple's `SKStoreReviewController`\n  and Google's similar APIs are designed for this.\n- **A/B testing copy, layout, paywall positioning.** Fine as long as\n  we don't A/B test the *price* someone is charged.\n- **Showing real social proof** (\"X people learning Punjabi with akhar\n  this week\") if it's true.\n\n---\n\n## Why this matters for our specific audience\n\nThe Punjabi diaspora is tight-knit. Reputation moves through Gurdwara\nWhatsApp groups, supplementary-school staff rooms, Sikh subreddits, and\nInstagram comment sections — fast.\n\n**One scammy interaction sinks us within weeks.** One genuinely good\ninteraction gets us recommended for years.\n\nThe right strategy is **be visibly more ethical than we strictly need\nto be**, not \"ethical enough to avoid getting in trouble.\" The cost of\nslow + trustworthy is paid in conversion percentages. The cost of fast\n+ scammy is paid in total addressable market we can never reach.\n\n---\n\n## See also\n\n- [mvp.md](./mvp.md) — what we're building first\n- [tiers.md](./tiers.md) — pricing and gating\n- [build-order.md](./build-order.md) — full feature sequence\n- [market-research.md](./market-research.md) — the competitive context\n"

Docs pushed. Now the auth question — which is the foundational decision blocking the MVP build.

## Why magic links are wrong for mobile

You're right to flag this. Magic links have a known mobile UX failure mode:

1. User taps "Sign in" in the mobile app
2. Types email, taps Send
3. **Switches to their email app** (this is the killer step)
4. Finds the email, taps the link
5. The link opens **either** the akhar mobile app via deep linking (good, IF correctly configured) **or** Safari/Chrome (bad — confused user is now in a browser, not the app, has no idea where their "logged in" session went)
6. Industry data on this: ~30–40% drop-off between "magic link sent" and "user actually logged in" on mobile

Plus: **App Store requires Sign in with Apple** as soon as we offer any other auth method, so we're adding that regardless.

## My recommended replacement

Three options, all natively supported by Supabase Auth, no passwords anywhere:

| Method | UX | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| **Sign in with Apple** | 1 tap, Face ID confirms, done | Default on iOS. Required by App Store anyway. |
| **Sign in with Google** | 1 tap, Google sheet confirms, done | Default on Android. Almost every heritage user has a Google account. |
| **Email + 6-digit OTP code** | Type email → get code in email → type code in app | Fallback for users who don't want social sign-in. No email-to-app handoff because the code is typed in the app. |

No passwords. No magic links. All three work identically on web and mobile.

**Order on the sign-in screen** (matters for conversion):
- Big "Continue with Apple" button (on iOS / macOS users this is one tap, biggest delight)
- Big "Continue with Google" button (works everywhere)
- Smaller "Use email instead →" text link → reveals email + OTP flow
- No "create account" vs "sign in" split — same flow for both (Supabase auto-creates on first OTP/social)

This is the same auth pattern Linear, Vercel, Cal.com, and Notion all converged on. It's the modern default.

## The migration

Existing magic-link users: they're stored in Supabase Auth by email. When they sign in with Apple/Google using the same email address, Supabase auto-links the accounts. Their existing data carries over. No data migration needed.

The only change is the UI on `/login` (replace email form with the three buttons) and the `signInWithOtp` server action (replace with `signInWithIdToken` for social + `signInWithOtp` with `type: 'email'` for OTP code instead of magic link).

## Sumeet's action items before I start coding

A few things have lead time outside our control — start these in parallel with my work:

1. **Apple Developer Program enrollment** ($99/yr) — takes 1–7 days for identity verification. **Required for Sign in with Apple** AND for App Store submission. Start this today.
2. **Google Cloud Console: enable Google Sign-In** for the akhar project — already have a GCP project for Vision OCR + TTS, just need to add OAuth credentials. ~10 min.
3. **Apple Developer Console: create Sign in with Apple service ID** — once Apple Dev account is approved.
4. **Supabase: enable Apple + Google providers** in Authentication → Providers tab. Paste the credentials from steps 2 + 3.

Once those four things are done, I can wire up the new auth in the codebase (probably ~2 hours of work).

## Ready to start?

If you're happy with the three-button auth (Apple + Google + OTP), I'll:
1. Start the Apple Dev enrollment guidance (tell you exactly what to click)
2. Walk you through enabling Google OAuth in GCP
3. Wait for those creds, then refactor `/login` + auth callback

If you want to discuss the auth flow more first (e.g. should we add Sign in with Email-OTP first then layer Apple/Google later? Should we skip OTP entirely? etc.) — tell me and we'll adjust.

### 2. Google OAuth credentials (~10 min)

Already have a GCP project from the Vision OCR / Chirp 3 TTS work (`lipi-497808`). Just add OAuth:

1. Go to **https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials?project=lipi-497808**
2. Click **"+ Create Credentials" → "OAuth client ID"**
3. If prompted to configure consent screen first:
   - App name: `akhar`
   - User support email: `hello@akhar.io`

   - Authorised domains: `akhar.io`, `supabase.co`
   - Developer email: your email
   - Save
4. Back at Create OAuth client ID:

   - Create
5. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** that appear in the popup. Paste both back to me.

### 3. Switch the Supabase OTP email template to send codes (not links)

By default Supabase sends a magic link. To get a 6-digit code instead:

1. **Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Email Templates → Magic Link**
2. Replace the template body with:
   ```
   <h2>Your akhar sign-in code</h2>
   <p>Your sign-in code is:</p>
   <h1 style="font-family: monospace; letter-spacing: 8px;">{{ .Token }}</h1>
   <p>This code expires in 1 hour.</p>
   <p>If you didn't request this, you can safely ignore this email.</p>
   ```
3. Subject line: `Your akhar sign-in code: {{ .Token }}`
4. Save

The `{{ .Token }}` placeholder is the 6-digit code Supabase generates. Without changing this template, the email contains a link instead of a code.

### 4. Once you have Google credentials, enable the provider in Supabase

1. **Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Providers → Google**
2. Enable
3. Paste Client ID + Client Secret from step 2
4. Save

(Apple provider enablement comes later, after step 1 completes.)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/login/actions.ts",
  "content": "\"use server\";\n\n// Auth server actions. Three flows, all passwordless:\n//   - Sign in with Apple (OAuth)     — required on iOS App Store\n//   - Sign in with Google (OAuth)    — most heritage users have a Google acct\n//   - Email + 6-digit OTP code       — fallback, replaces magic link\n//\n// Email OTP replaces the previous magic-link approach because magic links\n// have a known mobile UX failure mode: the user types email → switches to\n// their email app → clicks link → it opens in a browser instead of the\n// app. OTP codes are typed directly back into the app, no handoff.\n//\n// Requires the Supabase Magic Link email template to be configured with\n// `{{ .Token }}` (which sends the 6-digit code) instead of\n// `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` (which sends a link). See docs/mvp.md.\n\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\n\nfunction originFromHeaders(h: Headers): string {\n  const proto = h.get(\"x-forwarded-proto\") ?? \"https\";\n  const host = h.get(\"host\") ?? \"localhost:3000\";\n  return `${proto}://${host}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Step 1 of email OTP: trigger Supabase to send a 6-digit code.\n * Redirects to /login/verify so the user can enter the code.\n */\nexport async function sendOtp(formData: FormData) {\n  const email = String(formData.get(\"email\") ?? \"\").trim().toLowerCase();\n  const next = String(formData.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\");\n  if (!email || !email.includes(\"@\")) {\n    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(\"Enter a valid email\")}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`);\n  }\n\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  // shouldCreateUser=true so first-time sign-in also signs up — same flow\n  // for both, no separate \"register\" path.\n  const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n    email,\n    options: { shouldCreateUser: true },\n  });\n  if (error) {\n    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`);\n  }\n  redirect(\n    `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Step 2 of email OTP: verify the 6-digit code the user types.\n * On success, Supabase sets the session cookies and we redirect to `next`.\n */\nexport async function verifyOtp(formData: FormData) {\n  const email = String(formData.get(\"email\") ?? \"\").trim().toLowerCase();\n  const token = String(formData.get(\"token\") ?? \"\").trim();\n  const next = String(formData.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\");\n  if (!email || !token) {\n    redirect(\n      `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&error=${encodeURIComponent(\"Enter the 6-digit code\")}`,\n    );\n  }\n\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n    email,\n    token,\n    type: \"email\",\n  });\n  if (error) {\n    redirect(\n      `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`,\n    );\n  }\n  redirect(next);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resend the OTP code if the user requests a new one (e.g. it didn't\n * arrive, expired). Same as sendOtp but stays on the verify page.\n */\nexport async function resendOtp(formData: FormData) {\n  const email = String(formData.get(\"email\") ?? \"\").trim().toLowerCase();\n  const next = String(formData.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\");\n  if (!email) return;\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n    email,\n    options: { shouldCreateUser: true },\n  });\n  redirect(\n    `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&resent=1`,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Initiate OAuth with a social provider (Apple or Google). Supabase\n * handles the redirect dance — we ask it for the provider's auth URL and\n * send the user there. The provider sends them to Supabase, which sends\n * them back to /auth/callback with a code, which we exchange for a session.\n */\nexport async function signInWithProvider(formData: FormData) {\n  const provider = String(formData.get(\"provider\") ?? \"\") as \"google\" | \"apple\";\n  const next = String(formData.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\");\n  if (provider !== \"google\" && provider !== \"apple\") {\n    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(\"Unknown sign-in provider\")}`);\n  }\n\n  const h = await headers();\n  const origin = originFromHeaders(h);\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({\n    provider,\n    options: {\n      redirectTo: `${origin}/auth/callback?next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,\n    },\n  });\n  if (error || !data?.url) {\n    redirect(\n      `/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error?.message ?? \"OAuth init failed\")}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,\n    );\n  }\n  redirect(data.url);\n}\n\nexport async function signOut() {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  await supabase.auth.signOut();\n  redirect(\"/\");\n}\n"
}

Renders as a real <form> with hidden inputs so\n// it's a Server Action submission, not a client-side fetch — which means\n// it works even with JS disabled and avoids client-side OAuth state\n// management entirely.\n//\n// Branding follows each provider's published guidelines:\n//   Apple:  black background, white text, Apple logo on dark\n//   Google: white background, dark text, multicolour Google \"G\"\nimport { APPLE_LOGO_SVG, GOOGLE_LOGO_SVG } from \"./provider-logos\";\n\ntype Provider = \"apple\" | \"google\";\n\nconst STYLES: Record<Provider, { wrap: string; label: string }> = {\n  apple: {\n    wrap: \"bg-black text-white hover:bg-zinc-800 dark:bg-white dark:text-black dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\",\n    label: \"Continue with Apple\",\n  },\n  google: {\n    wrap: \"bg-white text-zinc-900 border border-zinc-300 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\",\n    label: \"Continue with Google\",\n  },\n};\n\nexport default function ProviderButton({\n  provider,\n  next,\n  action,\n}: {\n  provider: Provider;\n  next: string;\n  action: (formData: FormData) => Promise<void>;\n}) {\n  const styles = STYLES[provider];\n  return (\n    <form action={action}>\n      <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"provider\" value={provider} />\n      <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"next\" value={next} />\n      <button\n        type=\"submit\"\n        className={`flex w-full items-center justify-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-4 py-2.5 font-medium transition ${styles.wrap}`}\n      >\n        <span\n          className=\"inline-flex h-5 w-5 items-center justify-center\"\n          aria-hidden\n          dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{\n            __html: provider === \"apple\" ? APPLE_LOGO_SVG : GOOGLE_LOGO_SVG,\n          }}\n        />\n        <span>{styles.label}</span>\n      </button>\n    </form>\n  );\n}\n"

1	// Magic-link landing page. Supabase redirects the user here after they click
2	// the link in their email. We exchange the `code` query param for a real
3	// session (sets the auth cookies) and then send them to wherever they were
4	// trying to go (?next=).
5	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
6	import { serverClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
7	
8	export async function GET(request: Request) {
9	  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);
10	  const code = searchParams.get("code");
11	  const next = searchParams.get("next") ?? "/";
12	
13	  if (!code) {
14	    return NextResponse.redirect(
15	      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent("Missing code in callback URL")}`,
16	    );
17	  }
18	
19	  const supabase = await serverClient();
20	  const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);
21	  if (error) {
22	    return NextResponse.redirect(
23	      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`,
24	    );
25	  }
26	  return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}${next}`);
27	}
28

11	
12	const PUBLIC_PATHS = new Set(["/", "/login"]);
13	const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ["/auth/", "/api/"];
14	
15	function isPublic(pathname: string): boolean {
16	  if (PUBLIC_PATHS.has(pathname)) return true;
17	  return PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p));
18	}

20	export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
21	  let response = NextResponse.next({ request });
22	  const supabase = createServerClient(
23	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
24	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,
25	    {
26	      cookies: {
27	        getAll() {
28	          return request.cookies.getAll();
29	        },
30	        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
31	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>
32	            request.cookies.set(name, value),
33	          );
34	          response = NextResponse.next({ request });
35	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
36	            response.cookies.set(name, value, options),
37	          );
38	        },
39	      },
40	    },
41	  );
42	  // Touching getUser() triggers the auto-refresh of cookies if needed.
43	  const {
44	    data: { user },
45	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
46	
47	  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl;
48	  if (!user && !isPublic(pathname)) {
49	    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
50	    url.pathname = "/login";
51	    url.search = `?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname + search)}`;
52	    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
53	  }
54	
55	  return response;
56	}

> AGENT

That's a known-painful flow — Apple's enrollment system is notoriously brittle. The 403 on `submitIndividualEnrollment` plus the DNS resolution failure suggest something in your network or browser is interfering.

## Most likely causes (in order of likelihood)

### 1. iCloud Private Relay / VPN / browser extension blocking
The `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` is the telltale — something is intercepting Apple's DNS requests. Fix:
- **Turn off iCloud Private Relay** (Settings → Apple ID → iCloud → Private Relay → off)
- **Disable any VPN** (NordVPN, Cloudflare WARP, etc.)
- **Disable browser ad-blockers** (uBlock, Privacy Badger, Brave Shields)
- **Use Safari, not Chrome** — Apple's enrollment flow is most reliable in their own browser

### 2. 2FA not enabled on the Apple ID
Apple requires two-factor authentication on the Apple ID used for Developer Program enrollment. Without it, the submission silently 403s.

Check: **System Settings → Apple ID → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication** — must be **On**. If not, turn it on, sign out and back in, then retry enrollment.

### 3. Apple ID country/region mismatch with payment card
If your Apple ID region is set to one country and your card billing address is another, enrollment fails. Verify:
- Apple ID region: appleid.apple.com → Personal Information → Country/Region
- Card billing address country matches

### 4. If you picked "Organization" — D-U-N-S Number missing
Organization enrollment requires a D-U-N-S Number for Reliq Digital Ltd. If you don't have one, Apple's form 403s.

Fast workaround: **switch to Individual enrollment for now.** No D-U-N-S needed, approval is much faster (often same-day), and you can upgrade to Organization later inside the developer portal. The apps + revenue still go through correctly — the only difference is your name appears as the seller on the App Store instead of the company.

For akhar at this stage, **Individual is fine**. Switch to Organization once Reliq Digital is properly trading.

## My recommended retry sequence

1. Open **Safari** on macOS
2. Turn off iCloud Private Relay temporarily
3. Disable any VPN / browser extensions
4. Verify 2FA is on your Apple ID
5. Go to **https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/**
6. Pick **Individual** (not Organization)
7. Sign in with your Apple ID
8. Walk through the form, pay $99
9. Should submit successfully

If it 403s again from step 8: try from your phone hotspot instead of home WiFi (some ISPs / routers block parts of Apple's API).

## If it's STILL broken after all that

Call **Apple Developer Program Support: 0800 048 0408 (UK)** — they can manually push the enrollment through. Mention "403 on submitIndividualEnrollment endpoint" and they'll know exactly what's wrong. Phone wait is usually 5-15 min.

17	export default function HoverWord({ word, isActive, signedIn, onOpen, onClose }: Props) {
18	  const [morpheme, setMorpheme] = useState<Morpheme | null>(null);
19	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
20	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
21	  // "sticky" = popover was opened by click and should stay open until another
22	  // explicit close (click outside or click trigger again). Hover-opens are
23	  // not sticky and auto-close when the pointer leaves both trigger + popover.
24	  const [sticky, setSticky] = useState(false);
25	  const openTimer = useRef<number | null>(null);
26	  const closeTimer = useRef<number | null>(null);
27	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
28	
29	  useEffect(() => {
30	    if (!isActive || morpheme || loading) return;
31	    setLoading(true);
32	    setError(null);
33	    fetch(`/api/morpheme?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`)
34	      .then(async (r) => {
35	        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
36	        return r.json();
37	      })
38	      .then((m: Morpheme) => setMorpheme(m))
39	      .catch((e: unknown) => setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)))
40	      .finally(() => setLoading(false));
41	  }, [isActive, word, morpheme, loading]);
42	
43	  // Clear any in-flight timers when this component unmounts so we don't try
44	  // to open/close on a stale parent.
45	  useEffect(
46	    () => () => {
47	      if (openTimer.current) window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
48	      if (closeTimer.current) window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
49	    },
50	    [],
51	  );
52	
53	  function scheduleOpen() {
54	    if (closeTimer.current) {
55	      window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
56	      closeTimer.current = null;
57	    }
58	    if (isActive) return;
59	    openTimer.current = window.setTimeout(() => {
60	      onOpen();
61	      openTimer.current = null;
62	    }, HOVER_OPEN_MS);
63	  }
64	
65	  function scheduleClose() {
66	    if (sticky) return;
67	    if (openTimer.current) {
68	      window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
69	      openTimer.current = null;
70	    }
71	    if (!isActive) return;
72	    closeTimer.current = window.setTimeout(() => {
73	      onClose();
74	      closeTimer.current = null;
75	    }, HOVER_CLOSE_MS);
76	  }
77	
78	  function handleClick() {
79	    // Clicking pins (or unpins) the popover. If currently closed, open it
80	    // immediately and make it sticky; if open and sticky, unpin + close;
81	    // if open via hover (not sticky), just pin it.
82	    if (openTimer.current) {
83	      window.clearTimeout(openTimer.current);
84	      openTimer.current = null;
85	    }
86	    if (closeTimer.current) {
87	      window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
88	      closeTimer.current = null;
89	    }
90	    if (!isActive) {
91	      setSticky(true);
92	      onOpen();
93	    } else if (sticky) {
94	      setSticky(false);
95	      onClose();
96	    } else {
97	      setSticky(true);
98	    }
99	  }
100	
101	  // When the popover gets closed (e.g. by the parent because another word
102	  // was opened), reset sticky so the next interaction starts fresh AND
103	  // cancel any pending timers so they don't fire stale onClose/onOpen.
104	  useEffect(() => {
105	    if (!isActive) {
106	      if (sticky) setSticky(false);
107	      if (closeTimer.current) {
108	        window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
109	        closeTimer.current = null;
110	      }
111	    } else {
112	      // Becoming active cancels any in-flight close
113	      if (closeTimer.current) {
114	        window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
115	        closeTimer.current = null;
116	      }
117	    }
118	  }, [isActive, sticky]);
119	
120	  return (
121	    <span className="relative inline-block">
122	      <button
123	        ref={triggerRef}
124	        type="button"
125	        onClick={handleClick}
126	        onMouseEnter={scheduleOpen}
127	        onMouseLeave={scheduleClose}
128	        className={`cursor-pointer rounded transition-colors ${
129	          isActive
130	            ? "bg-amber-200 dark:bg-amber-900"
131	            : "hover:bg-amber-100 dark:hover:bg-amber-950"
132	        }`}
133	      >
134	        {word}
135	      </button>
136	      {isActive && (
137	        <MorphemePopover
138	          word={word}
139	          morpheme={morpheme}
140	          loading={loading}
141	          error={error}
142	          sticky={sticky}
143	          signedIn={signedIn}
144	          triggerEl={triggerRef.current}
145	          onClose={() => {
146	            setSticky(false);
147	            onClose();
148	          }}
149	          onHoverIn={() => {
150	            // Keep popover open while pointer is over it
151	            if (closeTimer.current) {
152	              window.clearTimeout(closeTimer.current);
153	              closeTimer.current = null;
154	            }
155	          }}
156	          onHoverOut={scheduleClose}
157	          onUpdate={(m) => setMorpheme(m)}
158	        />
159	      )}
160	    </span>
161	  );
162	}

1	"use client";

3	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
4	
5	// Plays a cached audio clip from /api/tts. Same as the popover/sentence
6	// speakers: HEADs the URL once, hides itself if no cache exists, plays
7	// the MP3 from R2 on tap.
8	export default function LetterAudio({
9	  text,
10	  label,
11	}: {
12	  text: string;
13	  label: string;
14	}) {
15	  const [available, setAvailable] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
16	  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);
17	  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);
18	  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`;
19	
20	  useEffect(() => {
21	    let cancelled = false;
22	    fetch(url, { method: "HEAD" })
23	      .then((r) => !cancelled && setAvailable(r.ok))
24	      .catch(() => !cancelled && setAvailable(false));
25	    return () => {
26	      cancelled = true;
27	    };
28	  }, [url]);
29	
30	  function play() {
31	    if (audioRef.current) {
32	      audioRef.current.pause();
33	      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;
34	    }
35	    const audio = new Audio(url);
36	    audioRef.current = audio;
37	    setPlaying(true);
38	    audio.onended = () => setPlaying(false);
39	    audio.onerror = () => setPlaying(false);
40	    audio.play().catch(() => setPlaying(false));
41	  }
42	
43	  if (available === false) return null;
44	  return (
45	    <button
46	      type="button"
47	      onClick={play}
48	      disabled={playing || available !== true}
49	      className="mt-4 inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-zinc-700 transition hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 disabled:opacity-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800"
50	    >
51	      <span>{playing ? "🔉" : "🔊"}</span>
52	      <span>{label}</span>
53	    </button>
54	  );
55	}
56

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/onboarding/actions.ts",
  "content": "\"use server\";\n\n// Save the onboarding answers and route the user to the right starting\n// place. Done in a Server Action so the redirect happens server-side\n// with the cookies already set — no flash of the wrong page.\n\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\n\ntype Goal = \"heritage\" | \"sakhi\" | \"gcse\" | \"curious\";\ntype PriorKnowledge = \"none\" | \"spoken\" | \"readable\";\n\n// Map (goal, prior_knowledge) → first page to land on.\n//\n// - readable + sakhi/heritage → straight into the library (they can\n//   already read; show them the value)\n// - none / spoken → /alphabet (they need the script foundation)\n// - gcse → /alphabet for now (no GCSE content yet; will swap to\n//   /learn/gcse when topic packs ship in MVP+1)\nfunction firstLandingPage(goal: Goal, prior: PriorKnowledge): string {\n  if (prior === \"readable\" && (goal === \"sakhi\" || goal === \"heritage\")) {\n    return \"/sakhi/1\";\n  }\n  return \"/alphabet\";\n}\n\nexport async function completeOnboarding(formData: FormData) {\n  const goal = String(formData.get(\"goal\") ?? \"\") as Goal;\n  const prior = String(formData.get(\"prior_knowledge\") ?? \"\") as PriorKnowledge;\n\n  // Validate against the CHECK constraints on the column.\n  const validGoals: Goal[] = [\"heritage\", \"sakhi\", \"gcse\", \"curious\"];\n  const validPrior: PriorKnowledge[] = [\"none\", \"spoken\", \"readable\"];\n  if (!validGoals.includes(goal) || !validPrior.includes(prior)) {\n    redirect(\"/onboarding?error=invalid\");\n  }\n\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) redirect(\"/login?next=/onboarding\");\n\n  const { error } = await supabase\n    .from(\"profiles\")\n    .update({\n      goal,\n      prior_knowledge: prior,\n      onboarding_completed_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n      updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n    })\n    .eq(\"user_id\", user.id);\n\n  if (error) {\n    // Database constraint violation or other failure — surface to user.\n    redirect(`/onboarding?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`);\n  }\n\n  redirect(firstLandingPage(goal, prior));\n}\n"
}

Skipped for the truly-public routes (so they\n  // can still see the landing page) and the onboarding page itself.\n  if (\n    user &&\n    !ONBOARDING_ALLOWED_PATHS.has(pathname) &&\n    !PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p))\n  ) {\n    const { data: profile } = await supabase\n      .from(\"profiles\")\n      .select(\"onboarding_completed_at\")\n      .eq(\"user_id\", user.id)\n      .maybeSingle();\n    if (!profile?.onboarding_completed_at) {\n      const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n      url.pathname = \"/onboarding\";\n      url.search = \"\";\n      return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n    }\n  }\n\n  return response;\n}"
}

Right, here's the exact step-by-step. Do them in order — each unblocks something.

---

## STEP 1: Supabase OTP email template (2 min) — biggest unblock

**This makes the email sign-in flow on dev preview actually work.**

1. Go to **https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/fsahapmiupwfljajyngw**
2. Left sidebar → **Authentication**
3. Left sub-sidebar (inside Authentication) → **Email Templates**
4. You'll see tabs: Confirm signup / Invite user / **Magic Link** / Change Email / Reset Password
5. Click the **Magic Link** tab
6. Find the **Subject heading** field. Replace whatever's there with:
   ```
   Your akhar sign-in code: {{ .Token }}
   ```
7. Find the **Message body (HTML)** field. **Replace the entire contents** with:
   ```html
   <h2>Your akhar sign-in code</h2>
   <p>Your sign-in code is:</p>
   <h1 style="font-family: monospace; letter-spacing: 8px;">{{ .Token }}</h1>
   <p>This code expires in 1 hour.</p>
   <p>If you didn't request this, you can safely ignore this email.</p>
   ```
8. Click **Save changes** (bottom of page)

**Verify it worked**: go to your Vercel preview URL → `/login` → type your email → click "Send 6-digit code" → check inbox. Should arrive with a 6-digit code (not a clickable link). Type it on the verify page → should sign you in.

If you get a link instead of a code, the template didn't save — try again.

---

## STEP 2: PostHog account (3 min) — unlocks me wiring analytics

1. Go to **https://eu.posthog.com/signup** (use **EU** region, not US — better for GDPR / your users)
2. Sign up with email or Google
3. When asked "Tell us about your project":
   - Product/website name: `akhar`
   - I want to track: pick **Web app**
4. After signup, you'll land on the dashboard. There's a "Get started" or "Install" page showing a code snippet — **don't run the snippet**, I'll do that.
5. Left sidebar → **Project settings** (cog icon at the bottom)
6. Find **Project API key** (starts with `phc_...`) and **copy it**
7. Paste it back to me here

(There's also a "Personal API key" — DO NOT share that. Just the Project API key.)

---

## STEP 3: Sentry account (3 min) — error tracking

1. Go to **https://sentry.io/signup/**
2. Sign up with email or Google
3. When asked which platform: pick **Next.js**
4. Project name: `akhar`
5. Region: **Europe (Frankfurt)** — again, GDPR-friendly for our users
6. After signup, Sentry shows you a "Configure Next.js" wizard. **Skip it / close it** — I'll handle the setup.
7. Left sidebar → **Settings → Projects → akhar → Client Keys (DSN)**
8. Copy the value labelled **DSN** (looks like `https://abc123@o12345.ingest.sentry.io/678901`)
9. Paste it back to me here

---

## STEP 4: Google OAuth credentials (10 min) — unlocks Google sign-in

### Part A: Configure OAuth consent screen (first time only)

1. Go to **https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials/consent?project=lipi-497808**
2. If prompted "User Type": pick **External** → Create
3. Fill in:
   - App name: `akhar`
   - User support email: your email (e.g. `sumeet@sumeetsaini.com`)
   - App logo: skip for now
   - **App domain section**:
     - Application home page: `https://akhar.io`
     - Application privacy policy: `https://akhar.io/privacy` (we'll create this page later — fine to put now)
     - Application terms of service: `https://akhar.io/terms` (same)
   - **Authorised domains**: add `akhar.io` and `supabase.co`
   - **Developer contact email**: your email
4. Click **Save and Continue**
5. **Scopes** page: scroll to bottom, click **Add or Remove Scopes**
   - Check boxes for: `userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`, `openid`
   - Click **Update**
6. Click **Save and Continue**
7. **Test users** page: add your own email so you can test before publishing → Save and Continue
8. **Summary**: review → click **Back to Dashboard**
9. On the consent screen page you're now on: click **Publish App** button (status changes from "Testing" to "In production"). Apple/Google will not approve our login flow if the consent screen is in test mode.

### Part B: Create the OAuth Client ID

1. Go to **https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials?project=lipi-497808**
2. Top of page: click **+ Create Credentials** → **OAuth client ID**
3. Application type: **Web application**
4. Name: `akhar Supabase Auth`
5. **Authorised JavaScript origins** — click "+ Add URI" for each:
   - `https://akhar.io`
   - `http://localhost:3000`
   - `https://fsahapmiupwfljajyngw.supabase.co`
6. **Authorised redirect URIs** — click "+ Add URI":
   - `https://fsahapmiupwfljajyngw.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`
   - (Just the one — Supabase handles the redirect to our app afterwards)
7. Click **Create**
8. A popup shows your **Client ID** (ends in `.apps.googleusercontent.com`) and **Client secret** (starts with `GOCSPX-`). **Copy both immediately** — the secret won't be shown again later.

### Part C: Enable Google provider in Supabase

1. Go to **https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/fsahapmiupwfljajyngw/auth/providers**
2. Find **Google** in the list → click the row to expand
3. Toggle **Enable Sign in with Google** to ON
4. Paste:
   - Client IDs (or **Client ID** field): the one ending in `.apps.googleusercontent.com`
   - Client Secret: the one starting with `GOCSPX-`
5. Leave "Skip nonce checks" unchecked
6. **Save**

**Verify**: go to dev preview `/login` → click "Continue with Google" → should redirect to Google's sign-in, then back to akhar signed in.

---

## STEP 5: Google Play Developer account ($25 one-time, ~24-48h approval)

1. Go to **https://play.google.com/console/signup**
2. Sign in with the Google account you want to use as developer (use a personal one — easy)
3. Choose **Yourself** (individual) as account type
4. Developer name: `Reliq Digital` (this is what shows on Play Store listings)
5. Contact details — your email, phone
6. Identity verification — they'll ask for a government ID (passport or driving licence photo). Have one ready.
7. Pay $25 with a card
8. Submit → wait for approval (usually 24-48h)

No further action until they approve. You'll get an email.

---

## STEP 6: Stripe account for sole trader (~30 min today, ~2-7 days verification)

1. Go to **https://dashboard.stripe.com/register**
2. Sign up with email
3. After verifying email, you'll be asked country: **United Kingdom**
4. Pick account type: **Individual / Sole Proprietor**
5. **Business details**:
   - Legal first/last name: your real name
   - Business name (trading as): `Reliq Digital`
   - Industry: **Software / Education** (or whichever fits closest)
   - Business website: `https://akhar.io`
6. **Personal details**: home address, date of birth (Stripe needs this for KYC under UK money-laundering rules)
7. **Bank details**: a UK bank account. Sort code + account number. Best to use a separate "business" account if you have one; personal account is fine if not (this is the account akhar revenue gets paid into).
8. **Tax info**: your NI number or UTR (Self Assessment reference)
9. Submit

Stripe sometimes verifies instantly, sometimes asks for documents (passport scan, proof of address). If they email asking for docs, send them within 24h.

---

Don't do this yet — wait until you've tested the full MVP flow on the Vercel preview URL and we're ready to send the akhar.io address to real users. I'll walk you through this one when the time comes (~10 min). It's task #45.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/srs.ts",
  "content": "// FSRS scheduling — modern spaced-repetition algorithm. Wraps ts-fsrs\n// with the shape of our srs_cards table so the server actions can call\n// scheduleNext(card, grade) and get back the row to UPDATE.\n//\n// Why FSRS over SM-2: ~30% better retention for the same review time.\n// Migration-friendly because our schema already stores the FSRS fields\n// (stability, difficulty, reps, lapses, state, due_at).\nimport {\n  fsrs,\n  Rating,\n  State,\n  type Card as FsrsCard,\n  type Grade,\n} from \"ts-fsrs\";\n\n// The DB row shape — exactly the columns of srs_cards we need.\nexport interface DbCard {\n  id: string;\n  surface: string;\n  added_at: string;        // ISO timestamp\n  due_at: string;          // ISO timestamp\n  stability: number;\n  difficulty: number;\n  reps: number;\n  lapses: number;\n  state: \"new\" | \"learning\" | \"review\" | \"relearning\";\n}\n\n// FSRS expects integer state codes; our DB stores them as strings for\n// readability. These two helpers keep the mapping in one place.\nconst STATE_TO_ENUM: Record<DbCard[\"state\"], State> = {\n  new: State.New,\n  learning: State.Learning,\n  review: State.Review,\n  relearning: State.Relearning,\n};\n\nconst ENUM_TO_STATE: Record<State, DbCard[\"state\"]> = {\n  [State.New]: \"new\",\n  [State.Learning]: \"learning\",\n  [State.Review]: \"review\",\n  [State.Relearning]: \"relearning\",\n};\n\nexport const RATING_AGAIN = Rating.Again;\nexport const RATING_HARD = Rating.Hard;\nexport const RATING_GOOD = Rating.Good;\nexport const RATING_EASY = Rating.Easy;\n\nconst scheduler = fsrs();\n\nfunction toFsrsCard(db: DbCard): FsrsCard {\n  return {\n    due: new Date(db.due_at),\n    stability: db.stability,\n    difficulty: db.difficulty,\n    elapsed_days: 0, // recalculated by FSRS from last_review\n    scheduled_days: 0,\n    learning_steps: 0,\n    reps: db.reps,\n    lapses: db.lapses,\n    state: STATE_TO_ENUM[db.state],\n    last_review: db.due_at ? new Date(db.due_at) : undefined,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Given a card and the user's grade, return the values to write back to\n * srs_cards AND the SRS review record to insert. Pure function — no DB\n * access; the caller persists.\n */\nexport function scheduleNext(card: DbCard, grade: Grade) {\n  const now = new Date();\n  const fsrsCard = toFsrsCard(card);\n  const result = scheduler.next(fsrsCard, now, grade);\n\n  return {\n    cardUpdate: {\n      due_at: result.card.due.toISOString(),\n      stability: result.card.stability,\n      difficulty: result.card.difficulty,\n      reps: result.card.reps,\n      lapses: result.card.lapses,\n      state: ENUM_TO_STATE[result.card.state],\n    },\n    review: {\n      card_id: card.id,\n      rating: grade,\n      reviewed_at: now.toISOString(),\n      elapsed_days:\n        (now.getTime() - new Date(card.due_at).getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24),\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Preview what each rating would schedule for a card — used by the UI to\n * show \"Hard → 2d, Good → 7d, Easy → 18d\" on the rating buttons so the\n * user understands the tradeoff before clicking.\n */\nexport function previewIntervals(card: DbCard): Record<Grade, string> {\n  const now = new Date();\n  const fsrsCard = toFsrsCard(card);\n  const log = scheduler.repeat(fsrsCard, now);\n  const fmt = (date: Date) => {\n    const diffMs = date.getTime() - now.getTime();\n    const diffMin = Math.round(diffMs / 60000);\n    if (diffMin < 60) return `${Math.max(1, diffMin)}m`;\n    const diffHr = Math.round(diffMin / 60);\n    if (diffHr < 24) return `${diffHr}h`;\n    const diffDay = Math.round(diffHr / 24);\n    if (diffDay < 30) return `${diffDay}d`;\n    const diffMo = Math.round(diffDay / 30);\n    if (diffMo < 12) return `${diffMo}mo`;\n    return `${Math.round(diffDay / 365)}y`;\n  };\n  return {\n    [Rating.Again]: fmt(log[Rating.Again].card.due),\n    [Rating.Hard]: fmt(log[Rating.Hard].card.due),\n    [Rating.Good]: fmt(log[Rating.Good].card.due),\n    [Rating.Easy]: fmt(log[Rating.Easy].card.due),\n  } as Record<Grade, string>;\n}\n"
}

Reads from the authed Supabase client so RLS\n// enforces ownership — even if the surface or user_id is tampered with,\n// the database refuses the write unless auth.uid() matches user_id.\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\n\nexport async function addToDeck(\n  surface: string,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  if (!surface || surface.length > 60) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"invalid surface\" };\n  }\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) return { ok: false, error: \"not signed in\" };\n\n  // Upsert by (user_id, surface) — adding a word that's already in the\n  // deck is a no-op rather than an error.\n  const { error } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .upsert(\n      { user_id: user.id, surface },\n      { onConflict: \"user_id,surface\", ignoreDuplicates: true },\n    );\n  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };\n  return { ok: true };\n}",
  "new_string": "\"use server\";\n\n// Per-user SRS deck actions. All reads + writes go through the authed\n// Supabase client so RLS enforces ownership — even a tampered user_id\n// in the request is refused unless auth.uid() matches.\nimport { revalidatePath } from \"next/cache\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { scheduleNext, type DbCard } from \"@/lib/srs\";\nimport type { Grade } from \"ts-fsrs\";\n\nexport async function addToDeck(\n  surface: string,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  if (!surface || surface.length > 60) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"invalid surface\" };\n  }\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) return { ok: false, error: \"not signed in\" };\n\n  // Upsert by (user_id, surface) — adding a word that's already in the\n  // deck is a no-op rather than an error.\n  const { error } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .upsert(\n      { user_id: user.id, surface },\n      { onConflict: \"user_id,surface\", ignoreDuplicates: true },\n    );\n  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n\n/**\n * Record a review for a single card and update its scheduling.\n *\n * Two writes, no transaction (RLS makes either safe individually):\n *   1. UPDATE srs_cards with the new due_at + FSRS state\n *   2. INSERT into srs_reviews for the history log\n *\n * The history table lets us compute retention curves, weakest words,\n * daily review counts, etc. later — costs almost nothing now.\n */\nexport async function reviewCard(\n  cardId: string,\n  rating: Grade,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) return { ok: false, error: \"not signed in\" };\n\n  // Load current card state (RLS ensures it belongs to this user).\n  const { data: row, error: loadErr } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .select(\"id, surface, added_at, due_at, stability, difficulty, reps, lapses, state\")\n    .eq(\"id\", cardId)\n    .single();\n  if (loadErr || !row) {\n    return { ok: false, error: loadErr?.message ?? \"card not found\" };\n  }\n\n  const card = row as unknown as DbCard;\n  const { cardUpdate, review } = scheduleNext(card, rating);\n\n  const { error: updateErr } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .update(cardUpdate)\n    .eq(\"id\", cardId);\n  if (updateErr) return { ok: false, error: updateErr.message };\n\n  const { error: insertErr } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_reviews\")\n    .insert({ ...review, user_id: user.id });\n  if (insertErr) return { ok: false, error: insertErr.message };\n\n  revalidatePath(\"/deck\");\n  return { ok: true };\n}"
}

Shows:\n//   - How many cards are due right now (the call-to-action)\n//   - Total deck size\n//   - Activity from the last 7 days\n//   - The full saved-words list (paginated later if it gets big)\n//\n// Per tiers.md, free tier sees the list (passive vocabulary scrapbook),\n// Pro tier sees the review session. For MVP we let everyone review;\n// the gate gets added when Stripe is wired.\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport LetterAudio from \"@/components/LetterAudio\";\n\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: \"Your deck — akhar.io\",\n};\n\nexport default async function DeckPage() {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) redirect(\"/login?next=/deck\");\n\n  // Three queries in parallel: due cards, total, recent reviews.\n  const now = new Date().toISOString();\n  const weekAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();\n  const [dueRes, totalRes, recentRes, cardsRes] = await Promise.all([\n    supabase\n      .from(\"srs_cards\")\n      .select(\"id\", { count: \"exact\", head: true })\n      .lte(\"due_at\", now),\n    supabase\n      .from(\"srs_cards\")\n      .select(\"id\", { count: \"exact\", head: true }),\n    supabase\n      .from(\"srs_reviews\")\n      .select(\"id\", { count: \"exact\", head: true })\n      .gte(\"reviewed_at\", weekAgo),\n    supabase\n      .from(\"srs_cards\")\n      .select(\"id, surface, added_at, due_at, state, reps\")\n      .order(\"added_at\", { ascending: false })\n      .limit(100),\n  ]);\n\n  const dueCount = dueRes.count ?? 0;\n  const totalCount = totalRes.count ?? 0;\n  const weekReviews = recentRes.count ?? 0;\n  const cards = (cardsRes.data ?? []) as Array<{\n    id: string;\n    surface: string;\n    added_at: string;\n    due_at: string;\n    state: string;\n    reps: number;\n  }>;\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 sm:py-10\">\n      <header className=\"mb-8\">\n        <h1 className=\"text-3xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          Your deck\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-2 text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n          Words you&apos;ve saved while reading. Review them daily for spaced\n          repetition.\n        </p>\n      </header>\n\n      {totalCount === 0 ? (\n        <section className=\"rounded-lg border border-dashed border-zinc-300 bg-zinc-50 p-8 text-center dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900\">\n          <p className=\"text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n            Your deck is empty. Save your first word by tapping the\n            <strong> + Save to deck</strong> button in any sakhi&apos;s word\n            popover.\n          </p>\n          <Link\n            href=\"/sakhi/1\"\n            className=\"mt-6 inline-block rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-2.5 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n          >\n            Start reading\n          </Link>\n        </section>\n      ) : (\n        <>\n          <section className=\"mb-8 grid grid-cols-3 gap-3\">\n            <Stat label=\"Due now\" value={dueCount} accent={dueCount > 0} />\n            <Stat label=\"Total cards\" value={totalCount} />\n            <Stat label=\"Reviews this week\" value={weekReviews} />\n          </section>\n\n          {dueCount > 0 ? (\n            <Link\n              href=\"/deck/review\"\n              className=\"mb-10 flex items-center justify-between rounded-xl bg-zinc-900 px-6 py-5 font-medium text-white transition hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n            >\n              <span className=\"text-lg\">\n                Start review · {dueCount} card{dueCount === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} due\n              </span>\n              <span className=\"text-2xl\">→</span>\n            </Link>\n          ) : (\n            <div className=\"mb-10 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 bg-zinc-50 p-6 text-center text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n              No cards due right now. Come back tomorrow — spaced repetition\n              works best when you let the words rest.\n            </div>\n          )}\n\n          <section>\n            <h2 className=\"mb-3 text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-wider text-zinc-500\">\n              All saved words\n            </h2>\n            <ul className=\"divide-y divide-zinc-200 dark:divide-zinc-800\">\n              {cards.map((c) => {\n                const dueDate = new Date(c.due_at);\n                const isDue = dueDate <= new Date();\n                return (\n                  <li key={c.id} className=\"flex items-center gap-3 py-3\">\n                    <span className=\"flex-1 font-serif text-lg text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n                      {c.surface}\n                    </span>\n                    <span className=\"hidden font-mono text-xs text-zinc-400 sm:inline\">\n                      {c.state} · {c.reps} reps\n                    </span>\n                    <span\n                      className={`shrink-0 text-xs ${isDue ? \"text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400\" : \"text-zinc-400\"}`}\n                    >\n                      {formatRelative(dueDate)}\n                    </span>\n                    <LetterAudio text={c.surface} label=\"\" />\n                  </li>\n                );\n              })}\n            </ul>\n            {cards.length === 100 && (\n              <p className=\"mt-4 text-center text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n                Showing 100 most recent. Pagination coming soon.\n              </p>\n            )}\n          </section>\n        </>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction Stat({\n  label,\n  value,\n  accent,\n}: {\n  label: string;\n  value: number;\n  accent?: boolean;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <div\n      className={`rounded-lg border p-4 ${\n        accent\n          ? \"border-amber-300 bg-amber-50 dark:border-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-950\"\n          : \"border-zinc-200 bg-white dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n      }`}\n    >\n      <div className=\"text-2xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n        {value}\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"mt-0.5 text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-zinc-500\">\n        {label}\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction formatRelative(date: Date): string {\n  const diffMs = date.getTime() - Date.now();\n  const past = diffMs < 0;\n  const abs = Math.abs(diffMs);\n  const min = Math.round(abs / 60000);\n  if (min < 60) return past ? \"due\" : `in ${min}m`;\n  const hr = Math.round(min / 60);\n  if (hr < 24) return past ? \"due\" : `in ${hr}h`;\n  const day = Math.round(hr / 24);\n  if (day < 30) return past ? \"due\" : `in ${day}d`;\n  const mo = Math.round(day / 30);\n  return past ? \"due\" : `in ${mo}mo`;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/deck/review/page.tsx",
  "content": "// Active review session. Pulls all due cards up-front (a single query),\n// passes them to a client component that walks the user through them\n// one at a time. After the last card we show a summary and link back\n// to /deck.\n//\n// We pull the morpheme JSON eagerly for each card from the public\n// morpheme_cache so the review session can show romanization + gloss\n// without round-tripping to the morpheme API per card.\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport type { Morpheme } from \"@/lib/types\";\nimport type { DbCard } from \"@/lib/srs\";\nimport ReviewSession from \"./ReviewSession\";\n\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: \"Review · Deck — akhar.io\",\n};\n\nexport default async function ReviewPage() {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const {\n    data: { user },\n  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) redirect(\"/login?next=/deck/review\");\n\n  const now = new Date().toISOString();\n  const { data: rows } = await supabase\n    .from(\"srs_cards\")\n    .select(\"id, surface, added_at, due_at, stability, difficulty, reps, lapses, state\")\n    .lte(\"due_at\", now)\n    .order(\"due_at\", { ascending: true })\n    .limit(100);\n  const cards = (rows ?? []) as unknown as DbCard[];\n\n  if (cards.length === 0) {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"mx-auto max-w-xl px-4 py-12 sm:px-6 text-center\">\n        <h1 className=\"text-3xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          All caught up\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-3 text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n          No cards due right now. Spaced repetition works best when you let\n          the words rest between reviews.\n        </p>\n        <Link\n          href=\"/deck\"\n          className=\"mt-6 inline-block rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-2.5 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n        >\n          Back to deck\n        </Link>\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Fetch the morpheme JSON for each card in a single query. Anon-read is\n  // allowed on morpheme_cache by RLS, so we can use the read-side client\n  // and not eat into the user-scoped client's permissions.\n  const readClient = createClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    { auth: { persistSession: false } },\n  );\n  const surfaces = cards.map((c) => c.surface);\n  const { data: morphemeRows } = await readClient\n    .from(\"morpheme_cache\")\n    .select(\"surface, morpheme_json\")\n    .in(\"surface\", surfaces);\n  const byKey = new Map<string, Morpheme>();\n  for (const m of (morphemeRows ?? []) as Array<{\n    surface: string;\n    morpheme_json: Morpheme;\n  }>) {\n    byKey.set(m.surface, m.morpheme_json);\n  }\n\n  const enriched = cards.map((c) => ({\n    card: c,\n    morpheme: byKey.get(c.surface) ?? null,\n  }));\n\n  return <ReviewSession items={enriched} />;\n}\n"
}

(\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            onClick={() => setRevealed(true)}\n            className=\"mt-12 rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 px-6 py-3 font-medium text-zinc-700 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\"\n          >\n            Show answer <span className=\"ml-2 text-xs text-zinc-400\">(space)</span>\n          </button>\n        ) : (\n          <>\n            {current.morpheme ? (\n              <div className=\"mt-6 space-y-2\">\n                <p className=\"font-mono text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n                  {current.morpheme.romanized}\n                </p>\n                <p className=\"text-lg text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n                  {current.morpheme.gloss_en}\n                </p>\n                {current.morpheme.senses && current.morpheme.senses.length > 1 && (\n                  <ul className=\"mt-2 space-y-1 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n                    {current.morpheme.senses.map((s, i) => (\n                      <li key={i}>\n                        <span className=\"font-medium\">{i + 1}.</span> {s.gloss_en}\n                      </li>\n                    ))}\n                  </ul>\n                )}\n              </div>\n            ) : (\n              <p className=\"mt-4 text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n                No dictionary entry cached for this word yet.\n              </p>\n            )}\n            <div className=\"mt-4\">\n              <LetterAudio text={current.card.surface} label=\"Hear it\" />\n            </div>\n          </>\n        )}\n      </section>\n\n      {/* Rating buttons — only after reveal */}\n      {revealed && intervals && (\n        <section className=\"mt-8 grid grid-cols-4 gap-2\">\n          {RATINGS.map((r) => (\n            <button\n              key={r.label}\n              type=\"button\"\n              onClick={() => rate(r.grade)}\n              disabled={submitting}\n              className={`flex flex-col items-center rounded-lg px-2 py-3 font-medium transition disabled:opacity-50 ${r.className}`}\n            >\n              <span>{r.label}</span>\n              <span className=\"mt-1 text-[10px] opacity-70\">\n                {intervals[r.grade]} · {r.shortcut}\n              </span>\n            </button>\n          ))}\n        </section>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
