  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env tsx\n/**\n * Audit cached audio for a sakhi (or for every prewarmed clip) and\n * re-synthesise anything that came out silent / clipped.\n *\n * The silent-word fallback in lib/google-tts.ts kicks in on synthesis,\n * but some early-cached entries pre-date that fallback OR slipped past\n * it. This script catches them after the fact.\n *\n * Threshold: MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES = 2000. Anything smaller is treated as\n * a clipped/silent stub and re-synthed.\n *\n * Usage:\n *   tsx scripts/audit-audio-quality.ts                   # all curriculum + sakhi 1\n *   tsx scripts/audit-audio-quality.ts --sakhi 1         # one sakhi's words + sentences\n *   tsx scripts/audit-audio-quality.ts --sakhi 1 --dry-run\n */\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\nimport { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { audioCacheSize, putCachedAudio, deleteCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\nconst MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES = 2000;\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst sakhiIdx = args.indexOf(\"--sakhi\");\nconst sakhiId = sakhiIdx >= 0 ? Number(args[sakhiIdx + 1]) : 1;\nconst dryRun = args.includes(\"--dry-run\");\n\nfunction tokenize(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    if (!seen.has(m[0])) {\n      seen.add(m[0]);\n      out.push(m[0]);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction splitSentences(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[^।?!]+[।?!]+[\"'”’)\\]]*|[^।?!]+$/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    const s = m[0].trim();\n    if (s && !seen.has(s)) {\n      seen.add(s);\n      out.push(s);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const db = new Database(path.join(process.cwd(), \"data\", \"sakhis.db\"), {\n    readonly: true,\n  });\n  const row = db\n    .prepare(`SELECT title_pa, body_pa FROM sakhis WHERE id = ?`)\n    .get(sakhiId) as { title_pa: string; body_pa: string } | undefined;\n  db.close();\n  if (!row) {\n    console.error(`sakhi id=${sakhiId} not found`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  const words = tokenize(`${row.title_pa}\\n\\n${row.body_pa}`);\n  const sentences = splitSentences(row.body_pa);\n  const all = [\n    ...words.map((w) => ({ kind: \"word\" as const, text: w })),\n    ...sentences.map((s) => ({ kind: \"sentence\" as const, text: s })),\n  ];\n\n  console.log(\n    `Auditing sakhi ${sakhiId}: ${words.length} unique words + ${sentences.length} sentences = ${all.length} clips${dryRun ? \" [dry run]\" : \"\"}\\n`,\n  );\n\n  let healthy = 0;\n  let missing = 0;\n  let rebuilt = 0;\n  let failed = 0;\n  const bad: { kind: string; text: string; size: number }[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {\n    const { kind, text } = all[i];\n    const size = await audioCacheSize(VOICE_NAME, text);\n    if (size === null) {\n      missing++;\n      bad.push({ kind, text, size: 0 });\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (size >= MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES) {\n      healthy++;\n      continue;\n    }\n    bad.push({ kind, text, size });\n  }\n\n  console.log(`Audit complete:`);\n  console.log(`  healthy: ${healthy}`);\n  console.log(`  missing: ${missing}`);\n  console.log(`  bad (< ${MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES}B): ${bad.length - missing}\\n`);\n\n  if (bad.length === 0) {\n    console.log(\"Nothing to fix.\");\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (dryRun) {\n    console.log(\"Would re-synth:\");\n    for (const b of bad) {\n      console.log(`  ${b.kind.padEnd(8)} ${b.size}B  ${b.text}`);\n    }\n    return;\n  }\n\n  console.log(\"Re-synthesising bad / missing clips...\\n\");\n  for (let i = 0; i < bad.length; i++) {\n    const { kind, text, size } = bad[i];\n    try {\n      if (size > 0) {\n        await deleteCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text);\n      }\n      const mp3 = await synthesize(text);\n      await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text, mp3);\n      rebuilt++;\n      console.log(\n        `  [${i + 1}/${bad.length}] ${kind.padEnd(8)} ${size}B → ${mp3.length}B  ${text}`,\n      );\n    } catch (err) {\n      failed++;\n      console.warn(\n        `  [${i + 1}/${bad.length}] FAILED ${kind} ${text}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`,\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  console.log(`\\nDone. rebuilt=${rebuilt} failed=${failed}`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

## Part 2: Full-sakhi play button + word-by-word highlighter

These two are one cohesive feature. Plan: a player at the top of the sakhi that walks through sentences sequentially. While each sentence plays, the current word gets highlighted in real-time using character-proportion estimation against the audio's `currentTime`.

The technical limitation worth being upfront about: **Chirp 3 HD doesn't expose word-level timing data** (only Wavenet does, via SSML marks). So we estimate word timings from character proportions — works visually but won't be frame-perfect. The audio is still smooth; only the highlight position is approximate.

  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Shared playback state for the sakhi reader. The <SakhiPlayer> bar at\n// the top owns the audio element + sequencing; <HoverWord> children\n// subscribe to know if they're the currently-spoken word so they can\n// highlight.\n//\n// Word-level timing is ESTIMATED from character-proportion against the\n// audio's currentTime — Chirp 3 HD doesn't expose word boundaries, so\n// we can't get exact timings without a forced-aligner. The highlight is\n// usually within ~100-300ms of the actual word, which reads as\n// \"follows along\" to a human eye.\n\nimport { createContext, useContext, useState, useCallback } from \"react\";\n\ninterface PlayingPosition {\n  sentenceIndex: number;\n  wordIndex: number | null;  // null = sentence playing but no word resolved yet\n}\n\ninterface SakhiPlayerContextValue {\n  /** Index of the currently-playing sentence, or null if paused/stopped */\n  playing: PlayingPosition | null;\n  setPlaying: (p: PlayingPosition | null) => void;\n}\n\nconst Ctx = createContext<SakhiPlayerContextValue>({\n  playing: null,\n  setPlaying: () => {},\n});\n\nexport function SakhiPlayerProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  const [playing, setPlayingState] = useState<PlayingPosition | null>(null);\n  // Stable setter so context consumers don't re-render needlessly.\n  const setPlaying = useCallback((p: PlayingPosition | null) => {\n    setPlayingState(p);\n  }, []);\n  return <Ctx.Provider value={{ playing, setPlaying }}>{children}</Ctx.Provider>;\n}\n\nexport function useSakhiPlayer() {\n  return useContext(Ctx);\n}\n\n/**\n * Returns true if (sentenceIndex, wordIndex) is the currently-spoken word.\n * Used by HoverWord (when rendered inside a sakhi) to highlight itself.\n */\nexport function useIsCurrentWord(sentenceIndex: number, wordIndex: number): boolean {\n  const { playing } = useSakhiPlayer();\n  return (\n    playing !== null &&\n    playing.sentenceIndex === sentenceIndex &&\n    playing.wordIndex === wordIndex\n  );\n}\n\n/** Likewise for the sentence — used for the \"this row is playing\" affordance. */\nexport function useIsCurrentSentence(sentenceIndex: number): boolean {\n  const { playing } = useSakhiPlayer();\n  return playing !== null && playing.sentenceIndex === sentenceIndex;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/components/SakhiPlayer.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Sticky bar at the top of the sakhi reader. Owns the audio element,\n// walks through sentences sequentially, drives the word-highlight context.\n//\n// Per-sentence playback already exists via the speaker icon on each\n// sentence row. This is the \"play the whole thing\" affordance plus the\n// machinery (current-word tracking) the row-level player doesn't need.\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { useSakhiPlayer } from \"./SakhiPlayerContext\";\n\ninterface Props {\n  sentences: string[]; // Punjabi sentences, in order, from SakhiReader\n}\n\nconst SENTENCE_GAP_MS = 400; // brief pause between sentences\n\nexport default function SakhiPlayer({ sentences }: Props) {\n  const { setPlaying } = useSakhiPlayer();\n  const [active, setActive] = useState(false);\n  const [index, setIndex] = useState(0); // next sentence to play\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  const tickRef = useRef<number | null>(null);\n  const gapRef = useRef<number | null>(null);\n  // Latest sentence being played, used by the word-position tracker.\n  const currentSentenceRef = useRef<number>(-1);\n  const wordOffsetsRef = useRef<number[]>([]);\n  const cancelledRef = useRef<boolean>(false);\n\n  // Stop everything cleanly on unmount.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    return () => {\n      cancelledRef.current = true;\n      stopTimers();\n      if (audioRef.current) {\n        audioRef.current.pause();\n        audioRef.current.src = \"\";\n      }\n      setPlaying(null);\n    };\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, []);\n\n  function stopTimers() {\n    if (tickRef.current) {\n      window.clearInterval(tickRef.current);\n      tickRef.current = null;\n    }\n    if (gapRef.current) {\n      window.clearTimeout(gapRef.current);\n      gapRef.current = null;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Build cumulative character-offsets per word so we can map currentTime\n  // → which word is being spoken. Word boundaries come from the same\n  // tokenisation rule as SakhiReader: Gurmukhi runs are words; everything\n  // else is a gap.\n  function tokenWordOffsets(text: string): { wordIndices: number[]; totalChars: number } {\n    const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;\n    const offsets: number[] = [];\n    let totalChars = 0;\n    let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n    while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n      offsets.push(totalChars);\n      totalChars += m[0].length;\n    }\n    return { wordIndices: offsets, totalChars };\n  }\n\n  async function playSentence(sentenceIdx: number) {\n    if (cancelledRef.current) return;\n    if (sentenceIdx >= sentences.length) {\n      // Done with the whole sakhi.\n      setActive(false);\n      setIndex(0);\n      setPlaying(null);\n      return;\n    }\n    const text = sentences[sentenceIdx];\n    currentSentenceRef.current = sentenceIdx;\n    const { wordIndices, totalChars } = tokenWordOffsets(text);\n    wordOffsetsRef.current = wordIndices.map((c) => c / Math.max(1, totalChars));\n    setIndex(sentenceIdx + 1);\n    setPlaying({ sentenceIndex: sentenceIdx, wordIndex: 0 });\n\n    // Fetch the cached audio. If it's missing (404), skip this sentence\n    // rather than abort the whole session — partial gaps are better than\n    // dead-stopping.\n    const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`;\n    const res = await fetch(url, { method: \"HEAD\" });\n    if (!res.ok) {\n      gapRef.current = window.setTimeout(\n        () => playSentence(sentenceIdx + 1),\n        SENTENCE_GAP_MS,\n      );\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const audio = new Audio(url);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n\n    // Word-position tick: every 50ms, find the latest word whose offset\n    // is ≤ (currentTime / duration). Visual sync is approximate but\n    // smooth.\n    tickRef.current = window.setInterval(() => {\n      if (!audio.duration || !isFinite(audio.duration)) return;\n      const fraction = audio.currentTime / audio.duration;\n      const offsets = wordOffsetsRef.current;\n      let idx = 0;\n      for (let i = 0; i < offsets.length; i++) {\n        if (offsets[i] <= fraction) idx = i;\n        else break;\n      }\n      setPlaying({ sentenceIndex: sentenceIdx, wordIndex: idx });\n    }, 50);\n\n    audio.onended = () => {\n      stopTimers();\n      gapRef.current = window.setTimeout(\n        () => playSentence(sentenceIdx + 1),\n        SENTENCE_GAP_MS,\n      );\n    };\n    audio.onerror = () => {\n      stopTimers();\n      gapRef.current = window.setTimeout(\n        () => playSentence(sentenceIdx + 1),\n        SENTENCE_GAP_MS,\n      );\n    };\n\n    audio.play().catch(() => {\n      // Autoplay can be blocked the very first time the user hits Play\n      // on iOS Safari — but since this is a click handler it should be\n      // fine. If it fails, just move on.\n      stopTimers();\n      gapRef.current = window.setTimeout(\n        () => playSentence(sentenceIdx + 1),\n        SENTENCE_GAP_MS,\n      );\n    });\n  }\n\n  function start() {\n    cancelledRef.current = false;\n    setActive(true);\n    // Resume from current index, or restart if at end\n    const from = index >= sentences.length ? 0 : index;\n    setIndex(from);\n    playSentence(from);\n  }\n\n  function pause() {\n    cancelledRef.current = true;\n    stopTimers();\n    if (audioRef.current) audioRef.current.pause();\n    setActive(false);\n    setPlaying(null);\n    // Decrement so resume replays the current sentence from the start\n    // (people expect \"resume\" to mean \"the sentence I was in the middle of\")\n    setIndex((i) => Math.max(0, i - 1));\n  }\n\n  function restart() {\n    cancelledRef.current = true;\n    stopTimers();\n    if (audioRef.current) audioRef.current.pause();\n    setActive(false);\n    setPlaying(null);\n    setIndex(0);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"sticky top-14 z-30 -mx-4 mb-6 flex items-center gap-3 border-b border-zinc-200 bg-white/95 px-4 py-2.5 backdrop-blur sm:-mx-6 sm:px-6 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950/95\">\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        onClick={active ? \"Pause\" : \"Play whole sakhi\"}\n      >\n        {active ? \"⏸\" : \"▶\"}\n      </button>\n      <div className=\"flex-1 text-sm\">\n        <div className=\"font-medium text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {active\n            ? 2	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
3	import HoverWord from "./HoverWord";

5	interface Props {
6	  bodyPa: string;
7	  bodyEn: string | null;
8	  signedIn: boolean;
9	}
10	
11	// Split paragraph into hoverable Gurmukhi tokens + non-Gurmukhi run-throughs.
12	function tokenize(paragraph: string): Array<{ kind: "word" | "gap"; text: string }> {
13	  const out: Array<{ kind: "word" | "gap"; text: string }> = [];
14	  const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;
15	  let last = 0;
16	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
17	  while ((m = re.exec(paragraph)) !== null) {
18	    if (m.index > last) {
19	      out.push({ kind: "gap", text: paragraph.slice(last, m.index) });
20	    }
21	    out.push({ kind: "word", text: m[0] });
22	    last = m.index + m[0].length;
23	  }
24	  if (last < paragraph.length) {
25	    out.push({ kind: "gap", text: paragraph.slice(last) });
26	  }
27	  return out;
28	}
29	
30	// Split a Punjabi paragraph into sentences. Each sentence keeps its
31	// terminator (। ? !) plus any trailing closing brackets/quotes so a
32	// parenthesised aside like "(...।)" stays one sentence.
33	function splitPa(paragraph: string): string[] {
34	  const out: string[] = [];
35	  const re = /[^।?!]+[।?!]+["'”’)\]]*|[^।?!]+$/g;
36	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
37	  while ((m = re.exec(paragraph)) !== null) {
38	    const s = m[0].trim();
39	    if (s) out.push(s);
40	  }
41	  return out;
42	}
43	
44	// Split an English paragraph into sentences. Same idea but with .?!
45	// Also tolerates trailing quotes/parens and accepts `:-` (the
46	// Punjabi-style intro marker, often carried through into translations)
47	// as a sentence terminator so the alignment with PA stays 1:1.
48	function splitEn(paragraph: string): string[] {
49	  const out: string[] = [];
50	  const re = /[^.?!]+(?:[.?!]+|:-)["')\]]*|\S[^.?!]*$/g;
51	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
52	  while ((m = re.exec(paragraph)) !== null) {
53	    const s = m[0].trim();
54	    if (s) out.push(s);
55	  }
56	  return out;
57	}
58	
59	// Pair PA sentences with EN sentences by index. If counts are off by ≤1
60	// we still align top-down; if they're wildly off we collapse the longer
61	// side so each row has both languages.
62	function pairSentences(pa: string[], en: string[]): Array<{ pa: string; en: string | null }> {
63	  if (en.length === 0) return pa.map((p) => ({ pa: p, en: null }));
64	  const rows: Array<{ pa: string; en: string | null }> = [];
65	  const n = Math.max(pa.length, en.length);
66	  // If counts match closely, zip by index.
67	  if (Math.abs(pa.length - en.length) <= Math.max(1, Math.floor(n / 4))) {
68	    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
69	      rows.push({ pa: pa[i] ?? "", en: en[i] ?? null });
70	    }
71	    return rows;
72	  }
73	  // Counts diverge — fall back to one row per side (whole paragraph each).
74	  return [{ pa: pa.join(" "), en: en.join(" ") }];
75	}
76	
77	export default function SakhiReader({ bodyPa, bodyEn, signedIn }: Props) {
78	  const [activeWord, setActiveWord] = useState<string | null>(null);
79	  const paragraphsPa = bodyPa.split(/\n\n+/).map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean);
80	  const paragraphsEn = (bodyEn ?? "")
81	    .split(/\n\n+/)
82	    .map((p) => p.trim())
83	    .filter(Boolean);
84	
85	  // Build a flat list of (PA sentence, EN sentence) rows across all
86	  // paragraphs. Paragraph boundaries are marked so we can render extra
87	  // spacing between them.
88	  type Row = { pa: string; en: string | null; paraEnd: boolean };
89	  const rows: Row[] = [];
90	  paragraphsPa.forEach((pa, i) => {
91	    const en = paragraphsEn[i] ?? "";
92	    const paired = pairSentences(splitPa(pa), splitEn(en));
93	    paired.forEach((r, j) => {
94	      rows.push({ pa: r.pa, en: r.en, paraEnd: j === paired.length - 1 });
95	    });
96	  });
97	
98	  return (
99	    <div className="space-y-3">
100	      {rows.map((row, i) => (
101	        <div
102	          key={i}
103	          className={row.paraEnd ? "pb-6" : ""}
104	        >
105	          <div className="group/sentence flex items-start gap-2">
106	            <SentencePlayButton text={row.pa} />
107	            <div className="font-serif text-lg leading-loose text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">
108	              {tokenize(row.pa).map((tok, j) => {
109	                if (tok.kind === "gap") return <span key={j}>{tok.text}</span>;
110	                const key = `${i}-${j}`;
111	                return (
112	                  <HoverWord
113	                    key={key}
114	                    word={tok.text}
115	                    isActive={activeWord === key}
116	                    signedIn={signedIn}
117	                    onOpen={() => setActiveWord(key)}
118	                    // Only blank if THIS word is still the active one — when
119	                    // moving from A to B, A's late close-timer must not erase
120	                    // B's open that fired in between.
121	                    onClose={() =>
122	                      setActiveWord((prev) => (prev === key ? null : prev))
123	                    }
124	                  />
125	                );
126	              })}
127	            </div>
128	          </div>
129	          {row.en ? (
130	            <div className="mt-1 font-serif text-base leading-relaxed text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400">
131	              {row.en}
132	            </div>
133	          ) : null}
134	        </div>
135	      ))}
136	    </div>
137	  );
138	}
139	
140	// Sentence-level playback. Same /api/tts endpoint as the word popover —
141	// route caches the MP3 by exact text, so re-plays are instant.
142	function SentencePlayButton({ text }: { text: string }) {
143	  const [state, setState] = useState<"idle" | "loading" | "playing">("idle");
144	  const [available, setAvailable] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
145	  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);
146	  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(text)}`;
147	
148	  useEffect(() => {
149	    let cancelled = false;
150	    fetch(url, { method: "HEAD" })
151	      .then((r) => !cancelled && setAvailable(r.ok))
152	      .catch(() => !cancelled && setAvailable(false));
153	    return () => { cancelled = true; };
154	  }, [url]);
155	
156	  function play() {
157	    if (audioRef.current) {
158	      audioRef.current.pause();
159	      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;
160	    }
161	    setState("loading");
162	    const audio = new Audio(url);
163	    audioRef.current = audio;
164	    audio.onplaying = () => setState("playing");
165	    audio.onended = () => setState("idle");
166	    audio.onerror = () => setState("idle");
167	    audio.play().catch(() => setState("idle"));
168	  }
169	
170	  if (available === false) return <div className="w-5 shrink-0" aria-hidden />;
171	  return (
172	    <button
173	      type="button"
174	      onClick={play}
175	      disabled={state === "loading" || available !== true}
176	      // Always visible on touch (no hover state to reveal it); fade in
177	      // only on hover-capable devices to keep the desktop reading flow clean.
178	      className="mt-1.5 shrink-0 p-1 text-zinc-400 transition hover:text-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-40 dark:text-zinc-500 dark:hover:text-zinc-200 [@media(hover:hover)]:opacity-0 [@media(hover:hover)]:group-hover/sentence:opacity-100"
179	      title="Play sentence"
180	      aria-label="Play sentence"
181	    >
182	      {state === "playing" ? "🔉" : state === "loading" ? "⋯" : "🔊"}
183	    </button>
184	  );
185	}
186

Let's actually think about both. They're connected to a bigger question — what is the akhar reader *for*?

## Point 1: hiding unprocessed sakhis

Quick answer: **yes, do this immediately.** Right now we have:
- 1 sakhi fully verified (sakhi 1, hand-cleaned PA + EN, all words have audio + dictionary entries)
- 404 sakhis where the body text is raw-ish OCR with some auto-translation
- A library index that promises all 405

Anyone clicking a random unprocessed one will see: OCR-quality Punjabi text + iffy English + hover-lookups that may trigger expensive Punjabipedia + nano-gpt calls + sometimes return nothing useful. **First impressions are catastrophic.** Better to show 5 good ones than 405 broken ones.

Implementation is straightforward: add a `processed` flag on the sakhis table, filter all index queries to `processed = true`. The hidden ones still live in the DB so we can process them incrementally and they become visible as they're ready. Index pages can show "5 sakhis available · 400 being added" to set expectations without overpromising.

**The hard problem this exposes**: at our current rate (a few hours per sakhi to fully verify), we'll process maybe ~50 sakhis before MVP launch. That's enough to feel like a real library but it's only ~12% of the corpus. The pipeline upgrade (LLM-assisted cleanup) is critical because manual processing alone won't get us much further than that.

## Point 2: archaic vs modern Punjabi — this is bigger than UX polish

You're hitting something fundamental here. Bhai Vir Singh wrote 1900-1950. The diction is genuinely hard:
- `ਨਾਉਂ` instead of modern `ਨਾਮ` (name)
- `ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ` instead of `ਖੱਤਰੀ` (Khatri caste)
- Sanskrit-origin vocabulary
- Persian loan-words still common
- Literary syntax (passive constructions, archaic conjugations)

For a heritage learner who can speak conversational Punjabi but never learnt to read, opening sakhi 1 and seeing literary 1920s diction is... an honest disappointment. They came to akhar to reconnect with the language they grew up hearing, and what we're showing them is a 100-year-old textbook style they don't recognize.

This was actually the whole reason for the **two-wings architecture** I sketched in `content-architecture.md`:

- **Read** wing (the sakhi library) — classical Punjabi literature. Position it as "Read the classics" rather than "Read Punjabi." Think Penguin Classics, not Duolingo.
- **Learn** wing — modern Punjabi via the Book 2/3-style content we author ourselves. Modern conversational stuff: family routines, going to a shop, weekend plans, GCSE-aligned vocab.

If we frame sakhis honestly as "classical literature for confident readers" and build modern content alongside, we serve both audiences without lying to either. Heritage learners who want easy modern reads go to Learn → Beginner Readers. Heritage learners who want to read the sakhis their dadi-ji used to tell go to Read → Library.

### Options to make sakhis themselves easier without changing what they ARE

A few practical things within the sakhi reader:

**A. Era badges on every sakhi listing.** "Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s". Sets expectations before they click. Honest framing reduces the disappointment vs an unmarked "Punjabi" sakhi.

**B. Difficulty stars (1-5)** computed from average word length, archaic-form frequency, sentence length. So a learner can pick "easy classical" first.

**C. Archaic-form annotations in hover.** When the user hovers ਨਾਉਂ, the popover already shows the lemma (ਨਾਮ). We could surface that more prominently: "ਨਾਉਂ (modern: ਨਾਮ)". Small change, big trust signal — "akhar knows this is archaic and explains it."

**D. A "modern voice" toggle.** Optional sidebar showing a contemporary Punjabi paraphrase next to the original. Tons of work to commission, defer for later. Maybe never — it conflicts with archival purpose.

**E. Curate the order.** Of the 405 sakhis, some are more accessible than others. Hand-picking which ones to show first means a beginner's first 5 sakhis are the easiest. Not random; chosen.

### What I'd actually do in the MVP

Combine the cheap version of A, B, C, and E:

1. Add `register` (classical/modern) and `difficulty_score` (1-5) to the sakhi table — populated manually as part of the verification pass
2. Surface both as small badges on the library index
3. For now, ALL processed sakhis are "Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · difficulty 3-4" — but the badges are there so future modern content slots into the same UI without a redesign
4. In the popover, when the morpheme's lemma differs from the surface form, show "modern form: X" inline rather than buried in a note field
5. Curate the 5 free sakhis specifically as the most accessible ones — short, narrative, recurring vocabulary

This doesn't *solve* the archaic problem (the texts are what they are) but it acknowledges it and helps users navigate. Long-term answer is the Learn track's modern content, which we're not building in MVP but is the next major content investment.

### The honest framing for marketing

We should be upfront about this on the landing page. Something like:

> akhar is two things in one.
>
> The **library** is classical Punjabi literature — the sakhis of the Gurus, Bhai Vir Singh's writings, the texts our grandparents read. Beautiful, formal, demanding. Read with us.
>
> The **course** (coming soon) is modern conversational Punjabi — for learners and GCSE candidates. Simple, practical, real.

This avoids the "I came for spoken Punjabi and got 1920s prose" disappointment because we set expectations honestly upfront.

## Where I think we should go

Two concrete actions, your call on order:

**Immediate (today/tomorrow):**
1. Add `processed` flag + filter, plus `register` + `difficulty_score` badges on the library. Wires through the data model so future content slots in naturally. ~half a day's work.

**Soon (this week or next):**
2. **Build the LLM-assisted processing pipeline** so we can get from 1→50 sakhis fast. Without this, the library stays embarrassingly empty regardless of how good the UX is. ~2-3 days.

**Bigger conversation (post-MVP):**
3. Modern content track — Book 2/3-style narratives, GCSE topic packs. Multi-week commitment but it's the heritage-learner answer.

Your grandma's reaction is actually really important data — keep it in mind.

Here's what I think:

## The grandma test tells us something

If a native Punjabi speaker is reading the classical sakhis and *learning* — finding it cool because she's encountering vocabulary she didn't know — that's not a UX problem to solve. That's the **product working as intended**. The classical register is doing real pedagogical work even for fluent speakers. That's a genuine moat, not a bug.

Compare what we'd lose by simplifying: this version of akhar can be the only place online where a Sikh kid in Slough reads the same words their great-grandfather read in 1920 — and where their grandma also encounters words she hasn't seen in 50 years. That's a piece of cultural transmission no Duolingo-style product can ever offer. The "challenging" part is the value.

## Why I'd argue against writing our own easy/medium/hard versions

Three real problems with the graded-reader-of-sakhis approach:

**1. The authority problem.** A Bhai Vir Singh sakhi about Guru Nanak isn't a random folk tale — it's a literary work by a recognized author treating sacred biography. Rewriting it as "ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਇੱਕ ਚੰਗੇ ਮੁੰਡੇ ਸਨ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਸੰਦ ਸੀ।" *(Nanak ji was a good boy. He liked water.)* invites a real "who said you could?" backlash from the community. Even well-intentioned rewrites of sacred narratives have a way of looking presumptuous. Imagine a startup writing "easy versions" of Bible parables and selling them — same dynamics.

**2. The art problem.** Bhai Vir Singh's prose is literature. Our "easy version" would be the workbook summary. We'd be replacing art with paraphrase. That's a quality downgrade, not a quality upgrade. The grandma-test only works because she's encountering *the actual writing*, not someone's simplification of it.

**3. The brand-split problem.** Right now akhar means one thing: a careful archive of classical Punjabi with modern tools wrapped around it. If half the library is "real sakhis" and half is "akhar's simplified retellings," users have to mentally track which is which. The brand stops meaning a single thing.

Also a practical one: writing 3 versions of 50-405 sakhis is *years* of content production, and most of it would be us paying someone (or generating with LLM) to produce sub-Bhai-Vir-Singh prose. That's a content-arms-race we can't win.

## What I'd do instead — same problem, different solution

The beginner-can't-read-sakhi-1 problem is real. But the answer is **scaffold around the original, don't replace it**:

**Pre-reading aids per sakhi:**
- **Plot summary in modern Punjabi** (5-10 lines): "ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਮੇਹਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਸਨ..." This is a SUMMARY, not a rewrite. It says "here's what happens in this sakhi." Different category — like reading a Wikipedia plot summary before tackling a novel.
- **Vocab preview**: 8-10 key archaic words from the sakhi shown upfront so they're not blocking comprehension. "Before you read, learn these words."
- **Audio playback** (we just built it) — reading along helps comprehension enormously
- **Archaic→modern annotations** in the popover — `ਨਾਉਂ → modern: ਨਾਮ`. We already do some of this; could surface it more prominently

**Honest reader UI:**
- Era badges: "Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s"
- Difficulty stars
- "Recommended for beginners" tag on the 5 most accessible ones

**Separate "modern reading" content under the Learn wing — NOT in the sakhi library:**
- The Book 2/3-style readers we already discussed
- Original modern Punjabi narratives by us (or commissioned writers)
- Topics like family routine, school day, weekend plans — *deliberately not religious*, so there's no authority question
- This is where total beginners get easy modern content
- Clearly framed as **language learning content**, not as sakhis

This way:
- Sakhi library stays a respected classical archive (your grandma's experience preserved + cultural integrity maintained)
- Learn track has clean modern content for beginners (their easy reads exist, just not pretending to be sakhi material)
- Two audiences served, brand stays sharp on both sides

## The one place rewriting CAN work — much later

If we ever do want sakhi-style content in modern Punjabi, the right move is **commission published Sikh authors who write Punjabi-language kids' books** to write new stories in the spirit of the sakhis, in modern register, with clear authorial credit. Not "akhar's simplified Sakhi 1" but "ten new sakhis written by [respected author] for young readers, in modern Punjabi." This is artistically legitimate. People will buy it. It doesn't try to replace Bhai Vir Singh — it sits alongside him.

But this is a Year 2 content investment, not an MVP feature.

## Concrete recommendation

For now:
1. **Don't write easy/medium/hard sakhi versions.** Keep the classical originals intact.
2. **Add the scaffolds**: per-sakhi plot summaries + vocab previews + era/difficulty badges + the modern-form annotations in the popover.
3. **Keep Beginner Readers in the Learn track** as a separate future feature — modern content, no sakhi pretense, no authority issues.
4. **Position carefully**: akhar reads classical Punjabi *brilliantly*. Learning resources for absolute beginners are coming. Don't conflate.

This honours your grandma's experience, avoids the community-authority landmine, doesn't dilute the brand, and is dramatically less content-production work than writing 200+ retellings.

Does that resonate, or are you still drawn to the simplified-versions idea? I can argue for the other side too if you want to pressure-test it.

## What I got wrong

I conflated two things. There's a real difference between:

1. **"Easy version of Bhai Vir Singh's sakhi"** — taking his 1920s prose and dumbing it down. This is what I was arguing against, and I still think it's wrong.

2. **"akhar's own modern retelling of Guru Nanak's birth"** — an original work about the same well-known events, written in modern Punjabi. This is what you're actually proposing. And it's totally legitimate.

The thing is, **there's a 200-year tradition of writing new sakhi retellings**. Every generation has produced new kids' books about Guru Nanak's life — Bhai Vir Singh's "Gur Balam Sakhian" itself was a re-telling for his era. Punjabi children's publishers like Singh Brothers and many UK Gurdwaras publish their own modern sakhi books constantly. Nobody objects because nobody's trying to replace the originals — they're adding to the tradition.

So the authority problem I raised is largely an *artefact of framing*. If we frame it as "akhar's simplified Bhai Vir Singh," it looks presumptuous. If we frame it as "akhar Stories: original modern retellings of the same events that Bhai Vir Singh and many others have told," we're a contributor to a healthy tradition, not a replacer.

## What I'd build

**akhar Stories** — a small, curated, modern-Punjabi library of the most important sakhis. **Not** a translation or simplification of anyone else's work. New original tellings of the same source events.

Two libraries side-by-side:

| Library | What | Who's it for |
|---|---|---|
| **The Archive** | Bhai Vir Singh, Bhai Kahn Singh Nabha, and the published classical sakhi authors. Texts as written. | Confident readers, grandmas, anyone wanting the literary register |
| **akhar Stories** | Our own modern retellings of ~20-30 core sakhi events (Guru Nanak's birth, Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago, the journey to Mecca, Mata Khivi's langar, the founding of Khalsa, etc.) | Beginners, kids, heritage learners getting started |

Both clearly labelled with provenance. Same hover-translation + audio infrastructure. Cross-linked: at the end of an akhar Stories piece, "Read the classical Bhai Vir Singh version of this sakhi →".

This is honest, traditional, and useful. It also opens the door for **commissioning respected Punjabi authors** later to write more — that's how the Sikh publishing tradition has worked for a century.

## The right scope for MVP

Not 405. Not even 50. **The 20-30 core sakhi events every Sikh family knows.** I can list them out — these are the ones that appear in basically every Sikh children's book:

- Guru Nanak's birth at Talwandi
- Childhood: the cobra shade, the snake-and-tree miracle
- Failed business: ਸੱਚਾ ਸੌਦਾ (the true bargain, feeding sadhus)
- Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago (the honest bread vs the rich man's feast)
- Visit to Mecca (turning the feet)
- Encounter with Sajjan Thug
- Wāhi-Guru emerging
- Guru Angad receives the gaddi
- Mata Khivi & langar
- Bibi Bhani's devotion
- The martyrdom of Guru Arjan
- Guru Hargobind's transformation: miri-piri
- Bhai Gurdas's writings
- Guru Tegh Bahadur's sacrifice for Kashmiri pandits
- Guru Gobind Singh: childhood, swords, the formation of the Khalsa at Anandpur (Vaisakhi 1699)
- Chamkaur, Sirhind, the Chaar Sahibzaade
- Baba Deep Singh's martyrdom
- ...

20-30 of these is the canon. They overlap heavily with what's already in the classical corpus we have, so we'd be telling **the same stories** the archive does — just in modern accessible Punjabi.

## Production realism

What this actually costs:

- **20-30 stories × ~500 words each in modern Punjabi** = ~12-15k words of original content
- **Workflow**: Claude/GPT drafts in modern Punjabi (it's pretty good at this — we use nano-gpt already for glosses), you and/or a fluent native speaker edit for register and accuracy, audio prewarm via Chirp 3
- **Time**: ~1-2 weeks of focused writing + editing if you do it yourself, or commission for ~£30-50/story
- **Per-story production**: probably 1-2 hours including editing + audio prewarm

Realistic to ship **5 akhar Stories as part of MVP**, then add 2-3 per week post-launch until the 20-30 are done. Within 2-3 months we'd have the full core canon in modern accessible Punjabi.

## Updated answer to your original question

So my recommendation flips. The MVP plan should be:

1. **Hide unprocessed classical sakhis** (still the right call)
2. **Process ~5 classical sakhis** for the archive (the most accessible Bhai Vir Singh ones)
3. **Write ~5 akhar Stories** for the modern library (the 5 most-loved core sakhis in accessible modern Punjabi)
4. **Two clearly-labelled libraries** in the reader UI
5. Same hover-translation + audio + save-to-deck experience across both — they're parallel content libraries, not different products

Free tier sees a couple of each. Pro tier sees all of each.

Grandma reads the classical ones because she's learning new vocab from Bhai Vir Singh. A heritage parent reads akhar Stories with their kid before bedtime. Both feel like akhar is built for them.

## What I'd want to confirm before building

- **Do you (or someone in your network) feel confident writing modern-Punjabi prose**, even with LLM drafts? Or do we need to plan from day one to commission?
- **Are you comfortable being the editorial voice** for the akhar Stories — picking which events to cover first, sanity-checking the register, ensuring respectful tone?
- **List of the first 5 sakhis to write** — want to do this together? I can propose a list, you (and ideally grandma) sanity-check it.

If yes to all three, I think this is the right call and your instinct was correct. I was wrong to push back so hard.

Yeah you're right, I overthought the two-library thing. One library with smart difficulty/era labelling is better UX and stays conceptually cleaner.

## What one unified library looks like

The user opens **Library** and sees all sakhis in one place. Each entry shows:

```
ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ                              ★★    [Modern]
The birth of Guru Nanak                                    akhar Stories · 2 min read

ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ                              ★★★★  [Classical]
The birth of Guru Nanak                                    Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · 8 min read

ਬਾਲ ਜੀਵਨ - ਸਪ ਦੀ ਛਾਂ                       ★★★   [Classical]
Childhood: the snake's shade                               Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · 6 min read
```

Same story (Guru Nanak's birth) appears once as modern akhar Stories at ★★, once as the classical Bhai Vir Singh at ★★★★. User picks based on where they're at. No "two libraries" friction — it's one shelf with everything on it, labelled honestly.

Alternative grouping (probably cleaner): one row per *event*, with the versions stacked underneath:

```
The birth of Guru Nanak                          [Guru Nanak · Book 1 · Childhood]
  ★★   Modern · akhar Stories · 2 min          → Read
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · 8 min → Read

Childhood: the snake's shade
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · 6 min → Read
  (modern version coming soon)

Childhood: the cobra at midday
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh, 1920s · 7 min → Read
  ★★   Modern · akhar Stories · 3 min          → Read
```

This makes it really clear: same story, pick your level. The grouping itself is a feature ("I want to read about Guru Nanak's childhood — what versions do you have?"). And it makes the modern coverage visible without making it look like a separate product.

## Implementation impact

Schema change to support this is small. Add three columns to the `sakhis` table:
- `event_key` — text slug like `guru-nanak-birth`, links related versions
- `register` — `classical` / `modern`
- `difficulty` — int 1-5

The current 405 classical sakhis all get `register='classical'` and a hand-picked `difficulty` during the verification pass. The new akhar Stories we write get `register='modern'` and matching `event_key` to the classical they retell.

Library UI groups by `event_key` when there's more than one version, falls back to a flat row when there's only one. Filter chips at the top — "All / Easy first / Modern only / Classical only" — let users slice however they want.

## Reading experience stays the same regardless

Both versions share the same reader: parallel text + hover translation + audio + save-to-deck + sentence playback + word highlight. We're not building two readers, just two content types feeding one reader.

The only different bit is the **header info** at the top of each sakhi:
- Classical: "Bhai Vir Singh · Gur Balam Sakhian · 1920s · ★★★★"
- Modern: "akhar Original · written by [you/contributor] · 2026 · ★★"

It's also another content production project that doesn't exist today, that requires us to write modern Punjabi prose, that adds a data-model change, that delays MVP. We don't know yet whether the **existing** classical-sakhi reading experience even works for real users — because no real users have tried it.

What I'd actually do if I were you:

The product gets theoretically better with every conversation but practically worse because no learning is happening. We're not there yet but we're sliding that way. Right. 3+3, paired together. Let's do it. On the blending question — yes, I think it works, but the UX detail matters. Let me walk through it.

## The natural grouping: pair them by event

If we pick the **same 3 events** for both modern and classical versions, the library is dead simple:

```
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  GURU NANAK · CHILDHOOD                                  3 stories

  ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ                   The birth of Guru Nanak
  ★★ Easy · akhar Stories · 2 min          → Read
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh · 8 min   → Read

  ਸੱਚਾ ਸੌਦਾ                         The True Bargain
  ★★ Easy · akhar Stories · 2 min          → Read
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh · 7 min   → Read

  ਭਾਈ ਲਾਲੋ ਅਤੇ ਮਲਿਕ ਭਾਗੋ            Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago
  ★★ Easy · akhar Stories · 2 min          → Read
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh · 9 min   → Read
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

User sees 3 story titles. Each is "the same sakhi, two ways." Beginner reads the modern one first; if they enjoyed it they tap the classical version next and now they're primed — they know the events, so the harder vocabulary just adds register and depth.

This is the *killer pedagogical loop* honestly. It's exactly how language teachers use "graded readers" — read the easy version to internalise the plot + core vocab, then read the source to feel the literary register. We get that for free by pairing.

## Why this beats the alternatives

Three other layouts I considered:

**A. Flat list with badges** — every sakhi is its own row. ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ appears twice (once Easy, once Classical) at different positions. **Problem**: feels like duplicates. User doesn't realise they're the same story until they read both.

**B. "Two libraries" sidebar** — separate tabs for Modern vs Classical. **Problem**: the very thing you (rightly) pushed back against. Splits the audience, makes one side feel like the "real" library and the other like the simplification corner.

**C. Toggle switch at top of each story** — "Read as Easy / Classical." **Problem**: hides the choice from the index. Users don't see "ah there's a modern version available" until they've already opened the classical one and bounced.

The grouped layout is the only one where the choice is visible AND honest about what's available AND positions both as first-class.

## One real question: what if a story only has one version?

For MVP, the **3 events have both versions**. Future content will have asymmetry — many classical sakhis with no modern equivalent, possibly some modern-only ones for very young readers. The layout handles this fine:

```
  ਪਾਣੀ ਨਾਨਕ ਨੂੰ ਉੱਪਰ ਚੱਕ ਲਿਆ           The water lifted Nanak
  ★★★★ Classical · Bhai Vir Singh · 6 min   → Read

  ਖੇਡਾਂ                              Childhood games (coming soon)
  ★ Easy · akhar Stories                    → Notify me
```

So users see what exists, what's coming, and what they can do now. No mystery, no clutter.

## What this needs from the data model

Schema change is small. Add to `sakhis` table:

- `event_key` text (e.g., `nanak-birth`, `sacha-sauda`, `lalo-bhago`) — same value for paired versions
- `register` text (`classical` / `modern`)  
- `difficulty` int 1-5
- `source` text (`Bhai Vir Singh — Gur Balam Sakhian, 1920s` / `akhar Stories`)
- `processed` boolean (already discussed)

For the 3 new modern stories, they get NEW rows in the same `sakhis` table — not a separate table. They share the event_key with their classical counterparts. They show up in the library grouped together automatically.

This means **akhar Stories aren't a separate system** — they're just sakhis with `register='modern'` and `source='akhar Stories'`. Same reader, same audio infrastructure, same save-to-deck, same everything. The classification is in metadata, not architecture. Easy to extend later (commission more, etc.) without restructuring.

## The 3 events I'd pick

Universal-recognition tier — these are the sakhis every Sikh child knows from grandparents' bedtime stories:

1. **ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ — The Birth of Guru Nanak**
   - Talwandi, the holy birth, Pandit Hardayal naming him
   - We already have a classical version (current sakhi 1)
   - Easy modern version is short: ~150 words of accessible Punjabi

2. **ਸੱਚਾ ਸੌਦਾ — The True Bargain**  
   - Father gives young Nanak 20 rupees to invest; Nanak feeds sadhus instead
   - Classic moral/spiritual lesson, kid-friendly
   - Already in the classical corpus

3. **ਭਾਈ ਲਾਲੋ ਅਤੇ ਮਲਿਕ ਭਾਗੋ — Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago**
   - Honest carpenter's bread bleeds milk; rich man's feast bleeds blood
   - Striking imagery, very memorable
   - Already in the classical corpus

These three together = the "Guru Nanak essentials" trio. Anyone who finishes these gets the foundational stories of Sikhi. Anyone who reads all 6 (modern + classical of each) has had real reading practice across registers.

## Honest question this raises — who writes the modern versions?

I want to flag this clearly. To write 3 modern akhar Stories that don't sound like LLM slop, we need a workflow:

**Option 1: You + Claude draft + grandma sanity-checks.** You set the register and vibe, Claude drafts based on the classical Bhai Vir Singh text, you edit for flow, grandma reads it and tells you what sounds off. Workable, gets done in a few days.

**Option 2: Commission a Punjabi writer.** ~£30-100 per story from a UK-based Punjabi children's-book author. Better register, more authentic, slower (a couple of weeks). Adds cost.

**Option 3: You write them entirely yourself.** You speak Punjabi at home. If you're comfortable writing 150-200 words of prose three times, do it. Most authentic.

**My recommendation: Option 1 for MVP.** It's fast, you stay in editorial control, the LLM drafts are usable for register guidance, grandma's involvement gives them real authenticity. Move to Option 2 when we commission more stories post-launch.

The whole thing: ~3-4 days of focused work for the content side, ~1 day for the engineering. Lines up with the MVP timeline.

  "content": "import Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\nimport { statSync, readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { AKHAR_STORIES, type AkharStory } from \"@/data/akhar-stories\";\n\nconst DB_PATH = path.join(process.cwd(), \"data\", \"sakhis.db\");\nconst METADATA_PATH = path.join(process.cwd(), \"data\", \"sakhi-metadata.json\");\n\nlet _db: Database.Database | null = null;\nlet _dbInode: number | null = null;\n\n// The lipi-dict-rip build pipeline rewrites this DB out-of-band. | null;\n  // Editorial fields, populated from metadata + akhar-stories\n  register: \"classical\" | \"modern\";\n  event_key: string | null;\n  difficulty: number;\n  source: string;\n  processed: boolean;\n}\n\n// ------------ Classical sakhis (data/sakhis.db) ------------\n\ninterface RawSakhiRow {\n  id: number;\n  book_id: number;\n  primary_guru_id: number | null;\n  ordinal: number | null;\n  title_pa: string;\n  title_en: string | null;\n  body_pa: string;\n  body_en: string | null;\n  char_count_pa: number;\n  seq_in_book: number;\n  book_title_pa: string;\n  book_title_en: const meta = metadata()[String(row.id)] ?? {};\n  return {\n    ...row,\n    register: \"classical\",\n    event_key: meta.event_key ?? null,\n    difficulty: meta.difficulty ?? 3,\n    source:   seq_in_book: 0,\n    book_title_pa: \"akhar Stories\",\n    book_title_en: \"akhar Stories\",\n    book_author: \"akhar\",\n    book_year: 2026,\n    guru_name_pa: null,\n    guru_name_en: null,\n    register: \"modern\",\n    event_key: s.event_key,\n    difficulty: s.difficulty,\n    source: s.source,\n    processed: true, // modern stories are always launch-ready if defined\n  };\n}\n\nconst guru_name_en\n  FROM sakhis s\n  JOIN books b ON s.book_id = b.id\n  LEFT JOIN gurus g ON s.primary_guru_id = g.id\n`;\n\nexport function listGurus(): Guru[] {\n  const all = sakhiDb()\n ORDER BY g.id\n    `)\n    .all() as Guru[];\n  // Recompute per-guru sakhi_count using *only* processed sakhis (classical\n  // + modern) so the library doesn't promise empty corners. Used to power any list that should ONLY\n * show launch-ready content (i.e. the library, guru pages, etc.).\n */\nexport function listProcessedSakhis(): SakhiRow[] {\n  const classical = (\n    sakhiDb().prepare(`${CLASSICAL_SELECT} ORDER BY s.book_id, s.seq_in_book`).all() as RawSakhiRow[]\n  )\n    .map(decorateClassical)\n    .filter((r) => r.processed);\n  const modern = AKHAR_STORIES.map(akharToSakhiRow);\n  return [...modern, ...classical];\n}\n\n/** Same filter as listProcessedSakhis but restricted to one Guru. */\nexport function listProcessedSakhisForGuru(guruId: number): SakhiRow[] {\n  return listProcessedSakhis().filter((r) => r.primary_guru_id === guruId);\n}\n\n/**\n * Group processed sakhis by event_key for the library UI. Entries with\n * the same event_key (e.g. classical + modern of the same story) collapse\n * into one group. Entries without an event_key get their own singleton\n * group (key derived from the row id).\n */\nexport interface EventGroup {\n  event_key: string;\n  title_pa: string;     // the title to display for the group (modern preferred)\n  title_en: string | null;\n  primary_guru_id: number | null;\n  versions: SakhiRow[]; // sorted by difficulty ascending (easy first)\n}\n\nexport function listEventGroups(rows?: SakhiRow[]): EventGroup[] {\n  const all = rows ?? listProcessedSakhis();\n  const groups = new Map<string, SakhiRow[]>();\n  for (const r of all) {\n    // Singleton fallback uses the row id so we don't accidentally merge\n    // unrelated event-key-less rows.\n    const key = r.event_key ?? `__id_${r.id}`;\n    if (!groups.has(key)) groups.set(key, []);\n    groups.get(key)!.push(r);\n  }\n  return Array.from(groups.entries()).map(([key, versions]) => {\n    versions.sort((a, b) => a.difficulty - b.difficulty);\n    // Prefer modern version's title for the display heading (more\n    // accessible to the average visitor); fall back to whatever the\n    // first version has.\n    const modern = versions.find((v) => v.register === \"modern\");\n    const lead = modern ?? versions[0];\n    return {\n      event_key: key,\n      title_pa: lead.title_pa,\n      title_en: lead.title_en,\n      primary_guru_id: lead.primary_guru_id,\n      versions,\n    };\n  });\n}\n\n// ------------ Single sakhi lookup (handles both id types) ------------\n\nexport function getSakhi(id: number | string): SakhiRow | null {\n  if (typeof id === \"string\") {\n    const akhar = AKHAR_STORIES.find((s) => s.id === id);\n    return akhar ? akharToSakhiRow(akhar) : null;\n  }\n  const row = sakhiDb()\n    .prepare(`${CLASSICAL_SELECT} WHERE s.id = ?`)\n    .get(id) as RawSakhiRow | undefined;\n  if (!row) return null;\n  return decorateClassical(row);\n}\n\n/**\n * Find related sakhis (other versions of the same event) — used in the\n * reader header to show \"also available: easy modern version\" etc.\n */\nexport function sakhiSiblings(id: number | string): SakhiRow[] {\n  const current = getSakhi(id);\n  if (!current?.event_key) return [];\n  return listProcessedSakhis().filter(\n    (r) => r.event_key === current.event_key && r.id !== id,\n  );\n}\n\nexport function sakhiNeighbors(id: number | string): { prev: number | string | null; next: number | string | null } {\n  // Among processed sakhis only, ordered by listProcessedSakhis()'s\n  // canonical order (modern first then classical by book/seq).\n  const all = listProcessedSakhis();\n  const i = all.findIndex((s) => s.id === id);\n  if (i === -1) return { prev: null, next: null };\n  return {\n    prev: i > 0 ? {
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/prewarm-akhar-stories.ts",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env tsx\n/**\n * Prewarm audio for the akhar Stories (modern Punjabi retellings of\n * core sakhi events, defined in data/akhar-stories.ts).\n *\n * Synthesises one MP3 per unique Gurmukhi word + per sentence + per\n * full-text playback. Skips entries already in R2.\n *\n *   tsx scripts/prewarm-akhar-stories.ts\n */\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { AKHAR_STORIES } from \"@/data/akhar-stories\";\nimport { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { audioCacheHas, putCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\nfunction tokenizeGurmukhi(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[਀-੿]+/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    if (!seen.has(m[0])) {\n      seen.add(m[0]);\n      out.push(m[0]);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction splitSentences(text: string): string[] {\n  const re = /[^।?!]+[।?!]+[\"'”’)\\]]*|[^।?!]+$/g;\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;\n  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {\n    const s = m[0].trim();\n    if (s && !seen.has(s)) {\n      seen.add(s);\n      out.push(s);\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nasync function ensureClip(text: string): Promise<{\n  status: \"cached\" | \"synthed\" | \"failed\";\n  bytes?: number;\n  err?: string;\n}> {\n  try {\n    if (await audioCacheHas(VOICE_NAME, text)) {\n      return { status: \"cached\" };\n    }\n    const mp3 = await synthesize(text);\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text, mp3);\n    return { status: \"synthed\", bytes: mp3.length };\n  } catch (err) {\n    return {\n      status: \"failed\",\n      err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),\n    };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const clips: { kind: string; text: string }[] = [];\n  for (const story of AKHAR_STORIES) {\n    const allText = `${story.title_pa}\\n\\n${story.body_pa}`;\n    for (const w of tokenizeGurmukhi(allText)) {\n      clips.push({ kind: \"word\", text: w });\n    }\n    for (const s of splitSentences(story.body_pa)) {\n      clips.push({ kind: \"sentence\", text: s });\n    }\n  }\n  // De-dup across all stories (modern words overlap heavily)\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const dedup = clips.filter((c) => {\n    if (seen.has(c.text)) return false;\n    seen.add(c.text);\n    return true;\n  });\n\n  console.log(`Prewarming ${dedup.length} unique clips across ${AKHAR_STORIES.length} akhar Stories\\n`);\n\n  let cached = 0, synthed = 0, failed = 0;\n  const conc = 2;\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker(id: number) {\n    while (cursor < dedup.length) {\n      const i = cursor++;\n      const c = dedup[i];\n      const r = await ensureClip(c.text);\n      if (r.status === \"cached\") {\n        cached++;\n      } else if (r.status === \"synthed\") {\n        synthed++;\n        console.log(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${dedup.length}] ${c.kind.padEnd(8)} ${r.bytes}B  ${c.text.slice(0, 40)}`);\n      } else {\n        failed++;\n        console.warn(`  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${dedup.length}] FAILED ${c.kind} ${c.text}: ${r.err}`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: conc }, (_, i) => worker(i + 1)));\n  console.log(`\\ncached=${cached} synthed=${synthed} failed=${failed}`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

  "content": "// PostHog client init. Browser-side product analytics.\n//\n// Configured for the EU region (data residency) with privacy-friendly\n// defaults — autocapture stays on (we want events) but we exclude form\n// contents and disable session replay until we explicitly opt-in for\n// paid users only.\n//\n// Identify users after sign-in via identifyUser() so events tie to the\n// real Supabase user id; otherwise they're anonymous distinct_ids.\n\"use client\";\n\nimport posthog from \"posthog-js\";\n\nlet _initialized = false;\n\nexport function initPostHog() {\n  if (_initialized || typeof window === \"undefined\") return;\n  const key = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY;\n  const host = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST;\n  if (!key || !host) return;\n\n  posthog.init(key, {\n    api_host: host,\n    person_profiles: \"identified_only\",  // don't create profiles for anonymous\n    capture_pageview: false,             // we'll capture pageviews via the route hook\n    capture_pageleave: true,\n    autocapture: {\n      // Strip form field contents from event metadata\n      element_attribute_ignorelist: [\"value\", \"data-value\"],\n    },\n    disable_session_recording: true,     // turn on later for paid users only\n    persistence: \"localStorage\",          // not cookies → no consent banner needed\n    enable_recording_console_log: false,\n  });\n  _initialized = true;\n}\n\nexport function identifyUser(userId: string, traits?: Record<string, unknown>) {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\" || !_initialized) return;\n  posthog.identify(userId, traits);\n}\n\nexport function resetUser() {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\" || !_initialized) return;\n  posthog.reset();\n}\n\nexport function capture(event: string, props?: Record<string, unknown>) {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\" || !_initialized) return;\n  posthog.capture(event, props);\n}\n\nexport { posthog };\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/components/Analytics.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Initializes PostHog on first client render + captures a pageview on\n// every route change (App Router). Mounted once in app/layout.tsx so it\n// runs everywhere without per-page wiring.\n//\n// We also lazy-identify the signed-in user once on init. The Supabase\n// session is read via a cheap /api/me lookup (see app/api/me/route.ts)\n// rather than threading the user object through every page.\n\nimport { useEffect } from \"react\";\nimport { usePathname, useSearchParams } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { capture, identifyUser, initPostHog } from \"@/lib/posthog\";\n\nexport default function Analytics() {\n  const pathname = usePathname();\n  const searchParams = useSearchParams();\n\n  // Init once on first render\n  useEffect(() => {\n    initPostHog();\n    // Best-effort identify — if signed in, link events to the user id.\n    fetch(\"/api/me\")\n      .then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null))\n      .then((u: { id?: string; email?: string } | null) => {\n        if (u?.id) identifyUser(u.id, { email: u.email });\n      })\n      .catch(() => {});\n  }, []);\n\n  // Pageview on every route change\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!pathname) return;\n    const url = pathname + (searchParams?.toString() ? `?${searchParams}` : \"\");\n    capture(\"page_viewed\", { path: pathname, url });\n  }, [pathname, searchParams]);\n\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

## Verification checklist

### PostHog (5 min after preview build)
1. Hard-reload the preview URL once
2. Open **https://eu.posthog.com → Activity** (left sidebar) → "Live events"
3. You should see `page_viewed` events flowing in within ~30 seconds of you visiting any page on the preview
4. ✅ If yes — PostHog is live

### Sentry (test once)
1. On the preview, open browser DevTools → Console
2. Type: `throw new Error("sentry test from preview")`
3. Open **https://sentry.io → Projects → akhar → Issues**
4. Within 30-60 seconds you should see "sentry test from preview"
5. ✅ If yes — Sentry is live

### Supabase email OTP
1. On preview `/login`, enter your email → "Send 6-digit code"
2. Check your inbox
3. **Pass**: email contains a 6-digit code, no clickable link → template change worked
4. **Fail**: email contains a magic link → go back to Supabase email template, redo step 1, save again

### Google sign-in
1. On preview `/login`, click "Continue with Google"
2. **Pass**: redirects to Google's account picker, you sign in, lands back on akhar signed in → Google OAuth set up correctly
3. **Fail with "provider not enabled"**: revisit Supabase Auth → Providers → Google → confirm toggle ON + Client ID + Secret saved
4. **Fail with "redirect_uri_mismatch"**: GCP OAuth client's redirect URIs don't include `https://fsahapmiupwfljajyngw.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback` — add it

### Apple sign-in (still on hold)
- Will work after Apple Support resolves your enrollment + you set up the Sign in with Apple Service ID in Apple Developer console + paste credentials into Supabase. Not testable yet.

## One thing you'll need to do for production deploys

Right now PostHog + Sentry keys live in `.env.local` which works on dev preview because Vercel's preview deployments inherit env vars from the project. **But you need to add them to Vercel's project env vars too** so prod builds get them:

1. Vercel dashboard → akhar project → **Settings → Environment Variables**
2. Add these three (apply to Production + Preview + Development):
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` = `phc_miCskiHHoGfkmDj2zYqoGmnPUo8qCuMP7Ar7CePb5Ckv`
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` = `https://eu.i.posthog.com`
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` = `https://558f39e1cb583e8ec133d2b3424802c4@o4511485846749184.ingest.de.sentry.io/4511485866868816`
3. Save → trigger a redeploy (push any commit or use "Redeploy" button in Vercel)

Without this, analytics + error tracking only work on dev preview, not on prod when we point akhar.io.

mp3 = await synthesize(t.text);\n            await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, t.text, mp3);\n            synthed++;\n            console.log(\n              `  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${audioTargets.length}] ${t.kind.padEnd(8)} ${mp3.length}B  ${t.text.slice(0, 40)}`,\n            );\n          } catch (err) {\n            failed++;\n            console.warn(\n              `  [w${id} ${i + 1}/${audioTargets.length}] FAILED ${t.kind} ${t.text}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err}`,\n            );\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: conc }, (_, i) => worker(i + 1)));\n      console.log(`\\nAudio fill done. synthed=${synthed} failed=${failed}`);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

Fix: server-side prefetch all morphemes for the sakhi's words on page load, pass them down as props. Zero fetches needed at hover time.

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/morpheme-cache.ts",
  "old_string": "export function markMorphemeProcessed(script: string, surface: string): boolean {\n  const r = db()\n    .prepare(\n      `UPDATE morpheme_cache SET processed = 1, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n       WHERE script = ? AND surface = ?`,\n    )\n    .run(script, surface);\n  return r.changes > 0;\n}",
  "new_string": "export function markMorphemeProcessed(script: string, surface: string): boolean {\n  const r = db()\n    .prepare(\n      `UPDATE morpheme_cache SET processed = 1, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n       WHERE script = ? AND surface = ?`,\n    )\n    .run(script, surface);\n  return r.changes > 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Batch-fetch morphemes for many surface forms at once. Used by pages\n * that render text with hover-lookups so the popover can show instantly\n * instead of round-tripping /api/morpheme on every hover.\n *\n * Returns a map keyed by surface — missing words are simply absent\n * from the map (caller falls back to the existing fetch flow).\n */\nexport function getCachedMorphemesForWords(\n  surfaces: string[],\n  script = \"gurmukhi\",\n): Record<string, Morpheme> {\n  if (surfaces.length === 0) return {};\n  // De-dup first so the IN-clause isn't 500 long when the same word\n  // appears 10 times in a sakhi.\n  const unique = Array.from(new Set(surfaces));\n  // SQLite's parameter limit is generous (32k by default) — well above\n  // any sakhi's word count, so one query is fine.\n  const placeholders = unique.map(() => \"?\").join(\",\");\n  const rows = db()\n    .prepare(\n      `SELECT surface, morpheme_json, processed\n       FROM morpheme_cache\n       WHERE script = ? AND surface IN (${placeholders})`,\n    )\n    .all(script, ...unique) as {\n      surface: string;\n      morpheme_json: string;\n      processed: number;\n    }[];\n  const out: Record<string, Morpheme> = {};\n  for (const r of rows) {\n    const m = JSON.parse(r.morpheme_json) as Morpheme;\n    out[r.surface] = { ...m, processed: r.processed === 1 };\n  }\n  return out;\n}"
}

ਚੂੜ੍ਹਕਾਣੋਂ ਦੇ ਲਾਗੇ ਭੁਖੇ ਬੈਠੇ ਸੰਤਾਂ ਤਪੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀਹ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਦਾ ਆਟਾ, ਚਾਉਲ, ਦਾਲਾਂ, ਛੋਲੇ ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਖਾਣ ਪੀਣ ਦੀਆਂ ਚੀਜ਼ਾਂ ਬਾਲਕ ਉਮਰਾ ਦੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਲੈ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਸਨ, ਤੇ ਫੇਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਨਗਰ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਪਏ ਸਨ। ਜਦੋਂ ਨਗਰ ਨੇੜੇ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ, ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬਾਲਕ ਨੇ, ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਵਰੇਸ* ਵਿਚ ਸਨ, ਆਖਿਆ: ਤੂੰ ਜਾਹ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਤੇ ਮੈਂ ਅਜੇ ਘਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਾ ਆਪਣੇ। ਸੋ ਬਾਲਾ ਤਾਂ ਗਿਆ ਘਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੇ ਸੁਹਣਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਬਾਲਕਾ ਬੈਠ ਰਿਹਾ, ਬਾਹਰ ਇਕ ਸੁੱਕਾ ਪਿਆ ਸੀ ਤਲਾ, ਉਸ ਦੇ ਪੌੜਾਂ ਉਤੇ। ਅੱਖਾਂ ਲਈਓ ਸੁ ਮੀਟ ਤੇ ਸੋਚੇ: ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਦੁਖ ਕਿਉਂ ਹੈ? ਕੋਈ ਭੁੱਖਾ ਹੈ, ਕੋਈ ਰੋਗੀ ਹੈ, ਕੋਈ ਨੰਗਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਮਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਤਾਂ ਰੋਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਦੁਖ ਦੂਰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋਵੇ ? ਹੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਹੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ! ਤੂੰ ਕਰ ਦੂਰ ਦੁੱਖ ! ‘ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ', ' ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ' ਕਰਦੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਅੰਦਰ ਹੀ ਅੰਦਰ ਚੰਬੜ ਗਏ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕੋਈ ਬਾਲ ਓਦਰਿਆ ਹੋਵੇ ਤਾਂ ਮਾਂ ਆਈ ਵੇਖ ਕੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਚੰਬੜ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। *੧੨ ਬਰਸਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਤੇ ੨੦ ਤਕ ਦੇ ਬਾਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਆਖ ਲਈਦਾ ਹੈ

ਓਧਰ ਬਾਲਾ ਘਰ ਗਿਆ ਆਪਣੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ ਤੱਕਿਆ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਦੇ ਪੁਤਰ ਨਾਲ, ਤਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਜਾ ਦੱਸਿਆ: ਜੋ ਬਾਲਾ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਏ ਘਰ। ਬਾਬੇ ਨੇ ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਸਦਵਾ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਘਰ ਆਏ ਨੂੰ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ, ਤਾਂ ਓਸ ਨੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਆਇਆ ਤਾਂ ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੈ ਤੁਸਾਂ ਦਾ ਬੇਟਾ, ਪਰ ਨਗਰੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਖੜੋ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ ਤਾਲ ਕੰਢੇ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਘੱਲ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਸਾਸੂ ਘਰ। ਤਦ ਕਾਲੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਸੌਦਾ ਖਰੀਦਣ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਸੀ ਤੁਸਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਘਿਨਿਆ ਸੌਦਾ? ਤਾਂ ਓਸ ਕਿਹਾ: ਸਾਧਾਂ ਫਕੀਰਾਂ ਭੁੱਖਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਖੁਲਾ ਦਿਤੇ ਸੁ ਰੂਪੱਯੇ, ਆਖਦਾ ਸੀ ਇਹ ਹੈ ਖਰਾ ਸੌਦਾ, ਇਹ ਹੈ ਸੱਚਾ ਸੌਦਾ। ਇਹ ਸੁਣ ਕੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਚੜ੍ਹ ਗਿਆ ਗੁੱਸਾ, ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਲੈਕੇ ਟੁਰ ਪਏ ਲੱਭਣ। ਓਹ ਘਰੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਨਿਕਲੇ ਤਾਂ ਅੰਮਾਂ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਾ* ਨੇ ਨੌਕਰ ਘੱਲੇ ਮਗਰ ਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਆਪਣੀ ਧੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਨੂੰ ਜੋ ਮਤਾਂ ਪਿਉ ਮਾਰੇ ਤਾਂ ਧੀ ਕੋਲ ਹੋਈ ਤਾਂ ਛੁਡਾ ਲਏਗੀ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਚੜ੍ਹੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਤੋਂ। ਸੋ ਇਸੇ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਹੀ ਹੋਈ। ਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਜਾ ਡਿੱਠਾ ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ, ਜੋ ਅੱਖਾਂ ਮੀਟੀ ਬੈਠਾ ਸੀ, ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਦੁਖ ਆਪਣੇ ਵਡੇ ਬਾਬਲ-ਰੱਬ-ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਦਾ। ਗੁੱਸੇ ਭਰੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਬਾਹੋਂ ਪਕੜ ਉਠਾਇਆ, ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ ਖੜਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਤੇ ਵੱਧ ਘੱਟ ਬੋਲਿਆ, ਮਾੜੇ ਬਚਨ ਆਖੇ ਤੇ ਕੱਸਕੇ ਚਪੇੜਾਂ ਮਾਰੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਸੱਜੀ ਗਲ੍ਹ ਤੇ, ਦੋ ਮਾਰੀਆਂ ਖੱਬੀ ਗਲ੍ਹ ਤੇ,-ਪੱਟੇ ਜਾਣਿਆਂ! ਪੱਟ ਸੁੱਟਿਆ ਈ ਮੇਰਾ ਝੁੱਗਾਂ। ਹੁਣ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਭਰੇ ਦੇ ਕਰੜੇ ਹੱਥ ਉਠ ਹੀ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਪਈ ਭੈਣ ਦੌੜਦੀ ਦੌੜਦੀ ਤੇ ਚੰਬੜ ਗਈ ਬਾਬਲ ਨੂੰ ਤੇ ਹਿਲੋਰਾ ਦੇ ਕੇ ਪਰਾਂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਸੁ। ਸੋ ਪਰੇ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਉੱਲਰੇ ਹੱਥ ਬੀ। ਬੀਬੀ ਬੋਲੀ: ‘ਨਾਂ ਮੇਰੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਨਾ, ਮੇਰੇ ਵੀਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਮਾਰ, ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ ਮੇਰੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ ! *ਇਹ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਮਾਂ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਦਾ।

ਹੋਰ ਲੋਕੀ ਬੀ ਸੁਣਕੇ ਆ ਗਏ ਸਨ, ਨੌਕਰ ਬੀ ਬੀਬੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਨਾਲ ਆਏ ਸਨ, ਸਭ ਨੇ ਵਰਜਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਬੇ ਦੇ ਮਾਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੱਥ ਲਮਕ ਪਏ ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਰਨੋਂ ਰੁਕ ਗਏ। ਹੁਣ ਬਾਹੋਂ ਧੱਕਕੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਜੀ ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬੇਟੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਟੁਰੇ। ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬੇਟੇ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਬੋਲੇ ਨਾ ਕੂਏ। ਗੁਲਾਬਾਂ ਵਰਗੀਆਂ ਸੁਹਣੀਆਂ ਗਲਾਂ ਤੇ ਨੀਲ ਪੈ ਗਏ, ਤੇ ਦੋ ਚਾਰ ਅੱਥਰੂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੀਲਾਂ ਦੇ ਉਤੇ ਦੀ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਵਗ ਪਏ ਅਜੇ ਕੁਝ ਕਦਮ ਹੀ ਗਏ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਰਾਇਬੁਲਾਰ ਦੇ ਆਦਮੀ ਆ ਪਹੁੰਚੇ, ਬੋਲੇ- ਹੇ ਮਹਿਤਾ! ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੁੱਤ ਸਮੇਤ ਰਾਇ ਦੇ ਸੱਦਿਆ ਹੈ। ਤਦ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਰਾਇ ਵਲ ਜਾਣਾ ਪਿਆ, ਦਿਲ ਤਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਾਸੂ ਕਰਦਾ, ਪਰ ਮਾਲਕ ਦਾ ਹੁਕਮ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਮੋੜਦਾ। ਜਦ ਰਾਇ ਦੇ ਦਰ ਪਹੁੰਚੇ ਤਾਂ ਉਹ ਅਗੋਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਤੇ ਨੀਲ ਪਏ ਹੋਏ ਤੇ ਅੱਥਰੂ ਵਗੇ ਹੋਏ ਦੇਖਕੇ ਆਪ ਪਿਆ। ਉਠਕੇ ਜੱਫੀ ਪਾ ਲਈਓ ਸੂ, ਤੇ ਮੱਥਾ ਚੁੰਮ ਲਿਓਸੂ। ਪਿਠ ਤੇ ਹੱਥ ਫੇਰ ਛਾਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਲਾਇਓਸੂ, ਆਖਿਓ ਸੁਰਬ ਦੇ ਬਾਲਕੇ ! ਸਭ ਕੁਛ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ, ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ, ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ।” ਫੇਰ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਨੂੰ ਕਹਿਣ ਲਗਾ, ‘ਕਾਲੂ ਤੂੰ ਬੜਾ ਬੇ-ਤਰਸ ਹੈਂ, ਇਕੋ ਪੁੱਤ, ਉਹ ਰਬ ਦਾ ਬਾਲਕਾ, ਜੰਮਦਾ ਸੰਤ ਵਲੀ,* ਕਲਾਵਾਨ। ਤੂੰ ਬੇ-ਤਰਸ, ਨੀਲ ਪਾ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਨੀ ਮਾਰ ਮਾਰ ਕੇ ਵਲੀ ਅੱਲਾ ਦੇ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਤੇ, ਨਿਰਦਈ! ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਡਰ ਨਾ ਮੇਰਾ ਭਉ, ਨਾ ਲੋਕ ਲਾਜ।” ਫੇਰ ਭੁੱਬ ਮਾਰਕੇ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ, ‘ਕੀਹ ਕਰਾਂ, ਮੈਂ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ! ਹਾਇ ਮੈਂ ਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਤਾਂ ਅਜ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਰੱਖ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਏਸ ਰਬ ਪ੍ਯਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਤੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੇਵਾ, ਹੁਣ ਰੱਖਾਂ ਤਾਂ ਜਗਤ ਕਹੇਗਾ, ਜੋਰੋ ਜੋਰੀ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਸੂ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ।” *ਵਲੀ-ਰਬ ਦਾ ਪਿਆਰਾ।

ਤਦ ਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ-ਰਾਇ ਜੀ ਇਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਰਤੂਤਾਂ ਬੀ ਸੋਚੋ, ਪੱਟ ਸੁੱਟਿਆ ਸੂ ਇਸ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ। ਰਾਇ ਕਿਹਾ: ' ਆਹ ਲੈ ਵੀਹ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਤੇ ਪੱਟਿਆ ਨਾ ਜਾਹ, ਪਰ ਖ਼ਬਰਦਾਰ ਜੇ ਕਦੇ ਫੇਰ ਹੱਥ ਚੁੱਕਿਆ ਬੱਚੇ ਉਤੇ। ਤੂੰ ਹਿਸਾਬ ਕਰਕੇ ਦੱਸ ਜਿਤਨਾ ਧਨ ਤੇਰਾ ਅਜ ਤਾਈਂ ਬੱਚੇ ਨੇ ਗੁਆਇਆ ਹੈ, ਮੈਂ ਭਰ ਦਿਆਂ ਤੇ ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਪੈਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰ। ਦੇਖ, ਜਿਤਨੀ ਦੌਲਤ ਮੇਰੇ ਘਰ ਹੈ ਏਸ ਦੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੋਈ ਹੈ, ਜਿਤਨੀ ਮਾਇਆ ਜਗਤ ਵਿਚ ਹੈ ਏਸ ਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਅੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਮੋਦੀ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਅੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਪੁੱਤ ਹੈ ਪਿਕਾਂਬਰ* ਹੈ। ਕਾਲੂ! ਦੇਖ ਜਗਤ ਇਸ ਦਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਸੱਜੇ ਹੱਥ ਬੈਠਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹਈ। ਤੂੰ ਦੇਖੇਂਗਾ ਕਿ ਨਾ ਪਰ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਨਾਉਂ ਤੇ ਲੱਖਾਂ ਰੁਪਏ ਸਦਕੇ ਕਰਿਆ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਜਿਸ ਮਾਇਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੂੰ ਰੋਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਜਗਤ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਨਾਂ ਤੇ ਵਾਰ ਵਾਰ ਸੱਟੇਗਾ। ਜਿਥੇ ਜਿਥੇ ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਧਰੇਗਾ ਮਾਇਆ ਉਥੇ ਲੇਟਣੀਆਂ ਲਿਆ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਖਬਰਦਾਰ ਜੋ ਤੂੰ ਕਦੇ ਫਿਟੇ ਮੂੰਹ ਬੀ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ ਤਾਂ! ਤੇਰੇ ਘਰ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਤਾਂ ਟੋਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੇ ਆਖੇਂ ਮੈਂ ਫੇਰ ਨਾ ਮਾਰਸਾਂ। ਤਦ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਰਮ ਆਈ, ਰਾਇ ਨੂੰ ਹਥ ਜੋੜਕੇ ਅਖਿਓਸੁ ਹੁਣ ਬਖਸ਼ੋ ਫੇਰ ਨਾ ਕਰਸਾਂ ਤੇ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਬੀ ਮੋੜ ਦਿਤਿਓਸੁ। ਤਾਂ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਟੋਰਿਆ ਤੇ ਸੁਹਣਾ ਬਾਲਕ ਆ ਮਾਂ ਭੈਣ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਿਆ। (ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਦਾ ਵਿਆਹ) ਥੋੜੇ ਦਿਨ ਮਗਰੋਂ ਐਸੀ ਗਲ ਬਣ ਗਈ ਕਿ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਦੀ ਕੁੜਮਾਈ ਹੋ ਗਈ। ਬਿਆਸਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਾਰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ ਨਗਰ ਸੀ, ਏਥੇ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਸੀ ਸੂਬੇ ਦਾ ਵੱਡਾ ਹਾਕਮ ਦੌਲਤ ਖਾਂ ਲੋਧੀ ਪਠਾਣ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਪਾਸ ਸੀ ਇਕ ਨੌਕਰ-ਜੈ ਰਾਮਦਾਸ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ। ਇਹਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਜੁਆਨ ਸੀ, ਗੱਭਰੂ। ਇਹ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੀ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਨੌਕਰੀ ਤੇ ਸੀ ਵਡਾ *ਜੋ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ਰ ਜੀ ਵਲੋਂ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਆਵੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਪੈਗ਼ੰਬਰ। ਤੇ ਆਮ ਬੋਲੀ ਵਿਚ ਆਖੀਦਾ ਹੈ-ਪਿਕਾਂਬਰ।

ਇਤਬਾਰੀ ਨਵਾਬ ਦਾ। ਇਹ ਕਿਸੇ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਕੰਮ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਆਇਆ ਤਾਂ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਦੀ ਕੁੜਮਾਈ ਹੋ ਗਈ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ। ਇਹ ਉ ਵੀ ਬਹੁਤ ਭਲਾ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਸਭ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਸੁਖੀ ਸੀਗਾ। ਫੇਰ ਵਿਆਹ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ ਤੇ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਚਲੀ ਗਈ ਸਾਹੁਰੇ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ ਪੁਰ। ਜੇ ਗੋਂਦਵਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਬੇੜੀ ਵਿਚ ਬੈਠਕੇ ਹੋ ਜਾਈਏ ਬਿਆਸ ਨਦੀ ਤੋਂ ਪਾਰ ਤਾਂ ਕੁਛ ਦੂਰ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਏ ਸੁਲਤਾਨ ਪੁਰ' ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਤਾਂਈਂ ਵਸਦਾ ਏ। ਰਾਇ ਬੁਲਾਰ ਰੱਬੀ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਸੁਖੀ ਵੇਖਣਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਸੀ, ਪਰ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਦਾ ਸੁਭਾਉ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਵਟਾਂਦਾ ਤੇ ਰਾਇ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਾਸ ਬੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਗੱਭਰੂ ਹੋ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ ਮਸੂ ਭੇਂ ਹੋ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ। ਮਸੂ ਭੇਂ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਮੁੱਛਾਂ ਦਾ ਰਤਾ ਰਤਾ ਦਿੱਸਣ ਲਗ ਪੈਣਾ। ਇਹ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਏ ਜੁਆਨੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ। ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿਚ ਸੋਚੀ ਕਿ ਜੇ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਭੇਜ ਦੇਈਏ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ, ਜਾ ਰਹੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਭੈਣ ਪਾਸ ਤਾਂ ਸੁਖੀ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੀ, ਰੋਜ਼ ਰੋਜ਼ ਦੀ ਕਲਹਾ ਮਿਟ ਜਾਸੀ। ਸੋ ਜੈਰਾਮ ਦਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਜਦ ਓਹ ਫੇਰ ਤਿਲਵੰਡੀ ਆਯਾ, ਤਾਂ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਾਸ ਲੈ ਜਾਓ ਤੇ ਓਥੇ ਕੋਈ ਸੁਖੱਲਾ ਜਿਹਾ ਕੰਮ ਲੁਆ ਦਿਓ, ਦੋਵੇਂ ਭੈਣ ਭਰਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਸੁਖੀ ਰਹਿਸਣ। ਤੁਸੀਂ ਬੀ ਭਾਗਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੋ, ਵਲੀ ਅੱਲਾ* ਨੂੰ ਪਾਸ ਰੱਖਕੇ। ਮੇਰੀ ਨਗਰੀ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਦੁਖ ਮਿਲਣਾ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੀ'। ਇਹ ਗੱਲ ਜੈਰਾਮ ਦੇ ਦਿਲ ਲੱਗੀ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਨੇ ਹਾਂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ। ਜੀ ਵਿਚ ਖੁਸ਼ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਮੇਰੇ ਪਾਸ ਰਹੇਗਾ। *ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਮਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਪਿਆਰਾ। ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਰੱਬ ਨੇ ਵਡਾ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਹੋਵੇ। ਪੂਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਸੰਤ।

ਇਸ ਘਰ ਵਿਚ-ਨਿੱਕੇ ਜਿਹੇ ਕੱਚੇ ਕੋਠੇ ਵਿਚ-ਤ੍ਰੈ ਕੁ ਦਿਨ ਰਹਿੰਦਿਆਂ ਹੋਏ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਤੁਰਨੇ ਨੂੰ ਤਿਆਰ ਹੋਣ ਲਗੇ, ਪਰ ਲਾਲੋ ਨੇ ਹੱਥ ਜੋੜੇ, ਅੱਖਾਂ ਪਿਆਰ ਨਾਲ ਹੰਝੂ ਭਰੀਆਂ ਹੋ ਗਈਆਂ ਤੇ ਆਖਿਆ-ਐਡੀ ਛੇਤੀ ਨਾ ਕਰੋ, ਕੁਛ ਦਿਨ ਹੋਰ ਠਹਿਰੋ, ਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦਿਓ ਤਾਂ ਜਾਓ।" ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਕੇ ਹੋਰ ਠਹਿਰ ਪਏ। ਹੁਣ ਇਉਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਹੋ ਗਈ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਤੜਕੇ ਹੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਚਲੇ ਜਾਣਾ ਤੇ ਓਥੇ ਯਾ ਤਾਂ ਰੋੜਾਂ ਦੀ ਥੜੀ ਉਤੇ ਯਾ ਰੇਤੇ ਦੀ ਥਲੀ ਉਤੇ ਚੌਂਕੜਾ ਮਾਰ ਬੈਠਣਾ, ਆਪਣੇ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਵਿਚ ਲਗੇ ਬੈਠੇ ਰਹਿਣਾ। ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਲੋਕੀ ਤਪ ਕਰਨਾ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਸਰੀਰ ਨਾਲ ਨਿਰਾ ਤਪ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਨ ਕਰਦੇ, ਉਹ ਤਾਂ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਧਾਰ ਕੇ ਬੈਠਦੇ ਸੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਵਿਚ। ਨਗਰ ਵਿਚ ਮਸ਼ਹੂਰ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ ਕਿ ਇਕ ਵੇਦੀ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਬੜੀ ਭਾਰੀ ਤਪਸ੍ਯਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਾ ਕੁਛ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਨਾ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਬਾਹਰ ਰੇਤਿਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਉੱਗੇ ਅੱਕ ਦੇ ਫੁੱਲਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਪੰਜ ਚਾਰ ਕਰੂੰਬਲੀਆਂ ਖਾ ਕੇ ਇਕੋ ਜਗ੍ਹਾ ਬੈਠਾ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸਮਾਧੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੀ, ਪਰ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਇਹ ਆਖਣ, ‘ਦੇਖੋ ਵੇਦੀ ਹੋਕੇ ਤਰਖਾਣ ਨੀਵੀਂ ਜਾਤ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਨਾਲ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਮਰਾਸੀ ਕਿ ਡੂੰਮ ਰਖਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੂ। ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ਜੇ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਿਚ ਕਿਸੇ ਕੰਮੇ ਜਾਏ ਤਾਂ ਲੋਕੀਂ ਇਥੋਂ ਤਾਂਈਂ ਆਖਣ ਕਿ ਅਹੁ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਜੇ ਕੁਰਾਹੀਏ ਦਾ ਡੂੰਮ ਜੋ ਜਾਤਿ ਕੁਜਾਤਿ ਰਲਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਜੇ।” ਸੋ ਕੁਛ ਦਿਨਾਂ ਪਿਛੋਂ ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ਤਾਂ ਆਗਿਆ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਘਰ ਚਲਾ ਗਿਆ ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਥੇ ਹੀ ਟਿਕੇ ਰਹੇ। ਜਿਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ *ਰੇਤ ਅੰਕ ਆਹਾਰ ਕਰਿ ਰੋੜਾਂ ਦੀ ਫਿਰਿ ਕਰੀ ਵਿਛਾਈ। ਭਾਰੀ ਕਰੀ ਤਪੱਸਿਆ ਵਡੇ ਭਾਗ ਹਰਿ ਸਿਉ ਬਣਿ ਆਈ। ਭਾਗ

ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਰੱਤੇ ਬੈਠਦੇ ਸੇ ਉਹ ਥਾਉਂ ਹੁਣ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਰੋੜੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਾਉਂ ਹੈ, ਉਸ ਪਾਸ ਯਾਦਗੀਰੀ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਬੀ ਹੈ। ਏਥੇ ਭਾਈ ਲਾਲੋ ਦੀ ਖੂਹੀ ਬੀ ਹੈ। ਦੋ ਦੀਵਾਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਕਾਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਲਾਗ ਵਾਰ ਹੈ। ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਪਾਸ ਹੈਸੀ ਫੇਰ ਅਕਾਲੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਕਬਜ਼ਾ ਕੀਤਾ। ਹੁਣ ਦੇਸ਼ ਵੰਡ ਦੇ ਮਗਰੋਂ ਪਤਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਿ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਨੇ ਐਸੇ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਿੰਞ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ। ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕਿੰਨਾ ਚਿਰ ਏਥੇ ਟਿਕੇ। ਕੁਛ ਲੋਕੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੇਲੇ ਆ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਤੇ ਸਿਖ ਮਤਿ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ; ਪਰ ਇਕ ਦਿਨ ਦੋ ਚਾਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਸਮਝਾਉਣ ਆਏ ਕਿ ਜਾਤ ਦਾ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਰਖੋ, ਤੁਸੀਂ ਉੱਚ ਕੁਲ ਵੇਦਾਚਾਰਯ-ਵੇਦੀ ਹੋ। ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਿਰੁੱਤਰ ਹੋ ਗਏ। ਆਖਰ ਲੋਕੀ ਨਾਨਕ ਤਪਾਂ ਕਹਿਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ । ਕਈ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ‘ਨਾਨਕ ਸ਼ਾਹ' ਆਖਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ। ਆਮ ਲੋਕੀਂ ਤਾਂ ਦੂਰੋਂ ਨੇੜਿਓਂ ਆਉਂਦੇ, ਸਤਿਸੰਗ ਦਾ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ, ਪਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਤੇ ਮੁਲਾਣੇ ਖਿਝਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਡਰ ਪਿਆ ਕਿ ਜੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਲੋਕ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਗਰ ਲਗ ਪਏ ਤਾਂ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਕੌਣ ਪੁੱਛੇਗਾ ? ਏਮਨਾਬਾਦ ਵਿਚ ਇਕ ਪਠਾਣ ਖਾਨ ਹਾਕਮ ਸੀ, ਮਾਨੋ ਰਾਜਾ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਉਸਦਾ ਕਾਰਦਾਰ ਸੀ। ਸੋ ਮੁਲਾਣਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਤਾਂ ਨਵਾਬ ਪਾਸ ਤੇ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਨੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਪਾਸ ਚੁਗਲੀਆਂ ਕਰਨੀਆਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ। ਹੋਰ ਬੀ ਉਪ੍ਰਾਲੇ ਕੀਤੇ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਏਥੋਂ ਉਠ ਜਾਣ। ਇਕ ਦਿਨ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਜਦ ਕਿ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਕੀਤਾ। ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਤੇ ਸਾਧੂਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਾਹਲ ਪੂੜੇ, ਪੂੜੀਆਂ, ਖੀਰਾਂ, ਲੁੱਚੀਆਂ, ਕਚੌਰੀਆਂ ਆਦਿ ਭੋਜਨ ਖੁਆਉਣੇ। ਸੋ ਇਹ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਦੇ ਮਲਕ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਾਧੂਆਂ ਤੇ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਦੇ ਘੱਲੇ ਗਏ। ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਖੁਣਸ ਮਾਰਿਆਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਬੀ ਸੱਦ ਘੱਲਿਆ। ਜਾਣਦੇ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਆਉਣਗੇ ਤਾਂ *ਗੁੱਸਾ, ਸਾਡ਼ਾ, ਈਰਖਾ।

ਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚੜ੍ਹੇਗਾ। ਸੋ ਐਸਾ ਹੀ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਭੋਜਨ ਖਾਣ ਨਾ ਗਏ। ਤਦ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਚੁਗਲੀ ਵੱਟੀ ਕਿ ਦੇਖੋ ਮਲਕ ਜੀ, ਨਾਨਕ ਤਪਾ ਕੇਡਾ ਹੰਕਾਰੀ ਹੈ, ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਿਉਤਾ ਬੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੁ ਮੰਨਿਆ। ਭਾਗੋ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚੜ੍ਹ ਗਿਆ, ਉਸਨੇ ਫੇਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਕਿ ਜਾਓ ਮੇਰੇ ਪਾਸ ਸੱਦਕੇ ਲਿਆਓ। ਪਰ ਜਦ ਸੱਦਣ ਲਈ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਗਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਆਪ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ, “ ਅਸੀਂ ਫਕੀਰ ਲੋਕ ਹਾਂ, ਸਾਡਾ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਨਾਲ ਕੀ ਕੰਮ।” ਜਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਚੁਗਲ-ਵੱਟਾਂ ਨੇ ਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਹੋਰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚਾੜ੍ਹਿਆ। ਤਦ ਮਲਕ ਨੇ ਪੰਜਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫੇਰ ਘੋਲਿਆ ਕਿ ਨਾ ਆਵੇ ਤਾਂ ਫੜ ਲਿਆਓ। ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਹੁਕਮ ਸੁਣਕੇ ਹੱਸੇ ਤੇ ਟੁਰ ਪਏ। ਅੱਗੇ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਮੁਲਕ ਉਦਾਲੇ ਲੋਕ ਬੈਠੇ ਸਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਅੰਦਰ ਲੰਘਕੇ ਚੁਪ ਖੜੇ ਹੋ ਗਏ। ਤਦ ਮੁਲਕ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ-‘ਹੇ ਤਪਾ, ਤੂੰ ਸ਼ੂਦਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਰੋਟੀਆਂ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਤੇ ਸੁੱਚੇ ਤੇ ਪਵਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜਾਂ ਤੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ! ਫਿਰ ਤੂੰ ਡੂੰਮਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਵਰਤਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਤੇ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਤਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ* ਇਹ ਕੀ ਗਲ ਹੈ?” ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ, “ ਅਸੀਂ ਦਰਵੇਸ਼ ਹਾਂ ਰਬ ਦੇ, ਜਿਥੋਂ ਦੇਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਖਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਾਂ।” ਮਲਕ ਬੋਲਿਆ, ‘ਫੇਰ ਮੇਰਾ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਬੀ ਖਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ।” ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਮੁਸਕਰਾਏ ਤੇ ਬੋਲੇ, ਹਛਾ ਮੁਲਕ ਜੀ! ਕੋਈ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਮੰਗਾਓ ਆਪਣੇ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਦੀ।” ਉਧਰ ਲਾਲੋ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰੋਂ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਦਾ ਟੁੱਕਰ ਲੈ ਆ।” ਜਦ ਦੋਇ ਆ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਇਕ ਹੱਥ ਵਿਚ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਤੇ ਦੂਜੇ ਵਿਚ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਦਾ ਟੱਕਰ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਬਾਹਾਂ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਕਰਕੇ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘੁੱਟਿਆ, ਨਿਪੀੜਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦੇਖੋ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਦੁੱਧ ਦੀਆਂ ਬੂੰਦਾਂ ਸਿੰਮ ਪਈਆਂ ਤੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਦੀ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਲਹੂ ਦੀਆਂ ਬੂੰਦਾਂ ਸਿੰਮ ਪਈਆਂ। ਇਹ ਦੇਖਕੇ ਸਾਰੀ ਮਜਲਸ, ਜੋ ਸ਼ਹਿਰਦੇ ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੀ, ਹਰਯਾਨ ਰਹਿ ਗਈ ਤੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਡਰ ਗਏ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਤਪਾ ਬੜਾ ਕਲਾਵਾਨ ਤੇ *ਪਰੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ, ਨਫਰਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।

ਕਰਾਮਾਤੀ ਹੈ। ਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਆਇਆ ਨਾਲੇ ਸ਼ਰਮਿੰਦਗੀ ਬੀ ਆਈ। ਤਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਬੋਲੇ, ‘ਦੇਖ ਮੁਲਕ! ਕਿਕਰ ਦੇ ਬੀਜ ਨੂੰ ਕੰਡੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਪਰ ਜਦ ਬੀਜ ਉਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਬੂਟਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕੰਡੇ ਨਿਕਲ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ, ਤਿਵੇਂ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ, ਪਾਪ ਤੇ ਅਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਕਮਾਈ ਦੇ ਮਾਹਲ ਪੂੜੇ, ਕਚੌਰੀਆਂ, ਲੁੱਚੀਆਂ ਸੁਆਦਲੇ ਹਨ ਖਾਣ ਨੂੰ, ਪਰ ਧਰਮੀ ਪੁਰਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ, ਜਦ ਉਹ ਖਾ ਜਾਣ, ਤਾਂ ਪੀੜ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਨਾਲ ਕਮਾਏ ਧਨ ਦੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਧਰਮੀਂ ਹਿਰਦਿਆਂ ਵਰਜਿਤ ਹਨ, ਖਾਣੇਂ ਮਨ੍ਹੇ ਹਨ। ਤੇ ਐਸੇ ਦਾਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਬੀ ਉਸਦਾ ਪੁੰਨ ਫਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਦਾ, ਸਗੋਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਪਾਪਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਇਕੱਠੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੋਵੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਦੰਡ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।” ਇਉਂ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਆ ਗਏ ਤੇ ਲਾਲੋ ਦੇ ਕੱਚੇ ਕੋਠੇ ਵਿਚ ਜਾ ਵੜੇ। ਇਸ ਸਾਖੀ ਵਿਚ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਮੱਤਿ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰੋ, ਉਸ ਤੇ ਗੁਜ਼ਰਾਨ ਕਰੋ, ਉਸ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਦਾਨ ਕਰੋ, ਉਹ ਫਲੇਗਾ, ਉਹ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਲੋਕ ਪ੍ਰਲੋਕ ਸੁਖ ਦੇਵੇਗਾ।
