  "01-nanak": {
    "1": {
      "body_pa": "ਸਾਡੇ ਸੋਹਣੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਹੈ। ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ੧੪੬੯ ਈਸਵੀ ਨੂੰ ਇਸ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਆਏ ਸਨ। ਤਦੋਂ ਇਥੇ ਬਹਿਲੋਲ ਲੋਧੀ ਦਾ ਰਾਜ ਸੀ। ਜੇ ਹਿਸਾਬ ਸਿਰ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੀਏ ਤਾਂ ਤਦੋਂ ਸੰਮਤ ਸੀ ੧੫੨੬ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮੀ।\n\nਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਰੱਬ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਪਾਸੋਂ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਆਉਣ ਨੂੰ 'ਅਵਤਾਰ' ਆਖੀਦਾ ਹੈ। ਰਬ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਸੀ ਜੋ ਉਹ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਭਲੇ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਲਾਉਣ, ਆਪੋ ਵਿਚ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰਨਾ ਸਿਖਾਲਣ ਤੇ ਰੱਬ ਜੀ ਨਾਲ ਬੀ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਸੁਹਣੀ ਮਤਿ ਦੇਣ।\n\nਜਿਸ ਪਿੰਡ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਉਸਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਰਾਇ ਭੋਇ ਦੀ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ। ਇਹ ਥਾਂ ਲਾਹੌਰ ਤੋਂ ਲਹਿੰਦੇ ਵਲ ਨੂੰ ਹੈ ਕੋਈ ੧੭ ਯਾ ੨੦ ਕੋਹ ਦੀ ਵਿੱਥ ਉਤੇ। ਹੁਣ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ 'ਨਨਕਾਣਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ'। ਇਹ ਸ਼ਰਕਪੁਰ ਦੇ ਪਰਗਨੇ ਜ਼ਿਲਾ ਸ਼ੇਖੂਪੁਰਾ (ਪਾਕਿਸਤਾਨ) ਵਿਚ ਹੈ।\n\n(ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਦਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਰਾਇ ਪੁਰ, ਫੇਰ ਪਿਆ ਰਾਇ ਭੋਇ ਦੀ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ।)\n\nਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਬੀਬੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਾ ਜੀ, ਅਤੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਰਾਮ ਜੀ; ਪਰ ਲੋਕੀਂ ਬੁਲਾਉਂਦੇ 'ਕਾਲੂ ਜੀ' ਕਰਕੇ ਹੀ ਸਨ। ਆਪ 'ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ' ਸਨ ਤੇ 'ਬੇਦੀ' ਕਹਾਉਂਦੇ ਸਨ।\n\nਕਾਲੂ ਜੀ ਕੀਹ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦੇ ਸਨ? ਜਿਸ ਪਿੰਡ ਵਸਦੇ ਸਨ ਉਸ ਨਾਲ ਹੋਰ ਕਿਤਨੇ ਹੀ ਪਿੰਡ ਸਨ; ਇਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ 'ਤਪਾ' ਆਖਦੇ ਸਨ। ਇਸ ਤਪੇ ਦਾ ਇਕ ਰਾਇ ਸੀ। 'ਰਾਇ' ਛੋਟੇ ਰਾਜਾ ਨੂੰ ਆਖੀਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਰਾਏ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ 'ਰਾਇ ਬੁਲਾਰ'। ਇਸ ਰਾਇ ਬੁਲਾਰ ਨੇ ਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਕਾਰਦਾਰ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ। ਕਾਰਦਾਰ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਜੋ ਜ਼ਮੀਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਹਿਸਾਬ ਲੇਖਾ ਰਖੇ ਤੇ ਲੈਣ ਦੇਣ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਭੁਗਤਾਵੇ; ਜੋ ਰਾਇ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੇ ਕੰਮ ਆਪ ਨਾ ਕਰਨੇ ਪੈਣ। ਇਹ ਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਹੋਰ ਕੰਮ ਕਾਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਮੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਬੀ ਸਾਰੇ ਹਿਸਾਬ ਰਖਦਾ ਸੀ, ਇਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਇਸਨੂੰ ਪਟਵਾਰੀ ਬੀ ਆਖਦੇ ਸਨ। ਇਹ ਹੋਰ ਸਾਰੇ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ ਦੇ ਪਟਵਾਰੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਵਡਕਾ ਬੀ ਸੀ।\n\nਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਸੰਮਤ ੧੫੨੧ ਨੂੰ ਇਕ ਕਾਕੀ ਜਨਮੀ ਸੀ; ਉਸ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ 'ਨਾਨਕੀ'। ਤੇ ਲਾਡ ਨਾਲ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਬੁਲਾਉਂਦੇ ਸਨ 'ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ'। ਇਹ ਬੀਬੀ ਬੜੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਸੀ। ਛੋਟੀ ਉਮਰੇ ਹੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਸੋਹਣੀ ਹੋਸ਼ ਵਾਲੀ ਸੀ। ਛੋਟੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੀ ਮਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਨਿੱਕੇ ਨਿੱਕੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਮਾਂ ਪਾਸੋਂ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ ਜੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਸੁਣਦੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਸੀ। ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ ਬੀ ਕਰਦੀ ਸੁਣਦੀ ਸੀ, ਬੁਝਾਰਤਾਂ ਬੀ ਪਾਉਂਦੀ ਸੀ, ਪਰ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ ਜੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਤੇ ਭਲਿਆਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਹਾਲ ਸੁਣਕੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਖੁਸ਼ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਰਦੀ ਸੀ। ਜਦੋਂ ਬੀਬੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਹਾਣ ਦੀਆਂ ਕੁੜੀਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਖੇਡਦੀ ਸੀ ਤਾਂ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਰਲਕੇ ਨਿੱਕੇ ਨਿੱਕੇ ਗੀਤ ਗਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਸੀ।\n\nਗੀਤਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਵੀਰ ਦੇ ਗੀਤ ਬੀ ਗਾਉਂਦੀ ਸੀ। ਇਸ ਦਾ ਜੀ ਲੋਚਦਾ ਸੀ ਕਿ ਰਬ ਜੀ ਮੇਰੇ ਲਈ ਵੀਰ ਬੀ ਘੱਲਣ। ਇਹ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਟੱਪੇ ਗਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਸੀ:-\n\nਆ ਵੀਰਾ ਮੇਰਿਆ, ਭੈਣ ਵਾਜਾਂ ਪਈ ਮਾਰੇ,\nਆ ਵੀਰਾ ਸੋਹਣਿਆ, ਭੈਣ ਤੈਥੋਂ ਗਈ ਵਾਰੇ!",
      "body_en": "Our beloved Guru's name is Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Sri Guru Ji came into this world in the year 1469 CE. At that time Bahlol Lodhi ruled here. Working by the Indian calendar, the year was 1526 Bikrami.\n\nWhen a Guru is sent into this world from the Lord, it is called an 'avatar'. The Lord had sent him so that he would set people to good deeds, teach them to love one another, and impart the beautiful wisdom of loving the Lord too.\n\nThe village where his avatar took place was named Rai Bhoi di Talwandi. This place lies west of Lahore, at a distance of about 17 or 20 kos. Today it is called 'Nankana Sahib'. It is in the parganah of Sharakpur, district Sheikhupura (Pakistan).\n\n(Talwandi's first name was Rai Pur; later it became Rai Bhoi di Talwandi.)\n\nThe Guru's mother was named Bibi Tripta Ji, and his father Mehta Kalu Ram Ji — but people just called him 'Kalu Ji'. He was a 'Khatri' by caste, of the 'Bedi' sub-caste.\n\nWhat work did Kalu Ji do? Around the village where they lived there were many other villages too; together these were called a 'tappa'. This tappa had a 'rai'. A 'rai' is what a minor king is called. This rai's name was 'Rai Bular'. Rai Bular had appointed Mehta Kalu Ji as his kardar. A kardar is one who keeps the accounts of lands and other matters and handles transactions — so that the rai need not do every task himself. Mehta Kalu, besides his other work, also kept the records of the lands, so he was also called a patwari. He was senior over all the other villages' patwaris too.\n\nIn Mehta Kalu's home, in Samvat 1521, a baby girl was born; her name was 'Nanki'. And with affection people called her 'Bibi Nanki'. This Bibi was very loving. Even at a small age she was bright and aware. From an early age she would help her mother with little tasks and listen to her mother's stories about the Lord. She would tell and hear stories and ask riddles too, but she was happiest when listening to talk of the Lord and the lives of good people. When Bibi played with girls her own age, she would join them in singing little songs.\n\nAmong these songs she would also sing songs about a brother. Her heart yearned that the Lord would send her a brother too. She would sing little couplets like these:-\n\nCome, my brother — your sister is calling out,\nCome, handsome brother — your sister adores you!",

They need grandma's editorial review\nbefore \"launch quality.\"\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport sqlite3\nimport os\n\nROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\n# When run from any cwd, find the project root via the file path\nROOT = \"/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar\"\nMANUAL_FIXES = f\"{ROOT}/corpus/sakhis/manual-fixes.json\"\nSAKHIS_DB = f\"{ROOT}/data/sakhis.db\"\n\n# ---------------- Sakhi 16: Rai Bular's Love (includes Sacha Sauda) -----\n\nSAKHI_16_TITLE_EN = \"Rai Bular's Love\"\n\nSAKHI_16_BODY_PA = \"\"\"ਚੂੜ੍ਹਕਾਣੋਂ ਦੇ ਲਾਗੇ ਭੁਖੇ ਬੈਠੇ ਸੰਤਾਂ ਤਪੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀਹ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਦਾ ਆਟਾ, ਚਾਉਲ, ਦਾਲਾਂ, ਛੋਲੇ ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਖਾਣ ਪੀਣ ਦੀਆਂ ਚੀਜ਼ਾਂ ਬਾਲਕ ਉਮਰਾ ਦੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਲੈ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਸਨ, ਤੇ ਫੇਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਨਗਰ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਪਏ ਸਨ। ਜਦੋਂ ਨਗਰ ਨੇੜੇ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ, ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬਾਲਕ ਨੇ, ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਵਰੇਸ ਵਿਚ ਸਨ, ਆਖਿਆ: \"ਤੂੰ ਜਾਹ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਤੇ ਮੈਂ ਅਜੇ ਘਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਣਾ ਆਪਣੇ।\" ਸੋ ਬਾਲਾ ਤਾਂ ਗਿਆ ਘਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੇ ਸੁਹਣਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਬਾਲਕਾ ਬੈਠ ਰਿਹਾ, ਬਾਹਰ ਇਕ ਸੁੱਕਾ ਪਿਆ ਸੀ ਤਲਾ, ਉਸ ਦੇ ਪੌੜਾਂ ਉਤੇ। ਅੱਖਾਂ ਲਈਓ ਸੁ ਮੀਟ ਤੇ ਸੋਚੇ: \"ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਦੁਖ ਕਿਉਂ ਹੈ? ਕੋਈ ਭੁੱਖਾ ਹੈ, ਕੋਈ ਰੋਗੀ ਹੈ, ਕੋਈ ਨੰਗਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਮਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਤਾਂ ਰੋਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਦੁਖ ਦੂਰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋਵੇ?\" \"ਹੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਹੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ! ਤੂੰ ਕਰ ਦੂਰ ਦੁੱਖ!\" 'ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ', 'ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ' ਕਰਦੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਅੰਦਰ ਹੀ ਅੰਦਰ ਚੰਬੜ ਗਏ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕੋਈ ਬਾਲ ਓਦਰਿਆ ਹੋਵੇ ਤਾਂ ਮਾਂ ਆਈ ਵੇਖ ਕੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਚੰਬੜ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।\n\n(੧੨ ਬਰਸਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਤੇ ੨੦ ਤਕ ਦੇ ਬਾਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਕੁਮਾਰ ਆਖ ਲਈਦਾ ਹੈ।)\n\nਓਧਰ ਬਾਲਾ ਘਰ ਗਿਆ ਆਪਣੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ ਤੱਕਿਆ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਦੇ ਪੁਤਰ ਨਾਲ, ਤਦ ਕਿਸੇ ਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਜਾ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਜੋ ਬਾਲਾ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਏ ਘਰ। ਬਾਬੇ ਨੇ ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਸਦਵਾ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਘਰ ਆਏ ਨੂੰ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ, ਤਾਂ ਓਸ ਨੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ \"ਆਇਆ ਤਾਂ ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੈ ਤੁਸਾਂ ਦਾ ਬੇਟਾ, ਪਰ ਨਗਰੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਖੜੋ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ ਤਾਲ ਕੰਢੇ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਘੱਲ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਸਾਸੂ ਘਰ।\" ਤਦ ਕਾਲੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ \"ਸੌਦਾ ਖਰੀਦਣ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਸੀ ਤੁਸਾਂ ਨੂੰ, ਕੋਈ ਘਿਨਿਆ ਸੌਦਾ?\" ਤਾਂ ਓਸ ਕਿਹਾ \"ਸਾਧਾਂ ਫਕੀਰਾਂ ਭੁੱਖਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਖੁਲਾ ਦਿਤੇ ਸੁ ਰੂਪੱਯੇ, ਆਖਦਾ ਸੀ ਇਹ ਹੈ ਖਰਾ ਸੌਦਾ, ਇਹ ਹੈ ਸੱਚਾ ਸੌਦਾ।\" ਇਹ ਸੁਣ ਕੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਚੜ੍ਹ ਗਿਆ ਗੁੱਸਾ, ਬਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਲੈਕੇ ਟੁਰ ਪਏ ਲੱਭਣ। ਓਹ ਘਰੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਨਿਕਲੇ ਤਾਂ ਅੰਮਾਂ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਾ ਨੇ ਨੌਕਰ ਘੱਲੇ ਮਗਰ ਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਆਪਣੀ ਧੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਨੂੰ ਜੋ ਮਤਾਂ ਪਿਉ ਮਾਰੇ ਤਾਂ ਧੀ ਕੋਲ ਹੋਈ ਤਾਂ ਛੁਡਾ ਲਏਗੀ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਚੜ੍ਹੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਤੋਂ। ਸੋ ਇਸੇ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਹੀ ਹੋਈ।\n\nਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਜਾ ਡਿੱਠਾ ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ, ਜੋ ਅੱਖਾਂ ਮੀਟੀ ਬੈਠਾ ਸੀ, ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਦੁਖ ਆਪਣੇ ਵਡੇ ਬਾਬਲ-ਰੱਬ-ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਦਾ। ਗੁੱਸੇ ਭਰੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਬਾਹੋਂ ਪਕੜ ਉਠਾਇਆ, ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ ਖੜਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਤੇ ਵੱਧ ਘੱਟ ਬੋਲਿਆ, ਮਾੜੇ ਬਚਨ ਆਖੇ ਤੇ ਕੱਸਕੇ ਚਪੇੜਾਂ ਮਾਰੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਸੱਜੀ ਗਲ੍ਹ ਤੇ, ਦੋ ਮਾਰੀਆਂ ਖੱਬੀ ਗਲ੍ਹ ਤੇ। \"ਪੱਟੇ ਜਾਣਿਆਂ! ਪੱਟ ਸੁੱਟਿਆ ਈ ਮੇਰਾ ਝੁੱਗਾ।\" ਹੁਣ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਭਰੇ ਦੇ ਕਰੜੇ ਹੱਥ ਉਠ ਹੀ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਪਈ ਭੈਣ ਦੌੜਦੀ ਦੌੜਦੀ ਤੇ ਚੰਬੜ ਗਈ ਬਾਬਲ ਨੂੰ ਤੇ ਹਿਲੋਰਾ ਦੇ ਕੇ ਪਰਾਂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਸੁ। ਸੋ ਪਰੇ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਉੱਲਰੇ ਹੱਥ ਬੀ। ਬੀਬੀ ਬੋਲੀ: \"ਨਾਂ ਮੇਰੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਨਾ, ਮੇਰੇ ਵੀਰਨ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਮਾਰ, ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ ਮੇਰੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼!\"\n\n(ਇਹ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਮਾਂ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਮਹਿਤਾ ਕਾਲੂ ਨਾਉਂ ਸੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਪਿਤਾ ਜੀ ਦਾ।)\n\nਹੋਰ ਲੋਕੀ ਬੀ ਸੁਣਕੇ ਆ ਗਏ ਸਨ, ਨੌਕਰ ਬੀ ਬੀਬੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਨਾਲ ਆਏ ਸਨ, ਸਭ ਨੇ ਵਰਜਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਬਾਬੇ ਦੇ ਮਾਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੱਥ ਲਮਕ ਪਏ ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਰਨੋਂ ਰੁਕ ਗਏ। ਹੁਣ ਬਾਹੋਂ ਧੱਕਕੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਜੀ ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬੇਟੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਟੁਰੇ। ਸੁਹਣੇ ਬੇਟੇ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਬੋਲੇ ਨਾ ਕੂਏ। ਗੁਲਾਬਾਂ ਵਰਗੀਆਂ ਸੁਹਣੀਆਂ ਗਲਾਂ ਤੇ ਨੀਲ ਪੈ ਗਏ, ਤੇ ਦੋ ਚਾਰ ਅੱਥਰੂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੀਲਾਂ ਦੇ ਉਤੇ ਦੀ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਵਗ ਪਏ। ਅਜੇ ਕੁਝ ਕਦਮ ਹੀ ਗਏ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਰਾਇਬੁਲਾਰ ਦੇ ਆਦਮੀ ਆ ਪਹੁੰਚੇ, ਬੋਲੇ: \"ਹੇ ਮਹਿਤਾ! ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੁੱਤ ਸਮੇਤ ਰਾਇ ਦੇ ਸੱਦਿਆ ਹੈ।\"\n\nਤਦ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਰਾਇ ਵਲ ਜਾਣਾ ਪਿਆ, ਦਿਲ ਤਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਾਸੂ ਕਰਦਾ, ਪਰ ਮਾਲਕ ਦਾ ਹੁਕਮ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਮੋੜਦਾ। ਜਦ ਰਾਇ ਦੇ ਦਰ ਪਹੁੰਚੇ ਤਾਂ ਉਹ ਅਗੋਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਤੇ ਨੀਲ ਪਏ ਹੋਏ ਤੇ ਅੱਥਰੂ ਵਗੇ ਹੋਏ ਦੇਖਕੇ ਆਪ ਪਿਆ। ਉਠਕੇ ਜੱਫੀ ਪਾ ਲਈਓ ਸੂ, ਤੇ ਮੱਥਾ ਚੁੰਮ ਲਿਓਸੂ। ਪਿਠ ਤੇ ਹੱਥ ਫੇਰ ਛਾਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਲਾਇਓਸੂ, ਆਖਿਓ \"ਸੁਰਬ ਦੇ ਬਾਲਕੇ! ਸਭ ਕੁਛ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ, ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ, ਤੇਰਾ ਹੈ।\" ਫੇਰ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਨੂੰ ਕਹਿਣ ਲਗਾ: \"ਕਾਲੂ ਤੂੰ ਬੜਾ ਬੇ-ਤਰਸ ਹੈਂ, ਇਕੋ ਪੁੱਤ, ਉਹ ਰਬ ਦਾ ਬਾਲਕਾ, ਜੰਮਦਾ ਸੰਤ ਵਲੀ, ਕਲਾਵਾਨ। ਤੂੰ ਬੇ-ਤਰਸ, ਨੀਲ ਪਾ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਨੀ ਮਾਰ ਮਾਰ ਕੇ ਵਲੀ ਅੱਲਾ ਦੇ ਚਿਹਰੇ ਤੇ, ਨਿਰਦਈ! ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਡਰ ਨਾ ਮੇਰਾ ਭਉ, ਨਾ ਲੋਕ ਲਾਜ।\" ਫੇਰ ਭੁੱਬ ਮਾਰਕੇ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਕੀਹ ਕਰਾਂ, ਮੈਂ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ! ਹਾਇ ਮੈਂ ਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਤਾਂ ਅਜ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਰੱਖ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਏਸ ਰਬ ਪ੍ਯਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਤੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੇਵਾ, ਹੁਣ ਰੱਖਾਂ ਤਾਂ ਜਗਤ ਕਹੇਗਾ, ਜੋਰੋ ਜੋਰੀ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਸੂ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤ ਨੂੰ।\"\n\n(ਵਲੀ - ਰਬ ਦਾ ਪਿਆਰਾ।)\n\nਤਦ ਬਾਬੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਰਾਇ ਜੀ ਇਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਰਤੂਤਾਂ ਬੀ ਸੋਚੋ, ਪੱਟ ਸੁੱਟਿਆ ਸੂ ਇਸ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ।\" ਰਾਇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਆਹ ਲੈ ਵੀਹ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਤੇ ਪੱਟਿਆ ਨਾ ਜਾਹ, ਪਰ ਖ਼ਬਰਦਾਰ ਜੇ ਕਦੇ ਫੇਰ ਹੱਥ ਚੁੱਕਿਆ ਬੱਚੇ ਉਤੇ। ਤੂੰ ਹਿਸਾਬ ਕਰਕੇ ਦੱਸ ਜਿਤਨਾ ਧਨ ਤੇਰਾ ਅਜ ਤਾਈਂ ਬੱਚੇ ਨੇ ਗੁਆਇਆ ਹੈ, ਮੈਂ ਭਰ ਦਿਆਂ ਤੇ ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਪੈਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰ। ਦੇਖ, ਜਿਤਨੀ ਦੌਲਤ ਮੇਰੇ ਘਰ ਹੈ ਏਸ ਦੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੋਈ ਹੈ, ਜਿਤਨੀ ਮਾਇਆ ਜਗਤ ਵਿਚ ਹੈ ਏਸ ਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਅੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਮੋਦੀ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਅੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਪੁੱਤ ਹੈ ਪਿਕਾਂਬਰ ਹੈ। ਕਾਲੂ! ਦੇਖ ਜਗਤ ਇਸ ਦਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਸੱਜੇ ਹੱਥ ਬੈਠਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹਈ। ਤੂੰ ਦੇਖੇਂਗਾ ਕਿ ਨਾ ਪਰ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਨਾਉਂ ਤੇ ਲੱਖਾਂ ਰੁਪਏ ਸਦਕੇ ਕਰਿਆ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਜਿਸ ਮਾਇਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੂੰ ਰੋਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਜਗਤ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਨਾਂ ਤੇ ਵਾਰ ਵਾਰ ਸੱਟੇਗਾ। ਜਿਥੇ ਜਿਥੇ ਇਹ ਕਦਮ ਧਰੇਗਾ ਮਾਇਆ ਉਥੇ ਲੇਟਣੀਆਂ ਲਿਆ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਖਬਰਦਾਰ ਜੋ ਤੂੰ ਕਦੇ ਫਿਟੇ ਮੂੰਹ ਬੀ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ ਤਾਂ! ਤੇਰੇ ਘਰ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਤਾਂ ਟੋਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੇ ਆਖੇਂ ਮੈਂ ਫੇਰ ਨਾ ਮਾਰਸਾਂ।\" ਤਦ ਕਾਲੂ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਰਮ ਆਈ, ਰਾਇ ਨੂੰ ਹਥ ਜੋੜਕੇ ਅਖਿਓਸੁ \"ਹੁਣ ਬਖਸ਼ੋ ਫੇਰ ਨਾ ਕਰਸਾਂ\" ਤੇ ਰੁਪੱਯੇ ਬੀ ਮੋੜ ਦਿਤਿਓਸੁ। ਤਾਂ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਟੋਰਿਆ ਤੇ ਸੁਹਣਾ ਬਾਲਕ ਆ ਮਾਂ ਭੈਣ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਿਆ।\n\n(ਪਿਕਾਂਬਰ — ਜੋ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ਰ ਜੀ ਵਲੋਂ ਦੁਨੀਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਆਵੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਪੈਗ਼ੰਬਰ। ਆਮ ਬੋਲੀ ਵਿਚ ਆਖੀਦਾ ਹੈ ਪਿਕਾਂਬਰ।)\n\nਥੋੜੇ ਦਿਨ ਮਗਰੋਂ ਐਸੀ ਗਲ ਬਣ ਗਈ ਕਿ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਦੀ ਕੁੜਮਾਈ ਹੋ ਗਈ। ਬਿਆਸਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਾਰ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ ਨਗਰ ਸੀ, ਏਥੇ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਸੀ ਸੂਬੇ ਦਾ ਵੱਡਾ ਹਾਕਮ ਦੌਲਤ ਖਾਂ ਲੋਧੀ ਪਠਾਣ। ਇਸ ਦੇ ਪਾਸ ਸੀ ਇਕ ਨੌਕਰ — ਜੈ ਰਾਮਦਾਸ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ। ਇਹਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਜੁਆਨ ਸੀ, ਗੱਭਰੂ। ਇਹ ਕਰਦਾ ਸੀ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਨੌਕਰੀ ਤੇ ਸੀ ਵਡਾ ਇਤਬਾਰੀ ਨਵਾਬ ਦਾ। ਇਹ ਕਿਸੇ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਕੰਮ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਆਇਆ ਤਾਂ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਦੀ ਕੁੜਮਾਈ ਹੋ ਗਈ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ। ਇਹ ਉ ਵੀ ਬਹੁਤ ਭਲਾ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਸਭ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਸੁਖੀ ਸੀਗਾ।\n\nਫੇਰ ਵਿਆਹ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ ਤੇ ਬੀਬੀ ਨਾਨਕੀ ਚਲੀ ਗਈ ਸਾਹੁਰੇ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ। ਜੇ ਗੋਂਦਵਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਬੇੜੀ ਵਿਚ ਬੈਠਕੇ ਹੋ ਜਾਈਏ ਬਿਆਸ ਨਦੀ ਤੋਂ ਪਾਰ ਤਾਂ ਕੁਛ ਦੂਰ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਏ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ, ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਤਾਂਈਂ ਵਸਦਾ ਏ। ਰਾਇ ਬੁਲਾਰ ਰੱਬੀ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਸੁਖੀ ਵੇਖਣਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਸੀ, ਪਰ ਮਹਿਤੇ ਕਾਲੂ ਦਾ ਸੁਭਾਉ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਵਟਾਂਦਾ ਤੇ ਰਾਇ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਾਸ ਬੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਗੱਭਰੂ ਹੋ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ। ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿਚ ਸੋਚੀ ਕਿ ਜੇ ਬਾਲਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਭੇਜ ਦੇਈਏ ਸੁਲਤਾਨਪੁਰ, ਜਾ ਰਹੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਭੈਣ ਪਾਸ ਤਾਂ ਸੁਖੀ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੀ, ਰੋਜ਼ ਰੋਜ਼ ਦੀ ਕਲਹਾ ਮਿਟ ਜਾਸੀ। ਸੋ ਜੈਰਾਮ ਦਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਜਦ ਓਹ ਫੇਰ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਆਯਾ, ਤਾਂ ਰਾਇ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ \"ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਾਸ ਲੈ ਜਾਓ ਤੇ ਓਥੇ ਕੋਈ ਸੁਖੱਲਾ ਜਿਹਾ ਕੰਮ ਲੁਆ ਦਿਓ, ਦੋਵੇਂ ਭੈਣ ਭਰਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਸੁਖੀ ਰਹਿਸਣ। ਤੁਸੀਂ ਬੀ ਭਾਗਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੋ, ਵਲੀ ਅੱਲਾ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਸ ਰੱਖਕੇ। ਮੇਰੀ ਨਗਰੀ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਦੁਖ ਮਿਲਣਾ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਜਾਸੀ।\" ਇਹ ਗੱਲ ਜੈਰਾਮ ਦੇ ਦਿਲ ਲੱਗੀ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਨੇ ਹਾਂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ। ਜੀ ਵਿਚ ਖੁਸ਼ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਮੇਰੇ ਪਾਸ ਰਹੇਗਾ।\n\n(ਵਲੀ ਅੱਲਾ — ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਮਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਪਿਆਰਾ। ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਰੱਬ ਨੇ ਵਡਾ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਹੋਵੇ। ਪੂਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਸੰਤ।)\"\"\"\n\nSAKHI_16_BODY_EN = \"\"\"Near Chuhrkana, the boy Guru Nanak Dev Ji had given twenty rupees worth of flour, rice, lentils, chickpeas, and other food and drink to hungry saints and ascetics sitting there, and was now returning home to his town of Talwandi. As the town drew near, the handsome boy — now in his teenage years — said to Bala: \"You go home; I'm not going home just yet.\" So Bala went home, and the lovely Nanak sat on the steps of a dried-up pond outside the town. He closed his eyes and thought: \"Why is there suffering in the world? Some are hungry, some are sick, some are naked, when someone's loved one dies they weep — how can suffering be removed?\" \"O Kartar, O Kartar! Take away suffering!\" Repeating 'Kartar Nirankar', 'Kartar Nirankar', he clung inwardly to the Creator, the way a longing child, when its mother arrives, clings to her.\n\n(A boy between the ages of 12 and 20 is called a 'kumar'.)\n\nMeanwhile Bala had gone home. His family had seen him go out with Mehta Kalu's son, and so someone went and told Baba Kalu that Bala had come home. Baba sent for Bala and asked him, and Bala said: \"Your son did come with me, but he stopped outside the town by the pond's edge and sent me home.\" Then Kalu Ji asked: \"I had sent you to buy goods — did you get any goods?\" Bala said: \"He gave the rupees away to feed hungry sadhus and faqirs; he kept saying this was the true bargain, this was the honest deal.\" Hearing this, the father was overcome with anger and set out with Bala to find him. As they left the house, Mother Tripta sent servants after them, and along with them her daughter Nanaki — so that if the father struck, the daughter would be near and could save him from his angry father. And so it happened.\n\nBaba Kalu found his son sitting with eyes closed, telling his Great Father — God — of the world's pain. Filled with anger, Kalu seized his arm and yanked him up, said harsh words, scolded him, and struck him hard — two slaps on the right cheek, two on the left. \"You ruined boy! You have destroyed my household!\" He was raising his harsh hands to strike again when his sister came running and clung to her father, pushing him aside with a shake. The raised hands fell away. The girl cried: \"No, my father, no — don't strike my brother, spare him, my father, spare him!\"\n\n(This was the name of Guru Nanak Sahib's mother, and Mehta Kalu was the name of the Guru's father.)\n\nOther people had also come on hearing the commotion, and the servants had come along with the girl. When everyone restrained him, Baba's striking hands hung down and he stopped hitting. Now, pushing the boy by the arm, the father led his lovely son along. The handsome boy neither spoke nor cried. Bruises had risen on those rose-like beautiful cheeks, and a few tears flowed down over those bruises. They had gone only a few steps when Rai Bular's men arrived and said: \"O Mehta! The Rai has called you and your son.\"\n\nThen Mehta Kalu had to go to the Rai. His heart did not want to, but how could he refuse his master's command? When they reached the Rai's door, he, on seeing the bruises on Guru Nanak's face and the tears that had flowed, fell himself. He rose and embraced him and kissed his forehead. He stroked his back and pressed him to his chest, saying: \"Child of the Sovereign! All is yours, all is yours, all is yours.\" Then he said to Mehta: \"Kalu, you are very pitiless. Your one son — a child of God, born a saint, a wali, gifted with miracles. You, pitiless one, have raised bruises on the face of Wali Allah by striking him, you cruel man! You have neither fear of God nor awe of me nor regard for the world's shame.\" Then the Rai cried out and said: \"What can I do — I am a Muslim! Alas, were I not Muslim, today I would keep this beloved of God in my own house and serve him. If I keep him now, the world will say a Muslim has forcibly taken a Khatri's son.\"\n\n(Wali — beloved of God.)\n\nThen Baba Kalu said: \"Rai Ji, think also of what he does — he has ruined me.\" The Rai said: \"Here, take twenty rupees and don't be ruined. But take warning: never again raise a hand against the child. Calculate and tell me how much wealth the child has cost you up to today; I will pay it, and you cherish your money. Look — all the wealth in my house is his gift; all the wealth in the world is his. He is Allah's steward, he is Allah's son, a prophet. Kalu! See, the world eats what he gives; he is the one who sits at God's right hand. Whether you see it or not, the world will one day give millions of rupees in his name. The wealth you weep over, the world will fling again and again in his name. Wherever he sets foot, wealth will come rolling. Beware that you never even speak a harsh word to him! I send him back to your house only if you swear not to strike him again.\" Then Kalu was ashamed; he folded his hands to the Rai and said: \"Forgive me now, I will not do it again,\" and returned the twenty rupees. So the Rai sent them on, and the lovely boy came home to his mother and sister.\n\n(Pikambar — one who is sent by the Lord into the world is called a pikambar (prophet). In common speech it is said pikambar.)\n\nA few days later it came to pass that Bibi Nanaki's engagement was arranged. Across the Beas was the town of Sultanpur. There lived the great governor of the province, Daulat Khan Lodi the Pathan. He had in his service a servant — Jai Ram Das, a Khatri. He was a young man, in the bloom of youth, doing government service, and a great confidant of the Nawab. He came to Talwandi on some official business, and Bibi Nanaki's engagement was arranged with him. He too was very good, and was prosperous in every way.\n\nThen the marriage took place and Bibi Nanaki went to her in-laws' house in Sultanpur. If one boards a boat at Goindwal and crosses the Beas river, then a little further on is Sultanpur, which is still inhabited today. Rai Bular wanted to see the divine child happy, but Mehta Kalu's nature would not change, and the Rai could not keep the child himself, who was now growing into a young man. The Rai thought in his heart: \"If we could somehow send the boy to Sultanpur, to be with his sister, then he will be happy and the daily quarrel will end.\" So when Jai Ram Das next came to Talwandi, the Rai said to him: \"Take Sri Nanak Ji with you and give him some easy work there; let brother and sister live happily together. You too will become blessed by keeping Wali Allah near you. In my town, the suffering of the beloved of God will end.\" This pleased Jai Ram's heart and he agreed. In his heart he was glad: \"The beloved of God will stay with me.\"\n\n(Wali Allah — beloved friend of God. One whom God has made great. A perfect saint.)\"\"\"\n\nSAKHI_16_COMMENT = (\n    \"Hand-cleaned body_pa: removed stray * footnote markers, fixed quote \"\n    \"spacing, closed orphan quotes, pulled inline footnotes into \"\n    \"parenthetical paragraphs (kumar definition, mother/father names, \"\n    \"wali definition, pikambar definition, wali allah definition). \"\n    \"Broke wall-of-text into 9 paragraphs at narrative boundaries: \"\n    \"Nanak sits by pond meditating | Bala returns / Kalu sends for him \"\n    \"/ Tripta sends Nanaki | Kalu beats Nanak / Nanaki saves him / Rai's \"\n    \"men arrive | scene at Rai Bular's door / Rai embraces Nanak / \"\n    \"scolds Kalu | Rai pays Kalu 20 rupees, demands no more hitting | \"\n    \"Nanaki's engagement arranged | Marriage / Rai plans to send Nanak \"\n    \"to Sultanpur. Body_en is a fresh hand-translation matching the PA \"\n    \"paragraphs 1:1. Title fixed: 'Rai Bulats love' -> \\\"Rai Bular's \"\n    \"Love\\\". DRAFT — needs grandma editorial pass for register + accuracy.\"\n)\n\n# ---------------- Sakhi 38: Milk or Blood (Bhai Lalo + Malik Bhago) -----\n\nSAKHI_38_TITLE_EN = \"Milk or Blood\"\n\nSAKHI_38_BODY_PA = \"\"\"ਇਸ ਘਰ ਵਿਚ — ਨਿੱਕੇ ਜਿਹੇ ਕੱਚੇ ਕੋਠੇ ਵਿਚ — ਤ੍ਰੈ ਕੁ ਦਿਨ ਰਹਿੰਦਿਆਂ ਹੋਏ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਤੁਰਨੇ ਨੂੰ ਤਿਆਰ ਹੋਣ ਲਗੇ, ਪਰ ਲਾਲੋ ਨੇ ਹੱਥ ਜੋੜੇ, ਅੱਖਾਂ ਪਿਆਰ ਨਾਲ ਹੰਝੂ ਭਰੀਆਂ ਹੋ ਗਈਆਂ ਤੇ ਆਖਿਆ: \"ਐਡੀ ਛੇਤੀ ਨਾ ਕਰੋ, ਕੁਛ ਦਿਨ ਹੋਰ ਠਹਿਰੋ, ਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦਿਓ ਤਾਂ ਜਾਓ।\" ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਕੇ ਹੋਰ ਠਹਿਰ ਪਏ।\n\nਹੁਣ ਇਉਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਹੋ ਗਈ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਤੜਕੇ ਹੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਚਲੇ ਜਾਣਾ ਤੇ ਓਥੇ ਯਾ ਤਾਂ ਰੋੜਾਂ ਦੀ ਥੜੀ ਉਤੇ ਯਾ ਰੇਤੇ ਦੀ ਥਲੀ ਉਤੇ ਚੌਂਕੜਾ ਮਾਰ ਬੈਠਣਾ, ਆਪਣੇ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਵਿਚ ਲਗੇ ਬੈਠੇ ਰਹਿਣਾ। ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਲੋਕੀ ਤਪ ਕਰਨਾ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਸਰੀਰ ਨਾਲ ਨਿਰਾ ਤਪ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਨ ਕਰਦੇ, ਉਹ ਤਾਂ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਧਾਰ ਕੇ ਬੈਠਦੇ ਸੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਵਿਚ। ਨਗਰ ਵਿਚ ਮਸ਼ਹੂਰ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ ਕਿ ਇਕ ਵੇਦੀ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਬੜੀ ਭਾਰੀ ਤਪਸ੍ਯਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਾ ਕੁਛ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਨਾ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਬਾਹਰ ਰੇਤਿਆਂ ਵਿਚ ਉੱਗੇ ਅੱਕ ਦੇ ਫੁੱਲਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਪੰਜ ਚਾਰ ਕਰੂੰਬਲੀਆਂ ਖਾ ਕੇ ਇਕੋ ਜਗ੍ਹਾ ਬੈਠਾ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸਮਾਧੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੀ। ਪਰ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਇਹ ਆਖਣ, \"ਦੇਖੋ ਵੇਦੀ ਹੋਕੇ ਤਰਖਾਣ ਨੀਵੀਂ ਜਾਤ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਨਾਲ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ ਮਰਾਸੀ ਕਿ ਡੂੰਮ ਰਖਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੂ।\" ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ਜੇ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਿਚ ਕਿਸੇ ਕੰਮੇ ਜਾਏ ਤਾਂ ਲੋਕੀਂ ਇਥੋਂ ਤਾਂਈਂ ਆਖਣ ਕਿ \"ਅਹੁ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਜੇ ਕੁਰਾਹੀਏ ਦਾ ਡੂੰਮ ਜੋ ਜਾਤਿ ਕੁਜਾਤਿ ਰਲਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਜੇ।\" ਸੋ ਕੁਛ ਦਿਨਾਂ ਪਿਛੋਂ ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ਤਾਂ ਆਗਿਆ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਘਰ ਚਲਾ ਗਿਆ ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਥੇ ਹੀ ਟਿਕੇ ਰਹੇ।\n\n(ਰੇਤ ਅੰਕ ਆਹਾਰ ਕਰਿ ਰੋੜਾਂ ਦੀ ਫਿਰਿ ਕਰੀ ਵਿਛਾਈ। ਭਾਰੀ ਕਰੀ ਤਪੱਸਿਆ ਵਡੇ ਭਾਗ ਹਰਿ ਸਿਉ ਬਣਿ ਆਈ।)\n\nਜਿਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਰੱਤੇ ਬੈਠਦੇ ਸੇ ਉਹ ਥਾਉਂ ਹੁਣ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਰੋੜੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਾਉਂ ਹੈ, ਉਸ ਪਾਸ ਯਾਦਗੀਰੀ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਬੀ ਹੈ। ਏਥੇ ਭਾਈ ਲਾਲੋ ਦੀ ਖੂਹੀ ਬੀ ਹੈ।\n\nਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕਿੰਨਾ ਚਿਰ ਏਥੇ ਟਿਕੇ। ਕੁਛ ਲੋਕੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੇਲੇ ਆ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਤੇ ਸਿਖ ਮਤਿ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ; ਪਰ ਇਕ ਦਿਨ ਦੋ ਚਾਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਸਮਝਾਉਣ ਆਏ ਕਿ ਜਾਤ ਦਾ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਰਖੋ, ਤੁਸੀਂ ਉੱਚ ਕੁਲ ਵੇਦਾਚਾਰਯ-ਵੇਦੀ ਹੋ। ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਿਰੁੱਤਰ ਹੋ ਗਏ। ਆਖਰ ਲੋਕੀ ਨਾਨਕ ਤਪਾਂ ਕਹਿਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ। ਕਈ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ 'ਨਾਨਕ ਸ਼ਾਹ' ਆਖਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ। ਆਮ ਲੋਕੀਂ ਤਾਂ ਦੂਰੋਂ ਨੇੜਿਓਂ ਆਉਂਦੇ, ਸਤਿਸੰਗ ਦਾ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ, ਪਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਤੇ ਮੁਲਾਣੇ ਖਿਝਣ ਲਗ ਪਏ, ਕਿਉਂਕਿ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਡਰ ਪਿਆ ਕਿ ਜੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਲੋਕ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਗਰ ਲਗ ਪਏ ਤਾਂ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਕੌਣ ਪੁੱਛੇਗਾ?\n\nਏਮਨਾਬਾਦ ਵਿਚ ਇਕ ਪਠਾਣ ਖਾਨ ਹਾਕਮ ਸੀ, ਮਾਨੋ ਰਾਜਾ ਸੀ ਤੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਉਸਦਾ ਕਾਰਦਾਰ ਸੀ। ਸੋ ਮੁਲਾਣਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਤਾਂ ਨਵਾਬ ਪਾਸ ਤੇ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਨੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਪਾਸ ਚੁਗਲੀਆਂ ਕਰਨੀਆਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ। ਹੋਰ ਬੀ ਉਪ੍ਰਾਲੇ ਕੀਤੇ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਏਥੋਂ ਉਠ ਜਾਣ।\n\nਇਕ ਦਿਨ ਆ ਗਿਆ ਜਦ ਕਿ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਕੀਤਾ। ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਤੇ ਸਾਧੂਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਾਹਲ ਪੂੜੇ, ਪੂੜੀਆਂ, ਖੀਰਾਂ, ਲੁੱਚੀਆਂ, ਕਚੌਰੀਆਂ ਆਦਿ ਭੋਜਨ ਖੁਆਉਣੇ। ਸੋ ਇਹ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਦੇ ਮਲਕ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਾਧੂਆਂ ਤੇ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਦੇ ਘੱਲੇ ਗਏ। ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਖੁਣਸ ਮਾਰਿਆਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਬੀ ਸੱਦ ਘੱਲਿਆ। ਜਾਣਦੇ ਸਨ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਆਉਣਗੇ ਤਾਂ ਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚੜ੍ਹੇਗਾ।\n\n(ਖੁਣਸ — ਗੁੱਸਾ, ਸਾੜਾ, ਈਰਖਾ।)\n\nਸੋ ਐਸਾ ਹੀ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਭੋਜਨ ਖਾਣ ਨਾ ਗਏ। ਤਦ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣਾਂ ਚੁਗਲੀ ਵੱਟੀ ਕਿ \"ਦੇਖੋ ਮਲਕ ਜੀ, ਨਾਨਕ ਤਪਾ ਕੇਡਾ ਹੰਕਾਰੀ ਹੈ, ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਿਉਤਾ ਬੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੁ ਮੰਨਿਆ।\" ਭਾਗੋ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚੜ੍ਹ ਗਿਆ, ਉਸਨੇ ਫੇਰ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਘੱਲਿਆ ਕਿ \"ਜਾਓ ਮੇਰੇ ਪਾਸ ਸੱਦਕੇ ਲਿਆਓ।\" ਪਰ ਜਦ ਸੱਦਣ ਲਈ ਬ੍ਰਾਹਮਣ ਗਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਆਪ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਅਸੀਂ ਫਕੀਰ ਲੋਕ ਹਾਂ, ਸਾਡਾ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹ ਨਾਲ ਕੀ ਕੰਮ।\" ਜਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨਾ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਚੁਗਲ-ਵੱਟਾਂ ਨੇ ਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਹੋਰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਚਾੜ੍ਹਿਆ। ਤਦ ਮਲਕ ਨੇ ਪੰਜਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫੇਰ ਘੋਲਿਆ ਕਿ \"ਨਾ ਆਵੇ ਤਾਂ ਫੜ ਲਿਆਓ।\" ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਹੁਕਮ ਸੁਣਕੇ ਹੱਸੇ ਤੇ ਟੁਰ ਪਏ।\n\nਅੱਗੇ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਮੁਲਕ ਉਦਾਲੇ ਲੋਕ ਬੈਠੇ ਸਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਅੰਦਰ ਲੰਘਕੇ ਚੁਪ ਖੜੇ ਹੋ ਗਏ। ਤਦ ਮੁਲਕ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਹੇ ਤਪਾ, ਤੂੰ ਸ਼ੂਦਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਘਰ ਰੋਟੀਆਂ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਤੇ ਸੁੱਚੇ ਤੇ ਪਵਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜਾਂ ਤੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ! ਫਿਰ ਤੂੰ ਡੂੰਮਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਵਰਤਦਾ ਹੈਂ ਤੇ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਤਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਕੀ ਗਲ ਹੈ?\" ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ: \"ਅਸੀਂ ਦਰਵੇਸ਼ ਹਾਂ ਰਬ ਦੇ, ਜਿਥੋਂ ਦੇਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਖਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਾਂ।\" ਮਲਕ ਬੋਲਿਆ: \"ਫੇਰ ਮੇਰਾ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਬੀ ਖਾ ਲੈਂਦੇ।\"\n\n(ਤਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ — ਪਰੇ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ, ਨਫਰਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।)\n\nਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਮੁਸਕਰਾਏ ਤੇ ਬੋਲੇ: \"ਹਛਾ ਮੁਲਕ ਜੀ! ਕੋਈ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਮੰਗਾਓ ਆਪਣੇ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਭੋਜ ਦੀ।\" ਉਧਰ ਲਾਲੋ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ: \"ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰੋਂ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਦਾ ਟੁੱਕਰ ਲੈ ਆ।\" ਜਦ ਦੋਇ ਆ ਗਏ ਤਾਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਇਕ ਹੱਥ ਵਿਚ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਤੇ ਦੂਜੇ ਵਿਚ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਦਾ ਟੱਕਰ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਬਾਹਾਂ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਕਰਕੇ ਦੋਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘੁੱਟਿਆ, ਨਿਪੀੜਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦੇਖੋ ਕੋਧਰੇ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਦੁੱਧ ਦੀਆਂ ਬੂੰਦਾਂ ਸਿੰਮ ਪਈਆਂ ਤੇ ਮਲਕ ਭਾਗੋ ਦੀ ਲੁੱਚੀ ਕਚੌਰੀ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਲਹੂ ਦੀਆਂ ਬੂੰਦਾਂ ਸਿੰਮ ਪਈਆਂ। ਇਹ ਦੇਖਕੇ ਸਾਰੀ ਮਜਲਸ, ਜੋ ਸ਼ਹਿਰਦੇ ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਬੈਠੀ ਸੀ, ਹਰਯਾਨ ਰਹਿ ਗਈ ਤੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਡਰ ਗਏ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਤਪਾ ਬੜਾ ਕਲਾਵਾਨ ਤੇ ਕਰਾਮਾਤੀ ਹੈ।\n\nਮਲਕ ਨੂੰ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਆਇਆ ਨਾਲੇ ਸ਼ਰਮਿੰਦਗੀ ਬੀ ਆਈ। ਤਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਬੋਲੇ: \"ਦੇਖ ਮੁਲਕ! ਕਿਕਰ ਦੇ ਬੀਜ ਨੂੰ ਕੰਡੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਪਰ ਜਦ ਬੀਜ ਉਗਦਾ ਹੈ ਤੇ ਬੂਟਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕੰਡੇ ਨਿਕਲ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ, ਤਿਵੇਂ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ, ਪਾਪ ਤੇ ਅਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਕਮਾਈ ਦੇ ਮਾਹਲ ਪੂੜੇ, ਕਚੌਰੀਆਂ, ਲੁੱਚੀਆਂ ਸੁਆਦਲੇ ਹਨ ਖਾਣ ਨੂੰ, ਪਰ ਧਰਮੀ ਪੁਰਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ, ਜਦ ਉਹ ਖਾ ਜਾਣ, ਤਾਂ ਪੀੜ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਨਾਲ ਕਮਾਏ ਧਨ ਦੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਧਰਮੀਂ ਹਿਰਦਿਆਂ ਵਰਜਿਤ ਹਨ, ਖਾਣੇਂ ਮਨ੍ਹੇ ਹਨ। ਤੇ ਐਸੇ ਦਾਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਬੀ ਉਸਦਾ ਪੁੰਨ ਫਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਦਾ, ਸਗੋਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਪਾਪਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਇਕੱਠੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੋਵੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਦੰਡ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।\"\n\nਇਉਂ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਆਪ ਜੀ ਬਾਹਰ ਆ ਗਏ ਤੇ ਲਾਲੋ ਦੇ ਕੱਚੇ ਕੋਠੇ ਵਿਚ ਜਾ ਵੜੇ। ਇਸ ਸਾਖੀ ਵਿਚ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਮੱਤਿ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰੋ, ਉਸ ਤੇ ਗੁਜ਼ਰਾਨ ਕਰੋ, ਉਸ ਵਿਚੋਂ ਦਾਨ ਕਰੋ, ਉਹ ਫਲੇਗਾ, ਉਹ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਲੋਕ ਪ੍ਰਲੋਕ ਸੁਖ ਦੇਵੇਗਾ।\"\"\"\n\nSAKHI_38_BODY_EN = \"\"\"They had stayed in this house — in the small mud hut — for about three days when Sri Guru Ji prepared to set out. But Lalo folded his hands, his eyes filled with loving tears, and said: \"Don't go so soon, stay a few more days; give us your darshan before you go.\" Sri Guru Ji, seeing his love, stayed on.\n\nNow this routine took shape: Guru Ji would go out at dawn and sit cross-legged either on a heap of pebbles or on a stretch of sand, absorbed in remembrance of Waheguru. What people call doing 'tapas' — but Guru Ji was not merely subjecting his body to penance; he sat there holding Waheguru in his attention, in love. Word spread in the town that a Bedi Khatri was doing severe penance, eating and drinking nothing, sitting in one place after eating four or five buds of the akk flowers that grew wild in the sand, his samadhi unbroken. But along with that, they would also say: \"Look — a Bedi, yet he lives in the house of a low-caste carpenter. And he has kept a Muslim mirasi, a doom, with him.\" If Mardana went into the bazaar on any errand, people would even say: \"There goes the doom of that misguided man who is mingling caste with no-caste.\" So after some days Mardana took leave and went home, but Guru Ji stayed on.\n\n(He made the sand his food, then spread the pebbles around him. He did great tapasya, and great fortune was joined with Hari.)\n\nThe place where Guru Ji sat absorbed in love with Waheguru is there now and is called Roori Sahib; beside it there is also a memorial sarovar. Bhai Lalo's well is also here.\n\nGuru Ji stayed here a long time. Some people would come at one time or another, meet him and take the Sikh teachings; but one day two or four brahmins came to argue with him, saying: \"Maintain the consideration of caste; you are of high lineage, a Vedacharya Bedi.\" But before Guru Ji's reasoning, they were left without answer. In the end people began calling him 'Nanak Tapa.' Many Muslims began saying 'Nanak Shah.' Ordinary people came from near and far, taking the benefit of satsang, but the brahmins and mullahs began to seethe — for both feared that if everyone followed him, who would attend to them?\n\nIn Eminabad there was a Pathan Khan ruler — practically a raja — and Malik Bhago was his official. So the mullahs began carrying tales to the Nawab, and the brahmins to Malik Bhago. They tried other means too to make Guru Ji leave.\n\nA day came when Malik Bhago held a brahm bhoj — a great feast — in his house. A brahm bhoj is when brahmins and sadhus are fed mahalpurey, puris, kheer, luchis, kachoris, and similar foods. So invitations went out from the Malik to all the sadhus and brahmins. Out of spite, the brahmins also sent an invitation to Guru Ji. They knew that if Guru Ji did not come, the Malik would get angry.\n\n(Khuns — anger, jealousy, envy.)\n\nAnd so it happened that Guru Ji did not go to eat at his house. Then the brahmins gossiped: \"See, Malik Ji, what a proud man this Nanak Tapa is — he didn't even accept your invitation.\" Bhago became angry; he sent the brahmin back, saying: \"Go and bring him to me.\" But when the brahmin went to call him, Guru Ji said: \"We are faqirs; what have we to do with a king?\" When Guru Ji didn't go, the gossipers fanned the Malik's anger further. Then the Malik again sent five men, saying: \"If he doesn't come, fetch him by force.\" Hearing the order, Guru Ji smiled and set off.\n\nWhen he arrived, people sat all around the Malik. Guru Ji walked in and stood silent. Then the Malik said: \"O tapa, you eat at the houses of shudras and do not come to my pure, sacred brahm bhoj! And you keep company with dooms and shun us Khatris. What is this?\" Guru Ji said: \"We are dervishes of God; we eat what is given.\" The Malik said: \"Then eat my brahm bhoj too.\"\n\n(Tahunda hai — you push away, you despise.)\n\nGuru Ji smiled and said: \"Very well, Malik Ji! Have some luchi-kachori brought from your brahm bhoj.\" Then he said to Lalo: \"Bring a piece of kodra-bread from your home.\" When both arrived, Guru Ji took the luchi-kachori in one hand and the kodra bread in the other, stretched out his arms, and squeezed both — and behold, drops of milk oozed from the kodra, and drops of blood oozed from Malik Bhago's luchi-kachori. Seeing this, the whole gathering of townspeople was astonished, and all were afraid that this tapa was very powerful and miraculous.\n\nThe Malik felt anger and also shame. Then Guru Ji said: \"See, Malik! The seed of the kikar tree has no thorns, but when the seed sprouts and the plant grows, thorns come out. In the same way, the mahalpurey, kachoris, and luchis made from earnings of force, oppression, sin, and unrighteousness are tasty to eat, but when righteous people eat them, they cause pain. Therefore foods earned through oppression are forbidden to righteous hearts — they must not be eaten. And those who give such donations do not receive the merit of charity; instead, they receive the punishment of the sins by which it was gathered.\"\n\nSo saying, he came out and entered Lalo's mud hut. In this sakhi Guru Ji has taught us: do honest work, live by it, give from it. It will bear fruit; what is given will bring you peace in this world and the next.\"\"\"\n\nSAKHI_38_COMMENT = (\n    \"Hand-cleaned body_pa: removed inline * footnote markers, pulled \"\n    \"the embedded doha (Rēt aṅka āhāra...) into its own parenthetical, \"\n    \"pulled khuns + tahunda glosses into parenthetical lines. Split the \"\n    \"original 3 wall-of-text paragraphs into 10 narrative paragraphs: \"\n    \"Lalo asks Guru to stay | Daily tapas / town gossip | (doha quote) \"\n    \"| Roori Sahib geography note | brahmin/mullah resistance | \"\n    \"Eminabad ruler + Malik Bhago | the brahm bhoj invitation | Guru \"\n    \"doesn't go / Malik orders fetch | the milk / blood demonstration \"\n    \"| Guru's teaching + closing moral. Body_en is a fresh hand-\"\n    \"translation matching the PA paragraphs 1:1. Title_en stays as \"\n    \"'Milk or Blood'. DRAFT — needs grandma editorial pass for register + accuracy.\"\n)\n\ndef main():\n    with open(MANUAL_FIXES, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n        data = json.load(f)\n\n    book = data.setdefault(\"01-nanak\", {})\n\n    book[\"16\"] = {\n        \"title_en\": SAKHI_16_TITLE_EN,\n        \"body_pa\": SAKHI_16_BODY_PA,\n        \"body_en\": SAKHI_16_BODY_EN,\n        \"comment\": SAKHI_16_COMMENT,\n    }\n    book[\"38\"] = {\n        \"title_pa\": \"ਦੁੱਧ ਕਿ ਲਹੂ\",\n        \"title_en\": SAKHI_38_TITLE_EN,\n        \"body_pa\": SAKHI_38_BODY_PA,\n        \"body_en\": SAKHI_38_BODY_EN,\n        \"comment\": SAKHI_38_COMMENT,\n    }\n\n    # Sort the book's keys numerically for clean diffs\n    def sort_key(k):\n        return int(k) if k.isdigit() else -1\n    data[\"01-nanak\"] = {k: book[k] for k in sorted(book.keys(), key=sort_key) if k != \"_comment\"}\n    if \"_comment\" in book:\n        # Keep _comment at top\n        data[\"01-nanak\"] = {\"_comment\": book[\"_comment\"], **{k: data[\"01-nanak\"][k] for k in data[\"01-nanak\"]}}\n\n    with open(MANUAL_FIXES, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n        json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)\n    print(f\"Wrote {MANUAL_FIXES}\")\n\n    # Also update data/sakhis.db directly so the cleaned bodies ship even\n    # before rebuilding from the corpus pipeline.\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(SAKHIS_DB)\n    cur = conn.cursor()\n\n    cur.execute(\n        \"UPDATE sakhis SET title_en = ?, body_pa = ?, body_en = ?, char_count_pa = ? # Landing page research for akhar.io

## 1. Teardowns

**Duolingo** — Hero: *"The free, fun and effective way to learn a language."* Single primary CTA ("Get started"). The headline is three adjectives doing all the work; the page underneath is essentially a course picker plus a Trustpilot-style proof bar ("Loved by language learners worldwide", App of the Year awards, ~500M downloads). Notably they hide *what you actually do in a lesson* — the product is so well-known the hero doesn't bother. Lesson: only mass-market incumbents get to write copy this abstract.

**Babbel** — Hero: *"The effective way to learn a language online"* / *"Learn to speak a new language with confidence... so you can reach your goal of having real-life conversations faster."* CTA: "Start learning." Below: method explanation, "200+ language experts," "92% of users improved proficiency in 2 months," "25M+ subscriptions." This is the model template: outcome promise + methodology + numerical credibility + testimonials + FAQ.

**Busuu** — Hero: *"New language, new opportunities, new you"* — vague aspirational. CTA: "Learn for free." Leans hard on community ("120 million learners") and B2B logos (Puma, DHL, Uber). The "new you" framing is exactly the kind of generic self-help copy a heritage learner would scroll past.

**Pimsleur** — Hero: *"Learn New Languages Online: Effective Programs for Beginners"* / *"Get Conversational Quickly."* CTA: "Start 7-day Free Trial." SEO-led headline (literally written for Google). Strong on press logos (Forbes, Travel+Leisure, Psychology Today) and a clear three-step method. Pimsleur's whole hook is *audio-first speaking* — and they say so within a screen-height.

**italki** — Hero: *"Start real learning, see clear progress"* with three sub-bullets: *"No subscriptions"*, *"Tired of app learning? Speak with a native teacher"*, *"A wide variety of tutors."* Above-the-fold is mostly **teacher faces with prices** — the product *is* the supply, so they show the supply. Smart pattern for a content-heavy product like yours.

**Hallow** (faith) — Hero: *"Find God's Peace in Prayer"* / *"Join Mark Wahlberg and Jonathan Roumie on Hallow, the #1 prayer app."* Celebrity endorsement *in the sub-headline*, not buried. Live counter: *"1,568,115,259 prayers prayed."* Authenticity signaled via specific named content (Rosary, Sacred Heart Novena) — not via "we respect tradition" platitudes. This is the playbook to steal.

**YouVersion Bible** — Hero: *"The Holy Bible. For Everyone. 100% Free."* / *"Trusted translations, in your language."* Dual CTA: "Start Reading" / "Listen." Hero is six words doing enormous work — *Everyone* (anti-gatekeeping), *Free* (anti-paywall), *Trusted translations* (authenticity). Underneath is **named content** (David & Goliath, The Prodigal Son) — the *stories themselves* are the social proof.

**Rosetta Stone** — Hero: *"A new era of Rosetta Stone is here."* Self-referential, brand-led. Works only because they have the brand equity. Not a model for you.

**Heritage Language Tool** (heritage-landing.vercel.app) — the only direct comp. Hero: *"Reconnect with Your Heritage Voice"* / *"...for heritage speakers and diaspora communities to speak their native language with confidence, emotion, and pride."* Opens with the exact pain question: *"Do you understand your heritage language but struggle to speak it confidently?"* Then *"The language is yours, but it doesn't always feel that way."* Then urgency: *"Our elders are growing older. Family stories are fading."* This is brutally on-target copy — and you should arguably do a version of it for *reading* specifically.

## 2. Patterns that consistently win

- **NN/g**: users spend ~57% of viewing time above the fold. The hero's job is *not* to close — it's to make scrolling feel worthwhile.
- **One headline, one promise, one CTA.** Babbel, Pimsleur, Hallow, Bible.com all do this. Busuu's "new you" is the cautionary tale.
- **Specificity beats superlatives.** "92% improved in 2 months" > "highly effective." "1.5B prayers prayed" > "the world's leading prayer app."
- **Show the product, don't describe it.** italki shows teacher faces; Bible.com shows story names; Babbel shows app screenshots. A wall of words above the fold is a tell that you don't trust the product.
- **Methodology section is table stakes** in language ed (Babbel "Proven Method," Pimsleur "3-step," Rosetta "The Method"). Buyers want to believe there's a *system*, not just content.
- **Press logos > B2B logos** for B2C learners. "As seen in Forbes" lands; "trusted by Uber HR" doesn't.

## 3. Heritage positioning, done well

Two things the Heritage Language Tool nails that generic apps can't touch:

1. **Naming the asymmetry**: *"understand but struggle to speak"* (for you: *"recognise the sounds but can't read the script"*). Heritage learners feel weirdly *behind* and weirdly *ahead* simultaneously; naming this is the whole game.
2. **Naming the stakes**: family, elders, identity, shame. Generic apps sell "fluency in 3 months." Heritage apps sell *belonging*.

What they handle as objections: shame at imperfect speech, no safe practice partner, "I've tried Duolingo and it felt childish." You'll want a fourth: *"I'm not religious / I don't want a scripture app."*

## 4. Anti-patterns to avoid

- **"Learn [language] for free"** — generic, SEO-bait, signals you're a Duolingo clone.
- **Stock photos of smiling multi-ethnic people in cafés.** Heritage learners read this as "for tourists."
- **Streak/gamification imagery in hero.** Will trigger immediate "this is Duolingo for Punjabi" filter.
- **Vague aspirational copy** ("new language, new you"). Heritage learners aren't reinventing themselves; they're recovering something.
- **Hiding the content library.** If your differentiator is *real sakhis*, the names of those sakhis should be on the page, the way Bible.com lists Prodigal Son and David & Goliath.
- **"Trusted by 500M learners"** when you don't have them. Don't fake-scale; lean into curation instead.

## 5. Recommendations for akhar.io

**Above the fold — one screen, three jobs:**

- **Headline (name the asymmetry):** Something like *"Read Punjabi the way your grandparents did."* Or sharper, problem-first: *"You can speak Punjabi. Now read it."* Or content-first: *"Learn Punjabi through the stories of the Gurus — not flashcards of fruit."* Test all three; the third is the most defensible because it bakes in your differentiator and the anti-Duolingo position simultaneously.
- **Sub-headline (name the mechanism):** *"Parallel-text sakhis with hover etymology, word-by-word audio, and two reading levels. Made for heritage readers and GCSE/A-Level Panjabi students."* — this single sentence does positioning, product, *and* audience qualification.
- **Visual:** Not a phone mockup. Show **a real sakhi excerpt** in Gurmukhi + romanisation + English, with one word highlighted mid-hover showing etymology. The product *is* the screenshot. This is your italki-teacher-faces moment.
- **Primary CTA:** *"Read your first sakhi"* (zero-friction, content-led — not "Sign up free"). Secondary: *"How it works"* anchor link.

**Sections below, in order:**

1. **The library, named.** Show 6–8 actual sakhi titles with the Guru, the book, the reading time. This is your Bible.com / Hallow move — the content *is* the proof. Anti-Duolingo signal.
2. **"For you if..."** — three columns: *Heritage reader (UK/Canada/US diaspora)* · *AQA GCSE/A-Level student* · *Adult learner reconnecting*. Qualifies traffic; makes the right people self-identify.
3. **How it works** — three steps, with a real screenshot per step (parallel text · hover lookup · sentence audio with highlighting). Methodology section is table stakes.
4. **Why sakhis, not flashcards** — your manifesto paragraph. Address the objection directly: *"Not a scripture app. Not a kids' app. Stories first, language second."* This is where you separate from both Duolingo *and* SikhNet/iGurbani.
5. **Two reading levels demo** — same sakhi, classical vs modern, side-by-side. This is a uniquely visual differentiator. Use it.
6. **Credibility you actually have:** the corpus stats (*"405 sakhis from 5 classical sources, every word linked to its dictionary entry"*), any teacher/scholar quotes, AQA syllabus coverage notes. Numbers about *content depth* beat user-count numbers you don't have.
7. **Testimonials** — even 3 short ones from beta heritage learners are worth more than abstract claims. Prioritise quotes that name the asymmetry ("I could speak with my dad but couldn't read a single page — now I can read a whole sakhi").
8. **FAQ** — handle: "Do I need to know Gurmukhi?" / "Is this a religious app?" / "How does this differ from SikhNet?" / "GCSE coverage?" / "Pricing?"
9. **Closing CTA** — repeat *"Read your first sakhi"* with no signup wall on at least one.

**Credibility signals that will actually move this audience:**

- Corpus scale stated concretely (*"405 sakhis, 6 Gurus, fully aligned audio"*).
- Source attribution to real classical texts (Suraj Prakash, Janamsakhi traditions, etc.) — heritage learners' parents will look for this.
- An endorsement from one named granthi, professor, or AQA teacher beats 100 anonymous five-star reviews.
- A free, no-signup "read one sakhi" path. Bible.com and Hallow both let you taste before logging in; you should too.
- AQA spec alignment (if real) called out by name — that's a high-intent SEO + credibility two-fer.

**One opinionated take:** your single biggest risk is sounding *worthy*. Sakhi content can drift into reverent register fast, and reverent copy doesn't convert heritage 20-somethings who are the actual buyers. Borrow Hallow's trick of being unapologetically specific about the tradition while keeping the *copy voice* warm, modern, and confident. The Heritage Language Tool's *"the language is yours, but it doesn't always feel that way"* is the emotional register to aim for.

Research is back — here's the synthesis + my opinionated take on the current landing page + a proposed redesign. Let me know which direction before I build.

# What's wrong with the current landing page

Going through it ruthlessly (`app/page.tsx`):

1. **"Read classical Punjabi, word by word"** — you nailed it: this positions us as a *reading tool*, not a *learning product*. It's literally a feature description, not a value prop. A heritage learner scanning this in 2 seconds thinks "academic" and bounces.

2. **Hero subtext does positioning, methodology, AND audience in one breath** — Babbel/Pimsleur all keep these as separate sections. Cramming "modern + classical, hover for etymology, save to deck" into one paragraph means none of it lands.

3. **Library shown to logged-out users** — your call to gate it, and I agree (more on this below).

4. **"Built for the diaspora — beginners, heritage learners, and anyone who never got the chance to learn the language they grew up hearing"** is actually the *best line on the page* and it's buried at the bottom in 12px grey text. That's the *real* emotional hook and it should be way more prominent.

5. **No mention of stories, Gurus, history, or context** in the hero — which is the actual differentiator. We're hiding what makes us different and leading with what makes us sound like a dictionary.

# Key research findings (compressed)

- **Sub-agent looked at**: Duolingo, Babbel, Busuu, Pimsleur, italki, Hallow (faith), Bible.com, Rosetta, Heritage Language Tool (the closest direct comp).
- **One headline, one promise, one CTA.** Don't try to do everything above the fold.
- **Specificity beats superlatives.** "92% improved in 2 months" beats "highly effective."
- **Show the product, don't describe it.** italki shows teacher faces. Bible.com shows story names. We should show a real sakhi with a hover popover mid-action.
- **Heritage positioning wins by naming the asymmetry**: "you can understand it but can't read it." The Heritage Language Tool's *"the language is yours, but it doesn't always feel that way"* is the emotional register.
- **For akhar specifically, the biggest anti-patterns**: stock photos of smiling tourists in cafés, "learn Punjabi for free" SEO bait, Duolingo-style gamification imagery, vague "new you" copy.
- **Credibility signals that work for us** (we don't have user-count to brag): corpus depth ("405 sakhis from 5 classical sources"), source attribution (Bhai Vir Singh, classical janamsakhis), an endorsement from one named granthi or AQA teacher, AQA syllabus alignment called out by name.
- **The risk to avoid**: sounding *worthy/reverent*. Sakhi content drifts there fast and reverent copy doesn't convert 20-somethings.

# Proposed redesign

**Above the fold — one screen, three jobs:**

- **Headline**: `Learn Punjabi through the stories your grandparents grew up with.`
- **Sub-headline**: `Real sakhis from the lives of the Gurus, in modern Punjabi and the classical literary register. Hover any word for meaning, etymology, and audio. Made for heritage readers and GCSE/A-Level Panjabi students.`
- **Visual** (the hero image): a **live screenshot of a sakhi** — parallel Gurmukhi + English, with one word actively hovered showing a popover with romanisation + gloss + audio button. The product *is* the screenshot. No phone mockup, no smiling stock face.
- **Primary CTA**: `Sign up to start reading` (since you want content gated). Secondary: `How it works` anchor link.

**Sections below (in order):**

1. **The library, named (but locked)** — show 6-8 actual sakhi titles in a "what's inside" preview, each with a lock icon → sign-in. Heritage learners see *"Birth of Guru Nanak"*, *"The True Bargain"*, *"Milk or Blood"* and recognise these — instant credibility.
2. **For you if...** — three columns: heritage reader · GCSE/A-Level student · adult learner reconnecting. Self-qualifies traffic.
3. **How it works** — three steps with real screenshots: parallel text → hover any word → sentence audio with highlighting.
4. **Why sakhis, not flashcards** — the manifesto. Address the objection: *"Not a scripture app. Not Duolingo for Punjabi. Stories first, language second."*
5. **Two reading levels demo** — same sakhi shown classical vs modern, side by side. Uniquely visual differentiator.
6. **Built on the classical sources** — list the books we're working from (Bhai Vir Singh, etc.). The corpus stats give us authority no startup can fake quickly.
7. **FAQ** — "Do I need to know Gurmukhi already?" / "Is this religious?" / "AQA coverage?" / "Pricing?"
8. **Closing CTA**.

# One tension I want to flag before building

You said *"if you are not logged in you shouldn't see or do any content."* The research strongly disagrees — Bible.com, Hallow, italki all let you *taste* before sign-up because content IS the proof. For us, that would mean letting a logged-out visitor read **one** sakhi (probably the modern Birth of Guru Nanak) without auth, with the rest of the library locked. The deck, hover lookups, audio, etc., would still need sign-in to *save* — but they could read one to *feel* the product.

**Three options — which one?**

{

  "content": "# Landing page research (2026-05-31)\n\nDeep research conducted by a sub-agent into what makes language-learning + education landing pages convert, with specific recommendations for akhar.io's positioning to heritage learners + AQA GCSE/A-Level Panjabi candidates.\n\nDecision taken from this research: **Stories framing** for the hero (\"Learn Punjabi through the stories your grandparents grew up with\") + **full content gating** (no sakhi access without sign-in — overrides the research recommendation that taste-first converts better; user prefers cleaner funnel for MVP).\n\n---\n\n## 1. Teardowns\n\n**Duolingo** — Hero: *\"The free, fun and effective way to learn a language.\"* Single primary CTA (\"Get started\"). The headline is three adjectives doing all the work; the page underneath is essentially a course picker plus a Trustpilot-style proof bar (\"Loved by language learners worldwide\", App of the Year awards, ~500M downloads). Notably they hide *what you actually do in a lesson* — the product is so well-known the hero doesn't bother. Lesson: only mass-market incumbents get to write copy this abstract.\n\n**Babbel** — Hero: *\"The effective way to learn a language online\"* / *\"Learn to speak a new language with confidence... so you can reach your goal of having real-life conversations faster.\"* CTA: \"Start learning.\" Below: method explanation, \"200+ language experts,\" \"92% of users improved proficiency in 2 months,\" \"25M+ subscriptions.\" This is the model template: outcome promise + methodology + numerical credibility + testimonials + FAQ.\n\n**Busuu** — Hero: *\"New language, new opportunities, new you\"* — vague aspirational. CTA: \"Learn for free.\" Leans hard on community (\"120 million learners\") and B2B logos (Puma, DHL, Uber). The \"new you\" framing is exactly the kind of generic self-help copy a heritage learner would scroll past.\n\n**Pimsleur** — Hero: *\"Learn New Languages Online: Effective Programs for Beginners\"* / *\"Get Conversational Quickly.\"* CTA: \"Start 7-day Free Trial.\" SEO-led headline (literally written for Google). Strong on press logos (Forbes, Travel+Leisure, Psychology Today) and a clear three-step method. Pimsleur's whole hook is *audio-first speaking* — and they say so within a screen-height.\n\n**italki** — Hero: *\"Start real learning, see clear progress\"* with three sub-bullets: *\"No subscriptions\"*, *\"Tired of app learning? Speak with a native teacher\"*, *\"A wide variety of tutors.\"* Above-the-fold is mostly **teacher faces with prices** — the product *is* the supply, so they show the supply. Smart pattern for a content-heavy product like ours.\n\n**Hallow** (faith) — Hero: *\"Find God's Peace in Prayer\"* / *\"Join Mark Wahlberg and Jonathan Roumie on Hallow, the #1 prayer app.\"* Celebrity endorsement *in the sub-headline*, not buried. Live counter: *\"1,568,115,259 prayers prayed.\"* Authenticity signaled via specific named content (Rosary, Sacred Heart Novena) — not via \"we respect tradition\" platitudes. This is the playbook to steal.\n\n**YouVersion Bible** — Hero: *\"The Holy Bible. For Everyone. 100% Free.\"* / *\"Trusted translations, in your language.\"* Dual CTA: \"Start Reading\" / \"Listen.\" Hero is six words doing enormous work — *Everyone* (anti-gatekeeping), *Free* (anti-paywall), *Trusted translations* (authenticity). Underneath is **named content** (David & Goliath, The Prodigal Son) — the *stories themselves* are the social proof.\n\n**Rosetta Stone** — Hero: *\"A new era of Rosetta Stone is here.\"* Self-referential, brand-led. Works only because they have the brand equity. Not a model for us.\n\n**Heritage Language Tool** (heritage-landing.vercel.app) — the only direct comp. Hero: *\"Reconnect with Your Heritage Voice\"* / *\"...for heritage speakers and diaspora communities to speak their native language with confidence, emotion, and pride.\"* Opens with the exact pain question: *\"Do you understand your heritage language but struggle to speak it confidently?\"* Then *\"The language is yours, but it doesn't always feel that way.\"* Then urgency: *\"Our elders are growing older. Family stories are fading.\"* This is brutally on-target copy — and we should arguably do a version of it for *reading* specifically.\n\n## 2. Patterns that consistently win\n\n- **NN/g**: users spend ~57% of viewing time above the fold. The hero's job is *not* to close — it's to make scrolling feel worthwhile.\n- **One headline, one promise, one CTA.** Babbel, Pimsleur, Hallow, Bible.com all do this. Busuu's \"new you\" is the cautionary tale.\n- **Specificity beats superlatives.** \"92% improved in 2 months\" > \"highly effective.\" \"1.5B prayers prayed\" > \"the world's leading prayer app.\"\n- **Show the product, don't describe it.** italki shows teacher faces; Bible.com shows story names; Babbel shows app screenshots. A wall of words above the fold is a tell that you don't trust the product.\n- **Methodology section is table stakes** in language ed (Babbel \"Proven Method,\" Pimsleur \"3-step,\" Rosetta \"The Method\"). Buyers want to believe there's a *system*, not just content.\n- **Press logos > B2B logos** for B2C learners. \"As seen in Forbes\" lands; \"trusted by Uber HR\" doesn't.\n\n## 3. Heritage positioning, done well\n\nTwo things the Heritage Language Tool nails that generic apps can't touch:\n\n1. **Naming the asymmetry**: *\"understand but struggle to speak\"* (for us: *\"recognise the sounds but can't read the script\"*). Heritage learners feel weirdly *behind* and weirdly *ahead* simultaneously; naming this is the whole game.\n2. **Naming the stakes**: family, elders, identity, shame. Generic apps sell \"fluency in 3 months.\" Heritage apps sell *belonging*.\n\nWhat they handle as objections: shame at imperfect speech, no safe practice partner, \"I've tried Duolingo and it felt childish.\" We need a fourth: *\"I'm not religious / I don't want a scripture app.\"*\n\n## 4. Anti-patterns to avoid\n\n- **\"Learn [language] for free\"** — generic, SEO-bait, signals we're a Duolingo clone.\n- **Stock photos of smiling multi-ethnic people in cafés.** Heritage learners read this as \"for tourists.\"\n- **Streak/gamification imagery in hero.** Will trigger immediate \"this is Duolingo for Punjabi\" filter.\n- **Vague aspirational copy** (\"new language, new you\"). Heritage learners aren't reinventing themselves; they're recovering something.\n- **Hiding the content library.** If our differentiator is *real sakhis*, the names of those sakhis should be on the page, the way Bible.com lists Prodigal Son and David & Goliath. **Note**: we are gating content per user decision, so we'll show sakhi *titles* (locked icons) as a preview rather than full library access.\n- **\"Trusted by 500M learners\"** when we don't have them. Don't fake-scale; lean into curation instead.\n\n## 5. Recommendations for akhar.io\n\n**Above the fold — one screen, three jobs:**\n\n- **Headline**: *\"Learn Punjabi through the stories your grandparents grew up with.\"*\n- **Sub-headline**: *\"Real sakhis from the lives of the Gurus, in modern Punjabi and the classical literary register. Hover any word for meaning, etymology, and audio. Made for heritage readers and GCSE/A-Level Panjabi students.\"*\n- **Visual**: Not a phone mockup. Show **a real sakhi excerpt** in Gurmukhi + romanisation + English, with one word highlighted mid-hover showing etymology. The product *is* the screenshot.\n- **Primary CTA:** *\"Sign up to start reading\"* (per gating decision).\n\n**Sections below, in order:**\n\n1. **The library, locked.** Show 6–8 actual sakhi titles with the Guru, book, reading time, lock icon. This is the Bible.com / Hallow move — the content *is* the proof. Anti-Duolingo signal.\n2. **\"For you if...\"** — three columns: *Heritage reader (UK/Canada/US diaspora)* · *AQA GCSE/A-Level student* · *Adult learner reconnecting*. Qualifies traffic; makes the right people self-identify.\n3. **How it works** — three steps with a real screenshot per step (parallel text · hover lookup · sentence audio with highlighting). Methodology section is table stakes.\n4. **Why sakhis, not flashcards** — manifesto paragraph. Address the objection directly: *\"Not a scripture app. Not a kids' app. Stories first, language second.\"* Separates us from both Duolingo *and* SikhNet/iGurbani.\n5. **Two reading levels demo** — same sakhi, classical vs modern, side-by-side. Uniquely visual differentiator.\n6. **Credibility we actually have:** corpus stats (*\"405 sakhis from 5 classical sources, every word linked to its dictionary entry\"*), any teacher/scholar quotes, AQA syllabus coverage notes. Numbers about *content depth* beat user-count numbers we don't have.\n7. **Testimonials** — even 3 short ones from beta heritage learners worth more than abstract claims. Prioritise quotes that name the asymmetry (\"I could speak with my dad but couldn't read a single page — now I can read a whole sakhi\"). **Status: don't have these yet; defer.**\n8. **FAQ** — handle: \"Do I need to know Gurmukhi?\" / \"Is this a religious app?\" / \"How does this differ from SikhNet?\" / \"GCSE coverage?\" / \"Pricing?\"\n9. **Closing CTA** — repeat *\"Sign up to start reading\"*.\n\n**Credibility signals that will actually move this audience:**\n\n- Corpus scale stated concretely (*\"405 sakhis, 6 Gurus, fully aligned audio\"*).\n- Source attribution to real classical texts (Suraj Prakash, Janamsakhi traditions, etc.) — heritage learners' parents will look for this.\n- An endorsement from one named granthi, professor, or AQA teacher beats 100 anonymous five-star reviews.\n- AQA spec alignment (if real) called out by name — that's a high-intent SEO + credibility two-fer.\n\n**One opinionated take:** the single biggest risk is sounding *worthy*. Sakhi content can drift into reverent register fast, and reverent copy doesn't convert heritage 20-somethings who are the actual buyers. Borrow Hallow's trick of being unapologetically specific about the tradition while keeping the *copy voice* warm, modern, and confident. The Heritage Language Tool's *\"the language is yours, but it doesn't always feel that way\"* is the emotional register to aim for.\n\n---\n\n## Sources\n\n- [CXL — How to build a high-converting landing page](https://cxl.com/blog/how-to-build-a-high-converting-landing-page/)\n- [CXL — Above the fold](https://cxl.com/blog/above-the-fold/)\n- [NN/g — Homepage design principles](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/homepage-design-principles/)\n- [Heritage Language Tool](https://heritage-landing.vercel.app/)\n- [Caffeine Marketing — Top EdTech landing pages 2025](https://www.caffeinemarketing.com/blog/top-13-edtech-landing-page-designs)\n- [Unbounce — State of SaaS landing pages](https://unbounce.com/conversion-rate-optimization/the-state-of-saas-landing-pages/)\n- [Marketing Examples — Landing pages](https://www.marketingexamples.com/landing-page)\n- [Busuu — What is a heritage language](https://www.busuu.com/en/languages/heritage-language)\n- Landing pages teardowned directly: babbel.com, busuu.com, pimsleur.com, italki.com, hallow.com, bible.com, rosettastone.com, duolingo.com\n"

1	// Refresh Supabase session cookies on every server request AND enforce
2	// "must be signed in" for app routes. Public routes:
3	//   /              (landing page — the pitch)
4	//   /login         (sign-in chooser: Apple / Google / email-OTP)
5	//   /login/verify  (enter the 6-digit OTP code)
6	//   /auth/*        (OAuth callback for Apple / Google)
7	//   /api/*         (handlers do their own auth where needed)
8	//   static assets
9	// Everything else (sakhi, guru, deck, etc.) redirects to /login?next=...
10	//
11	// Additionally: signed-in users who haven't completed onboarding get
12	// bounced to /onboarding (except when they're already there or hitting
13	// API/auth routes).
14	import { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
15	import { createServerClient } from "@supabase/ssr";
16	
17	const PUBLIC_PATHS = new Set(["/", "/login", "/login/verify"]);
18	const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ["/auth/", "/api/"];
19	// Routes a signed-in but not-yet-onboarded user is allowed to reach,
20	// on top of all the truly public routes above. /onboarding itself, sign-
21	// out, and the auth/API surfaces need to stay accessible.
22	const ONBOARDING_ALLOWED_PATHS = new Set(["/onboarding", "/"]);
23	
24	function isPublic(pathname: string): boolean {
25	  if (PUBLIC_PATHS.has(pathname)) return true;
26	  return PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p));
27	}
28	
29	export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
30	  let response = NextResponse.next({ request });
31	  const supabase = createServerClient(
32	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
33	    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,
34	    {
35	      cookies: {
36	        getAll() {
37	          return request.cookies.getAll();
38	        },
39	        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
40	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>
41	            request.cookies.set(name, value),
42	          );
43	          response = NextResponse.next({ request });
44	          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
45	            response.cookies.set(name, value, options),
46	          );
47	        },
48	      },
49	    },
50	  );
51	  // Touching getUser() triggers the auto-refresh of cookies if needed.
52	  const {
53	    data: { user },
54	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
55	
56	  const { pathname, search } = request.nextUrl;
57	  if (!user && !isPublic(pathname)) {
58	    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
59	    url.pathname = "/login";
60	    url.search = `?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname + search)}`;
61	    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
62	  }
63	
64	  // Gate signed-in users on completing onboarding before they reach any
65	  // real product surface. Skipped for the truly-public routes (so they
66	  // can still see the landing page) and the onboarding page itself.
67	  if (
68	    user &&
69	    !ONBOARDING_ALLOWED_PATHS.has(pathname) &&
70	    !PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p))
71	  ) {
72	    const { data: profile } = await supabase
73	      .from("profiles")
74	      .select("onboarding_completed_at")
75	      .eq("user_id", user.id)
76	      .maybeSingle();
77	    if (!profile?.onboarding_completed_at) {
78	      const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
79	      url.pathname = "/onboarding";
80	      url.search = "";
81	      return NextResponse.redirect(url);
82	    }
83	  }
84	
85	  return response;
86	}
87	
88	export const config = {
89	  matcher: [
90	    "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|mp3)$).*)",
91	  ],
92	};
93

recognise\n      </h2>\n      <p className=\"mx-auto mt-3 max-w-xl text-center text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n        From the janamsakhi traditions and the writings of Bhai Vir Singh —\n        each one paired with a simpler modern retelling.\n      </p>\n      <ul className=\"mx-auto mt-8 grid max-w-2xl gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2\">\n        {featuredGroups.map((g) => (\n          <li\n            key={g.event_key}\n            className=\"flex items-center justify-between rounded-lg border border-zinc-200 bg-zinc-50 px-4 py-3 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-900\"\n          >\n (\n        <p className=\"mt-4 text-center text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n          + {totalGroups - featuredGroups.length} more in the library\n        </p>\n      )}\n    </section>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction export const metadata = {
  title: "Learn Gurmukhi — akhar.io",
  description:
    "A guided path through the Gurmukhi script: 35 letters, vowel signs, special symbols, and reading practice. Modelled on JS Nagra's Panjabi Made Easy.",

// The alphabet section is a sequential curriculum, not a reference grid.
// Letters → nukta → reference chart → recognition test → (matras + concepts
// added incrementally in follow-up commits).
export default function AlphabetIndex() {
  const primer = CURRICULUM.filter((l) => l.kind === "primer");
  const letters = CURRICULUM.filter((l) => l.kind === "letter");
  const nuktaAndRef = CURRICULUM.filter(
    (l) => l.kind === "nukta-group" || l.kind === "chart" || l.kind === "exercise",
  );
  const mukta = CURRICULUM.filter((l) => l.kind === "mukta");
  const matras = CURRICULUM.filter((l) => l.kind === "matra");
  // Diacritics + stories interleave in the curriculum order so the index
  // mirrors the actual sequence the learner will go through.
  const conceptsAndStories = CURRICULUM.filter(
    (l) => l.kind === "concept" || l.kind === "story",
  );
  const glossary = CURRICULUM.filter((l) => l.kind === "glossary");

  let idx = 1;
  return (
    <div className="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 sm:py-10">
      <header className="mb-10 border-b border-zinc-200 pb-6 dark:border-zinc-800">
        <p className="text-sm uppercase tracking-widest text-zinc-500">
          ਪੈਂਤੀ ਅੱਖਰ · paintee akhar
        </p>
        <h1 className="mt-2 text-3xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">
          Learn Gurmukhi
        </h1>
        <p className="mt-3 max-w-2xl text-base text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400">
          A guided path through the Punjabi script — one concept at a time,
          with real example words, reading practice, and audio for every
          word. Built around the classic methodology of JS Nagra&apos;s
          <em> Panjabi Made Easy</em>.
        </p>
      </header>

      <Section title="Start here">
        <LessonList lessons={primer} startIndex={idx} />
      </Section>
      {(() => { idx += primer.length; return null; })()}

  "content": "---\nname: feedback-landing-copy\ndescription: Copy rules for akhar.io marketing pages — what NOT to say (unbuilt features, edtech jargon, \"Gurmukhi\")\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nThree constraints Sumeet imposed on landing-page (and other marketing) copy on 2026-05-31:\n\n**1. Don't advertise features that aren't built yet.**\n- No GCSE / A-Level / AQA mentions. The exam-prep angle is roadmap, not MVP.\n- Generally: never put a capability on the landing page unless a user could actually use it today. If it's \"coming soon\" → leave it out entirely, don't tease.\n\n**Why:** Sumeet hates seeing claims he can't back up. Trust matters more than completeness.\n**How to apply:** Whenever I write marketing copy, audit against the current built feature set. If unsure, ask before claiming.\n\n**2. Don't use \"heritage learner\" / \"heritage reader\" / similar edtech jargon.**\n- Use concrete descriptions instead: \"you grew up around the language,\" \"you can speak some but never learned to read,\" \"diaspora kid,\" \"coming back to it.\"\n- Plain words beat academic labels for this audience.\n\n**Why:** The term lands cold — too academic, too clinical for a warm consumer product. Sumeet wants the copy voice to feel like a Punjabi person talking to another Punjabi person, not an edtech marketer.\n**How to apply:** Describe situations, not categories. Audience cards should lead with what the reader's life looks like, not a label for them.\n\n**3. Don't call the script \"Gurmukhi\". Use \"Punjabi\" / \"Punjabi script\" / \"Punjabi alphabet\".**\n- \"complete Punjabi course\" not \"complete Gurmukhi course\"\n- \"the Punjabi alphabet (paintee akhar)\" not \"the Gurmukhi alphabet\"\n- \"Do I need to read Punjabi already?\" not \"Do I need to know Gurmukhi?\"\n- \"paintee akhar\" stays — it's the in-script name for the 35 letters, not a script-name claim.\n\n**Why:** Calling everyday Punjabi reading \"Gurmukhi\" over-religious-ifies it. Gurmukhi connotes Gurbani / scripture / Sikh-religious context; the product teaches general Punjabi literacy through (Sikh) cultural stories — those are different framings. Heritage Hindus + Muslims + non-religious folks reading Punjabi shouldn't feel othered by the script's name.\n**How to apply:** Anywhere I'm about to say \"Gurmukhi\" in user-facing copy, swap for \"Punjabi\" or \"the Punjabi alphabet/script\". Only exception: when explicitly discussing scripture or the script's etymology, where \"Gurmukhi\" is the historically accurate term.\n\nSee also: [[project-punjabi-platform]] for the overall product positioning, [[user-punjabi-learning]] for the user's own learning context.\n"
}

"Just sakhis" works for a specific kind of learner (you, me, the heritage-cultural-curious crowd), but most people learning Punjabi want to be able to actually *talk* — to their dadi-ji, at the dukaan, with their cousins. That's a different job from reading classical literature. If we don't serve that, we're a niche literary tool, not a Punjabi learning app.

Here's the tension I want to be honest about: **sakhis are our differentiator, but they're nobody's "must-have."** People want sakhis when they discover us, not when they're searching for "learn Punjabi." So we need basics as the *gateway* and sakhis as the *depth*.

A few ways this could shake out, with tradeoffs:

**A) Bolt on a basics module.** Short lessons on greetings/family/numbers/colors/tenses, separate from sakhis. Clean, fast to build. Risk: we look like Duolingo with a fancy library attached — basics feel un-akhar.

**B) Themed lessons that bridge into sakhis.** Each theme (family, food, work, weather) has bite-size vocabulary + a sample dialogue + a short sakhi snippet using those words. *"Family" lesson teaches mata/pita/bhain/veer, then you read the opening of sakhi 1 where Tripta Ji and Mehta Kalu Ji are named.* This is the most "us" approach but content-heavy.

**C) Conversational track + sakhi track as parallel paths.** Two clear journeys on the homepage. Users pick "I want to talk to my family" or "I want to read the stories." This is the most honest about the two audiences but feels less unified.

Good — that gives us a clear north star. **Basics → Reading practice → Sakhis → Gurbani**, with a real progression system that always tells you "what's next."

Here's a sketch of how I'd lay out the spine. Push back hard on anything that feels wrong.

## A 5-stage path

**Stage 1: Foundations** (weeks 1-2)
35 letters, matras, diacritics — bite-size, audio-first. First ~50 essential words drawn from sakhi vocabulary (people, simple nouns). Outcome: can sound out any Punjabi word.

**Stage 2: Everyday Punjabi** (weeks 3-6)
Themed mini-lessons (5-10 min each): family · numbers · colors · time · home · food · weather · money · feelings · simple verbs. Each theme = 10-15 words + 1 sentence pattern + a 2-3 sentence "reading bite." Tenses introduced gently as you meet them. Outcome: can read short modern sentences.

**Stage 3: Modern sakhis** (weeks 7-12)
The akhar Stories. Full readings with hover etymology + audio + saved-words flowing into your deck. Lessons here = "read one sakhi + review its new vocab." Outcome: independent reading of modern Punjabi prose.

**Stage 4: Classical sakhis** (weeks 13+)
Bhai Vir Singh + janamsakhis — literary register, archaic vocabulary, longer sentences. Outcome: read Bhai Vir Singh comfortably.

**Stage 5: Gurbani** (advanced)
Selected shabads with translation, transliteration, grammar notes for archaic constructions. Optional — your "now I can finally read Japji" payoff.

## What a single lesson looks like

5-10 minutes, always the same shape:
1. **3-5 new words** with audio + romanization + meaning
2. **One pattern** showing how they connect ("X ਦਾ ਨਾਉਂ Y ਹੈ")
3. **One reading bite** — a real sentence using them, sakhi-derived where possible
4. **Quick check** — recognize / hear / type
5. **Words auto-save** to your deck for SRS

## The path UI

Think Duolingo's vertical path, but adult: a clean vertical line of nodes, each node a lesson or a sakhi or a reading. You always see the next 2-3 nodes ahead. You can jump back to anything you've completed. **Onboarding's `prior_knowledge` field drops you in at the right stage** — `none` starts at Stage 1, `spoken` at Stage 2, `readable` at Stage 3.

## What I'd steal from Duolingo (and what I wouldn't)

**Steal:** the always-visible "next step," 5-min commitment threshold, topic clusters, visual progress, light streak signal.
**Skip:** XP/crowns/leagues, owl notifications, endless drilling, child-energy gamification — your audience is adults learning their ancestral language, not 12-year-olds.

---

## Three decisions I want your gut on before going further

1. **Sequential or open?** Strict unlock (Stage 2 locked until Stage 1 done) vs suggested-but-skippable (path shows the recommended order but power users can jump anywhere). I lean **suggested-but-skippable** — heritage learners often have weird gaps and hate gatekeeping. But strict gives stronger "I'm progressing" feeling.

2. **How early do sakhis appear?** Three options:
   - *Stage 3+ only* (clean separation: basics first, sakhis as reward)
   - *Stage 2 micro-snippets* (one-line sakhi quotes appear as reading bites, full sakhis come at Stage 3)
   - *Day one* (every reading bite, even on Day 1, is a real sakhi line) — most differentiating, hardest to author

3. **Grammar — explicit or implicit?** Babbel teaches grammar in dedicated lessons ("today: past tense"). Pimsleur teaches it by repeated patterns, never naming the rule. For reaching Gurbani eventually, I think we need **some explicit notes inline** ("This verb is in the historic present — common in classical Punjabi narration"), surfaced when it matters but not as standalone lessons.

Which of these three do you have the strongest opinion on?

The vocab-gated sakhi idea is the best thing in this conversation. Let me sketch what it actually means in practice, because it changes how we design lessons.

## The unlock loop

Every sakhi gets a **vocabulary requirement list** — the high-frequency words you need to know to read it without the hover popup feeling like a crutch. Each lesson teaches a chunk of those words. When you've learned enough, the sakhi "unlocks" and appears on your path as the next milestone.

**Concretely, for sakhi 1 (Birth of Guru Nanak):** maybe 25 required words — mother/father/sister/brother, the names (Nanak/Tripta/Kalu/Nanaki), to-be/to-say/to-do, "village," "year." Do the *family*, *names*, and *common verbs* themes → "Birth of Guru Nanak" unlocks on your path.

This creates a really nice loop:
- "Learn these 15 words and you can read the Birth of Guru Nanak" — concrete motivation
- Sakhi acts as the **payoff**, not as another lesson
- Reading it teaches you ~20 new words in context, which feed back into your deck and unlock the *next* sakhi
- The path naturally rhythms: **lessons → sakhi → lessons → sakhi → lessons → classical sakhi**

## What this means for the 4 stages

Same shape, Gurbani gone:
1. **Foundations** — letters + sounds + first ~50 sakhi words
2. **Everyday Punjabi** — themes (family, food, numbers, etc.) — each theme also pre-loading words for an upcoming sakhi
3. **Modern sakhis** — akhar Stories unlock as you complete the relevant themes
4. **Classical sakhis** — Bhai Vir Singh + janamsakhis unlock once you've absorbed enough modern register

Themes aren't arbitrary — they're chosen because **each one unlocks 1-2 specific sakhis**. That's the design discipline that keeps it sakhi-focused without forcing sakhis on Day 1.

## The next thing to nail

I think the question to answer next is: **what does the user actually see when they log in?**

Two candidates:

**A. A vertical path** (Duolingo-style). Today's lesson at the top, next 2-3 nodes visible, sakhi milestones glowing with "12/15 words to unlock." Feels like progression. Risk: rigid, easy to feel "behind."

**B. A dashboard** — "Continue lesson" tile + "Saved words to review" tile + "Sakhis you can read now" tile + "Sakhis you're close to unlocking" tile. More flexible, less "what to do next" obvious.

I lean **A** for absolute beginners (the path is the whole product) and a **dashboard that includes a path** for returning users. Maybe the same screen, just configured by stage.

Which one feels more like how you'd want a learner to land?

Both calls are right and they tighten the design discipline significantly.

**On names** — yes, agreed. Names are sakhi-specific (Tripta/Kalu/Mardana/Bhai Lalo/Malik Bhago aren't reusable vocabulary), and padding "family theme" with them would make the lesson feel hollow. Best handling: each sakhi gets a tiny **"cast" intro** at the top — *"In this sakhi: Mehta Kalu Ji (Nanak's father), Mata Tripta Ji (his mother), Bibi Nanaki (his sister)..."* — quick read, doesn't pretend to be a vocab lesson. Names get hover popovers too, so the reader can always re-check.

**On coverage discipline** — this is the rule that makes or breaks the whole thing. Every non-name word in a sakhi must be covered by the themes the learner has done by the time it unlocks. Otherwise the unlock is a lie. This means we design themes *backwards from the sakhi vocabulary*, not forwards from a generic textbook.

Practically, that means for any sakhi:
1. Tokenize it
2. Strip out proper nouns (auto via the cast list)
3. Strip out things that are purely classical-register decoration handled by hover (e.g., literary archaisms — they get glossed in-line, not pre-taught)
4. Whatever's left = the required vocab set
5. Every word in that set must belong to a theme

The themes that emerge will probably look weirder than Duolingo's. Sakhi 1's vocab will demand themes like *"common modern verbs (be/say/do/go)"* and *"family + village life"* — but it'll also force in things like *"the small world of a child"* (cradle, courtyard, pond) and maybe *"religious figures we'll keep meeting"* (sant, faqir, sadhu — these recur across sakhis 1, 16, 38). That's fine — it's honest to the reading goal.

## The actual structure

- **Sacha Sauda** → maps to *work, money, giving*
- **Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago** → maps to *food, honest work, hospitality*

Some themes won't have a natural sakhi event:
- **Colors** — no sakhi is about colors
- **Numbers / dates / telling time** — these appear *inside* sakhis but no sakhi is *about* them
- **Days of the week, months** — same
- **Modern things** (technology, transport, jobs) — anachronistic to sakhis

For these we'd have a theme without a sakhi payoff — just vocab + generic practice. That's probably fine, but worth deciding now whether:
- (a) Every theme tries to have a sakhi, even if it's a stretch (force *"colors"* into the Wali Kandari story because there's a mention of water/sky/mountains?)
- (b) Some themes just don't have a sakhi payoff and that's OK
- (c) We design *themes* so they naturally map to sakhis, even if that means smaller / weirder themes ("the small world of childhood" instead of "colors")

> AGENT

Yes — the alphabet → mukta → muharni → simple sentences → vocab sequence is the *actual* traditional Punjabi pedagogy. JS Nagra structures his book this way for a reason: muharni in particular is the unlock that takes you from "I recognise the letters" to "I can read any word." Skipping it is what most modern apps get wrong.

## Stage 1 as I understand it

This is pre-vocab-themes, all about reading capability:

1. **Paintee akhar** — the 35 letters with audio + recognition
2. **Mukta words** — reading consonant-only words (ਘਰ, ਕਮਲ, ਜਨਮ). Builds *letters → words* fluency before matras complicate things.
3. **Muharni** — the systematic consonant × matra grid (ਕ ਕਾ ਕਿ ਕੀ ਕੁ ਕੂ ਕੇ ਕੈ ਕੋ ਕੌ ...). Heavy drill but the unlock.
4. **Diacritics** — tippi/bindi (nasalisation) + addhak (gemination)
5. **Basic sentences** — short sentences using everything above, sakhi-derived where possible

Only *after* Stage 1 do we get into themed vocab.

I think our `/alphabet` curriculum already covers letters + mukta + some diacritics (from what I saw in `data/curriculum.ts`), but I'm not sure muharni gets its own dedicated drill section. Worth checking — if not, that's a real gap.

## Stage 2 — the themes question

Here's where I think real research helps, because there are three different lenses for picking themes:

1. **Standard L2 curriculum themes** (CEFR-aligned) — greetings, family, numbers, food, time, weather, home, school, transport, feelings, etc. ~20-25 themes.
2. **Traditional Punjabi school curriculum** — what India's state Punjabi syllabus actually teaches in years 1-3 (often different priorities, more cultural).
3. **Heritage-learner-specific** — what *diaspora* learners actually need first: family terms (for dadi-ji conversations), religious-cultural figures (sant/sadhu/granthi for sakhi reading), Punjab geography, common honorifics, kinship terms beyond the English equivalents (mama, masi, bua etc).

The right answer is probably a blend, but the proportions matter — heavy on heritage-learner needs in the early themes, mainstream L2 themes coming in later.

## Where research would help

I'd want to look at:

- **JS Nagra's full curriculum sequence** (since we already model on it) — what specifically does he have for muharni + what order do his post-alphabet topics come in?
- **The Indian Punjabi school syllabus** (CBSE / Punjab board, Years 1-3) — what's the canonical order Punjabi-medium kids learn in?
- **Heritage-language curricula** — how do Yiddish/Hebrew/Mandarin heritage programs sequence themes for diaspora kids vs total beginners?
- **Sikh missionary college Punjabi courses** (if any are public) — they have specifically the heritage-learner-meets-cultural-text problem we have

## What I'd ask you

Before I spin off a research agent — **which of those three lenses do you want to weight heaviest?** I think there are three possible product positions:

- (a) **Modern L2 standard** with cultural seasoning — basically Duolingo's themes, with sakhi payoffs. Broadest market, least differentiated.
- (b) **Traditional Punjabi-school sequence** — what an Indian kid learns first. Most "authentic" but maybe too primary-school-feeling for adult diaspora.
- (c) **Heritage-learner-led** — themes ordered by what your dadi-ji conversation needs first, then broadens. Most differentiated, narrowest initial audience.

My gut says **(c) with (a) layered in later** — own the heritage learner first, then broaden. But I want your read.
