The heritage-pedagogy literature (Beaudrie/Ducar/Potowski, Kagan) is firm: HL learners are bored by what they already passively know (colours, numbers) and hungry for what their parents never taught them in English (kinship granularity, religious register, festival vocabulary). akhar should follow HL pedagogy, not the GCSE textbook tradition we currently mirror.

1	# Curriculum research: theme sequence for akhar.io
2	
3	Background: akhar.io teaches Gurmukhi reading and Punjabi vocabulary to UK/Canada/US diaspora learners who can usually understand some spoken Punjabi but cannot read script. Stages 0–4 (alphabet → mukta → muharni → diacritics → basic sentences) are decided. This document researches what should fill Stage 5+: the **theme sequence** for vocabulary expansion, with sakhi (Guru-story) payoffs at the end of relevant themes.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Executive summary
8	
9	Across four lenses, three things converge:
10	
11	1. **Personal-world first.** Every credible curriculum (UK GCSE Panjabi, PSEB Class 1, NETA Hebrew Alpha, Workers Circle Yiddish, Integrated Chinese, Ma Liping, SHL Spanish) opens the same way: *greetings → self → family → home → school/daily routine → food*. This is not coincidence; it tracks the actual frequency distribution of beginner discourse and gives a heritage learner immediate recognition wins.
12	2. **Heritage learners are not L2 beginners.** The HL literature (Kagan, Beaudrie, Potowski, Ducar) is unanimous that heritage curricula should (a) skip nothing-to-something vocabulary they already passively know, (b) front-load *literacy on top of existing orality*, and (c) prioritise culturally specific vocabulary their parents never coded for them in English (kinship beyond "uncle/aunt", religious/ritual terms, register variation).
13	3. **Culture is not the dessert, it's the load-bearing structure.** NETA Hebrew, Ma Liping Chinese and Yiddish at Workers Circle all bind language to text-as-identity early. Saving sakhis for "after the vocab" is exactly the L2-beginner mistake heritage pedagogy warns against. Sakhis should appear *as the unit anchor*, not as a reward badge.
14	
15	**Top-line recommendation:** build a 12-theme spine where each theme is *anchored by* a cultural artefact (sakhi, folk song, festival, or proverb) rather than tacking one on at the end. Order: greetings/self → family (Birth of Guru Nanak) → home → food (Bhai Lalo/Malik Bhago) → daily routine → school/learning → festivals/gurpurabs → people & community (Bhagat Puran Singh / charity sakhi) → places & travel → nature & seasons → trades & work → emotions & inner life. Defer GCSE-style abstract themes (politics, global issues, careers) to a later track.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Lens A: JS Nagra & the UK GCSE Panjabi tradition
20	
21	### What the Nagra books actually contain
22	
23	The Nagra series (Nagra Publications, Coventry; first published mid-1980s, multiple revisions through 2017) has four primary volumes plus workbooks. Concrete TOC data is hard to surface online — apnaorg.com hosts scans but pages are image-only; Amazon listings provide blurbs only ([Book 1](https://www.amazon.com/Punjabi-Made-Easy-Bk-1/dp/187038301X), [Book 2](https://www.amazon.com/Panjabi-Made-Easy-English-Punjabi/dp/1870383753), [Book 3 blurb on Blackwell's](https://blackwells.co.uk/bookshop/product/Panjabi-Made-Easy-Book-3-by-Jagat-Singh-Nagra-author/9781870383387)).
24	
25	From publisher descriptions, library catalogue records and Goodreads metadata:
26	
27	- **Book 1 (48pp)**: 35 paintee akhar with picture-keyed example word per letter, then the matra/lagaan set (sihari, bihari, aunkar, dulainkar, lavan, dulavan, hora, kanaura), tippi/bindi/addhak, the *muharni* table (consonant × vowel grid drilled systematically), and short word lists. No themed sentences.
28	- **Workbook 1**: tracing, matching, odd-one-out drills on the same content.
29	- **Book 2**: GCSE Foundation-tier prep. Theme-organised lessons with vocab + simple dialogue + comprehension Qs. Themes inferred from publisher description and the AQA spec it targets: family, home, school, food, free time, festivals.
30	- **Book 3 (revised 2017 for new GCSE)**: covers full AQA Foundation + Higher, expanding into social issues, travel, careers.
31	
32	### How Nagra handles muharni
33	
34	Muharni gets a **dedicated systematic drill** in Book 1 (single chapter, table format). This is the canonical Indian-school approach inherited intact. The drill is mechanical, not contextualised — no sentences, just the 35 × ~10 consonant-vowel grid pronounced as a chant. Our Stage 2 is already aligned with this.
35	
36	### What Nagra Book 3 covers (via AQA spec)
37	
38	The current [AQA GCSE Panjabi 8683 specification](https://www.aqa.org.uk/subjects/panjabi/gcse/panjabi-8683/specification/subject-content/themes) defines three themes that Nagra Book 3 maps to:
39	
40	1. **Identity & culture**: me/family/friends, relationships, marriage; technology & social media; free time (music, cinema, food, sport); customs & festivals in Panjabi-speaking communities.
41	2. **Local/national/international**: home/town/region, social issues (charity, healthy living), global issues (environment, poverty), travel & tourism.
42	3. **Current and future study & employment**: studies, school life, post-16 education, careers.
43	
44	### What to steal from Nagra; what to drop
45	
46	**Steal:** picture-keyed letter intro; the muharni drill (we already do this); the family→home→school→food→festivals progression in Book 2.
47	
48	**Drop / modernise:**
49	- Nagra is built for a 14-year-old sitting GCSE. Adult diaspora learners do not care about "my school subjects" or "post-16 education choices". Themes 2 and 3 of the AQA spec are mostly noise for our audience.
50	- Nagra's customs/festivals coverage is thin and treated as one chapter; we have much richer cultural material to draw on.
51	- Books are static; there's no SRS, no audio drill, no listening comprehension — all things we have leverage on.
52	- The whole series is mute on heritage-learner gaps (kinship terms, religious register).
53	
54	---
55	
56	## 3. Lens B: Indian Punjabi school syllabus (PSEB / NCERT)
57	
58	### Concrete sequence
59	
60	PSEB ("Punjab Pustak" / "Punjabi Pustak", Class 1, 1st language) is the canonical Indian text. Direct PDF is hosted by PSEB ([pseb.ac.in/books](https://www.pseb.ac.in/books)) and mirrored at [Byju's](https://cdn1.byjus.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Punjab-Board-Class-1-Punjabi-Language-Textbook.pdf) and [SelfStudys](https://www.selfstudys.com/books/punjab/state-books/class-1st/punjabi-pustak/6804). [AglaSem's PSEB Class 1 syllabus page](https://schools.aglasem.com/pseb-class-1-syllabus-punjabi/) confirms the high-level structure.
61	
62	The standard PSEB Class 1 sequence is:
63	
64	1. Paintee akhar (with picture-keyed mnemonics — same approach as Nagra)
65	2. Matras introduced one at a time with example words
66	3. Mukta words (no matra) — short reading practice
67	4. Two-letter, three-letter, four-letter word ladders
68	5. Simple two-word and three-word sentences
69	6. Short rhymes/poems (this is heavy in PSEB — multiple memorisable verses per year)
70	7. Short prose paragraphs on themes: *mera parivar* (my family), *mera ghar* (my home), *mera school*, *phull* (flowers), *rut* (seasons), *tyohar* (festivals)
71	8. Moral-story prose pieces from Class 2 onward (often Panchatantra, occasionally Sikh)
72	
73	NCERT does not publish a dedicated Punjabi-as-first-language series for Classes 1–3 in the way it does Hindi (*Rimjhim*); Punjabi-medium schools mostly use PSEB books. CBSE Punjabi-as-MIL kicks in later and parallels the PSEB sequence.
74	
75	### What to steal; what to drop
76	
77	**Steal:** the mukta-words-before-matras ordering (already done); heavy use of rhyme/song memorisation for matra internalisation (we underexploit this); short prose paragraphs on *mera parivar*, *mera ghar*, *rut*, *tyohar* as canonical first themes.
78	
79	**Drop:** moral-story Panchatantra fare (generic, not specifically Punjabi-cultural — sakhis serve this role better for us); poetic memorisation as a primary mode (works for 6-year-olds, not for 35-year-old diaspora professionals); the assumption of an oral baseline higher than our users have.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 4. Lens C: Heritage-language curricula in other languages
84	
85	This is the most useful lens because these languages have decades of dedicated HL pedagogy that Punjabi simply does not.
86	
87	### Hebrew — NETA / Bishvil Ha-Ivrit
88	
89	NETA is the leading US/UK Jewish-day-school Hebrew program (~20,000 students, 175 schools; [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neta_Hebrew); [AVI CHAI program page](https://avichai.org/program-listings/bishvil-ha-ivrit/)). Four sequential levels. **Alpha** (beginner) is 20 thematic units; intermediate books are organised around themes like *colour and form*, *symbols in Judaism*, *friendship*. NETA's design principle: every unit pairs a linguistic target with a Jewish-cultural anchor. Heritage learners aren't asked to learn Hebrew and then "discover" Jewish culture; the two are taught as one thing.
90	
91	**Implication for us:** structure each theme so the cultural anchor (sakhi, festival, song) defines the vocabulary, not the other way around.
92	
93	### Mandarin — Ma Liping Chinese
94	
95	The dominant US Chinese weekend-school text ([Mandarin Mama overview](https://mandarinmama.com/ma-liping-chinese-curriculum/); [series intro](https://sites.google.com/site/mlpchineseinfo/Home/mlpchineseinfo-eng/intro-to-mlp-curriculum)), 11 volumes K–Gr10. Explicitly designed for "Chinese American children of Chinese immigrants" — the textbook equivalent of our user. Notable design moves:
96	- **Direct Character Recognition** from day one, no pinyin scaffold for the first three years. Decoded text wins over phonetic crutch — the analogue for us is "Gurmukhi from day one, no transliteration crutch in the main path".
97	- Vocabulary themes hew tightly to the *daily life of a Chinese-American kid*: home, family, weekend Chinese school, festivals, food.
98	- Each volume = three units, each unit = ~10 weeks (a useful pacing benchmark).
99	
100	### Arabic — Al-Kitaab vs heritage tracks
101	
102	Al-Kitaab (Georgetown UP) is the dominant L2 textbook but is widely critiqued as wrong for heritage learners (see Teaching Arabic as a Heritage Language, Routledge 2019). Heritage-tracked university programs typically: (a) skip the formal-MSA-only stance and treat dialect as legitimate, (b) accelerate vocabulary because students already know food/family/greeting terms, (c) emphasise reading literacy as the actual gap. **Implication:** don't waste a week teaching the words for "mother" and "father" — diaspora Punjabis already know *biji/mummy/papa/daddy/pita-ji*; the unit on family should teach Gurmukhi spellings of words they already say, plus the kinship terms English flattens (chacha vs taya vs mama vs phupa).
103	
104	### Yiddish — Workers Circle / YIVO
105	
106	[Workers Circle Yiddish program](https://www.circle.org/yiddish) (largest in US outside academia) opens with "Learn to Read the Yiddish Alef-Beys" as a discrete short course, then beginner conversation/reading. Distinctive: thematic *cultural* electives (poetry, women religious leaders, Itsik Manger songs) run in parallel to language-skill courses from very early. The cultural strand and the language strand are not sequenced — they're interleaved. This is a strong argument for making sakhis *available* throughout the path, not gated behind theme completion.
107	
108	### Spanish — SHL (most-developed HL field)
109	
110	Beaudrie, Ducar & Potowski (2014, *Heritage Language Teaching: Research and Practice*, McGraw-Hill) — the standard reference — list seven goals for HL instruction. The two most relevant for us: **transfer of literacy skills** (orality → reading) and **acquisition/development of cultural awareness**. UCLA's [National Heritage Language Resource Center](https://nhlrc.ucla.edu) consistently recommends *macro-based* approaches (content-, theme-, project-, task-based) over discrete-grammar drills, because HL learners are bored by what they already know but hungry for what their parents never taught them.
111	
112	Concrete SHL syllabus structures (e.g. CUNY's [SPA 2201HS](https://academicworks.cuny.edu/ny_oers/19/), Texas A&M Commerce's SPA 333) typically open with *identity and family* and *food and traditions* before moving to *community*, *immigration narratives*, *literature*.
113	
114	### Cross-cutting heritage-learner patterns
115	
116	1. **Vocabulary prioritisation differs from L2.** Don't teach colours and numbers as Unit 1; learners likely know these passively. Do teach kinship granularity, religious/ritual register, idioms parents use, code-switched terms learners can't yet decode (e.g. "*sat sri akal*", "*shukrana*", "*ardas*").
117	2. **Literacy on top of orality.** The bottleneck is reading, not vocabulary. Front-load decoding practice on words learners already say.
118	3. **Identity affirmation.** Bicultural identity content (festivals, rituals, family elders, immigration stories) is *core curriculum*, not enrichment.
119	4. **Register variation matters early.** Polite/familial register (addressing elders), religious register (*ji*-honorifics, gurudwara vocabulary), informal banter — all need explicit teaching that L2 learners get later.
120	5. **Macro / content-based** beats discrete skill drill for engagement.
121	
122	---
123	
124	## 5. Lens D: Sikh institutional courses
125	
126	Material is sparse and inconsistent.
127	
128	- **Sikh Missionary College, Ludhiana** ([smc.org](https://sikhmissionarycollege.org/p.10.correspondence-course.html)): two-year correspondence course, eight trimesters. Covers shabad meaning (viakhya), Sikh history, stories, philosophy. Available in Punjabi, Hindi, English. This is *Sikhi-content* through Punjabi, not Punjabi-language teaching. Useful as a content source for sakhis and historical episodes, not as a curriculum model.
129	- **Khalsa Primary School, UK** ([khalsaschool.co.uk](https://www.khalsaschool.co.uk/old-curriculum/)) and Slough Punjabi School use the UK MFL scheme of work (read/write/speak/listen) adapted for Punjabi, mapped to KS1/KS2 levels. Themes mirror UK primary-MFL conventions (family, home, food, school) plus Sikh ethos content.
130	- **Guru Nanak Khalsa School (US)** ([khalsaschool.us](https://khalsaschool.us/curriculum/punjabi-curriculum)) uses an 8-level Gurmukhi progression with target reading speeds (120 wpm by Level 7), content explicitly Sikh-history-flavoured from Mughal period to Operation Blue Star.
131	- **NSW NESA Punjabi K–10 syllabus** ([NESA](https://educationstandards.nsw.edu.au/wps/portal/nesa/k-10/learning-areas/languages/punjabi-k-10-2019)) and the **Khalsa Punjabi School Australia** resources ([punjabischool.com.au](https://punjabischool.com.au/punjabiresources)) follow standard MFL macro-skills with Stage 1–6 progression.
132	
133	**Takeaway:** Sikh institutional courses confirm the family→home→school→food sequence and the centrality of Sikh-historical content, but offer no novel curriculum-design insight beyond what GCSE and PSEB already give.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Cross-cutting observations
138	
139	**Where all lenses agree:**
140	
141	- Opening 4–6 themes are nearly identical across all sources: *greetings & self → family → home → school/daily routine → food → festivals*.
142	- Themes should be concrete and visualisable before they get abstract.
143	- Literacy is the bottleneck for heritage learners, not vocabulary.
144	
145	**Where they disagree:**
146	
147	- **GCSE/Nagra** pushes into abstract civic themes (environment, careers, social issues) because the exam demands it. **HL pedagogy** and PSEB primary do not — they stay in concrete cultural-life themes much longer.
148	- **Nagra and PSEB** treat culture (festivals, stories) as a single chapter. **NETA, Ma Liping, SHL Spanish** treat culture as the *organising principle* of each unit.
149	- **L2 textbooks** front-load colours/numbers/days. **HL curricula** skip or compress these because learners passively know them.
150	
151	**Resolution for akhar.io:** follow HL pedagogy on macro-design and theme prioritisation; borrow GCSE/Nagra's concrete theme inventory but stop at the personal-cultural themes (don't chase the GCSE abstract themes for v1).
152	
153	---
154	
155	## 7. Proposed theme sequence for akhar.io
156	
157	Twelve themes for v1, ordered. Each is anchored by a cultural artefact (sakhi, festival, song, proverb) rather than ending with one. "Sakhi payoff" indicates whether we already have suitable retold-sakhi content.
158	
159	| # | Theme | Vocabulary focus | Cultural anchor | Sakhi status |
160	|---|---|---|---|---|
161	| 1 | **Hello & me** | greetings (sat sri akal, namaskar), name, age, where I'm from, *ji*-honorifics | Why "Sat Sri Akal" — short etymology piece | No sakhi; etymology card |
162	| 2 | **Family** | parivar, kinship granularity (chacha/taya/mama/phupa/masi/bhua), elders, generations | **Birth of Guru Nanak** | Have it |
163	| 3 | **Home** | ghar, rooms, household objects, beds/charpai, kitchen vs sitting room | A short Bhai Vir Singh domestic scene (we have these in corpus) | Use existing |
164	| 4 | **Food & honest work** | roti, dal, sabzi, mithai, langar; verbs for eat/cook/serve | **Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago** | Have it |
165	| 5 | **Daily routine** | wake/sleep/eat/work/pray; times of day; *amrit vela* | Short piece on *amrit vela* practice | No sakhi; cultural explainer |
166	| 6 | **School & learning** | parhna, likhna, kitab, school, teacher; verbs of study | Young Guru Nanak at school ("the lesson that broke the slate") | Need to write |
167	| 7 | **Festivals & gurpurabs** | tyohar, Vaisakhi, Diwali/Bandi Chhor, Lohri, gurpurab; nagar kirtan | **Vaisakhi 1699 / formation of the Khalsa** (age-appropriate retell) | Need to write |
168	| 8 | **People & community / seva** | sangat, seva, gurudwara, charity; verbs of helping | **Bhagat Puran Singh & Pingalwara** (modern saint) — fits charity theme we already serve | Have charity-marketplace content; need a focused sakhi |
169	| 9 | **Places & travel** | pind (village), shehar (city), Punjab geography, rivers (panj-aab), gurudware (Nankana Sahib, Amritsar) | A short geography piece on the five rivers | No sakhi; cultural map |
170	| 10 | **Nature & seasons** | rut, sardi/garmi/barsat, sun/moon/stars, flowers, trees, common animals | Bhai Vir Singh nature poem snippet | Use existing corpus |
171	| 11 | **Trades & work** | farmer/tarkhan/lohar/julaha/kisan; verbs of labour; tools | **Bhagat Namdev / Bhagat Kabir** — bhagats from labouring castes whose bani sits in SGGS | Need to write |
172	| 12 | **Emotions & inner life** | khushi, gham, pyaar, dard, sabar, chardi-kala; abstract nouns | A short Japji-derived reflection or a Guru Tegh Bahadur sakhi on sacrifice | Need to write (cultural sensitivity required) |
173	
174	After theme 12, the path tips into the existing classical-sakhi reading track (Bhai Vir Singh, full sakhis) which we already host.
175	
176	**Things to defer past v1** (these are GCSE-style themes that don't fit a diaspora-cultural reader): technology/social media, sport, politics/global issues, careers/jobs, post-16 education, healthy/unhealthy living. Worth picking up only if we build a teen GCSE-prep track later.
177	
178	**Things to interleave, not sequence** (per Workers Circle pattern): short cultural-elective content (a folk song lyric, a one-line proverb, a 2-minute sakhi audio) should be unlockable in parallel with the theme path, not gated by it. Identity-affirming content should feel ambient, not earned.
179	
180	---
181	
182	## 8. Open questions for Sumeet
183	
184	1. **Audience age inside "diaspora adult".** Is the design target a 35-year-old professional reconnecting with heritage, or a 16-year-old GCSE candidate? The proposed sequence is built for the former. If the latter is in scope, themes 2 and 3 from the AQA spec (social media, careers, global issues) need a parallel track.
185	2. **How religious do we go?** Themes 7, 8, 11, 12 all sit on Sikh ground. A non-Sikh Punjabi (Punjabi Hindu, Punjabi Muslim, secular British-Asian) might prefer Punjab-cultural framing over Sikhi-cultural framing. Do we serve them or are we explicitly Sikh-Punjabi?
186	3. **Modern Punjab vs nostalgic-village Punjab.** Most of our existing sakhi content and Bhai Vir Singh corpus is pre-Partition village Punjab. Should we add modern themes (city life, diaspora itself, Punjabi pop culture)? Heritage-pedagogy literature says yes — learners want to see their actual lives reflected — but our corpus says no.
187	4. **How long is a "theme"?** Ma Liping uses 8–10 weeks per unit; NETA Alpha covers 20 units across a school year. For a self-paced adult app, what's our pacing target — 1 theme per week of casual use, or 1 theme per month? This affects how deep each theme goes.
188	5. **Sakhi gap.** Themes 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 need new retold-sakhis written in simple modern Punjabi. Is that a content commission (Sumeet writes), an LLM-assisted draft + human edit pipeline, or a community contribution model?
189	6. **What about Patshahi 6/7/8/9?** Per project memory, our sakhi corpus is light on Gurus 6, 7, 8, 9. Theme 12 (sacrifice / inner life) is a natural home for Guru Tegh Bahadur (9). Theme 8 (seva) is natural for Guru Har Rai (7). Worth aligning content acquisition with theme rollout.
190

> AGENT

Research is in. Synthesizing + making the auto-mode calls on the open questions.

## Top three findings

1. **Personal-world-first is universal** — every credible curriculum (UK GCSE, PSEB, NETA Hebrew, Ma Liping Chinese, Spanish-for-Heritage) opens with the same 4-6 themes: greetings → family → home → school/daily routine → food. Not coincidence; tracks actual beginner discourse frequency.

2. **Heritage learners are NOT L2 beginners.** The HL literature is unanimous: skip vocabulary your learner already knows passively (colors, numbers, "uncle/aunt"). Teach instead the things English flattens out — kinship granularity (chacha/taya/mama/phupa), religious-cultural register, idioms parents use untranslated.

3. **Sakhis should ANCHOR themes, not END them.** This is the biggest design shift from what we discussed. NETA, Ma Liping, Workers Circle all bind language to text-as-identity *early*. "Vocab lesson → sakhi as reward" is the L2-beginner mistake HL pedagogy warns against. Each theme should be *built around* a sakhi, not chase one.

## Proposed 12-theme spine (full table in `docs/curriculum-research.md`)

| # | Theme | Sakhi anchor | Have it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hello & me | "Sat Sri Akal" etymology | No sakhi needed |
| 2 | Family | Birth of Guru Nanak | ✓ |
| 3 | Home | Bhai Vir Singh domestic scene | use corpus |
| 4 | Food & honest work | Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago | ✓ |
| 5 | Daily routine | *amrit vela* explainer | No sakhi needed |
| 6 | School & learning | Young Nanak / broken slate | **need to write** |
| 7 | Festivals & gurpurabs | Vaisakhi 1699 | **need to write** |
| 8 | Seva & community | Bhagat Puran Singh | **need to write** |
| 9 | Places & travel | Panj-aab geography | No sakhi needed |
| 10 | Nature & seasons | Bhai Vir Singh nature poem | use corpus |
| 11 | Trades & work | Bhagat Namdev / Kabir | **need to write** |
| 12 | Emotions & inner life | Guru Tegh Bahadur sacrifice | **need to write** (sensitive) |

After theme 12 → existing classical sakhi track.

**Defer past v1**: tech/social media, sport, politics, careers, healthy living. GCSE noise for our audience.

## My calls on the open questions (auto mode)

1. **Audience age** → 35-yo professional reconnecting. We already stripped GCSE positioning; the path follows.
2. **How religious** → Sikh-Punjabi explicitly. You're a Sikh-Punjabi building this; all 3 existing akhar Stories are Sikh; the FAQ already handles non-Sikh sensitivities ("not a scripture app, the focus is the language"). Pretending we're equally serving Hindu/Muslim Punjabis would be dishonest positioning. Sikh-Punjabi-first; non-Sikh Punjabis welcome but not the design target.
3. **Modern vs village Punjab** → Lean classical-village for sakhi content (that's our corpus moat), but contemporary framing for *theme cards* and explainer copy. Don't try to manufacture modern sakhis we don't have.
4. **Pacing** → 1 theme per 1-2 weeks of casual use; 10-12 week course total for foundation → all 12 themes. Roughly Ma Liping-pace, half NETA-pace.
5. **Sakhi gap (5 new ones needed)** → LLM-assisted draft → grandma editorial pass, same pipeline that produced the existing 3. Not a blocker for curriculum design; gates rollout of themes 6-12.
6. **Patshahi 6/7/8/9 coverage** → Align with theme rollout (Guru Tegh Bahadur for theme 12, Guru Har Rai for theme 8) — kills two birds.

## Next concrete step

The research changes one important thing in our model: **sakhi-as-anchor, not sakhi-as-payoff**. That has implications for how the path UI looks (the sakhi is the centre of each theme, not a milestone at the end) and for the landing page copy (which still says "save words to your deck and read sakhis as you go").

I'd hold off on changing the landing again until we've agreed the new theme-anchored model is right. The natural next step is to **sketch what one theme actually looks like as a sequence of lessons** — pick "Family" (since we have the sakhi), design the 5-8 lessons that lead in and out of the Birth of Guru Nanak, see if the shape works. If it does, the path UI and landing copy follow.

Want me to draft the "Family" theme as a concrete lesson sequence next, or push back on any of my open-question calls first?

31	## Key parser mechanisms
32	
33	**`scripts/build-sakhi-db.py`** — per-book BOOKS config drives splitting:
34	- `_find_body_start`: skips TOC by requiring ≥2 prose paragraphs (≥150 chars) before next chapter heading
35	- Monotonicity in `split_sakhis`: rejects backward ordinal jumps (footnotes) and jumps >+15 (years/sloka tags)
36	- Runaway-body section reset: when current sakhi accumulates >50k chars and a heading appears with ord ≤2 + real prose following, treat as volume boundary
37	- **`section_break_after_title_re`** per-book: when a chapter title matches (e.g. "ਜੋਤੀ ਜੋਤਿ" = Guru's passing, "ਅਮਰਿਤਾ ਵਿਚ ਪ੍ਰਵੇਸ਼" = entry into immortality), the next Patshahi restarts ordinals at 1. Critical for Bhai Vir Singh's multi-Patshahi books.
38	- `title_reject_re` per-book: filters known-bad heading patterns (Gurbani verses in 02-angad, footnote interjections "ਹੇ (ਮੈਂ)" + month names like "ਮਾਰਚ" in 02-09)
39	- `guru_for(section, ordinal)` per-book: maps multi-guru books to per-sakhi `primary_guru_id`
40	
41	**`sakhis/manual-fixes.json`** — per-book per-seq overrides applied after splitting. Each entry can set `title_pa`, `title_en`, `body_strip_prefix_re`, or `delete: true`. ~20 entries currently — most fix single-character OCR artifacts (curly quote `”`, leading function word like `ਨੂੰ`, doubled words).
42	
43	**`scripts/qc-sakhis.py`** — flags every sakhi for title quality (too short, garbage chars, trailing fragments), body coherence (no recent terminator, tiny/huge), and runs in <1s. Currently 43/405 flagged (10.6%); most are BODY_NO_RECENT_TERMINATOR false positives where the OCR didn't preserve a trailing `।`.
44	
45	## OCR pipeline
46	
47	`scripts/ocr-vision.py` — Google Cloud Vision DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION (key at `~/.config/lipi/vision-key.json`). The `_column_sorted_paragraphs` function now handles full-width chapter titles correctly: pulls them out of column flow, slots them by y-position between body bands. **Don't use `--columns 2`** for Bhai Vir Singh books — the pre-split cuts full-width titles in half. Single-column OCR + column-aware sorting gives clean titles + correct body reading order.
48	
49	`scripts/clean-ocr.py` — strips garbage lines, frequency-detects running headers, merges multi-line chapter titles across blank lines into a single titled paragraph terminated with `।`. The title-continuation threshold is `len(s) <= 25` chars (raised from 15 to handle longer wrapped titles).
50	
51	## To improve further (would need new sources)
52	
53	- **Gurus 6, 7, 8, 9**: need dedicated Punjabi sakhi PDFs. Looking for Bhai Vir Singh-style narrative collections or similar.
54	- **Ramdas (currently 26)**: more chapters embedded in the "ਹਰਿਨਾਮ ਤੀਰਥ" 22k body and "ਅੰਤਰ" 67k body. Would need a smarter recursive splitter that examines large-body sakhis for embedded markers.

Basic sentences\n\n**Open question on foundations:** does our current /alphabet curriculum have a *dedicated* muharni drill section? Worth verifying before declaring Stage 0–4 done. Also the reading-practice content in /alphabet currently uses JS Nagra's example words — needs to be regenerated using sakhi-derived vocabulary so the landing promise (\"real sakhi vocabulary from your first sentence\") is true.\n\n**Stage 5+ (themes)** — 12-theme spine, sakhi as ANCHOR (not payoff):\n\n| # | Theme | Sakhi anchor | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Hello & me | \"Sat Sri Akal\" etymology card | no sakhi |\n| 2 | Family | Birth of Guru Nanak | ✓ exists |\n| 3 | Home | Bhai Vir Singh domestic scene | use corpus |\n| 4 | Food & honest work | Bhai Lalo & Malik Bhago | ✓ exists |\n| 5 | Daily routine | amrit vela explainer | no sakhi |\n| 6 | School & learning | Young Nanak / broken slate | TO WRITE |\n| 7 | Festivals & gurpurabs | Vaisakhi 1699 (Khalsa formation) | TO WRITE |\n| 8 | Seva & community | Bhagat Puran Singh | TO WRITE |\n| 9 | Places & travel | Panj-aab geography | no sakhi |\n| 10 | Nature & seasons | Bhai Vir Singh nature poem | use corpus |\n| 11 | Trades & work | Bhagat Namdev / Kabir | TO WRITE |\n| 12 | Emotions & inner life | Guru Tegh Bahadur sacrifice | TO WRITE (sensitive) |\n\nAfter theme 12 → existing classical sakhi track (Bhai Vir Singh, full corpus).\n\n## Key design rules\n\n- **Sakhi as theme anchor, not theme payoff.** NETA Hebrew + Ma Liping + SHL Spanish all bind language to text-as-identity *early*. The L2 mistake is teaching vocab and putting cultural text \"after\" — heritage-language pedagogy says the cultural artefact organises the unit.\n- **No proper names in vocab themes.** Tripta/Kalu/Mardana/Lalo/Bhago are sakhi-specific, not transferable vocabulary. Each sakhi instead gets a tiny \"cast\" intro at the top — quick read, doesn't pretend to be a vocab lesson. Names get hover popovers like any other word.\n- **Coverage discipline.** Every non-name word in a sakhi must be covered by themes the learner has done by the time it unlocks — otherwise the unlock is a lie. Themes are designed *backwards* from sakhi vocab needs, not forwards from a generic textbook.\n- **Skip what heritage learners already know.** Don't unit-1 colors and numbers; learners already know \"blue\" passively. Teach instead the things English flattens (chacha vs taya vs mama vs phupa) and the things parents never explained (Sat Sri Akal etymology, *ji*-honorific use, langar, sangat).\n- **Path UI: Duolingo-style vertical** (suggested-but-skippable, not strict gating). Onboarding's `prior_knowledge` field drops user at the right stage: `none` → Stage 0, `spoken` → Stage 5 (themes), `readable` → Stage 8+ (modern sakhis).\n- **Pacing target:** 1 theme per 1-2 weeks casual use; 10-12 weeks for the full Stage 5+ path. Halfway between Ma Liping (8-10wk/unit) and NETA (~2wk/unit).\n- **Defer past v1:** technology/social media, sport, politics, careers, healthy living — GCSE noise for adult diaspora audience. Pick up only if/when teen GCSE track happens (not soon).\n\n## Sakhi gap — content production needed\n\nFive new modern simple sakhis to write (themes 6, 7, 8, 11, 12). Pipeline = LLM-assisted draft → Sumeet's grandma editorial pass. Same model that produced the existing 3 akhar Stories. Sakhi 12 (Guru Tegh Bahadur) needs extra care — sensitive material.\n\nWorth aligning with the [[project-sakhi-db-state]] Patshahi-6/7/8/9 coverage gap: theme 8 (seva) can introduce Guru Har Rai context; theme 12 (sacrifice) is the natural home for Guru Tegh Bahadur. Two birds.\n\n## Where work paused on 2026-06-01\n\nLast unanswered question Sumeet was deciding on: **draft the \"Family\" theme as a concrete lesson sequence next** (to validate the model in detail before designing path UI + updating landing), OR push back on my auto-mode decisions first. Building hasn't started — landing page still describes the OLD \"sakhi-as-payoff\" model in its FAQ / pillars / how-it-works copy. **When resuming: that landing pass needs updating to match the new \"sakhi-anchored\" framing.**\n\nSee [[feedback-landing-copy]] for the copy constraints any landing update has to honour.\n"
}

2	// to the right Sentry config based on whether we're in Node.js or Edge
3	// runtime. Without this, server-side errors don't reach Sentry.
4	import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nextjs";
5	
6	export async function register() {
7	  const dsn = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN;
8	  if (!dsn) return;

10	  Sentry.init({
11	    dsn,
12	    tracesSampleRate: 0.1,
13	    sendDefaultPii: false,

16	}

## The paywall conversation

Standard heritage-app patterns I've seen — Babbel, Memrise, Hallow, language apps in general — split roughly on this axis:

- **Free** = "enough to fall in love with the pedagogy"
- **Pro** = "the whole library + the moat"

Here's a sketch for akhar — push back hard:

| Feature | Free | Pro |
|---|---|---|
| Foundations (paintee + mukta + muharni + matras + diacritics + sentences) | ✅ Full | — |
| Themes 1-3 (Hello/me, Family, Home) | ✅ Full | — |
| Themes 4-12 | Locked preview | ✅ Full |
| First 3 sakhis in library (the akhar Stories) | ✅ Full | — |
| All 405 classical sakhis | First 3 only | ✅ Full |
| Hover popovers (gloss + audio) | ✅ Full | — |
| Full dictionary entries (Punjabipedia, etymology depth) | Hover gloss only | ✅ Full |
| Save words to deck | Up to 30 | ✅ Unlimited |
| SRS review (the FSRS engine) | Daily limit (5 cards) | ✅ Full review session |
| Offline audio downloads | — | ✅ Full |

**Why this split:**
- Free is *genuinely useful* — someone can learn to read Punjabi and finish 3 sakhis without paying. That's the "fall in love" allotment.
- Pro is *the moat* — the full course, the classical library, the SRS engine running at full strength. The completionist + serious learner stuff.
- The "value moment" is sharp: you finish the Family theme + sakhi, hit the next-theme paywall, you can *see* the rest of the path. Conversion intent maxes out exactly there.

**Pricing I'd float** (no strong opinion until we test):
- £6.99/month
- £49.99/year (annual saves ~40%, hits the "this is good value" mental threshold)
- Maybe lifetime at £149 — heritage learners are emotionally committed buyers; some will pay once and never bother again. Also helps cash flow.
- 7-day free Pro trial on signup

## One real product gap I want to flag

When a beginner finishes the foundations curriculum, they currently have no obvious "next step" except *"go open a sakhi."* That's a big difficulty jump. Without vocab themes as a bridge, a learner will hit even the easy akhar Stories cold and feel overwhelmed.

Two ways to soften this without building the full theme path:

**(a) A guided first-sakhi flow.** The first time you finish foundations + open Birth of Guru Nanak, the reader walks you through the first paragraph with explicit "tap this word" prompts. A scripted onboarding moment, not a full theme system. 1-2 days of work.

**(b) Just accept the jump for MVP** — the akhar Stories are already much simpler than the classical sakhis, and the parallel English on every line is a real safety net. Watch what the analytics say and address if people bounce at that point.

I lean **(b)** — ship faster, learn from real signal. Add (a) if early data shows people dropping off at first sakhi.

## Approved Plan:
# MVP launch plan — ship today

## Context

We're shipping the **foundations Punjabi course + the 6 launch-ready sakhis** today. No paywall, no vocab themes, no path UI, no native apps — everything else explicitly deferred. The strategic call (made just now): launch a smaller honest thing, get real usage signal, then build the 12-theme spine and Stripe later.

What's already working: auth code (Apple/Google/OTP), onboarding, foundations curriculum (`/alphabet`), sakhi reader, library (6 processed), deck SRS, PostHog + Sentry wiring. What's between us and akhar.io being live: a few honesty fixes in copy, Vercel production env vars, manual verification of auth providers, DNS flip.

The user explicitly wants this **broken into bite-size steps executed one at a time** — not a monolithic "go." Phase A is fully my work; B is fully Sumeet's; C is collaborative; D is monitoring.

---

## Phase A — Code fixes I can do (~30 min, one block, single commit)

### A1. Fix the landing FAQ that overpromises a Pro tier
**File**: `app/page.tsx` line 459 (FAQ — "How much does it cost?")

Current copy promises a future Pro tier with "full spaced-repetition review, the full letters-and-reading curriculum, and downloadable audio" — but full SRS + the full curriculum are launching free. Only audio downloads is legitimately future.

Replace with something honest and forward-looking, e.g.:
> "Free while we're growing. We'll introduce paid features later — once we know which parts learners value most. If you want to help shape that, just sign up."

### A2. Hide the Apple Sign In button until Apple Dev enrollment is live
**Files**:
- `app/login/page.tsx` — the three-button chooser
- `app/login/ProviderButton.tsx` if separate Apple/Google logic exists there
- Don't delete the code — just conditionally render only Google + email-OTP. Re-enable when Apple Dev lands.

### A3. Drop the GCSE option from onboarding
**File**: `app/onboarding/page.tsx` lines 67–70 (per audit). GCSE is out of v1 scope per the [[feedback-landing-copy]] memory rule (no unbuilt-feature claims). The onboarding radio currently lets people self-identify as GCSE candidates which is incoherent with the landing.

Drop the GCSE option from the goal field. Keep heritage / sakhi / curious / similar.

### A4. Typecheck + local smoke
- `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass
- `npm run dev` + `curl http://localhost:3000/` returns 200
- Manually click through `/`, `/login`, `/library`, `/sakhi/1` in a browser to spot anything visually broken

### A5. Commit + push to `dev`
Single commit titled e.g. "Pre-launch polish — drop Pro-tier promise + hide Apple Sign In + drop GCSE option". Push triggers Vercel preview build.

---

## Phase B — Sumeet's verification + Vercel config (~30 min)

Wait for the Vercel preview from A5 to build, then run these against the preview URL.

### B1. Set production env vars in Vercel

Vercel project → **Settings → Environment Variables**. Add each to **Production + Preview + Development** unless noted.

| Var | Value source | Critical? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` | from `.env.local` | for analytics |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` | `https://eu.i.posthog.com` | for analytics |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` | from `.env.local` | for error tracking |
| `GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON` | contents of `~/.config/lipi/vision-key.json` | **audio will 404 without this** |
| `R2_ENDPOINT` | from `.env.local` | for audio cache reads |
| `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | from `.env.local` | for audio cache reads |
| `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | from `.env.local` | for audio cache reads |
| `R2_BUCKET` | from `.env.local` | for audio cache reads |
| `NANOGPT_API_KEY` | from `.env.local` | for /api/morpheme fallback (rare in prod since lipi.db caches everything) |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | from `.env.local` | for server-side auth |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | from `.env.local` | required everywhere |

For `GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON` specifically: paste the entire JSON file contents as a single value (Vercel accepts multi-line strings). The fallback `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (a file path) does NOT work on Vercel — no persistent filesystem.

After saving, Vercel needs a **Redeploy** to pick up new env vars. Push any commit or use the Redeploy button.

### B2. Verify Supabase OTP email template
Supabase dashboard → Auth → Email Templates → "Magic Link". Template body must contain `{{ .Token }}` (the 6-digit code), not `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`. Save. If template still has the link version, this is the fix that unblocks email sign-in.

### B3. Confirm Google OAuth provider is configured
Supabase dashboard → Auth → Providers → Google. Toggle ON. Client ID + Client Secret must be set (from Google Cloud Console OAuth credentials). Redirect URI registered in Google Console must include `https://fsahapmiupwfljajyngw.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`.

### B4. End-to-end smoke test on Vercel preview URL

Open the latest preview URL in a fresh browser session, then run through:

1. Visit `/` — landing loads, no console errors
2. Click "Sign up to start reading" → `/login` loads with **2 options visible** (Google + email-OTP). Apple button should be hidden after A2.
3. Sign in with email OTP → enter your email → receive a 6-digit code (not a link) → enter the code → land on `/onboarding`
4. Complete onboarding → land in `/library` or `/alphabet` based on prior_knowledge
5. Open a sakhi → **audio plays** when you tap the speaker icon (this is the GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON test)
6. Hover any word → popover shows romanisation + gloss instantly (no "Decomposing…" flash)
7. Save a word → it appears in `/deck`
8. Sign out → land back on `/`
9. Sign in with Google → end up signed in
10. Visit Sentry dashboard → 0 new errors from your session
11. Visit PostHog dashboard → see `page_viewed` events from your session

If any step fails, that's the launch blocker — fix before proceeding to Phase C.

---

## Phase C — Production deploy + DNS (~15 min, do together)

### C1. Merge dev → main
After Phase B passes:
```
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git merge dev
git push origin main
```
This triggers Vercel's production deploy.

### C2. Smoke test the Vercel production URL
Same 11-step smoke as B4, but against the production URL (`akhar-foo.vercel.app` style, before DNS).

### C3. Cloudflare DNS — point akhar.io at Vercel
Cloudflare dashboard → akhar.io zone → DNS records:
- Delete any existing A / CNAME on `@` and `www`
- Add CNAME `@` → `cname.vercel-dns.com` (proxied OFF — Vercel handles TLS)
- Add CNAME `www` → `cname.vercel-dns.com`
- In Vercel project → Settings → Domains → Add `akhar.io` and `www.akhar.io`

DNS propagation 1-5 minutes typically. Vercel auto-provisions Let's Encrypt cert.

### C4. Smoke test akhar.io
Once DNS resolves, open akhar.io in a fresh browser. Re-run the critical B4 steps (auth, audio, hover). If green: **we're live**.

---

## Phase D — Post-launch monitoring (rest of today, low touch)

### D1. Watch Sentry hourly for the first 6 hours
Use the existing token in `.env.local`. One-liner I can run on demand:
```
source .env.local && curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN" \
  "https://de.sentry.io/api/0/projects/reliq/akhar/issues/?statsPeriod=24h&query=is:unresolved" \

7	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";

9	
10	type Goal = "heritage" | "sakhi" | "gcse" | "curious";

12	
13	// Map (goal, prior_knowledge) → first page to land on.
14	//
15	// - readable + sakhi/heritage → straight into the library (they can
16	//   already read; show them the value)
17	// - none / spoken → /alphabet (they need the script foundation)
18	// - gcse → /alphabet for now (no GCSE content yet; will swap to
19	//   /learn/gcse when topic packs ship in MVP+1)
20	function firstLandingPage(goal: Goal, prior: PriorKnowledge): string {
21	  if (prior === "readable" && (goal === "sakhi" || goal === "heritage")) {
22	    return "/sakhi/1";
23	  }
24	  return "/alphabet";
25	}

27	export async function completeOnboarding(formData: FormData) {
28	  const goal = String(formData.get("goal") ?? "") as Goal;
29	  const prior = String(formData.get("prior_knowledge") ?? "") as PriorKnowledge;
30	
31	  // Validate against the CHECK constraints on the column.
32	  const validGoals: Goal[] = ["heritage", "sakhi", "gcse", "curious"];
33	  const validPrior: PriorKnowledge[] = ["none", "spoken", "readable"];
34	  if (!validGoals.includes(goal) || !validPrior.includes(prior)) {
35	    redirect("/onboarding?error=invalid");
36	  }
37	
38	  const supabase = await serverClient();
39	  const {
40	    data: { user },
41	  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
42	  if (!user) redirect("/login?next=/onboarding");
43	
44	  const { error } = await supabase
45	    .from("profiles")
46	    .update({

## Now: B2 — Verify Supabase OTP email template

This is the one Supabase config that can't be checked from here (the auth.config schema is fenced off). You need to do this manually:

1. Go to [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard) → **akhar project** → **Authentication** → **Email Templates** → click **"Magic Link"**
2. Look at the template body. The critical check: does it use `{{ .Token }}` or `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`?
   - **`{{ .Token }}`** → users receive a 6-digit code (what we want)
   - **`{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`** → users receive a clickable link (broken, since our `/login/verify` page expects a 6-digit code)
3. If it's the URL version, replace the whole body with something like:

```
<h2>Your code</h2>
<p>Hi,</p>
<p>Your sign-in code for akhar.io is:</p>
<p style="font-size: 32px; letter-spacing: 4px; font-weight: bold;">{{ .Token }}</p>
<p>This code expires in 60 minutes. If you didn't request it, just ignore this email.</p>
```

4. **Save** the template.

Tell me when that's done (or confirm it's already set correctly) and we'll move to **B3 (Google OAuth verification)** — which I'll then collapse into a single end-to-end smoke since Google verification is just "does sign-in work."

> AGENT

That warning matters — Supabase's built-in email service is rate-limited (~2-4 emails per hour on free tier, sometimes a bit more). If your launch brings any kind of signup burst — even 10 people in a WhatsApp group all trying to sign up at once — the later ones will hit the limit and get nothing. Bad day 1.

Two ways forward:

**(A) Set up Resend (or similar) as custom SMTP before launch — ~30 min**
- Sign up at https://resend.com (free tier: 100 emails/day, 3,000/month — way more than launch needs)
- Add `akhar.io` as a sending domain
- Add the SPF + DKIM TXT records they give you to **Cloudflare DNS** (which we're touching anyway for the Vercel domain flip in C3 — kill two birds)
- Grab the API key
- In Supabase → Auth → SMTP Settings → paste Resend SMTP credentials + set the "from" address
- Send yourself a test OTP to confirm
- Adds ~30 min before launch but unlocks real scale

**(B) Ship with the built-in SMTP, accept the risk**
- Fastest path to live (no extra work today)
- If signups arrive faster than ~3/hour, the later ones get nothing for ~20 min
- You'd be live but with auth flaking under the lightest burst
- Switch to Resend day 2 when you see actual volume

For a **launch day specifically** — where any flaked auth leaves a sour first impression — I'd genuinely recommend (A). 30 minutes is cheap insurance against "I tried to sign up but never got the code."

## Step 1 — Sign up at Resend + add akhar.io

1. Go to **https://resend.com/signup** — sign up with your work email (whatever you want associated). Free tier is fine.
2. Once you're in, in the left sidebar click **Domains** → **Add Domain**.
3. Enter **`akhar.io`** (just the root, no subdomain).
4. **Region**: pick **Frankfurt** (EU) since the rest of our stack is EU. Default may already be that.
5. Click **Add**.

You should land on a screen showing **3 DNS records** to add (an `MX` record, a `TXT` SPF record, and a `TXT` DKIM record — sometimes a 4th `TXT` for DMARC).

**Don't add them to Cloudflare yet — just keep that Resend screen open.** Once you're at the "verify DNS" screen, tell me you're there and I'll walk you through Step 2 (Cloudflare).

## Step 4 — Create a Resend API key

The API key is what Supabase will use to authenticate when sending the OTP emails. Don't reuse the test key Resend gives you on signup — create a fresh one scoped just for this.

1. In Resend, click **API Keys** in the left sidebar → **Create API Key**
2. Name it something memorable: **`akhar-supabase-smtp`**
3. **Permission**: pick **"Sending access"** (NOT full access — Supabase only needs to send, not read or manage)
4. **Domain**: restrict to **`akhar.io`** so this key can only send from that domain
5. Click **Add** — Resend shows you the key **once**. Copy it immediately (starts with `re_...`).

**Don't paste the key here** — it's a secret. Just confirm you've got it copied. Then I'll walk you through Step 5 (Supabase SMTP config), which is where you'll paste it.

Two things I need from you to wire it up:

1. **The GitHub username** that's connected to your Vercel (the one that owns `reliq-digital/akhar`). Probably something like `reliq-digital` or similar — what's the exact username?

2. **An email associated with that GitHub account**. Two options:

   **a) The "noreply" email GitHub gives every account** (Recommended — keeps your private email out of commits):
   - Log in as that GitHub user → go to **https://github.com/settings/emails**
   - At the bottom there's a checkbox **"Keep my email addresses private"** — when on, GitHub shows you a noreply email of the form:
     `12345678+username@users.noreply.github.com`
   - Copy that exact email and paste it here

   **b) Or just the primary email on that account** — whatever address is set as primary in GitHub → Settings → Emails. (Less private but works.)

Once you paste those two, I'll:
- `git config --local user.email` + `user.name` so this repo authors commits as that identity
- Rewrite the dev branch's 6 recent commits with the new author (via `git rebase --exec --reset-author`)
- Force-push dev — Vercel re-runs the deploy, sees commits authored by the right user, ships

The change only affects `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar`. Your other projects keep using your current global git config.

> AGENT

**Build is READY** ✅ and your observation is fair.

The good news: that key — `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` — is *designed* to be public. Supabase calls it the "publishable" key (formerly "anon" key). It's literally meant to be in the client bundle, visible to anyone who opens DevTools. Security is handled by Row Level Security policies on the database side, not by hiding this key. So no actual security leak. **But** — yes, it's terrible UX that an underlying fetch error bubbled the raw header string into the user-facing message. A proper sign-up flow should catch that and show "Something went wrong — try again." We should harden that error path post-launch, but it's not a blocker today.

3	// Auth server actions. Three flows, all passwordless:
4	//   - Sign in with Apple (OAuth)     — required on iOS App Store
5	//   - Sign in with Google (OAuth)    — most heritage users have a Google acct
6	//   - Email + 6-digit OTP code       — fallback, replaces magic link
7	//
8	// Email OTP replaces the previous magic-link approach because magic links
9	// have a known mobile UX failure mode: the user types email → switches to
10	// their email app → clicks link → it opens in a browser instead of the
11	// app. OTP codes are typed directly back into the app, no handoff.
12	//
13	// Requires the Supabase Magic Link email template to be configured with
14	// `{{ .Token }}` (which sends the 6-digit code) instead of
15	// `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` (which sends a link). See docs/mvp.md.
16	
17	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
18	import { headers } from "next/headers";
19	import { serverClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
20	
21	function originFromHeaders(h: Headers): string {
22	  const proto = h.get("x-forwarded-proto") ?? "https";
23	  const host = h.get("host") ?? "localhost:3000";
24	  return `${proto}://${host}`;
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Step 1 of email OTP: trigger Supabase to send a 6-digit code.
29	 * Redirects to /login/verify so the user can enter the code.
30	 */
31	export async function sendOtp(formData: FormData) {
32	  const email = String(formData.get("email") ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
33	  const next = String(formData.get("next") ?? "/");
34	  if (!email || !email.includes("@")) {
35	    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent("Enter a valid email")}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`);
36	  }
37	
38	  const supabase = await serverClient();
39	  // shouldCreateUser=true so first-time sign-in also signs up — same flow
40	  // for both, no separate "register" path.
41	  const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({
42	    email,
43	    options: { shouldCreateUser: true },
44	  });
45	  if (error) {
46	    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`);
47	  }
48	  redirect(
49	    `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,
50	  );
51	}
52	
53	/**
54	 * Step 2 of email OTP: verify the 6-digit code the user types.
55	 * On success, Supabase sets the session cookies and we redirect to `next`.
56	 */
57	export async function verifyOtp(formData: FormData) {
58	  const email = String(formData.get("email") ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
59	  const token = String(formData.get("token") ?? "").trim();
60	  const next = String(formData.get("next") ?? "/");
61	  if (!email || !token) {
62	    redirect(
63	      `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&error=${encodeURIComponent("Enter the 6-digit code")}`,
64	    );
65	  }
66	
67	  const supabase = await serverClient();
68	  const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
69	    email,
70	    token,
71	    type: "email",
72	  });
73	  if (error) {
74	    redirect(
75	      `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`,
76	    );
77	  }
78	  redirect(next);
79	}
80

93	  });

95	    `/login/verify?email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}&resent=1`,
96	  );
97	}
98	
99	/**
100	 * Initiate OAuth with a social provider (Apple or Google). Supabase
101	 * handles the redirect dance — we ask it for the provider's auth URL and
102	 * send the user there. The provider sends them to Supabase, which sends
103	 * them back to /auth/callback with a code, which we exchange for a session.
104	 */
105	export async function signInWithProvider(formData: FormData) {
106	  const provider = String(formData.get("provider") ?? "") as "google" | "apple";
107	  const next = String(formData.get("next") ?? "/");
108	  if (provider !== "google" && provider !== "apple") {
109	    redirect(`/login?error=${encodeURIComponent("Unknown sign-in provider")}`);
110	  }
111	
112	  const h = await headers();
113	  const origin = originFromHeaders(h);
114	  const supabase = await serverClient();
115	  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({
116	    provider,
117	    options: {
118	      redirectTo: `${origin}/auth/callback?next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,
119	    },
120	  });
121	  if (error || !data?.url) {
122	    redirect(
123	      `/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error?.message ?? "OAuth init failed")}&next=${encodeURIComponent(next)}`,
124	    );
125	  }
126	  redirect(data.url);
127	}
128	
129	export async function signOut() {
130	  const supabase = await serverClient();
131	  await supabase.auth.signOut();
132	  redirect("/");
133	}
134	
```

The error "Token has expired or is invalid" *almost always* means Supabase didn't recognise the code at verify time — which can be:
- Code mismatch (typo)
- Expired (Supabase's default OTP TTL is ~1 hour)
- Already-used (one attempt per code)
- **Magic-link clicked instead of code entered** — if the email contains both `{{ .Token }}` and `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`, clicking the link would go through a flow that ends up with "Token invalid"

That last one is my top suspicion. If you have access to the Supabase email template again, double-check the body — it should ONLY have `{{ .Token }}`, no link, no `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`.

=== next.config — does it tell Vercel to include data/ + lipi.db? ===
import type { NextConfig } from "next";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // `better-sqlite3` is a native module — Next.js's bundler can't rewrite it
  // and trying to inline it breaks the build. Mark it external so it's
  // require()-d at runtime from node_modules instead.
  serverExternalPackages: ["better-sqlite3"],

  // Bundle the SQLite data files into the serverless function output so the
  // deployed code can read them at runtime. Vercel's outputFileTracing walks
  // the import graph but won't follow runtime path strings like
  // `path.join(cwd, "data/sakhis.db")`, so we have to opt them in explicitly.
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    "/**/*": ["./data/sakhis.db", "./lipi.db"],
  },
};

export default nextConfig;

Once\n// we have proper Sentry server-side coverage we can drop this.\nimport { NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\n\ninterface Probe {\n  name: string;\n  ok: boolean;\n  detail?: string;\n}\n\nexport const dynamic = \"force-dynamic\";\nexport const runtime = \"nodejs\";\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const probes: Probe[] = [];\n\n  // 1. Is the cwd what we expect?\n  const cwd = process.cwd();\n  probes.push({ name: \"cwd\", ok: true, detail: cwd });\n\n  // 2. Can we require better-sqlite3?\n  try {\n    const Database = (await import(\"better-sqlite3\")).default;\n    probes.push({ name: \"import:better-sqlite3\", ok: true });\n\n    // 4. Same for lipi.db\n    try {\n      const db = new Database(path.join(cwd, \"lipi.db\"), { readonly: true });\n      const row = db.prepare(\"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM morpheme_cache\").get() as {\n        n: number;\n      };\n      db.close();\n      probes.push({\n        name: \"sqlite:lipi.db\",\n        ok: true,\n        detail: `${row.n} morpheme rows`,\n      });\n    } catch (e) {\n      probes.push({\n        name: \"sqlite:lipi.db\",\n        ok: false,\n        detail: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e),\n      });\n    }\n  } catch (e) {\n    probes.push({\n      name: \"import:better-sqlite3\",\n      ok: false,\n      detail: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e),\n    });\n  }\n\n  // 6. Env var presence (don't echo values)\n  const envChecks = [\n    \"NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL\",\n    \"NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY\",\n    \"SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY\",\n    \"GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON\",\n    \"R2_ENDPOINT\",\n    \"R2_BUCKET\",\n    \"NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY\",\n    \"NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN\",\n  ];\n  for (const k of envChecks) {\n    probes.push({ name: `env:${k}`, ok: !!process.env[k] });\n  }\n\n  const allOk = probes.every((p) => p.ok);\n  return NextResponse.json({ ok: allOk, probes }, { status: allOk ? 200 : 500 });\n}\n"

> AGENT

Got it. `lipi.db` fails with **"unable to open database file"** because `lib/morpheme-cache.ts` opens it in default *read-write* mode (sets WAL journal mode etc.) — but Vercel's filesystem is read-only at runtime. `sakhis.db` works because `lib/sakhi-db.ts` opens it with `{ readonly: true }`.

Fixing:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01KDJSbDSfYt8xkLwpdB8pV4
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/morpheme-cache.ts",
  "old_string": "function db(): Database.Database {\n  if (_db) return _db;\n  _db = new Database(path.join(process.cwd(), \"lipi.db\"));\n  _db.pragma(\"journal_mode = WAL\");\n  _db.exec(`\n    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS morpheme_cache (\n      script TEXT NOT NULL,\n      surface TEXT NOT NULL,\n      morpheme_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n      processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n      updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n      PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)\n    );\n  `);\n  // Schema migration for legacy DBs that pre-date the processed column\n  const cols = _db\n    .prepare(`PRAGMA table_info(morpheme_cache)`)\n    .all() as { name: string }[];\n  if (!cols.some((c) => c.name === \"processed\")) {\n    _db.exec(\n      `ALTER TABLE morpheme_cache ADD COLUMN processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,\n    );\n  }\n  return _db;\n}",
  "new_string": "// On Vercel the filesystem is read-only, so we can't WAL-init or migrate\n// schema at runtime. We do those steps only in development (where writes\n// are how the cache gets authored). In production we just open the DB\n// read-only and trust the committed-to-git lipi.db is complete.\nconst IS_DEV = process.env.NODE_ENV !== \"production\";\n\nfunction db(): Database.Database {\n  if (_db) return _db;\n  const dbPath = path.join(process.cwd(), \"lipi.db\");\n  if (IS_DEV) {\n    _db = new Database(dbPath);\n    _db.pragma(\"journal_mode = WAL\");\n    _db.exec(`\n      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS morpheme_cache (\n        script TEXT NOT NULL,\n        surface TEXT NOT NULL,\n        morpheme_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n        processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n        updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n        PRIMARY KEY (script, surface)\n      );\n    `);\n    // Schema migration for legacy DBs that pre-date the processed column\n    const cols = _db\n      .prepare(`PRAGMA table_info(morpheme_cache)`)\n      .all() as { name: string }[];\n    if (!cols.some((c) => c.name === \"processed\")) {\n      _db.exec(\n        `ALTER TABLE morpheme_cache ADD COLUMN processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,\n      );\n    }\n  } else {\n    // Production: read-only open. No WAL setup, no schema migration —\n    // both would fail on Vercel's read-only filesystem with an opaque\n    // \"unable to open database file\" because SQLite tries to create\n    // the -shm/-wal sidecar files.\n    _db = new Database(dbPath, { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true });\n  }\n  return _db;\n}"
}

> AGENT

The DB file itself still has WAL mode persisted in its header. Even with `readonly: true`, SQLite tries to access the (missing) `-wal` sidecar. Fix: change lipi.db's persistent journal mode from WAL to DELETE so it's openable without sidecars:

> TOOL

```json

  "description": "Convert lipi.db from WAL to DELETE journal mode"
}

1	// OAuth callback landing page. Supabase redirects users here after they
2	// complete the Apple / Google sign-in flow. We exchange the `code` query
3	// param for a real session (sets the auth cookies) and then send them to
4	// wherever they were trying to go (?next=).
5	//
6	// Email OTP doesn't hit this route — that flow is fully server-side via
7	// verifyOtp() in app/login/actions.ts; the session cookies are set as
8	// part of that Server Action's response. This route exists only for OAuth.
9	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
10	import { serverClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
11	
12	export async function GET(request: Request) {
13	  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);
14	  const code = searchParams.get("code");
15	  const next = searchParams.get("next") ?? "/";
16	
17	  if (!code) {
18	    return NextResponse.redirect(
19	      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent("Missing code in callback URL")}`,
20	    );
21	  }
22	
23	  const supabase = await serverClient();
24	  const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);
25	  if (error) {
26	    return NextResponse.redirect(
27	      `${origin}/login?error=${encodeURIComponent(error.message)}`,
28	    );
29	  }
30	  return NextResponse.redirect(`${origin}${next}`);
31	}
32	
```

> AGENT

Two layered things:

1. **The actual error** `flow_state_already_used` happens before any final redirect. It means Supabase is rejecting the OAuth state from a *previous* attempt that's still in your browser cookies (the abandoned localhost flow earlier).

2. **The akhar.io redirect on error** happens because Supabase's behavior is: redirect to `Site URL` (not the requested `redirectTo`) when OAuth errors out. So even though we set Site URL to `akhar.io` correctly for production, it bites us during testing while DNS isn't pointed yet.

Two fixes:

### Immediate — clear stale OAuth cookies + retry

Open https://akhar-git-dev-reliq-digitals-projects.vercel.app in **a fresh incognito window**. Old localhost test left state in cookies which is what's tripping it. Incognito = no cookies = clean slate.

### Defensive — temporarily change Site URL to the preview so error redirects still resolve while DNS isn't flipped

Everything\n// here is read-only for v1; editing onboarding answers, deleting account,\n// stats etc. all come post-launch when we've seen real usage.\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { signOut } from \"@/app/login/actions\";\n\nconst SUPPORT_EMAIL = \"support@akhar.io\";\n\n// Mapping from stored values back to the labels we showed in onboarding.\n// Keep these in sync with app/onboarding/page.tsx whenever those copy\n// strings change.\nconst GOAL_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {\n  heritage: \"I grew up around the language\",\n  sakhi: \"To read classical sakhis + Punjabi literature\",\n  gcse: \"GCSE / A-Level Panjabi exam (legacy)\",\n  curious: \"Just curious\",\n};\n\nconst PRIOR_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {\n  none: \"Starting from scratch\",\n  spoken: \"I can speak some but can't read\",\n  readable: \"I can read some Punjabi already\",\n};\n\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: \"Profile — akhar.io\",\n};\n\nexport default async function ProfilePage() {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) redirect(\"/login?next=/profile\");\n\n  // Sign-in method comes from the user's identities array — populated by\n  // Supabase based on which provider(s) they used (google / email / etc.)\n  const providers = (user.identities ?? [])\n    .map((i) => i.provider)\n    .filter((p): p is string => Boolean(p));\n  const primaryProvider = providers[0] ?? \"email\";\n\n  // Onboarding answers live in the profiles table. Default to null if the\n  // user hasn't completed onboarding (shouldn't happen since proxy.ts\n  // gates that, but be defensive).\n  const { data: profile } = await supabase\n    .from(\"profiles\")\n    .select(\"goal, prior_knowledge\")\n    .eq(\"user_id\", user.id)\n    .maybeSingle();\n\n  const goalLabel = profile?.goal ? GOAL_LABELS[profile.goal] ?? profile.goal : null;\n  const priorLabel = profile?.prior_knowledge\n    ? PRIOR_LABELS[profile.prior_knowledge] ?? profile.prior_knowledge\n    : null;\n\n  // Pretty-name the provider for display.\n  const providerLabel =\n    primaryProvider === \"google\"\n      ? \"Google\"\n      : primaryProvider === \"apple\"\n        ? \"Apple\"\n        : primaryProvider === \"email\"\n          ? \"Email + 6-digit code\"\n          : primaryProvider;\n\n  return (\n    <main className=\"mx-auto max-w-2xl px-4 py-10 sm:px-6 sm:py-12\">\n      <header className=\"mb-8 border-b border-zinc-200 pb-6 dark:border-zinc-800\">\n        <h1 className=\"text-2xl font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          Your account\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-1 text-sm text-zinc-500\">\n          What we know about you, and how to reach us.\n        </p>\n      </header>\n\n      <section className=\"space-y-6\">\n        <Field label=\"Email\" value={user.email ?? \"(no email)\"} />\n        <Field label=\"Signing in with\" value={providerLabel} />\n        {goalLabel && <Field label=\"Your goal\" value={goalLabel} />}\n        {priorLabel && <Field label=\"Starting level\" value={priorLabel} />}\n      </section>\n\n      <section className=\"mt-10 border-t border-zinc-200 pt-6 dark:border-zinc-800\">\n        <h2 className=\"text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n          Need help?\n        </h2>\n        <p className=\"mt-2 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n          Email{\" \"}\n          <a\n            href={`mailto:${SUPPORT_EMAIL}?subject=${encodeURIComponent(\"akhar.io support\")}`}\n            className=\"text-zinc-900 underline hover:text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-50 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n          >\n            {SUPPORT_EMAIL}\n          </a>\n          {\" \"}— anything from a typo in a sakhi to a deeper question about\n          how the app works. We&apos;ll reply.\n        </p>\n      </section>\n\n      <section className=\"mt-10 border-t border-zinc-200 pt-6 dark:border-zinc-800\">\n        <form action={signOut}>\n          <button\n            type=\"submit\"\n            className=\"rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:border-zinc-600 dark:hover:bg-zinc-900\"\n          >\n            Sign out\n          </button>\n        </form>\n        <p className=\"mt-3 text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n          You can sign back in any time with the same{\" \"}\n          {primaryProvider === \"google\" ? \"Google account\" : \"email\"}.\n        </p>\n      </section>\n\n      <footer className=\"mt-12 text-center text-xs text-zinc-400\">\n        <Link href=\"/library\" className=\"underline hover:text-zinc-600\">\n          ← Back to the library\n        </Link>\n      </footer>\n    </main>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction Field({ label, value }: { label: string; value: string }) {\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div className=\"text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-zinc-500\">{label}</div>\n      <div className=\"mt-1 text-base text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">{value}</div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Honestly? You're right and this is the actual hole in the product. Right now `/alphabet` is a long index where you can click anything → there's no sense that you've *learned* anything. No "you mastered this, now try that." It's a hosted textbook, not a learning app.

What real mastery-based progression looks like:

**Per letter / unit**
- See letter → pick sound (or audio → pick letter): 4/5 correct in a row before "✓ learned"
- Locked next-letter tile until current one's ticked
- Letters come back periodically as spaced-review, so you don't forget by Lesson 30

**Per line of letters** (the 5-at-a-time grouping the traditional curriculum already uses)
- After each individual letter, a mini-quiz on the *whole line* (10 items mixing recognition + audio + match-meanings)
- ~80% to pass → unlocks the next line

**Per matra → mukta-words → reading-sentences**
- Each stage has its own "you can do this" check
- Reading sentences: tap the meaning of the sentence, drag English fragments into order, etc.

**Per sakhi**
- After reading: 2-3 comprehension questions ("Who is Mehta Kalu?", "What did Nanak give the sadhus?")
- "Read the next sakhi" only unlocks after passing

The principle: **progress should feel earned**. Right now nothing about /alphabet is gated, so finishing means scrolling, not learning. With mastery checks, getting to the next letter *means something*.

What I'd steal from Duolingo: visible "next" with lock icon, clear "you need X to unlock Y" messaging, the small dopamine hit of ✓ when you complete an exercise.
What I'd skip (same as before): XP, streaks, hearts, owl, leagues. Adult heritage learners hate that energy.

## Two honest considerations

**1. This is genuinely 2-3 weeks of work to do well.** Per-user progress tracking (new DB schema), lesson-completion criteria per lesson type, lock-state UI everywhere, the actual quiz components (letter-recognition / matching / drag-to-order), and the data-layer to record results. Not a weekend job if we want it to feel solid.

**2. It folds naturally into the curriculum path we already designed.** The 12-theme spine I researched + the vertical-Duolingo-style path UI we agreed on — both *require* mastery-based unlocks to be coherent. Without lock states, the path is just a list. So whatever mastery framework we build now, it's the same framework that powers the v2 themed curriculum later.

## The shipping question I want to put on the table

You've been pushing to ship today, but you also keep finding gaps that are *real*. Honest options:

- **Ship today as-is, mark mastery as v1.1** (~2-3 weeks). MVP becomes "see what we have, sign up early." Real users tell us which mastery checks matter most.
- **Delay launch by ~10 days to build the letter-line mastery flow first.** The minimum that closes today's gap is: per-letter recognition quiz → line-quiz → unlock next line. Skip matras/mukta/sakhi mastery for v1, do them in v1.1. Less ambitious than full mastery but enough that the app feels like an app.
- **Ship today + commit publicly to v1.1 in 2 weeks** with the mastery flow. Lets early users see the foundation now and shape what comes.

What's your gut?

## The split

**Reference** (always-accessible, no gating, no progress):
- Full alphabet chart — all 35 at a glance
- Muharni table — consonant × matra grid
- Sakhi library — what `/library` is today, just text + audio
- Dictionary lookups (already there via hover popovers)

**Course** (sequential, gated, progress-tracked):
- A path of lessons, each one teaching one concept (a letter, a matra, a sound rule, then later a sentence pattern, then a whole sakhi)
- Each lesson = ~5-8 exercises mixing 3-4 types (see below)
- Locked tiles ahead; clear "do this lesson to unlock the next"

Nav: `Home / Path / Reference / Deck / Profile`. The Path is the *action*; Reference is what you check when stuck.

## The path itself — first-pass layout

Each block is **one lesson** unless noted. Lessons inside a section are sequential; sections themselves are sequential.

**§1 Letters: line 1 (ੳ ਅ ੲ ਸ ਹ)**
- L1: ੳ
- L2: ਅ
- L3: ੲ
- L4: ਸ
- L5: ਹ
- L6: **Line 1 check** (mixes all 5 — ~12 exercises, 80% to pass)

**§2 Letters: line 2 (ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ ਙ)** — same shape, line check at end, but mixes in some §1 letters as reinforcement.

**§3-§7** same pattern through all 7 lines.

**§8 Nukta letters** (ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼) — one lesson each + line check.

**§9 Matras: short vowels** (sihari / aunkar) + check.

**§10 Matras: long vowels** (kanna / bihari / dulainkar / lavan / dulavan / hora / kanaura) + check.

**§11 Diacritics** (tippi, bindi, addhak) + check.

**§12 Mukta words** — read 3-letter words. Lessons teach 5 words at a time. Section check at the end.

**§13 Simple sentences** — sentence-level reading with comprehension multiple-choice.

**§14 Sakhi 1: Birth of Guru Nanak** — actual sakhi as a path unit. After reading: 3 comprehension Qs. Pass → §15 unlocks.

**§15 Sacha Sauda** → comprehension → unlocks the next.

**§16-onwards**: each processed sakhi is a path unit.

After §16+, the *path* runs out at our current content limit — natural stopping point that signals "you're caught up, more coming."

## Exercise types per lesson

Five types, mixed within a lesson so it doesn't get stale:

1. **Audio → tap the letter** (multiple choice, 4 options)
2. **Letter → tap the matching sound** (4 audio buttons)
3. **Type the romanization** ("type how you'd write ਕ in English letters" → "ka")
4. **Match pairs** — 4 letters left, 4 sounds right, drag to pair
5. **Tap in order** — 5 letters shown, audio plays a sequence, tap them in order

In a "Letter ਕ" lesson, maybe: 2 of (1), 2 of (2), 1 of (3), 1 of (4) — 6 exercises total. **Mastery = all 6 right.** Get one wrong, it reappears later in the same lesson. Get the SAME one wrong twice → redo the whole lesson.

For section checks: 10-15 exercises, 80% to pass.

## Placement test — yes, this is the right call

Onboarding's self-report is unreliable (people overestimate, underestimate, or aren't sure). A real test removes the lie. Proposed structure:

**7 questions, ~4 minutes, static (not adaptive — adaptive is v2)**

1. *Letter 1*: audio of "ka" → tap the right letter (4 options including ਕ ਖ ਗ ਟ)
2. *Letter 2*: see ਮ → tap the right sound (audio buttons)
3. *Letter 3*: audio of "tha" → tap the letter (harder — confusing similar letters)
4. *Matra 1*: see ਕਾ → tap "kaa" (vs "ki", "ku", "ke")
5. *Matra 2*: type the romanization of ਪਿਆਰ
6. *Mukta read*: see ਘਰ → tap "house" (vs "tree", "dog", "river")
7. *Sentence*: read ਉਹ ਘਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ — tap the meaning ("He goes home" vs distractors)

**Placement based on score:**

| Right | Starting position |
|---|---|
| 0-2 | §1 Lesson 1 (full course from scratch) |
| 3 | §3 (line 3 of letters) |
| 4 | §8 (nukta letters) |
| 5 | §9 (matras) |
| 6 | §12 (mukta words) |
| 7 | §13 (sentences) — or skip to §14 Sakhi 1 if they got Q7 right |

**Critical rule**: placement sets your *current* position. **Everything *before* is "available" (you can revisit for review, gets a green ✓-but-unstarted icon); everything *after* stays locked.** No skipping forward.

## The "do it more than once" question

Duolingo's mastery model is: each lesson has multiple levels (Bronze → Silver → Gold → etc.). You unlock the next lesson after *Bronze* (first pass), but you can come back to push to Gold.

I'd skip that complexity for v1. Simpler: each lesson is "done" when first-passed. Spaced review brings letters back in *later* lessons' exercises automatically (e.g., the §3 line check includes some §1 + §2 letters). The need to remember stuff comes from those reappearances, not from grinding the same lesson 3 times.

We can add a deeper "Push to mastery" mode in v2.

## Scope honest reality

This is **~3-4 weeks** of focused work to do well. Breakdown:

- **Week 1**: Schema (user_progress, exercise_results), Path UI shell, lesson runner shell, two exercise types
- **Week 2**: Remaining exercise types, all letter content converted to path lessons, line checks
- **Week 3**: Matras + mukta + sentences sections, placement test, onboarding rewire
- **Week 4**: Sakhi-as-unit (comprehension questions on each), Reference section UI split out from current /alphabet + /library

You said earlier you wanted to ship today. Now you're describing 3-4 weeks of work. Honest question:

- **(B)** Delay launch by ~3-4 weeks, ship with the path mastery flow live. First impression is "this is the real thing" — much stronger but takes the runway.
- **(C)** Hybrid: ship today, but block the homepage signup behind a "joining the beta — get early access" form. We collect emails now, ship to those users when path is ready. Lets you keep momentum without launching a half-thing.

What's your gut? I'd lean **(C)** — keeps you shipping today (you've earned that with how much you've done), but doesn't burn the first-impression on a half-built thing.
