## 1. PME Book 1 order — the actual sequence

PME Book 1 (and the traditional Punjab-school approach) goes roughly:

> **Letters → Mukta words → Matras → Diacritics → Muharni → Reading**

Your instinct's exactly right — mukta words come straight after letters because *you can already read them with just letter knowledge* (no matras needed). It's the first real "I read a Punjabi word!" win, and it consolidates letter recognition before adding matra complexity. So the path becomes:

**§1-§7**: The 35 letters, line by line (5 per line, with a Line Check after each)
**§8**: Nukta letters (the 5 borrowed sounds — ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼). Could also do this after Mukta-words; I'd put it here so all letters are taught before they appear in words.
**§9**: **Mukta words** — read actual Punjabi words with just letters you know. ਘਰ ਕਮਲ ਜਨਮ ਫਲ etc. Each lesson teaches 5-8 words; section ends with reading-comprehension check.
**§10**: Matras — short vowels first (sihari ਿ, aunkar ੁ). Each one becomes one lesson. Lessons end with reading words using that matra (ਕਿਰਨ, ਪੁਲ, etc.)
**§11**: Matras — long vowels (kanna ਾ, bihari ੀ, dulainkar ੂ, lavan ੇ, dulavan ੈ, hora ੋ, kanaura ੌ). Same shape.
**§12**: Diacritics (tippi ੰ, bindi ਂ, addhak ੱ) — one lesson each + check.
**§13**: **Muharni** — the systematic drill. Each consonant ×each matra in a grid. This is where it all consolidates. Probably 3-4 lessons covering rows of consonants.
**§14**: Multi-letter / mixed-matra words — start reading longer words combining everything.
**§15**: Simple sentences — sentence-level reading with comprehension.
**§16+**: Sakhis as path units (Birth of Guru Nanak first — already the simplest one).

So **15 sections before sakhis**, ~50-60 lessons total. Matches PME's gradual pace.

One **deviation from PME** worth flagging: PME does muharni as a *systematic chant table* (like multiplication tables — ਕ ਕਾ ਕਿ ਕੀ ...). Pedagogically powerful but also dull for adult diaspora learners. I'd keep the muharni section but make the lessons interactive (audio-pair, type-romanization on each grid square) rather than recite-the-table. ## 2. Finger-tracing — yes, technically possible. Here's the honest picture.

**Can we do it?** Yes, fully. HTML5 Canvas + pointer events captures finger strokes on touch screens (and mouse on desktop, useful for tablet/laptop users with a Wacom etc.). Three implementation tiers, increasing in quality:

1. **Pixel-coverage check** (simplest, ~1 day to build): show a faint letter outline; user traces; we check what % of the letter's pixels are covered by their drawing. Not perfect — they could scribble everywhere — but works as a "you traced it" check.
2. **Stroke-order check** (~3-4 days): we hand-define the canonical stroke order for each letter (start point → end point + direction). User's strokes must match. This is what most Asian-script writing apps actually do, including the good Mandarin/Japanese ones.
3. **ML handwriting recognition** (~weeks + infrastructure): train a model on user inputs vs canonical letters. Way more work than it's worth for v1.

**My recommendation**: tier 2 (stroke-order check) is the right target. The hand-define-the-strokes step is maybe an hour per letter set; doable in a weekend.

**Timing**: I'd put writing in **v1.2** (post-path-mastery launch), not v1.1. Reasoning:
- The reading path alone is 3-4 weeks of work. Adding writing on top stretches that.
- A *lot* of heritage learners want to read but don't care about writing — adding it changes the path scope without serving everyone.
- For those who do want it: a clean "Writing" toggle on each letter lesson — "I've traced this letter 3 times correctly" — is a clean separate concern.

**Free vs Pro?** I'd put **writing on the free tier**, not Pro. Reasoning:
- It's a real pedagogical differentiator — *most* apps don't teach writing. Making it free is a strong free-tier wedge.
- Pro should be: more content (themes 4-12), advanced SRS, offline audio, classical sakhi corpus full access. Things that scale value with engagement, not features that exist or don't.
- Writing exists or it doesn't — same code runs whether user pays or not. Locking it feels stingy.

What I'd put behind paywall later: SRS deck full review (free gets daily limit), full sakhi library (free gets first 6), themed vocab modules. The actual *learning capability* stays free.

# PME Book 1 — Structure (Nagra, 48 pp.)

**Verified PDF / full-text source**: [archive.org/details/PunjabiMadeEasyBook1](https://archive.org/details/PunjabiMadeEasyBook1) — full djvu text at [archive.org/stream/PunjabiMadeEasyBook1/Punjabi-Made-Easy-Book1_djvu.txt](https://archive.org/stream/PunjabiMadeEasyBook1/Punjabi-Made-Easy-Book1_djvu.txt). Page-image scan also at [apnaorg.com](https://apnaorg.com/books/gurmukhi/panjabi-made-easy-book-1/book.php?fldr=book).

## Section-by-section sequence

| Pages | Section | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1–10 | Front matter + "Important Note on Pronunciation" | Vowel system overview; retroflex vs. alveolar contrast diagrams (ṭ/th/ḍ/dh/ṇ vs. t/th/d/dh/n) — Nagra's signature lip/tongue position cues for L1-English readers |
| 11–17 | Consonant pronunciation diagrams | Individual letters with example words, Roman script, English gloss in 3 columns |
| 18–20 | **Painti chart** — all 35 letters on one page | Then walked through row by row: stops (k kh g gh ṅ) → affricates (ch chh j jh ñ) → retroflex (ṭ ṭh ḍ ḍh ṇ) → dentals (t th d dh n) → labials (p ph b bh m) → approximants (y r l v) → sibilant+h (s h). User's "line by line" recollection confirmed. |
| 21 | **5 nukta letters** (ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼) | Introduced together as "five extra farṛas" produced by adding a dot. Sits **immediately after the Painti**, before any matra work. |
| 22–23 | **Mukta** (no sign) + mukta words | Word list w/ Roman + English |
| 24–25 | **Kanna** (ā) | First matra taught — confirms user's recollection |
| 26–27 | **Sihari** (i) | |
| 28–29 | **Bihari** (ī) | |
| 30 | **Aunkar** (u) | |
| 31–32 | **Dulainkar** (ū) — "Duleka" in Nagra's spelling | |
| 33 | **Lavan** (e) — "Lava" | |
| 34 | **Dulavan** (ai) — "Dulava" | |
| 35–36 | **Hora** (o) | |
| 37 | **Kanaura** (au) — "Kanora" | Closes the 9-matra sequence |
| 38–39 | **Addhak** | First diacritic; gemination |
| 40–41 | **Tippi** | Nasalisation |
| 42 | **Bindi** | Alternate nasalisation |
| 43 | **Pairin Rara** (subscript ਰ) | Conjuncts begin |
| 44 | **Pairin Haha** (subscript ਹ) + word-final ਹ for tone | Tone is introduced *only* via the haha sub/final position — no explicit tone lesson |
| 45–48 | **Vocabulary appendix** — alphabetised glossary w/ page refs | Three-column: Gurmukhi / Roman / English |

## Important confirmations and corrections

- **Matra order confirmed**: Mukta → Kanna → Sihari → Bihari → Aunkar → Dulainkar → Lavan → Dulavan → Hora → Kanaura. Matches your recollection exactly (and differs from PSEB Class 1, which front-loads Kanna+Sihari+Bihari after only a handful of letters and intersperses matras with letter blocks).
- **No muharni grid**. Nagra does *not* drill the consonant×matra grid. Each matra page just gives example words for a handful of consonants taking that matra. If your curriculum wants muharni, that's a PSEB/traditional-pathshala move, not PME.
- **No sentences, no dialogues, no greetings, no numbers, no days of week**. Book 1 stops at single-word level. Sentences/dialogues start in **Book 2** (this is consistent across reviews and the workbook's scope). User's mental model that PME does reading practice in Book 1 is wrong — it's strictly letters → matras → diacritics → word list.
- **No quizzes/exercises inside the textbook**. Practice exists only in the **separate Workbook Bk. 1** (ISBN 1870383907) — tracing, fill-in, matching drills. The textbook itself is pure exposition.
- **Vocabulary skew**: family terms (mama, nana, dada), common nouns, names (Sham). Heavily concrete-noun, picture-anchored, no verbs-in-context.

## PME vs. PSEB Class 1 deltas (matters for your sequencing)

- PSEB introduces matras **interleaved** with consonant blocks (kids see ਕਾ, ਕਿ, ਕੀ within a few pages of learning ਕ). PME teaches **all 35 letters first**, then all matras. PME is a strict "shapes first, sounds-with-shapes later" sequence — more adult-L2 friendly, less child-immersion friendly.
- PSEB does sentences and short rhymes (ਕਾਵਾਂ, ਘੁੱਗੀਆਂ) by mid-book. PME Book 1 has zero connected text.
- PSEB doesn't treat the 5 nukta letters as a discrete block — they appear when needed. PME's "all 5 nukta together right after Painti" is a Nagra invention for the diaspora learner who's already seen them in Punjabi-English bilingual contexts (ਸ਼ਾਮ etc.).
- Both put addhak/tippi/bindi after matras, but PSEB sprinkles them earlier in compound words; PME isolates them as discrete lessons.

## Implication for your curriculum

PME Book 1 = **48 pages, ~10 hours of self-study, decode-only**. If you're modelling foundation on it, your equivalent stage ends at "learner can decode any single Gurmukhi word with matra + diacritic" — not "learner can read a sentence." Sentences/sakhi reading is a Book 2+ concern in PME's model. The muharni drill, if you want it, is your addition (or a PSEB import), not a PME inheritance.

## Two things PME Book 1 does NOT have (and I'd been assuming it did)

1. **No muharni drill.** The systematic consonant×matra grid is a PSEB / traditional-pathshala thing, *not* a Nagra tradition. PME just shows example words per matra for a handful of consonants.

2. **No sentences, no dialogues, no connected text.** Book 1 stops at *single-word level*. Sentences start in Book 2.

3. (Also: no in-text quizzes — those are in a separate workbook. So mastery checks are our addition, which is fine.)

## Decisions this forces

**(a) Muharni — include or skip?**
PME doesn't do it. But for diaspora adult learners who can't pattern-match like a kid immersed in the language, a systematic drill (read every consonant + matra combination) genuinely accelerates fluency. I'd argue *include it as our addition* — clearly framed as "after PME, our own consolidation drill" — but I want your gut here, since you said follow PME exactly.

**(b) The sentence-reading gap.**
PME Book 1 ends at conjuncts. Our next unit is sakhis, which are sentences. There's a real difficulty jump there. Two options:

- **Follow PME strictly** — finish conjuncts → jump straight into Sakhi 1 (Modern). The reader's hover popovers + parallel English do the scaffolding work that sentence-reading lessons would otherwise do.
- **Extend with our own sentence-reading section** between §12 and Sakhi 1 — covers basic sentence structure, common particles (ਹੈ, ਨੇ, ਨੂੰ, ਦਾ, ਦੀ, ਦੇ), simple SOV sentences, before jumping to sakhi prose.

I lean *extend with our own* — the sakhi prose is a sharp jump from "word level," and even with hover help, the leap risks bouncing learners. The PME-strict approach gambles that the sakhi reader's scaffolding is enough.

**(c) Pairin Rara + Pairin Haha — yes or merge?**
These appear in PME as discrete lessons (subscript ਰ for words like ਪ੍ਰੇਮ, subscript ਹ for tone). They're real and worth their own lessons in our path. But pedagogically dense — beginners hit conjuncts and tone at the same time. Could split, or could compress to one lesson.

**(d) Strict order: matras *all* come after the Painti + nukta + mukta, not interleaved.**
PSEB sprinkles matras in early (kids see ਕਾ within pages of ਕ). PME front-loads all letter shapes first. Your "follow PME" call means we're firmly in the PME camp: full Painti + nukta + mukta first, then all matras. That's a more adult-L2-friendly sequence anyway.

## What I'd propose as our v1.1 path

If you say yes to (a) and (b):

```
§1-§7 — 35 letters (Painti, by phonetic line)
§8     — 5 nukta letters
§9     — mukta words (real word reading begins)
§10    — 9 matras in PME order
§11    — addhak, tippi, bindi
§12    — pairin rara, pairin haha (tone introduction)
§13    — muharni consolidation (our addition — drill)
§14    — sentence reading (our addition — bridge to sakhi)
§15+   — sakhi 1 (Modern) as first sakhi unit, etc.
```

~60 lessons total before sakhis. Roughly mirrors PME's 48 pages plus our two bridge sections.

Your call on (a) muharni, (b) sentence-reading bridge, and (c) split or merge the two pairin lessons. Once those three are decided we have the actual curriculum spec for v1.1.

## Honest scope reality

The v1.1 plan I just wrote is **~3-4 weeks of focused work**. That's not me being slow — that's the minimum to do it well:

- Week 1: schema + path UI + lesson runner + 2 exercise types
- Week 2: remaining exercise types + 35 letter lessons + line checks
- Week 3: nukta + mukta + matras + diacritics + conjuncts + placement test
- Week 4: muharni + sentence reading + sakhi units + reference split + polish

**"Fast" can compress some of this, but it can't disappear.** If we ship a half-built path, that's worse than shipping no path — broken progression destroys trust harder than missing progression.

## Three honest options

**(A) Minimum-viable path — 5-7 days hard**
- Just §1-§7 letter lessons + line checks
- 2 exercise types (audio→letter, letter→audio)
- Basic mastery (4/5 correct, unlock next)
- No placement test (everyone starts at §1.1)
- No reference section split — current /alphabet stays as reference
- Skip §8-§14 (matras, diacritics, conjuncts, muharni, sentences) entirely
- Sakhis stay as library only, not path units
- **Launch positioning**: "akhar — start with the 35 letters of the Punjabi alphabet" — narrower than the current landing promises. We'd need to soften landing copy too.

**(B) Real foundation path — 14-18 days hard**
- §1-§12 (everything up to conjuncts) but skip §13 muharni + §14 sentences
- All 4-5 exercise types
- Placement test (7 questions, static)
- Reference section split out cleanly
- Sakhis stay in library as their own thing — not path units yet
- **Launch positioning**: "akhar — learn to read Punjabi from scratch with a proper path." Honest, complete, ships with sakhis as the discoverable next-step.

**(C) Full v1.1 as planned — 3-4 weeks**
- Everything in the spec
- Sakhis as path units with comprehension
- Reference section properly built
- **Launch positioning**: the original vision. The thing we actually want.

## What I'd push back on if I were you

You've done huge work today — auth, profile, home, SMTP, the SQLite fix. **None of it gets thrown away by delaying.** It all stays on dev waiting. Delaying isn't "losing today" — it's "saving today for the right launch."

I'd also flag: every time we've added scope today ("we need profile" → "we need home" → "we need path"), we've been right that the thing matters. But that pattern means **we're not actually trying to ship today** anymore. We're discovering what real-shippable looks like, which is something else.

## My recommendation

**Option B (real foundation path, 14-18 days).** It's the smallest version of the product that doesn't feel like a half-promise. Option A would mean we'd have to walk back landing copy and that hurts. Option C is the dream but you're already stretched.

If we go (B), I'd suggest:
- Today: stop trying to launch. Commit current dev work as "v1 foundation" and shift to v1.1 build.
- Day 1-7: schema + path UI shell + lesson runner + 2 exercise types + first 5 letter lessons working end-to-end (proof of mechanic)
- Day 8-14: remaining exercise types + all 35 letters + nukta + mukta + matras + diacritics + conjuncts content + placement test
- Day 15-18: polish, reference split, smoke testing, launch

What's your gut — A, B, or C? And: is there a real deadline driving "fast," or is it momentum-based ("I just want to be live")? Knowing which helps me make smarter calls on what to compress.

One row per (user, lesson). A row exists\n-- iff the user has at least started the lesson. completed_at being non-null\n-- means the lesson was passed; null means started-but-not-finished.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.lesson_progress (\n  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  lesson_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n  attempt_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  first_attempted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, lesson_id)\n);\n\n-- Per-exercise attempt log. Append-only (we never delete attempts).\n-- Used for: (a) accuracy stats; (b) spaced reinforcement decisions\n-- in future versions; (c) per-exercise reattempt-on-wrong logic.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.exercise_results (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  lesson_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  exercise_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  was_correct BOOLEAN NOT NULL,\n  attempted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_lesson_progress_user\n  ON public.lesson_progress(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_exercise_results_user_lesson\n  ON public.exercise_results(user_id, lesson_id);\n\n-- RLS: every row is owned by exactly one user, who alone can read/write it.\nALTER TABLE public.lesson_progress ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE public.exercise_results ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\n\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"lesson_progress_owner_all\" ON public.lesson_progress;\nCREATE POLICY \"lesson_progress_owner_all\" ON public.lesson_progress\n  FOR ALL TO authenticated\n  USING (user_id = auth.uid())\n  WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());\n\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"exercise_results_owner_read\" ON public.exercise_results;\nCREATE POLICY \"exercise_results_owner_read\" ON public.exercise_results\n  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (user_id = auth.uid());\n\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"exercise_results_owner_insert\" ON public.exercise_results;\nCREATE POLICY \"exercise_results_owner_insert\" ON public.exercise_results\n  FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());\nSQL\n\necho \"=== Migration SQL ===\"\nwc -l /tmp/akhar-v11-migration.sql\necho \"\"\n\n# Apply via Management API\nQUERY_JSON=$(python3 -c \"\nimport \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d \"$QUERY_JSON\" \\\n  \"https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_REF/database/query\" \\\n  | python3 -m json.tool 2>&1 | head -20",

// The akhar curriculum — modelled on JS Nagra's "Panjabi Made Easy Book 1"
// (1984, Nagra Publications). The book teaches Gurmukhi as a sequential
// path: one concept per lesson, real example words, reading practice.
//
// Lesson kinds:
//   - "letter"        a single Gurmukhi letter (paintee akhar or nukta)
//   - "nukta-group"   the 5 nukta letters introduced together
//   - "chart"         a reference grid (all letters in one view)
//   - "exercise"      recognition / matching test
//   - "mukta"         words with no vowel sign (inherent a)
//   - "matra"         a vowel sign (kannā, sihārī, etc.)
//   - "concept"       a special symbol or rule (adhikk, tippī, bindī, etc.)
//
// Words and sentences are hand-picked from the book itself (page refs noted)
// so the curriculum stays close to a pedagogically validated source.

export type LessonKind =
  | "primer"
  | "letter"
  | "nukta-group"
  | "chart"
  | "exercise"
  | "mukta"
  | "matra"
  | "concept"
  | "story"
  | "glossary";

export interface ExampleWord {
  pa: string;        // Gurmukhi
  iso: string;       // ISO 15919 romanization
  en: string;        // English meaning
  emoji?: string;    // optional emoji illustration
}

export interface LetterLesson {
  kind: "letter";
  slug: string;          // URL slug (use the char itself, URL-encoded)
  char: string;          // the Gurmukhi character
  name_pa: string;       // ਜੱਜਾ
  name_iso: string;      // jajjā
  ipa: string;           // /dʒə/
  group: string;         // for the chart grouping
  examples: ExampleWord[];
  not_word_initial?: boolean; // ਙ ਞ ਣ ੜ ਲ਼ — don't begin words
}

export interface NuktaGroupLesson {
  kind: "nukta-group";
  slug: string;
  letters: { char: string; name_pa: string; name_iso: string; ipa: string; examples: ExampleWord[] }[];
}

export interface ChartLesson {
  kind: "chart";
  slug: string;
  title: string;
  description: string;
}

export interface MatraLesson {
  kind: "matra";
  slug: string;
  matra: string;         // the vowel sign in isolation
  name_pa: string;       // ਕੰਨਾ
  name_iso: string;      // kannā
  sound_iso: string;     // ā
  length: "short" | "long";
  description_en: string;
  construction: { base: string; result: string; iso: string }[]; // ਕ + ਾ = ਕਾ
  examples: ExampleWord[];
  reading: string[];     // sentences using only what's been taught
}

export interface MuktaLesson {
  kind: "mukta";
  slug: string;
  examples: ExampleWord[];
  reading: string[];
}
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/course/types.ts",
  "content": "// Type definitions for the v1.1 course layer.\n//\n// The course is a sequence of PATH_SECTIONS, each containing an ordered\n// list of PathLessons. A lesson has a \"teach\" screen (which can reuse\n// existing content from data/curriculum.ts via curriculumRef) and a\n// set of mastery exercises.\n//\n// Exercises are a discriminated union — each kind has its own shape, so\n// the runner can switch on `kind` to render the right UI without runtime\n// type checks. Adding a new exercise kind = add to the union + add a\n// renderer + add a checker.\n//\n// Lesson IDs are slugs (e.g. \"letter-ooraa\") used as primary keys in\n// lesson_progress / exercise_results tables. They MUST be stable across\n// deploys — changing a slug breaks every user's progress against that\n// lesson. Pick once, never rename.\n\nexport type ExerciseKind =\n  | \"audio-pick-letter\"\n  | \"letter-pick-audio\"\n  | \"type-romanization\"\n  | \"match-pairs\"\n  | \"tap-in-order\";\n\ninterface ExerciseBase {\n  id: string;\n  kind: ExerciseKind;\n}\n\n// User hears audio for one letter, must pick it from N options.\nexport interface AudioPickLetterExercise extends ExerciseBase {\n  kind: \"audio-pick-letter\";\n  audioForLetter: string;   // the correct letter, whose audio plays\n  options: string[];        // N letters to choose from (must include the answer)\n}\n\n// User sees a letter, must tap which of N audio buttons matches.\nexport interface LetterPickAudioExercise extends ExerciseBase {\n  kind: \"letter-pick-audio\";\n  displayLetter: string;    // the correct letter, shown to user\n  audioOptions: string[];   // N letters whose audio is on buttons\n}\n\n// User sees a letter, types the romanization. acceptedAnswers covers\n// the common spellings (e.g. [\"sa\", \"sā\", \"saa\"] for ਸ — strip diacritics\n// + collapse whitespace before comparing).\nexport interface TypeRomanizationExercise extends ExerciseBase {\n  kind: \"type-romanization\";\n  displayLetter: string;\n  acceptedAnswers: string[];\n}\n\n// User drags letters to sounds (or vice versa). Pairs render as two\n// shuffled columns; correct = all pairs matched.\nexport interface MatchPairsExercise extends ExerciseBase {\n  kind: \"match-pairs\";\n  pairs: Array<{ letter: string; iso: string }>;\n}\n\n// User sees a row of letters; audio plays a sequence; user taps them in\n// the order heard.\nexport interface TapInOrderExercise extends ExerciseBase {\n  kind: \"tap-in-order\";\n  letters: string[];        // displayed in this order (shuffled at runtime)\n  sequence: string[];       // played in this order (the answer)\n}\n\nexport type Exercise =\n  | AudioPickLetterExercise\n  | LetterPickAudioExercise\n  | TypeRomanizationExercise\n  | MatchPairsExercise\n  | TapInOrderExercise;\n\nexport type LessonKind = \"teach-and-test\" | \"check\";\n\nexport interface PathLesson {\n  id: string;               // stable slug — primary key in DB\n  sectionId: string;        // which section this belongs to\n  kind: LessonKind;         // regular lesson vs end-of-section check\n  title: string;            // shown on path + lesson runner header\n  /**\n   * Optional reference into the existing data/curriculum.ts CURRICULUM array.\n   * When present, the teach screen renders that lesson's content. When\n   * absent (e.g. for \"check\" lessons), the teach screen is skipped.\n   */\n  curriculumRef?: string;\n  exercises: Exercise[];\n}\n\nexport interface PathSection {\n  id: string;               // route-safe slug (e.g. \"s1\", \"s10\")\n  num: string;              // display label (e.g. \"§1\", \"§10\")\n  title: string;\n  description: string;      // short blurb shown on path\n  lessonIds: string[];      // ordered\n}\n\nexport type LessonStatus = \"locked\" | \"available\" | \"completed\";\n\nexport interface UserProgressView {\n  lessonStatuses: Record<string, LessonStatus>;\n  currentLessonId: string | null;  // next available + not-completed lesson\n  completedCount: number;\n  totalCount: number;\n}\n"
}

 \"matra-dulainkar\",\n      \"matra-lavan\",\n      \"matra-dulavan\",\n      \"matra-hora\",\n      \"matra-kanaura\",\n      \"check-matras\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"s11\",\n    num: \"§11\",\n    title: \"Diacritics\",\n    description: \"Addhak, tippi, bindi.\",\n    lessonIds: [\n      \"diacritic-addhak\",\n      \"diacritic-tippi\",\n      \"diacritic-bindi\",\n      \"check-diacritics\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"s12\",\n    num: \"§12\",\n    title: \"Conjuncts\",\n    description: \"Subscript letters; tone introduction.\",\n    lessonIds: [\n      \"conjunct-pairin-rara\",\n      \"conjunct-pairin-haha\",\n      \"check-conjuncts\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"s13\",\n    num: \"§13\",\n    title: \"Muharni consolidation\",\n    description: \"Drill every consonant against every matra.\",\n    lessonIds: [\n      \"muharni-1\",\n      \"muharni-2\",\n      \"muharni-3\",\n      \"muharni-4\",\n      \"muharni-5\",\n      \"muharni-6\",\n      \"muharni-7\",\n      \"check-muharni\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"s14\",\n    num: \"§14\",\n    title: \"Sentence reading\",\n    description: \"Basic sentence structure and common particles.\",\n    lessonIds: [\n      \"sentence-1\",\n      \"sentence-2\",\n      \"sentence-3\",\n      \"sentence-4\",\n      \"sentence-5\",\n      \"check-sentences\",\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"s15\",\n    num: \"§15+\",\n    title: \"Sakhis\",\n    description: \"Read whole stories with comprehension checks.\",\n    lessonIds: [\n      \"sakhi-akhar-nanak-birth\",\n      \"sakhi-akhar-sacha-sauda\",\n      \"sakhi-akhar-dudh-lahu\",\n      \"sakhi-1\",\n      \"sakhi-16\",\n      \"sakhi-38\",\n    ],\n  },\n];\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Lesson catalog (Day-1: only §1 lessons are filled in)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// The five letters of Line 1. Used in both individual letter lessons\n// and the Line-1 check, so kept as a constant.\nconst LINE_1_LETTERS = [\"ੳ\", \"ਅ\", \"ੲ\", \"ਸ\", \"ਹ\"] as const;\n\n// Distractor pool for Line-1 exercises — letters from other lines that\n// learners might confuse with the Line-1 letters. Chosen for visual or\n// phonetic similarity to keep the multiple-choice meaningful.\nconst LINE_1_DISTRACTORS = [\"ਕ\", \"ਖ\", \"ਚ\", \"ਟ\", \"ਪ\", \"ਮ\", \"ਨ\"];\n\n// Helper: 4-option multiple choice with the correct letter + 3 distractors.\nfunction fourOptions(correct: string, others: string[]): string[] {\n  const pool = others.filter((l) => l !== correct);\n  // Pick 3 distractors deterministically; runtime shuffles the order so\n  // the correct option isn't always at index 0.\n  return [correct, pool[0], pool[1], pool[2]];\n}\n\nfunction letterLessonExercises(letter: string, iso: string[]): Exercise[] {\n  return [\n    {\n      id: `${letter}-audio-1`,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n      audioForLetter: letter,\n      options: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n    {\n      id: `${letter}-visual-1`,\n      kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n      displayLetter: letter,\n      audioOptions: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n    {\n      id: `${letter}-type-1`,\n      kind: \"type-romanization\",\n      displayLetter: letter,\n      acceptedAnswers: iso,\n    },\n    {\n      id: `${letter}-audio-2`,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n      audioForLetter: letter,\n      options: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n    {\n      id: `${letter}-visual-2`,\n      kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n      displayLetter: letter,\n      audioOptions: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n  ];\n}\n\n// Line 1 check: mixes all 5 letters across multiple exercise types. ~10\n// exercises, 80% to pass.\nconst LINE_1_CHECK_EXERCISES: Exercise[] = [\n  ...LINE_1_LETTERS.flatMap((letter): Exercise[] => [\n    {\n      id: `check1-${letter}-a`,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n      audioForLetter: letter,\n      options: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n    {\n      id: `check1-${letter}-v`,\n      kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n      displayLetter: letter,\n      audioOptions: fourOptions(letter, LINE_1_DISTRACTORS),\n    },\n  ]),\n  {\n    id: \"check1-match\",\n    kind: \"match-pairs\",\n    pairs: [\n      { letter: \"ੳ\", iso: \"oora\" },\n      { letter: \"ਅ\", iso: \"aira\" },\n      { letter: \"ੲ\", iso: \"iri\" },\n      { letter: \"ਸ\", iso: \"sa\" },\n    ],\n  },\n];\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = {\n  // §1 — Letters Line 1\n  \"letter-ooraa\": {\n    id: \"letter-ooraa\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n    title: \"ੳ — Oora\",\n    curriculumRef: \"letter-ੳ\",\n    exercises: letterLessonExercises(\"ੳ\", [\"oora\", \"ūṛā\", \"ura\"]),\n  },\n  \"letter-airaa\": {\n    id: \"letter-airaa\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n    title: \"ਅ — Aira\",\n    curriculumRef: \"letter-ਅ\",\n    exercises: letterLessonExercises(\"ਅ\", [\"aira\", \"airā\", \"a\"]),\n  },\n  \"letter-eeree\": {\n    id: \"letter-eeree\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n    title: \"ੲ — Iri\",\n    curriculumRef: \"letter-ੲ\",\n    exercises: letterLessonExercises(\"ੲ\", [\"iri\", \"īṛī\", \"i\"]),\n  },\n  \"letter-sassaa\": {\n    id: \"letter-sassaa\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n    title: \"ਸ — Sa\",\n    curriculumRef: \"letter-ਸ\",\n    exercises: letterLessonExercises(\"ਸ\", [\"sa\", \"sassā\", \"sassa\"]),\n  },\n  \"letter-hahaa\": {\n    id: \"letter-hahaa\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n    title: \"ਹ — Ha\",\n    curriculumRef: \"letter-ਹ\",\n    exercises: letterLessonExercises(\"ਹ\", [\"ha\", \"hāhā\", \"haha\"]),\n  },\n  \"check-line-1\": {\n    id: \"check-line-1\",\n    sectionId: \"s1\",\n    kind: \"check\",\n    title: \"Line 1 check\",\n    exercises: LINE_1_CHECK_EXERCISES,\n  },\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Lookup helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport function getSection(id: string): PathSection | undefined {\n  return PATH_SECTIONS.find((s) => s.id === id);\n}\n\nexport function getLesson(id: string): PathLesson | undefined {\n  return PATH_LESSONS[id];\n}\n\n/**\n * Flat ordered list of lesson IDs across all sections — the linear path\n * order. Used to determine which lesson unlocks next.\n */\nexport function allLessonIdsInOrder(): string[] {\n  return PATH_SECTIONS.flatMap((s) => s.lessonIds);\n}\n\n/**\n * The lesson that comes immediately after `id` in the path order, or\n * null if it's the last one (or not found).\n */\nexport function nextLessonId(id: string): string | null {\n  const order = allLessonIdsInOrder();\n  const i = order.indexOf(id);\n  if (i < 0 || i === order.length - 1) return null;\n  return order[i + 1];\n}\n\n/**\n * The lesson before `id`. Returns null for the first lesson or unknown id.\n */\nexport function previousLessonId(id: string): string | null {\n  const order = allLessonIdsInOrder();\n  const i = order.indexOf(id);\n  if (i <= 0) return null;\n  return order[i - 1];\n}\n\n/**\n * True if the lesson is \"authored\" — present in PATH_LESSONS. Many\n * lessonIds in PATH_SECTIONS reference future content not yet written;\n * those are stubs the path UI should render as \"coming soon.\"\n */\nexport function isLessonAuthored(id: string): boolean {\n  return id in PATH_LESSONS;\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/lib/course/progress.ts",
  "content": "// Server-side helpers for course progress. All functions take an\n// authenticated Supabase client (`createClient` from @supabase/ssr or our\n// serverClient()) — the RLS policies on lesson_progress / exercise_results\n// ensure each call only sees/writes the calling user's rows, so we never\n// pass user_id explicitly into queries.\n//\n// Status model: a lesson_progress row exists iff the user has at least\n// started the lesson. completed_at being NOT NULL means it was passed.\n// A lesson is \"available\" if it's the first lesson OR the previous\n// lesson in path order has a completed row. Otherwise it's \"locked\".\n\nimport type { SupabaseClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport {\n  PATH_LESSONS,\n  PATH_SECTIONS,\n  allLessonIdsInOrder,\n  isLessonAuthored,\n} from \"@/data/curriculum-v1.1\";\nimport type { LessonStatus, UserProgressView } from \"@/lib/course/types\";\n\ninterface ProgressRow {\n  lesson_id: string;\n  completed_at: string | null;\n  attempt_count: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Read all lesson_progress rows for the authenticated user. Returns a\n * map keyed by lesson_id. Missing keys = never touched.\n */\nasync function readProgressRows(\n  supabase: SupabaseClient,\n): Promise<Record<string, ProgressRow>> {\n  const { data, error } = await supabase\n    .from(\"lesson_progress\")\n    .select(\"lesson_id, completed_at, attempt_count\");\n  if (error) {\n    console.error(\"readProgressRows failed\", error);\n    return {};\n  }\n  const out: Record<string, ProgressRow> = {};\n  for (const row of data ?? []) out[row.lesson_id] = row as ProgressRow;\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Compute the full progress view: status per lesson, the current lesson\n * the user should land on, and aggregate counts. One DB call.\n */\nexport async function getUserProgress(\n  supabase: SupabaseClient,\n): Promise<UserProgressView> {\n  const rows = await readProgressRows(supabase);\n  const order = allLessonIdsInOrder();\n  const lessonStatuses: Record<string, LessonStatus> = {};\n  let currentLessonId: string | null = null;\n  let completedCount = 0;\n  let prevCompleted = true; // first lesson is always reachable\n\n  for (const lessonId of order) {\n    const row = rows[lessonId];\n    const isCompleted = !!row?.completed_at;\n    let status: LessonStatus;\n    if (isCompleted) {\n      status = \"completed\";\n      completedCount++;\n    } else if (prevCompleted) {\n      status = \"available\";\n      if (currentLessonId === null) currentLessonId = lessonId;\n    } else {\n      status = \"locked\";\n    }\n    lessonStatuses[lessonId] = status;\n    // Only authored lessons count toward unlocking — coming-soon stubs\n    // can't be \"completed\" by the user so they shouldn't gate the path.\n    prevCompleted = isCompleted || (status === \"available\" && !isLessonAuthored(lessonId));\n  }\n\n  return {\n    lessonStatuses,\n    currentLessonId,\n    completedCount,\n    totalCount: order.length,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Mark a lesson as completed (sets completed_at = NOW). Idempotent —\n * safe to call multiple times. Increments attempt_count if the row\n * already exists.\n */\nexport async function markLessonCompleted(\n  supabase: SupabaseClient,\n  userId: string,\n  lessonId: string,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const { error } = await supabase.from(\"lesson_progress\").upsert(\n    {\n      user_id: userId,\n      lesson_id: lessonId,\n      completed_at: new Date().toISOString(),\n    },\n    { onConflict: \"user_id,lesson_id\" },\n  );\n  if (error) {\n    console.error(\"markLessonCompleted failed\", { lessonId, error });\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Record a single exercise attempt. Used for accuracy stats + future\n * spaced reinforcement decisions. Append-only.\n */\nexport async function recordExerciseAttempt(\n  supabase: SupabaseClient,\n  userId: string,\n  lessonId: string,\n  exerciseId: string,\n  wasCorrect: boolean,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const { error } = await supabase.from(\"exercise_results\").insert({\n    user_id: userId,\n    lesson_id: lessonId,\n    exercise_id: exerciseId,\n    was_correct: wasCorrect,\n  });\n  if (error) {\n    console.error(\"recordExerciseAttempt failed\", { lessonId, exerciseId, error });\n    // Don't throw — losing an attempt log shouldn't break the lesson flow.\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Bump a lesson's attempt_count without marking it complete. Called when\n * a user starts a lesson — useful for the \"you failed, redo\" tracking.\n */\nexport async function incrementLessonAttempts(\n  supabase: SupabaseClient,\n  userId: string,\n  lessonId: string,\n): Promise<void> {\n  // Fetch existing then upsert with incremented count. Cheap because\n  // RLS scopes us to one user.\n  const { data } = await supabase\n    .from(\"lesson_progress\")\n    .select(\"attempt_count\")\n    .eq(\"lesson_id\", lessonId)\n    .maybeSingle();\n  const next = (data?.attempt_count ?? 0) + 1;\n  const { error } = await supabase.from(\"lesson_progress\").upsert(\n    { user_id: userId, lesson_id: lessonId, attempt_count: next },\n    { onConflict: \"user_id,lesson_id\" },\n  );\n  if (error) console.error(\"incrementLessonAttempts failed\", { lessonId, error });\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Path summary for the dashboard / header — small computed view.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport interface SectionSummary {\n  id: string;\n  num: string;\n  title: string;\n  description: string;\n  completedCount: number;\n  totalCount: number;\n  isCurrent: boolean;     // contains the user's current lesson\n}\n\n/**\n * Compute per-section summaries for use in the path UI: how many lessons\n * in each section are done, which section the user is \"in\" right now.\n */\nexport function summarizeSections(\n  progress: UserProgressView,\n): SectionSummary[] {\n  return PATH_SECTIONS.map((section) => {\n    const lessons = section.lessonIds;\n    const completed = lessons.filter(\n      (id) => progress.lessonStatuses[id] === \"completed\",\n    ).length;\n    const isCurrent =\n      !!progress.currentLessonId && lessons.includes(progress.currentLessonId);\n    return {\n      id: section.id,\n      num: section.num,\n      title: section.title,\n      description: section.description,\n      completedCount: completed,\n      totalCount: lessons.length,\n      isCurrent,\n    };\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve whether a user can access a given lesson — used to gate the\n * /course/[id] route. Locked → redirect to /course. Available or\n * Completed → render the lesson.\n */\nexport function canAccessLesson(\n  progress: UserProgressView,\n  lessonId: string,\n): boolean {\n  const status = progress.lessonStatuses[lessonId];\n  return status === \"available\" || status === \"completed\";\n}\n\n/**\n * For lessons not yet authored (in PATH_SECTIONS but not PATH_LESSONS),\n * we surface a friendly \"coming soon\" rather than 404. This list is\n * curated centrally so the path UI can render every section even when\n * its content isn't built yet.\n */\nexport function isComingSoonLesson(lessonId: string): boolean {\n  // Lesson IDs declared in sections but missing from PATH_LESSONS.\n  return PATH_SECTIONS.some((s) => s.lessonIds.includes(lessonId))\n    && !(lessonId in PATH_LESSONS);\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/course/page.tsx",
  "content": "// /course — the Duolingo-style vertical path. Server Component reads\n// the user's progress once, then renders every section + lesson tile\n// with the right state (✓ completed / → current / 🔒 locked / coming soon).\n//\n// Lesson tiles are <Link>s to /course/[lessonId] unless locked or\n// unauthored — those render as disabled <div>s so users can see what's\n// ahead without being able to skip into it.\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport {\n  PATH_SECTIONS,\n  PATH_LESSONS,\n  isLessonAuthored,\n} from \"@/data/curriculum-v1.1\";\nimport {\n  getUserProgress,\n  isComingSoonLesson,\n  summarizeSections,\n} from \"@/lib/course/progress\";\nimport type { LessonStatus } from \"@/lib/course/types\";\n\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: \"Course — akhar.io\",\n};\n\nexport default async function CoursePage() {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n  if (!user) redirect(\"/login?next=/course\");\n\n  const progress = await getUserProgress(supabase);\n  const sectionSummaries = summarizeSections(progress);\n\n  return (\n    <main className=\"mx-auto max-w-2xl px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 sm:py-12\">\n      <header className=\"mb-8\">\n        <p className=\"text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-zinc-500\">\n          Your path\n        </p>\n        <h1 className=\"mt-1 font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 sm:text-4xl dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {progress.completedCount === 0\n            ? \"Start with the letters.\"\n            : \"Keep going.\"}\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-2 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n          {progress.completedCount} of {progress.totalCount} lessons completed.\n        </p>\n      </header>\n\n      <div className=\"space-y-10\">\n        {sectionSummaries.map((section, sectionIdx) => {\n          const sectionData = PATH_SECTIONS[sectionIdx];\n          return (\n            <section key={section.id} className=\"space-y-3\">\n              <SectionHeader\n                num={section.num}\n                title={section.title}\n                description={section.description}\n                completedCount={section.completedCount}\n                totalCount={section.totalCount}\n                isCurrent={section.isCurrent}\n              />\n              <ol className=\"space-y-2\">\n                {sectionData.lessonIds.map((lessonId) => {\n                  const status = progress.lessonStatuses[lessonId] ?? \"locked\";\n                  const isCurrent = lessonId === progress.currentLessonId;\n                  const comingSoon = isComingSoonLesson(lessonId);\n                  return (\n                    <LessonTile\n                      key={lessonId}\n                      lessonId={lessonId}\n                      title={\n                        PATH_LESSONS[lessonId]?.title ??\n                        humaniseLessonId(lessonId)\n                      }\n                      kind={PATH_LESSONS[lessonId]?.kind}\n                      status={status}\n                      isCurrent={isCurrent}\n                      comingSoon={comingSoon}\n                    />\n                  );\n                })}\n              </ol>\n            </section>\n          );\n        })}\n      </div>\n\n      <footer className=\"mt-12 border-t border-zinc-200 pt-6 text-xs text-zinc-500 dark:border-zinc-800\">\n        <p>\n          Locked lessons unlock as you complete the ones before them.\n          Sections marked \"coming soon\" are still being written.\n        </p>\n      </footer>\n    </main>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SectionHeader({\n  num,\n  title,\n  description,\n  completedCount,\n  totalCount,\n  isCurrent,\n}: {\n  num: string;\n  title: string;\n  description: string;\n  completedCount: number;\n  totalCount: number;\n  isCurrent: boolean;\n}) {\n  const pct = totalCount === 0 ? 0 : (completedCount / totalCount) * 100;\n  return (\n    <div\n      className={`rounded-lg border p-4 ${\n        isCurrent\n          ? \"border-zinc-900 bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900\"\n          : \"border-zinc-200 bg-white dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n      }`}\n    >\n      <div className=\"flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3\">\n        <div>\n          <span className=\"text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-zinc-500\">\n            {num}\n          </span>\n          <h2 className=\"mt-0.5 font-serif text-xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n            {title}\n          </h2>\n        </div>\n        <span className=\"shrink-0 text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n          {completedCount}/{totalCount}\n        </span>\n      </div>\n      <p className=\"mt-1 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n        {description}\n      </p>\n      <div className=\"mt-3 h-1.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-800\">\n        <div\n          className=\"h-full bg-zinc-900 transition-all dark:bg-zinc-50\"\n          style={{ width: `${pct}%` }}\n        />\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction LessonTile({\n  lessonId,\n  title,\n  kind,\n  status,\n  isCurrent,\n  comingSoon,\n}: {\n  lessonId: string;\n  title: string;\n  kind?: \"teach-and-test\" | \"check\";\n  status: LessonStatus;\n  isCurrent: boolean;\n  comingSoon: boolean;\n}) {\n  const icon = comingSoon\n    ? \"…\"\n    : status === \"completed\"\n      ? \"✓\"\n      : status === \"available\"\n        ? isCurrent ? \"→\" : \"○\"\n        : \"🔒\";\n\n  const baseTile =\n    \"flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg border px-4 py-3 text-sm transition\";\n\n  // Coming-soon: never clickable, soft visual treatment.\n  if (comingSoon) {\n    return (\n      <li>\n        <div\n          className={`${baseTile} cursor-not-allowed border-dashed border-zinc-200 bg-zinc-50/50 text-zinc-400 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-900/50 dark:text-zinc-500`}\n        >\n          <span className=\"w-5 text-center\" aria-hidden>{icon}</span>\n          <span className=\"flex-1\">{title}</span>\n          <span className=\"text-xs\">Coming soon</span>\n        </div>\n      </li>\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Locked: visible but inactive, with lock affordance.\n  if (status === \"locked\") {\n    return (\n      <li>\n        <div\n          className={`${baseTile} cursor-not-allowed border-zinc-200 bg-zinc-50/50 text-zinc-400 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-900/50 dark:text-zinc-500`}\n          title=\"Complete the previous lesson to unlock\"\n        >\n          <span className=\"w-5 text-center\" aria-hidden>{icon}</span>\n          <span className=\"flex-1\">{title}</span>\n          {kind === \"check\" && (\n            <span className=\"rounded-md bg-zinc-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs text-zinc-500 dark:bg-zinc-800\">\n              Check\n            </span>\n          )}\n        </div>\n      </li>\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Available or Completed: clickable link to the lesson runner.\n  const accent = isCurrent\n    ? \"border-zinc-900 bg-zinc-900 text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:border-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n    : status === \"completed\"\n      ? \"border-emerald-200 bg-emerald-50/60 text-emerald-900 hover:bg-emerald-100 dark:border-emerald-900/40 dark:bg-emerald-950/40 dark:text-emerald-200 dark:hover:bg-emerald-900/40\"\n      : \"border-zinc-200 bg-white text-zinc-900 hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-100 dark:hover:border-zinc-600 dark:hover:bg-zinc-900\";\n\n  return (\n    <li>\n      <Link href={`/course/${lessonId}`} className={`${baseTile} ${accent}`}>\n        <span className=\"w-5 text-center\" aria-hidden>{icon}</span>\n        <span className=\"flex-1\">{title}</span>\n        {kind === \"check\" && (\n          <span\n            className={`rounded-md px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs ${\n              isCurrent\n                ? \"bg-white/20\"\n                : \"bg-zinc-100 text-zinc-600 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-400\"\n            }`}\n          >\n            Check\n          </span>\n        )}\n      </Link>\n    </li>\n  );\n}\n\n// Fallback for coming-soon stubs whose human title isn't in PATH_LESSONS yet.\nfunction humaniseLessonId(id: string): string {\n  return id\n    .replace(/-/g, \" \")\n    .replace(/\\b\\w/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase());\n}\n"
}

The v1.1 catalog only knows\n// which letter character each exercise is about; this resolves the\n// details when the exercise renders.\n\nimport { CURRICULUM } from \"@/data/curriculum\";\nimport type { LetterLesson } from \"@/data/curriculum\";\n\ninterface LetterInfo {\n  char: string;\n  name_pa: string;        // Punjabi name, e.g. \"ਸੱਸਾ\" — used for TTS audio\n  name_iso: string;       // romanized name, e.g. \"sassā\"\n  ipa: string;            // phonetic value, e.g. \"sə\"\n}\n\n// Build a lookup index once at module load.\nconst INDEX: Record<string, LetterInfo> = (() => {\n  const out: Record<string, LetterInfo> = {};\n  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {\n    if (lesson.kind === \"letter\") {\n      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;\n      out[l.char] = {\n        char: l.char,\n        name_pa: l.name_pa,\n        name_iso: l.name_iso,\n        ipa: l.ipa,\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n})();\n\n/**\n * Look up a letter's metadata by its Gurmukhi character. Returns null\n * if the character isn't in the curriculum yet (caller should treat as\n * a graceful skip rather than crash).\n */\nexport function lookupLetter(char: string): LetterInfo | null {\n  return INDEX[char] ?? null;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Small audio playback button. Fetches MP3 from /api/tts (which caches\n// every distinct word in R2, so repeats are instant) and plays it. Used\n// across all exercise types that need audio.\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\nexport default function AudioButton({\n  word,\n  label,\n  autoPlay = false,\n  size = \"md\",\n}: {\n  word: string;       // Gurmukhi text to pronounce — passed to /api/tts\n  label?: string;     // visible label (defaults to word if not given)\n  autoPlay?: boolean; // play once on mount\n  size?: \"sm\" | \"md\" | \"lg\";\n}) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\"idle\" | \"loading\" | \"playing\">(\"idle\");\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`;\n\n  function play() {\n    if (audioRef.current) {\n      audioRef.current.pause();\n      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;\n    }\n    setState(\"loading\");\n    const audio = new Audio(url);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n    audio.onplaying = () => setState(\"playing\");\n    audio.onended = () => setState(\"idle\");\n    audio.onerror = () => setState(\"idle\");\n    audio.play().catch(() => setState(\"idle\"));\n  }\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (autoPlay) {\n      const t = setTimeout(play, 200);\n      return () => clearTimeout(t);\n    }\n    // we intentionally only autoplay once on mount; subsequent renders\n    // don't retrigger.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, []);\n\n  const sz =\n    size === \"sm\" ? \"h-8 w-8 text-sm\"\n    : size === \"lg\" ? \"h-14 w-14 text-2xl\"\n    : \"h-11 w-11 text-base\";\n\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={play}\n      disabled={state === \"loading\"}\n      className={`inline-flex shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-zinc-100 ${sz} text-zinc-700 transition hover:bg-zinc-200 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-200 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700`}\n      aria-label={label ?? `Play ${word}`}\n      title={label ?? `Play ${word}`}\n    >\n      {state === \"playing\" ? \"🔉\" : state === \"loading\" ? \"⋯\" : \"🔊\"}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n"
}

They render the question, capture the user's\n// answer, and report correctness exactly once when the user submits.\n// Feedback styling (green/red flash, \"correct/incorrect\" badge) is\n// owned by the LessonRunner, not the components themselves — that\n// keeps the runner in charge of the state machine.\n\nimport { useMemo, useState } from \"react\";\nimport AudioButton from \"./AudioButton\";\nimport { lookupLetter } from \"@/lib/course/letter-lookup\";\nimport type {\n  AudioPickLetterExercise,\n  LetterPickAudioExercise,\n  TypeRomanizationExercise,\n  MatchPairsExercise,\n  TapInOrderExercise,\n} from \"@/lib/course/types\";\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Stable shuffle keyed off the exercise id so the option order doesn't\n// reshuffle on every re-render but does vary between exercises.\nfunction seededShuffle<T>(arr: T[], seed: string): T[] {\n  const out = [...arr];\n  let h = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < seed.length; i++) h = (h * 31 + seed.charCodeAt(i)) >>> 0;\n  for (let i = out.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {\n    h = (h * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0;\n    const j = h % (i + 1);\n    [out[i], out[j]] = [out[j], out[i]];\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\n// Look up the \"name\" of a letter for TTS — what's pronounced when we\n// \"play\" it. Falls back to the character itself if not found.\nfunction letterAudioWord(letter: string): string {\n  const info = lookupLetter(letter);\n  return info?.name_pa ?? letter;\n}\n\ninterface ExerciseShellProps {\n  prompt: React.ReactNode;\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}\n\nfunction ExerciseShell({ prompt, children }: ExerciseShellProps) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-6\">\n      <div className=\"text-sm text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400\">{prompt}</div>\n      {children}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// 1. Audio → tap the letter\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport function AudioPickLetterRenderer({\n  exercise,\n  onSubmit,\n}: {\n  exercise: AudioPickLetterExercise;\n  onSubmit: (wasCorrect: boolean) => void;\n}) {\n  const options = useMemo(\n    () => seededShuffle(exercise.options, exercise.id),\n    [exercise.id, exercise.options],\n  );\n\n  function pick(letter: string) {\n    onSubmit(letter === exercise.audioForLetter);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <ExerciseShell prompt=\"Tap the letter you hear.\">\n      <div className=\"flex justify-center\">\n        <AudioButton\n          word={letterAudioWord(exercise.audioForLetter)}\n          size=\"lg\"\n          autoPlay\n          label=\"Play the letter\"\n        />\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-4\">\n        {options.map((letter) => (\n          <button\n            key={letter}\n            type=\"button\"\n            onClick={() => pick(letter)}\n            className=\"rounded-xl border-2 border-zinc-200 bg-white px-4 py-6 font-serif text-4xl text-zinc-900 transition hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 active:scale-95 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-50 dark:hover:border-zinc-600 dark:hover:bg-zinc-900\"\n          >\n            {letter}\n          </button>\n        ))}\n      </div>\n    </ExerciseShell>\n  );\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// 2. \"border-zinc-900 bg-zinc-900 text-white dark:border-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900\"\n                  : \"border-zinc-200 bg-white text-zinc-700 hover:border-zinc-400 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-300\"\n              }`}\n            >\n              Pick\n            </button>\n          </div>\n        ))}\n      </div>\n    </ExerciseShell>\n  );\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// 3. Type the romanization\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport function TypeRomanizationRenderer({\n  exercise,\n  onSubmit,\n}: {\n  exercise: TypeRomanizationExercise;\n  onSubmit: (wasCorrect: boolean) => void;\n}) {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState(\"\");\n\n  function normalise(s: string): string {\n    return s\n      .toLowerCase()\n      .trim()\n      // strip ISO 15919 diacritics so \"sa\", \"sā\", \"saa\" all compare equal\n      .normalize(\"NFD\")\n      .replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, \"\")\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \"\");\n  }\n\n  function submit() {\n    if (!value.trim()) return;\n    const n = normalise(value);\n    const ok = exercise.acceptedAnswers.some((a) => normalise(a) === n);\n    onSubmit(ok);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <ExerciseShell prompt=\"Type how you'd write this letter in English letters (Roman script).\">\n      <div className=\"flex flex-col items-center gap-4\">\n        <span className=\"rounded-xl border-2 border-zinc-300 bg-white px-12 py-8 font-serif text-6xl text-zinc-900 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {exercise.displayLetter}\n        </span>\n        <input\n          autoFocus\n          type=\"text\"\n          value={value}\n          onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}\n          onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === \"Enter\" && submit()}\n          placeholder=\"type here\"\n          autoComplete=\"off\"\n          autoCorrect=\"off\"\n          autoCapitalize=\"off\"\n          spellCheck={false}\n          className=\"w-full max-w-xs rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-3 py-3 text-center font-mono text-lg text-zinc-900 focus:border-zinc-500 focus:outline-none dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\"\n        />\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={submit}\n          disabled={!value.trim()}\n          className=\"rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-2 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n        >\n          Check\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </ExerciseShell>\n  );\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// 4. Match pairs (letter ↔ ISO)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport function MatchPairsRenderer({\n  exercise,\n  onSubmit,\n}: {\n  exercise: MatchPairsExercise;\n  onSubmit: (wasCorrect: boolean) => void;\n}) {\n  const letters = useMemo(\n    () => seededShuffle(exercise.pairs.map((p) => p.letter), exercise.id + \"L\"),\n    [exercise.id, exercise.pairs],\n  );\n  const isos = useMemo(\n    () => seededShuffle(exercise.pairs.map((p) => p.iso), exercise.id + \"I\"),\n    [exercise.id, exercise.pairs],\n  );\n  const expected = useMemo(() => {\n    const m: Record<string, string> = {};\n    for (const p of exercise.pairs) m[p.letter] = p.iso;\n    return m;\n  }, [exercise.pairs]);\n\n  // Pairing state — { letter: iso | null }\n  const [pairs, setPairs] = useState<Record<string, string | null>>(() => {\n    const init: Record<string, string | null> = {};\n    for (const l of letters) init[l] = null;\n    return init;\n  });\n  const [selectedLetter, setSelectedLetter] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  // Which letter has each iso been assigned to? (for highlighting the iso column)\n  const usedIsos = new Set(Object.values(pairs).filter((x): x is string => !!x));\n\n  function tapLetter(letter: string) {\n    setSelectedLetter((cur) => (cur === letter ? null : letter));\n  }\n  function tapIso(iso: string) {\n    if (!selectedLetter) return;\n    setPairs((cur) => {\n      const next = { ...cur };\n      // If iso was already paired with someone else, unpair them first.\n      for (const k of Object.keys(next)) {\n        if (next[k] === iso) next[k] = null;\n      }\n      next[selectedLetter] = iso;\n      return next;\n    });\n    setSelectedLetter(null);\n  }\n\n  const allFilled = letters.every((l) => pairs[l]);\n\n  function submit() {\n    const allCorrect = letters.every((l) => pairs[l] === expected[l]);\n    onSubmit(allCorrect);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <ExerciseShell prompt=\"Tap a letter, then tap its romanization. Pair all four.\">\n      <div className=\"grid grid-cols-2 gap-4\">\n        <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n          {letters.map((letter) => (\n            <button\n              key={letter}\n              type=\"button\"\n              onClick={() => tapLetter(letter)}\n              className={`w-full rounded-lg border-2 px-3 py-4 font-serif text-3xl transition ${\n                selectedLetter === letter\n                  ? \"border-zinc-900 bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900\"\n                  : pairs[letter]\n                    ? \"border-emerald-300 bg-emerald-50/50 dark:border-emerald-900 dark:bg-emerald-950/40\"\n                    : \"border-zinc-200 bg-white hover:border-zinc-400 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n              }`}\n            >\n              {letter}\n              {pairs[letter] && (\n                <span className=\"ml-2 font-sans text-base text-zinc-500\">\n                  → {pairs[letter]}\n                </span>\n              )}\n            </button>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n          {isos.map((iso) => (\n            <button\n              key={iso}\n              type=\"button\"\n              onClick={() => tapIso(iso)}\n              disabled={!selectedLetter && !usedIsos.has(iso)}\n              className={`w-full rounded-lg border-2 px-3 py-4 font-mono text-lg transition ${\n                usedIsos.has(iso)\n                  ? \"border-emerald-300 bg-emerald-50/50 text-emerald-900 dark:border-emerald-900 dark:bg-emerald-950/40 dark:text-emerald-200\"\n                  : selectedLetter\n                    ? \"border-zinc-300 bg-white text-zinc-900 hover:border-zinc-500 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-50\"\n                    : \"border-zinc-100 bg-zinc-50 text-zinc-400 dark:border-zinc-900 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-600\"\n              }`}\n            >\n              {iso}\n            </button>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"flex justify-center\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={submit}\n          disabled={!allFilled}\n          className=\"rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-2 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n        >\n          Check\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </ExerciseShell>\n  );\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// 5. Tap letters in the order you hear\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nexport function TapInOrderRenderer({\n  exercise,\n  onSubmit,\n}: {\n  exercise: TapInOrderExercise;\n  onSubmit: (wasCorrect: boolean) => void;\n}) {\n  const shuffled = useMemo(\n    () => seededShuffle(exercise.letters, exercise.id),\n    [exercise.id, exercise.letters],\n  );\n  const [tapped, setTapped] = useState<string[]>([]);\n\n  function tap(letter: string) {\n    if (tapped.length >= exercise.sequence.length) return;\n    setTapped((cur) => [...cur, letter]);\n  }\n\n  function reset() {\n    setTapped([]);\n  }\n\n  function submit() {\n    const ok =\n      tapped.length === exercise.sequence.length &&\n      tapped.every((l, i) => l === exercise.sequence[i]);\n    onSubmit(ok);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <ExerciseShell prompt=\"Listen to the sequence. Tap the letters in the order you heard them.\">\n      <div className=\"flex flex-col items-center gap-4\">\n        {/* Concatenate the names into one TTS request so the sequence plays as one clip — easier than chaining. */}\n        <AudioButton\n          word={exercise.sequence.map(letterAudioWord).join(\" — \")}\n          size=\"lg\"\n          autoPlay\n          label=\"Play the sequence\"\n        />\n        <div className=\"flex min-h-[3rem] items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border-2 border-dashed border-zinc-300 px-4 py-2 dark:border-zinc-700\">\n          {tapped.length === 0 ? (\n            <span className=\"text-sm text-zinc-400\">Your taps appear here</span>\n          ) : (\n            tapped.map((l, i) => (\n              <span key={i} className=\"font-serif text-2xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n                {l}\n              </span>\n            ))\n          )}\n        </div>\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"grid grid-cols-5 gap-2\">\n        {shuffled.map((letter, i) => (\n          <button\n            key={i}\n            type=\"button\"\n            onClick={() => tap(letter)}\n            disabled={tapped.length >= exercise.sequence.length}\n            className=\"rounded-lg border-2 border-zinc-200 bg-white px-2 py-4 font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 transition hover:border-zinc-400 hover:bg-zinc-50 disabled:opacity-50 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950 dark:text-zinc-50\"\n          >\n            {letter}\n          </button>\n        ))}\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"flex justify-center gap-3\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={reset}\n          className=\"rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-zinc-700 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-900\"\n        >\n          Reset\n        </button>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={submit}\n          disabled={tapped.length !== exercise.sequence.length}\n          className=\"rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-2 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n        >\n          Check\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </ExerciseShell>\n  );\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// State machine for one run-through of a lesson.\n//\n// Lifecycle:\n//   teach  → exercises  → result (per exercise) → either next exercise\n//                                                 OR fail screen\n//                                                 OR completed screen\n//\n// Mastery rule (deliberately simple for v1.1):\n//   - User must answer every exercise correctly.\n//   - If they get one wrong, it goes back into the queue at the end.\n//   - If they get the SAME exercise wrong twice, the lesson fails →\n//     they can retry. Their attempt is recorded server-side either way.\n\nimport { useRouter } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { useState, useTransition } from \"react\";\nimport {\n  recordAttempt,\n  completeLesson,\n  markLessonAttempt,\n} from \"./actions\";\nimport {\n  AudioPickLetterRenderer,\n  LetterPickAudioRenderer,\n  TypeRomanizationRenderer,\n  MatchPairsRenderer,\n  TapInOrderRenderer,\n} from \"./exercises\";\nimport type { Exercise, PathLesson } from \"@/lib/course/types\";\n\ntype Phase =\n  | { kind: \"teach\" }\n  | { kind: \"exercise\"; index: number }\n  | { kind: \"feedback\"; index: number; wasCorrect: boolean; exercise: Exercise }\n  | { kind: \"failed\" }\n  | { kind: \"completed\" };\n\ninterface QueueState {\n  queue: Exercise[];                       // ordered remaining exercises\n  wrongCounts: Record<string, number>;     // exerciseId → times wrong\n}\n\nfunction dispatchRenderer(\n  exercise: Exercise,\n  onSubmit: (wasCorrect: boolean) => void,\n) {\n  switch (exercise.kind) {\n    case \"audio-pick-letter\":\n      return <AudioPickLetterRenderer exercise={exercise} onSubmit={onSubmit} />;\n    case \"letter-pick-audio\":\n      return <LetterPickAudioRenderer exercise={exercise} onSubmit={onSubmit} />;\n    case \"type-romanization\":\n      return <TypeRomanizationRenderer exercise={exercise} onSubmit={onSubmit} />;\n    case \"match-pairs\":\n      return <MatchPairsRenderer exercise={exercise} onSubmit={onSubmit} />;\n    case \"tap-in-order\":\n      return <TapInOrderRenderer exercise={exercise} onSubmit={onSubmit} />;\n  }\n}\n\nexport default function LessonRunner({\n  lesson,\n  teachContent,\n}: {\n  lesson: PathLesson;\n  teachContent: React.ReactNode | null;   // null for \"check\" lessons\n}) {\n  const router = useRouter();\n  const [, startTransition] = useTransition();\n\n  // Phase: where in the lifecycle we are.\n  const initialPhase: Phase =\n    teachContent === null || lesson.kind === \"check\"\n      ? { kind: \"exercise\", index: 0 }\n      : { kind: \"teach\" };\n  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<Phase>(initialPhase);\n\n  // The mutable queue + per-exercise wrong-counts. Persist across phase\n  // transitions; reset on a \"Try again\" after fail.\n  const [state, setState] = useState<QueueState>({\n    queue: lesson.exercises,\n    wrongCounts: {},\n  });\n\n  // ---- transitions --------------------------------------------------\n\n  function startExercises() {\n    setPhase({ kind: \"exercise\", index: 0 });\n  }\n\n  function handleSubmit(wasCorrect: boolean) {\n    if (phase.kind !== \"exercise\") return;\n    const exercise = state.queue[phase.index];\n\n    // Fire-and-forget the attempt log; failures here shouldn't block\n    // the user's flow.\n    startTransition(() => {\n      void recordAttempt(lesson.id, exercise.id, wasCorrect);\n    });\n\n    setPhase({ kind: \"feedback\", index: phase.index, wasCorrect, exercise });\n\n    if (!wasCorrect) {\n      // Bump the wrong-count for this exercise.\n      setState((cur) => ({\n        ...cur,\n        wrongCounts: {\n          ...cur.wrongCounts,\n          [exercise.id]: (cur.wrongCounts[exercise.id] ?? 0) + 1,\n        },\n      }));\n    }\n  }\n\n  function handleContinue() {\n    if (phase.kind !== \"feedback\") return;\n    const exercise = phase.exercise;\n\n    if (phase.wasCorrect) {\n      // Advance, or finish.\n      const nextIndex = phase.index + 1;\n      if (nextIndex >= state.queue.length) {\n        // Done — mark completed server-side, navigate back to /course.\n        setPhase({ kind: \"completed\" });\n        startTransition(() => {\n          void completeLesson(lesson.id).then(() => {\n            router.refresh();\n          });\n        });\n        return;\n      }\n      setPhase({ kind: \"exercise\", index: nextIndex });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Wrong: did they exceed two strikes on this exercise?\n    const wrongs = state.wrongCounts[exercise.id] ?? 0;\n    if (wrongs >= 2) {\n      setPhase({ kind: \"failed\" });\n      startTransition(() => {\n        void markLessonAttempt(lesson.id);\n      });\n      return;\n    }\n    // Re-enqueue at end + advance pointer.\n    setState((cur) => ({\n      ...cur,\n      queue: [...cur.queue, exercise],\n    }));\n    setPhase({ kind: \"exercise\", index: phase.index + 1 });\n  }\n\n  function handleRetry() {\n    setState({ queue: lesson.exercises, wrongCounts: {} });\n    setPhase(\n      teachContent === null || lesson.kind === \"check\"\n        ? { kind: \"exercise\", index: 0 }\n        : { kind: \"teach\" },\n    );\n  }\n\n  // ---- progress meter at the top ------------------------------------\n  // Counts the user's \"true\" progress = original-queue exercises that\n  // have moved past, not counting reattempts. Stable visual signal.\n\n  const originalIds = new Set(lesson.exercises.map((e) => e.id));\n  const completedOriginal =\n    phase.kind === \"exercise\"\n      ? state.queue.slice(0, phase.index).filter((e) => originalIds.has(e.id)).length\n      : phase.kind === \"feedback\"\n        ? state.queue.slice(0, phase.index).filter((e) => originalIds.has(e.id)).length\n        : phase.kind === \"completed\"\n          ? lesson.exercises.length\n          : 0;\n  const meter = (completedOriginal / lesson.exercises.length) * 100;\n\n  // ---- rendering ----------------------------------------------------\n\n  return (\n    <main className=\"mx-auto max-w-2xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6\">\n      <header className=\"mb-6 flex items-center gap-3\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => router.push(\"/course\")}\n          className=\"text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-700 dark:hover:text-zinc-200\"\n          aria-label=\"Back to path\"\n        >\n          ✕\n        </button>\n        <div className=\"flex-1\">\n          <div className=\"h-2 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-800\">\n            <div\n              className=\"h-full bg-emerald-500 transition-all\"\n              style={{ width: `${meter}%` }}\n            />\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </header>\n\n      {phase.kind === \"teach\" && (\n        <TeachScreen\n          lesson={lesson}\n          teachContent={teachContent}\n          onReady={startExercises}\n        />\n      )}\n\n      {phase.kind === \"exercise\" && (\n        <div className=\"py-4\">\n          {dispatchRenderer(state.queue[phase.index], handleSubmit)}\n        </div>\n      )}\n\n      {phase.kind === \"feedback\" && (\n        <FeedbackScreen\n          wasCorrect={phase.wasCorrect}\n          onContinue={handleContinue}\n        />\n      )}\n\n      {phase.kind === \"failed\" && <FailedScreen onRetry={handleRetry} />}\n\n      {phase.kind === \"completed\" && <CompletedScreen lessonTitle={lesson.title} />}\n    </main>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction TeachScreen({\n  lesson,\n  teachContent,\n  onReady,\n}: {\n  lesson: PathLesson;\n  teachContent: React.ReactNode | null;\n  onReady: () => void;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-6 py-6\">\n      <h1 className=\"text-center font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n        {lesson.title}\n      </h1>\n      <div className=\"rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 bg-white p-6 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\">\n        {teachContent ?? (\n          <p className=\"text-sm text-zinc-500\">No teach content available.</p>\n        )}\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"flex justify-center\">\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={onReady}\n          className=\"rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-6 py-3 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n        >\n          I&apos;m ready — start exercises →\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction FeedbackScreen({\n  wasCorrect,\n  onContinue,\n}: {\n  wasCorrect: boolean;\n  onContinue: () => void;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <div\n      className={`mt-6 rounded-xl p-6 ${\n        wasCorrect\n          ? \"border border-emerald-300 bg-emerald-50 dark:border-emerald-900 dark:bg-emerald-950\"\n          : \"border border-red-300 bg-red-50 dark:border-red-900 dark:bg-red-950\"\n      }`}\n    >\n      <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between gap-4\">\n        <p\n          className={`text-base font-medium ${\n            wasCorrect\n              ? \"text-emerald-900 dark:text-emerald-200\"\n              : \"text-red-900 dark:text-red-200\"\n          }`}\n        >\n          {wasCorrect ? \"Correct\" : \"Not quite — we'll bring this one back.\"}\n        </p>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={onContinue}\n          autoFocus\n          className={`rounded-lg px-4 py-2 font-medium ${\n            wasCorrect\n              ? \"bg-emerald-600 text-white hover:bg-emerald-700\"\n              : \"bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700\"\n          }`}\n        >\n          Continue →\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction FailedScreen({ onRetry }: { onRetry: () => void }) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mt-12 space-y-4 text-center\">\n      <h2 className=\"font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n        Not yet.\n      </h2>\n      <p className=\"mx-auto max-w-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n        That one tripped you up. No big deal — start the lesson again and the\n        repetition will lock it in.\n      </p>\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        onClick={onRetry}\n        className=\"rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-6 py-3 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n      >\n        Try again\n      </button>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction CompletedScreen({ lessonTitle }: { lessonTitle: string }) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mt-12 space-y-4 text-center\">\n      <div className=\"text-6xl\" aria-hidden>✓</div>\n      <h2 className=\"font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n        {lessonTitle}\n      </h2>\n      <p className=\"mx-auto max-w-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n        Locked in. The next lesson is waiting on your path.\n      </p>\n      <a\n        href=\"/course\"\n        className=\"inline-block rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-6 py-3 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200\"\n      >\n        Back to path →\n      </a>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

For letter lessons we look up the matching\n  // entry in the existing CURRICULUM by character. Both calls are right — and the cumulative-review one especially is what makes Duolingo actually stick. Let me restructure the §1 exercises:

**Drops:**
- Type-romanization exercise from letter lessons (you're right — it tests transcription, not letter knowledge)

**Adds:**
- Cumulative review inside each lesson. Each new-letter lesson tests the new letter + spaced-review on every previous letter in the section.

**New per-lesson mix** (§1):

| Lesson | New letter | Review of | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 ੳ | 5 on ੳ | — | 5 |
| L2 ਅ | 4 on ਅ | 1 on ੳ | 5 |
| L3 ੲ | 4 on ੲ | 1 ੳ + 1 ਅ | 6 |
| L4 ਸ | 4 on ਸ | 1 each (3 letters) | 7 |
| L5 ਹ | 4 on ਹ | 1 each (4 letters) | 8 |
