  "new_string": "// The five letters of Line 1. Used in both individual letter lessons\n// and the Line-1 check, so kept as a constant.\nconst LINE_1_LETTERS = [\"ੳ\", \"ਅ\", \"ੲ\", \"ਸ\", \"ਹ\"] as const;\n\n// Distractor pool for Line-1 exercises — letters from other lines that\n// learners might confuse with the Line-1 letters. Chosen for visual or\n// phonetic similarity to keep the multiple-choice meaningful.\nconst LINE_1_DISTRACTORS = [\"ਕ\", \"ਖ\", \"ਚ\", \"ਟ\", \"ਪ\", \"ਮ\", \"ਨ\"];\n\n// Helper: 4-option multiple choice with the correct letter + 3 distractors.\nfunction fourOptions(correct: string, others: string[]): string[] {\n  const pool = others.filter((l) => l !== correct);\n  // Pick 3 distractors deterministically; runtime shuffles the order so\n  // the correct option isn't always at index 0.\n  return [correct, pool[0], pool[1], pool[2]];\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the exercises for a single letter lesson with cumulative review.\n *\n * Pedagogy: every lesson focuses on ONE new letter (the \"starring\" letter)\n * but also briefly tests every previously-learned letter in the section.\n * That way a learner sees each letter in multiple lessons, not just the\n * one where it was introduced — spaced reinforcement happens naturally\n * inside the path rather than only at the end-of-section check.\n *\n * Mix:\n *   - newLetter: 4 exercises (or 5 if no review letters yet) — 2-3 audio-\n *     pick + 2 letter-pick, alternating\n *   - each previousLetter: 1 review exercise, alternating between\n *     audio-pick and letter-pick across the lesson\n *\n * Distractors come from the union of (other Line-1 letters) + (the\n * stock distractor pool) so options can include both familiar-but-\n * different and never-seen letters.\n */\nfunction letterLessonExercises(\n  newLetter: string,\n  previousLetters: readonly string[],\n): Exercise[] {\n  const distractorPool = [\n    ...LINE_1_LETTERS.filter((l) => l !== newLetter),\n    ...LINE_1_DISTRACTORS,\n  ];\n\n  const newLetterCount = previousLetters.length === 0 ? 5 : 4;\n  const out: Exercise[] = [];\n\n  // Starring exercises — focused practice on the new letter.\n  for (let i = 0; i < newLetterCount; i++) {\n    const useAudio = i % 2 === 0; // alternate kinds\n    out.push(\n      useAudio\n        ? {\n            id: `${newLetter}-new-audio-${i}`,\n            kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n            audioForLetter: newLetter,\n            options: fourOptions(newLetter, distractorPool),\n          }\n        : {\n            id: `${newLetter}-new-visual-${i}`,\n            kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n            displayLetter: newLetter,\n            audioOptions: fourOptions(newLetter, distractorPool),\n          },\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Review exercises — one per previously-learned letter, kinds\n  // alternating across the lesson.\n  previousLetters.forEach((prevLetter, i) => {\n    const useAudio = i % 2 === 0;\n    // Distractors for a review letter include the new letter (so the\n    // user has to discriminate the just-learned one from the older\n    // one) plus other letters.\n    const reviewDistractors = [\n      newLetter,\n      ...distractorPool.filter((l) => l !== prevLetter),\n    ];\n    out.push(\n      useAudio\n        ? {\n            id: `${prevLetter}-review-audio-${newLetter}`,\n            kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n            audioForLetter: prevLetter,\n            options: fourOptions(prevLetter, reviewDistractors),\n          }\n        : {\n            id: `${prevLetter}-review-visual-${newLetter}`,\n            kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n            displayLetter: prevLetter,\n            audioOptions: fourOptions(prevLetter, reviewDistractors),\n          },\n    );\n  });\n\n  return out;\n}"
}

A couple of things I deliberately *didn't* do that you might want later, just to flag:

2. **Animation on the exercise itself when frozen.** Right now it just dims to 70% opacity. A subtle scale or tilt might feel more "this is your answer, locked in." Cosmetic.

  "old_string": "  // ---- progress meter at the top ------------------------------------\n  // Counts the user's \"true\" progress = original-queue exercises that\n  // have moved past, not counting reattempts. Stable visual signal.\n\n  const originalIds = new Set(lesson.exercises.map((e) => e.id));\n  const completedOriginal =\n    phase.kind === \"exercise\"\n      ? state.queue.slice(0, phase.index).filter((e) => originalIds.has(e.id)).length\n      : phase.kind === \"feedback\"\n        ? state.queue.slice(0, phase.index).filter((e) => originalIds.has(e.id)).length\n        : phase.kind === \"completed\"\n          ? lesson.exercises.length\n          : 0;\n  const meter = (completedOriginal / lesson.exercises.length) * 100;",
  "new_string": "  // ---- progress meter at the top ------------------------------------\n  // Two halves: the bottom 80% fills as the user moves through the\n  // main pass; the top 20% fills during the review pass. Keeps the\n  // user oriented to which pass they're in without a separate label.\n  const originalIds = new Set(lesson.exercises.map((e) => e.id));\n  const mainProgress = (() => {\n    if (phase.kind === \"main-exercise\" || phase.kind === \"main-feedback\") {\n      return state.queue.slice(0, phase.index).filter((e) => originalIds.has(e.id)).length / lesson.exercises.length;\n    }\n    if (phase.kind === \"review-exercise\" || phase.kind === \"review-feedback\" || phase.kind === \"completed\") {\n      return 1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n  })();\n  const reviewProgress = (() => {\n    if (state.reviewQueue.length === 0) return phase.kind === \"completed\" ? 1 : 0;\n    if (phase.kind === \"review-exercise\" || phase.kind === \"review-feedback\") {\n      return Math.min(1, phase.index / state.reviewQueue.length);\n    }\n    if (phase.kind === \"completed\") return 1;\n    return 0;\n  })();\n  // 80% of bar is main pass, 20% is review pass — visually weighted to\n  // match where most of the work is.\n  const meter = mainProgress * 80 + reviewProgress * 20;"

> DEVELOPER

The correct or incorrect sounds plays multiople times and sometomes the sound plays on its own as well

> AGENT

Two real bugs — let me fix both:

**1. Multiple sound plays**: my FeedbackPanel useEffect depended on `onContinue` which is recreated on every parent render. Each new closure re-triggered the effect → new audio.

**2. Sound plays on its own**: the AudioPickLetter renderer has `autoPlay` on its letter audio. When phase switches `exercise` → `feedback`, the JSX branch changes, the renderer *remounts*, and autoPlay fires again — so you hear the letter, then the feedback sound, sometimes overlapping.

Fixing both:

> TOOL

id: toolu_011kFKA1WUgUyHdRyWoy2Mh3
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/course/[lessonId]/LessonRunner.tsx",
  "old_string": "  useEffect(() => {\n    // Play the right cue. Files live in /public/sounds/ — drop-in\n    // replacements work without any code change.\n    const src = wasCorrect ? \"/sounds/correct.mp3\" : \"/sounds/incorrect.mp3\";\n    const audio = new Audio(src);\n    audio.volume = 0.6;\n    audio.play().catch(() => {\n      // Browsers can block autoplay without a recent user gesture. The\n      // user just clicked an answer, so this should almost never fire,\n      // but if it does we silently skip rather than throwing.\n    });\n\n    const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {\n      if (e.key === \"Enter\") {\n        e.preventDefault();\n        onContinue();\n      }\n    };\n    document.addEventListener(\"keydown\", handler);\n    return () => document.removeEventListener(\"keydown\", handler);\n  }, [onContinue, wasCorrect]);",
  "new_string": "  // Audio plays once per panel-mount/wasCorrect change. Deliberately\n  // does NOT depend on onContinue — onContinue is a fresh closure\n  // every parent render, which used to retrigger this effect and stack\n  // duplicate audio.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const src = wasCorrect ? \"/sounds/correct.mp3\" : \"/sounds/incorrect.mp3\";\n    const audio = new Audio(src);\n    audio.volume = 0.6;\n    audio.play().catch(() => {\n      // Browsers can block autoplay without a recent user gesture. The\n      // user just clicked an answer, so this should almost never fire,\n      // but if it does we silently skip rather than throwing.\n    });\n  }, [wasCorrect]);\n\n  // Keyboard handler can rebind freely when onContinue changes without\n  // affecting the audio above.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {\n      if (e.key === \"Enter\") {\n        e.preventDefault();\n        onContinue();\n      }\n    };\n    document.addEventListener(\"keydown\", handler);\n    return () => document.removeEventListener(\"keydown\", handler);\n  }, [onContinue]);"
}

Pushed — preview rebuilds in ~1 min. What changes:

- **No more "Try again" screen** — wrong answers just keep cycling in the main pass. Same question wrong 5 times? It just keeps coming back at the end of the queue. No punishment.
- **Review pass kicks in cleanly** after the main pass completes — replays only the questions you were wrong on at least once, with the amber "↻ One more pass" banner
- **You can still bail** via the X in the header if you really want out — that just drops you back at /course with no progress recorded

Try the lesson where you got 2 questions wrong again — should now keep cycling them in the main pass, then naturally land you in the review pass at the end.

Ready to move on to Week 2 content authoring? §2-§7 = 30 more letters with cumulative review + 6 line-checks. The mechanic's solid; from here it's mostly extending the catalog.

End-of-line check: 2 exercises per letter (audio + visual) +\n * 1 match-pairs over the first 4 letters. ~11 total.\n */\nfunction lineCheckExercises(\n  letters: LineLetter[],\n  distractorPool: string[],\n  lineNum: number,\n): Exercise[] {\n  const out: Exercise[] = [];\n  for (const letter of letters) {\n    const audioId = `check${lineNum}-${letter.char}-a`;\n    const visualId = `check${lineNum}-${letter.char}-v`;\n    out.push({\n      id: audioId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n      audioForLetter: letter.char,\n      options: fourOptions(letter.char, distractorPool, audioId),\n    });\n    out.push({\n      id: visualId,\n      kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n      displayLetter: letter.char,\n      audioOptions: fourOptions(letter.char, distractorPool, visualId),\n    });\n  }\n  out.push({\n    id: `check${lineNum}-match`,\n    kind: \"match-pairs\",\n    pairs: letters.slice(0, 4).map((l) => ({ letter: l.char, iso: l.iso })),\n  });\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Generate every PathLesson entry for the 7 letter lines from LINES_DATA.\n * Lesson IDs come from the data table → stable across regenerations →\n * users' progress rows stay valid.\n */\nfunction buildLetterLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {\n  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};\n  for (const line of LINES_DATA) {\n    const lineLetters = line.letters.map((l) => l.char);\n    const distractorPool = ALL_PAINTI_LETTERS.filter(\n      (l) => !lineLetters.includes(l),\n    );\n\n    line.letters.forEach((letter, i) => {\n      const previousInLine = line.letters.slice(0, i).map((l) => l.char);\n      out[letter.slug] = {\n        id: letter.slug,\n        sectionId: line.sectionId,\n        kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n        title: letter.title,\n        curriculumRef: `letter-${letter.char}`,\n        exercises: letterLessonExercises(letter.char, previousInLine, distractorPool),\n      };\n    });\n\n    const checkId = `check-line-${line.lineNum}`;\n    out[checkId] = {\n      id: checkId,\n      sectionId: line.sectionId,\n      kind: \"check\",\n      title: `Line ${line.lineNum} check`,\n      exercises: lineCheckExercises(line.letters, distractorPool, line.lineNum),\n    };\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = buildLetterLessons();"
}

Self-contained so the reference page doesn't pull in\n// the course-runner's AudioButton (different sizing/affordance needs).\n\nimport { useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\nexport default function AudioPlayButton({\n  word,\n  label,\n}: {\n  word: string;\n  label?: string;\n}) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\"idle\" | \"loading\" | \"playing\">(\"idle\");\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`;\n\n  function play() {\n    if (audioRef.current) {\n      audioRef.current.pause();\n      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;\n    }\n    setState(\"loading\");\n    const audio = new Audio(url);\n    audioRef.current = audio;\n    audio.onplaying = () => setState(\"playing\");\n    audio.onended = () => setState(\"idle\");\n    audio.onerror = () => setState(\"idle\");\n    audio.play().catch(() => setState(\"idle\"));\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={play}\n      disabled={state === \"loading\"}\n      aria-label={label ?? `Play ${word}`}\n      className=\"flex h-10 w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-zinc-100 text-base text-zinc-700 transition hover:bg-zinc-200 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-200 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700\"\n    >\n      {state === \"playing\" ? \"🔉\" : state === \"loading\" ? \"⋯\" : \"🔊\"}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n"
}

The\n          name shown is what the audio pronounces.\n        </p>\n      </header>\n\n      <div className=\"space-y-10\">\n        {LINES_DATA.map((line) => {\n          const section = PATH_SECTIONS.find((s) => s.id === line.sectionId);\n          return (\n            <section key={line.sectionId}>\n              <div className=\"mb-4 flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3\">\n                <h2 className=\"font-serif text-xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n                  Line {line.lineNum}\n                </h2>\n                <span className=\"text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n                  {section?.description}\n                </span>\n              </div>\n              <div className=\"grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-5\">\n                {line.letters.map((letter) => {\n                  const info = lookupLetter(letter.char);\n                  return (\n                    <LetterCard\n                      key={letter.char}\n                      char={letter.char}\n                      namePa={info?.name_pa ?? letter.char}\n                      nameIso={info?.name_iso ?? letter.iso}\n                      ipa={info?.ipa}\n                    />\n                  );\n                })}\n              </div>\n            </section>\n          );\n        })}\n      </div>\n\n      <footer className=\"mt-12 border-t border-zinc-200 pt-6 text-xs text-zinc-500 dark:border-zinc-800\">\n        <p>\n          Audio plays via the same caching pipeline the course uses. If a\n          letter sounds off, the fix is in the TTS prompt (the name shown\n          on each card) — the file is regenerated on next request.\n        </p>\n      </footer>\n    </main>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction LetterCard({\n  char,\n  namePa,\n  nameIso,\n  ipa,\n}: {\n  char: string;\n  namePa: string;\n  nameIso: string;\n  ipa?: string;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"flex items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 bg-white p-4 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\">\n      <div className=\"flex-1 text-center\">\n        <div className=\"font-serif text-5xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          {char}\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"mt-2 font-serif text-base text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n          {namePa}\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"mt-0.5 font-mono text-xs text-zinc-500\">\n          {nameIso}\n        </div>\n        {ipa && ipa !== \"(vowel base)\" && (\n          <div className=\"mt-1 font-mono text-xs text-zinc-400\">{ipa}</div>\n        )}\n      </div>\n      <AudioPlayButton word={namePa} label={`Play ${namePa}`} />\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

1. **The name itself is unusual or rare** (e.g. ਟੈਂਕਾ for ਟ uses an English-influenced spelling that Chirp may stumble on)

- Edit the `name_pa` in `data/curriculum.ts` for that letter (change spelling so Chirp pronounces it correctly)

Either way: change the prompt → next request regenerates + caches in R2 → both the course and the reference page pick it up immediately, no code redeploy needed for individual letters.

app/api/tts/route.ts

import { getCachedAudio } from "@/lib/audio-cache";
import { VOICE_NAME } from "@/lib/google-tts";

export const runtime = "nodejs";

// Cache-only TTS route.
//
// Audio is generated server-side ahead of time by scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts.
// This route does NOT synthesize on demand — that decision avoids surprise
// GCP bills from bots and keeps hover latency predictable. On a cache miss
// the route returns 404 and the UI hides the play button gracefully.
export async function GET(request: Request) {
  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
  const word = searchParams.get("word");
  if (!word) {
    return Response.json({ error: "missing 'word' query param" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  const cached = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, word);
  if (!cached) {
    return Response.json({ error: "no cached audio" }, { status: 404 });
  }
  return new Response(new Uint8Array(cached.buffer), {
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "audio/mpeg",
      "Content-Length": String(cached.bytes),
      "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
    },
  });
}
```

Found it — `/api/tts` is *cache-only* by design (the original comment explains: "avoids surprise GCP bills from bots"). My changed letter names have no cached audio in R2 yet, so they 404.

Best fix: make the route fall through to on-demand synthesis when the caller is authenticated (your signed-in session = safe, bots can't burn through credit). Cache the result so it's only generated once.

1	// Small helper to look up letter metadata (name in Punjabi for TTS, ISO
2	// romanization for display) from our existing CURRICULUM data without
3	// duplicating it into the v1.1 catalog. The v1.1 catalog only knows
4	// which letter character each exercise is about; this resolves the
5	// details when the exercise renders.
6	
7	import { CURRICULUM } from "@/data/curriculum";
8	import type { LetterLesson } from "@/data/curriculum";
9	
10	interface LetterInfo {
11	  char: string;
12	  name_pa: string;        // Punjabi name, e.g. "ਸੱਸਾ" — used for TTS audio
13	  name_iso: string;       // romanized name, e.g. "sassā"
14	  ipa: string;            // phonetic value, e.g. "sə"
15	}
16	
17	// Build a lookup index once at module load.
18	const INDEX: Record<string, LetterInfo> = (() => {
19	  const out: Record<string, LetterInfo> = {};
20	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
21	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
22	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
23	      out[l.char] = {
24	        char: l.char,
25	        name_pa: l.name_pa,
26	        name_iso: l.name_iso,
27	        ipa: l.ipa,
28	      };
29	    }
30	  }
31	  return out;
32	})();
33	
34	/**
35	 * Look up a letter's metadata by its Gurmukhi character. Returns null
36	 * if the character isn't in the curriculum yet (caller should treat as
37	 * a graceful skip rather than crash).
38	 */
39	export function lookupLetter(char: string): LetterInfo | null {
40	  return INDEX[char] ?? null;
41	}
42

Returns null\n * if the character isn't in the curriculum yet (caller should treat as\n * a graceful skip rather than crash).\n */\nexport function lookupLetter(char: string): LetterInfo | null {\n  return INDEX[char] ?? null;\n}",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Look up a letter's metadata by its Gurmukhi character. Returns null\n * if the character isn't in the curriculum yet (caller should treat as\n * a graceful skip rather than crash).\n */\nexport function lookupLetter(char: string): LetterInfo | null {\n  return INDEX[char] ?? null;\n}\n\n// TTS prompt overrides per letter. The canonical letter-name (name_pa\n// in CURRICULUM) is what's shown to the user; this map decides what's\n// actually *sent* to /api/tts for audio playback. Use only when Chirp's\n// pronunciation of the canonical name is poor enough to mislead a\n// learner. Visible label stays canonical; audio is whatever sounds right.\n//\n// Every entry here MUST have its prewarmed MP3 in R2 — run\n// `tsx scripts/prewarm-words.ts <override-value>` after adding/changing\n// an entry, since /api/tts is cache-only.\nconst AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES: Record<string, string> = {\n  // Chirp 3 mangles the geminate retroflex flap (ੜਾੜਾ). Space-separating\n  // the two syllables makes it pronounce two distinct flaps cleanly.\n  \"ੜ\": \"ੜਾ ੜਾ\",\n};\n\n/**\n * What to send to /api/tts when playing the audio for a letter. Falls\n * back to the canonical name_pa, then to the character itself.\n */\nexport function audioWordForLetter(char: string): string {\n  if (char in AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES) return AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES[char];\n  return INDEX[char]?.name_pa ?? char;\n}"
}

## On the cross-line recaps — yes, this is the right call

Your instinct is exactly the spaced-repetition principle. Without it, by Line 7 the user has seen Line 1 letters maybe 6 times (across §1 + the §1 check), but nothing since. That's classic forgetting territory.

**Where the recap sits in the path:**

I'd append it to the section that just finished, as the last tile before moving on. So §2 becomes: 5 letter lessons → §2 check → §1+§2 recap → unlocks §3.

That way the user sees a clear pattern: *finish a line → check that line → recap everything → move on*.

**Question I want your gut on before building:**

A recap that includes *every* prior letter grows: 10 exercises after §2, 15 after §3, ... 30 after §7. That's a real "you sit down for 10 minutes" lesson by the end. Two ways to handle:

- **A) Full cumulative.** Every prior letter, 1 exercise each. Comprehensive — the user is genuinely re-touched on every letter. But late recaps are long.
- **B) Smart cumulative.** Cap each recap at ~12-15 exercises. Bias selection toward the *oldest* letters (highest forgetting risk) and the *current* line (freshest practice still needed). Same coverage philosophy, manageable length. This is what Duolingo's "personalized practice" does.

I lean (B) — pedagogically it's *better* than (A) because the longest review (post §7) covering 30 letters would have you doing each one only once anyway, which is barely better than nothing. Better to do 12 well-chosen ones with focus on the at-risk ones.

Either way, the implementation is similar — just the exercise-picking logic differs. Which feels right?

Generate every PathLesson entry for the 7 letter lines from LINES_DATA.\n * Lesson IDs come from the data table → stable across regenerations →\n * users' progress rows stay valid.\n */\nfunction buildLetterLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {\n  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};\n  for (const line of LINES_DATA) {\n    const lineLetters = line.letters.map((l) => l.char);\n    const distractorPool = ALL_PAINTI_LETTERS.filter(\n      (l) => !lineLetters.includes(l),\n    );\n\n    line.letters.forEach((letter, i) => {\n      const previousInLine = line.letters.slice(0, i).map((l) => l.char);\n      out[letter.slug] = {\n        id: letter.slug,\n        sectionId: line.sectionId,\n        kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n        title: letter.title,\n        curriculumRef: `letter-${letter.char}`,\n        exercises: letterLessonExercises(letter.char, previousInLine, distractorPool),\n      };\n    });\n\n    const checkId = `check-line-${line.lineNum}`;\n    out[checkId] = {\n      id: checkId,\n      sectionId: line.sectionId,\n      kind: \"check\",\n      title: `Line ${line.lineNum} check`,\n      exercises: lineCheckExercises(line.letters, distractorPool, line.lineNum),\n    };\n\n    // Recap after §2-§7 (no recap after §1 — line check already covers it).\n    if (line.lineNum >= 2) {\n      const recapId = `recap-line-${line.lineNum}`;\n      out[recapId] = {\n        id: recapId,\n        sectionId: line.sectionId,\n        kind: \"check\",\n        title:\n          line.lineNum === 2\n            ? \"Recap — Lines 1 & 2\"\n            : `Recap — Lines 1-${line.lineNum}`,\n        exercises: recapExercises(line.lineNum),\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = buildLetterLessons();"
}

resolve(parseFloat(out.trim())) : reject(new Error(`ffprobe exit ${code}`)));\n  });\n}\n\nasync function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number) {\n  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n    const proc = spawn(\"ffmpeg\", [\n      \"-y\",\n      \"-i\", inFile,\n      \"-ss\", String(startSec),\n      \"-af\", \"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025\", // 25ms fade in so the cut doesn't pop\n      \"-acodec\", \"libmp3lame\",\n      \"-q:a\", \"5\",\n      outFile,\n    ]);\n    let stderr = \"\";\n    proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n    proc.on(\"close\", (code) =>\n      code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exit ${code}\\n${stderr.slice(-400)}`)),\n    );\n  });\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  console.log(`Synthesizing: \"${sourceWord}\"`);\n  const sourceMp3 = await synthesize(sourceWord);\n  console.log(`  source: ${sourceMp3.length}B`);\n\n  const inFile = \"/tmp/akhar-trim-in.mp3\";\n  const outFile = \"/tmp/akhar-trim-out.mp3\";\n  writeFileSync(inFile, sourceMp3);\n\n  const sourceDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(inFile);\n  console.log(`  duration: ${sourceDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);\n  if (trimStart >= sourceDuration) {\n    console.error(`trim-start ${trimStart}s >= source duration ${sourceDuration}s`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  console.log(`Trimming first ${trimStart}s …`);\n  await ffmpegTrim(inFile, outFile, trimStart);\n  const trimmed = readFileSync(outFile);\n  const trimmedDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(outFile);\n  console.log(`  trimmed: ${trimmed.length}B, ${trimmedDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);\n\n  await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, targetKey, trimmed);\n  console.log(`✅ Uploaded as cache key: \"${targetKey}\"`);\n\n  unlinkSync(inFile);\n  unlinkSync(outFile);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\nEOF\n\n# First attempt: synthesize ਨਾੜਾੜਾ, trim 0.3s of leading \"ਨਾ\", upload as \"ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed\"\nnpx tsx scripts/trim-audio.ts \"ਨਾੜਾੜਾ\" \"ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed\" 0.3 2>&1",

1	// Synthesize a "leading word + target syllables" string, then trim the
2	// leading part to extract just the syllables we care about. Useful for
3	// letters/sounds that Chirp can only pronounce correctly in word-medial
4	// position (e.g. ੜ — no real Punjabi word starts with it).
5	//
6	// Usage:
7	//   tsx scripts/trim-audio.ts <source-word> <target-cache-key> <trim-start-sec>
8	//
9	// Writes the trimmed MP3 to R2 under <target-cache-key> so /api/tts
10	// can serve it (the cache-only route looks up by exact key).
11	import path from "node:path";
12	import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
13	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, unlinkSync } from "node:fs";
14	
15	const env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), ".env.local"), "utf8");
16	for (const line of env.split("\n")) {
17	  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);
18	  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];
19	}
20	
21	import { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from "@/lib/google-tts";
22	import { putCachedAudio } from "@/lib/audio-cache";
23	
24	const args = process.argv.slice(2);
25	if (args.length !== 3) {
26	  console.error("usage: tsx scripts/trim-audio.ts <source-word> <target-key> <trim-start-sec>");
27	  process.exit(1);
28	}
29	const [sourceWord, targetKey, trimStartStr] = args;
30	const trimStart = parseFloat(trimStartStr);
31	
32	async function ffmpegProbeDuration(file: string): Promise<number> {
33	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
34	    const p = spawn("ffprobe", [
35	      "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
36	      "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", file,
37	    ]);
38	    let out = "";
39	    p.stdout.on("data", (d) => (out += d.toString()));
40	    p.on("close", (code) => code === 0 ? resolve(parseFloat(out.trim())) : reject(new Error(`ffprobe exit ${code}`)));
41	  });
42	}
43	
44	async function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number) {
45	  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
46	    const proc = spawn("ffmpeg", [
47	      "-y",
48	      "-i", inFile,
49	      "-ss", String(startSec),
50	      "-af", "afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025", // 25ms fade in so the cut doesn't pop
51	      "-acodec", "libmp3lame",
52	      "-q:a", "5",
53	      outFile,
54	    ]);
55	    let stderr = "";
56	    proc.stderr.on("data", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));
57	    proc.on("close", (code) =>
58	      code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exit ${code}\n${stderr.slice(-400)}`)),
59	    );
60	  });
61	}
62	
63	async function main() {
64	  console.log(`Synthesizing: "${sourceWord}"`);
65	  const sourceMp3 = await synthesize(sourceWord);
66	  console.log(`  source: ${sourceMp3.length}B`);
67	
68	  const inFile = "/tmp/akhar-trim-in.mp3";
69	  const outFile = "/tmp/akhar-trim-out.mp3";
70	  writeFileSync(inFile, sourceMp3);
71	
72	  const sourceDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(inFile);
73	  console.log(`  duration: ${sourceDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);
74	  if (trimStart >= sourceDuration) {
75	    console.error(`trim-start ${trimStart}s >= source duration ${sourceDuration}s`);
76	    process.exit(1);
77	  }
78	
79	  console.log(`Trimming first ${trimStart}s …`);
80	  await ffmpegTrim(inFile, outFile, trimStart);
81	  const trimmed = readFileSync(outFile);
82	  const trimmedDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(outFile);
83	  console.log(`  trimmed: ${trimmed.length}B, ${trimmedDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);
84	
85	  await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, targetKey, trimmed);
86	  console.log(`✅ Uploaded as cache key: "${targetKey}"`);
87	
88	  unlinkSync(inFile);
89	  unlinkSync(outFile);
90	}
91	
92	main().catch((e) => {
93	  console.error(e);
94	  process.exit(1);
95	});
96

Indexes both top-level\n// Painti letters and the 5 nukta letters (which live inside a single\n// NUKTA_GROUP entry in CURRICULUM, not as their own top-level lessons).\nconst INDEX: Record<string, LetterInfo> = (() => {\n  const out: Record<string, LetterInfo> = {};\n  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {\n    if (lesson.kind === \"letter\") {\n      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;\n      out[l.char] = {\n        char: l.char,\n        name_pa: l.name_pa,\n        name_iso: l.name_iso,\n        ipa: l.ipa,\n      };\n    } else if (lesson.kind === \"nukta-group\") {\n      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {\n        out[nl.char] = {\n          char: nl.char,\n          name_pa: nl.name_pa,\n          name_iso: nl.name_iso,\n          ipa: nl.ipa,\n        };\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n})();"

1	// /course/[lessonId] — single-lesson runner.
2	//
3	// Server Component does the access checks (auth + can-access-this-lesson),
4	// resolves the teach content from data/curriculum.ts via the lesson's
5	// curriculumRef, and renders the LessonRunner (a Client Component) with
6	// everything pre-resolved. The runner then drives the state machine.
7	
8	import { notFound, redirect } from "next/navigation";
9	import { serverClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
10	import { getLesson } from "@/data/curriculum-v1.1";
11	import { CURRICULUM, type LetterLesson } from "@/data/curriculum";
12	import {
13	  getUserProgress,
14	  canAccessLesson,
15	  isComingSoonLesson,
16	} from "@/lib/course/progress";
17	import LessonRunner from "./LessonRunner";
18	import { LetterTeachContent } from "./TeachContent";
19	
20	export default async function LessonPage({
21	  params,
22	}: {
23	  params: Promise<{ lessonId: string }>;
24	}) {
25	  const { lessonId } = await params;
26	
27	  // Coming-soon stubs land here too — show a friendly explainer instead
28	  // of 404, since the path UI already advertises these as "coming soon."
29	  if (isComingSoonLesson(lessonId)) {
30	    return <ComingSoonPage lessonId={lessonId} />;
31	  }
32	
33	  const lesson = getLesson(lessonId);
34	  if (!lesson) notFound();
35	
36	  const supabase = await serverClient();
37	  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
38	  if (!user) {
39	    redirect(`/login?next=${encodeURIComponent(`/course/${lessonId}`)}`);
40	  }
41	
42	  // Block deep-linking into a locked lesson — send them back to /course
43	  // where they can see what they need to complete to unlock this one.
44	  const progress = await getUserProgress(supabase);
45	  if (!canAccessLesson(progress, lessonId)) {
46	    redirect("/course");
47	  }
48	
49	  // Resolve teach content. For letter lessons we look up the matching
50	  // entry in the existing CURRICULUM by character. Other lesson kinds
51	  // (matras, mukta, conjuncts, checks) will need their own teach
52	  // content renderers — added as those sections come online.
53	  let teachContent: React.ReactNode | null = null;
54	  if (lesson.curriculumRef?.startsWith("letter-")) {
55	    const ch = lesson.curriculumRef.replace("letter-", "");
56	    const entry = CURRICULUM.find(
57	      (e) => e.kind === "letter" && (e as LetterLesson).char === ch,
58	    ) as LetterLesson | undefined;
59	    if (entry) teachContent = <LetterTeachContent letter={entry} />;
60	  }
61	
62	  return <LessonRunner lesson={lesson} teachContent={teachContent} />;
63	}
64	
65	function ComingSoonPage({ lessonId }: { lessonId: string }) {
66	  return (
67	    <main className="mx-auto max-w-md px-4 py-16 text-center sm:px-6">
68	      <div className="text-4xl text-zinc-300 dark:text-zinc-700" aria-hidden>…</div>
69	      <h1 className="mt-4 font-serif text-2xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">
70	        Coming soon
71	      </h1>
72	      <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400">
73	        This lesson ({lessonId}) is being written. The path shows you
74	        what&apos;s next on the way.
75	      </p>
76	      <a
77	        href="/course"
78	        className="mt-6 inline-block rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 px-5 py-3 font-medium text-white hover:bg-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-200"
79	      >
80	        ← Back to path
81	      </a>
82	    </main>
83	  );
84	}
85

  "new_string": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// §9 Mukta words — words built from consonants only, no matra signs.\n// First \"real reading\" after the letters: each consonant carries its\n// inherent /ə/ sound, so you can read these immediately.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ninterface MuktaWord {\n  word: string;     // Gurmukhi\n  meaning: string;  // short English gloss for word-pick-meaning options\n}\n\n// 4 lessons of 4 words each + a final check covering all 16. Words are\n// short common mukta vocabulary (1-3 letters, no matras). Distractors\n// drawn from the same 16-word pool so the multiple-choice options are\n// all real Punjabi words, not nonsense.\nconst MUKTA_LESSONS: { lessonNum: number; words: MuktaWord[] }[] = [\n  { lessonNum: 1, words: [\n    { word: \"ਘਰ\", meaning: \"house\" },\n    { word: \"ਮਨ\", meaning: \"mind\" },\n    { word: \"ਪਲ\", meaning: \"moment\" },\n    { word: \"ਫਲ\", meaning: \"fruit\" },\n  ]},\n  { lessonNum: 2, words: [\n    { word: \"ਜਲ\", meaning: \"water\" },\n    { word: \"ਨਰ\", meaning: \"male\" },\n    { word: \"ਥਲ\", meaning: \"land\" },\n    { word: \"ਬਲ\", meaning: \"strength\" },\n  ]},\n  { lessonNum: 3, words: [\n    { word: \"ਜਨਮ\", meaning: \"birth\" },\n    { word: \"ਕਮਲ\", meaning: \"lotus\" },\n    { word: \"ਨਮਕ\", meaning: \"salt\" },\n    { word: \"ਪਰਖ\", meaning: \"test\" },\n  ]},\n  { lessonNum: 4, words: [\n    { word: \"ਅਮਨ\", meaning: \"peace\" },\n    { word: \"ਸਮਝ\", meaning: \"understanding\" },\n    { word: \"ਖਬਰ\", meaning: \"news\" },\n    { word: \"ਪਰਬਤ\", meaning: \"mountain\" },\n  ]},\n];\n\nconst ALL_MUKTA_WORDS: MuktaWord[] = MUKTA_LESSONS.flatMap((l) => l.words);\n\n/**\n * Distractor selection: pick N other words/meanings from the full pool,\n * seed-shuffled by exercise id so different exercises get different\n * 3-distractor sets (rather than the same 3 every time).\n */\nfunction distractorsFromPool<T>(\n  correct: T,\n  pool: T[],\n  seed: string,\n  n: number,\n): T[] {\n  const others = pool.filter((x) => x !== correct);\n  let h = 2166136261;\n  for (let i = 0; i < seed.length; i++) {\n    h = ((h ^ seed.charCodeAt(i)) * 16777619) >>> 0;\n  }\n  const shuffled = [...others];\n  for (let i = shuffled.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {\n    h = (h * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0;\n    const j = h % (i + 1);\n    [shuffled[i], shuffled[j]] = [shuffled[j], shuffled[i]];\n  }\n  return shuffled.slice(0, n);\n}\n\n/**\n * One mukta-word lesson: 2 exercises per new word (word→meaning and\n * audio→word, alternating), plus 1 review per previous word (meaning→word).\n */\nfunction muktaLessonExercises(\n  newWords: MuktaWord[],\n  reviewWords: MuktaWord[],\n): Exercise[] {\n  const meaningPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.meaning);\n  const wordPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.word);\n  const out: Exercise[] = [];\n\n  newWords.forEach((w, i) => {\n    // Alternate which \"first\" exercise we use to vary the lesson flow.\n    const startWithAudio = i % 2 === 0;\n    const audioId = `mukta-${w.word}-audio`;\n    const meaningId = `mukta-${w.word}-meaning`;\n    const audioEx: Exercise = {\n      id: audioId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.word,\n      options: [w.word, ...distractorsFromPool(w.word, wordPool, audioId, 3)],\n    };\n    const meaningEx: Exercise = {\n      id: meaningId,\n      kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n      word: w.word,\n      correctMeaning: w.meaning,\n      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.meaning, meaningPool, meaningId, 3),\n    };\n    if (startWithAudio) out.push(audioEx, meaningEx);\n    else out.push(meaningEx, audioEx);\n  });\n\n  reviewWords.forEach((w) => {\n    const id = `mukta-${w.word}-review-mpw`;\n    out.push({\n      id,\n      kind: \"meaning-pick-word\",\n      meaning: w.meaning,\n      correctWord: w.word,\n      distractorWords: distractorsFromPool(w.word, wordPool, id, 3),\n    });\n  });\n\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Mukta check: 1 exercise per word across all 4 lessons, alternating\n * between word-pick-meaning and audio-pick-word so the user demonstrates\n * both visual and aural recognition of every mukta word. ~16 exercises.\n */\nfunction muktaCheckExercises(): Exercise[] {\n  const meaningPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.meaning);\n  const wordPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.word);\n  return ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w, i): Exercise => {\n    if (i % 2 === 0) {\n      const id = `check-mukta-${w.word}-wpm`;\n      return {\n        id,\n        kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n        word: w.word,\n        correctMeaning: w.meaning,\n        distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.meaning, meaningPool, id, 3),\n      };\n    }\n    const id = `check-mukta-${w.word}-apw`;\n    return {\n      id,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.word,\n      options: [w.word, ...distractorsFromPool(w.word, wordPool, id, 3)],\n    };\n  });\n}\n\nfunction buildMuktaLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {\n  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};\n\n  MUKTA_LESSONS.forEach((lesson, i) => {\n    // Previous lesson words: take 1 per prior lesson, oldest-first\n    // round-robin so the cumulative review pattern matches the letter\n    // lessons (oldest words seen most often).\n    const reviewWords: MuktaWord[] = [];\n    if (i > 0) {\n      const cursors = MUKTA_LESSONS.slice(0, i).map(() => 0);\n      while (reviewWords.length < Math.min(i, 3)) {\n        let advanced = false;\n        for (let li = 0; li < i; li++) {\n          if (reviewWords.length >= 3) break;\n          const pos = cursors[li];\n          const candidates = MUKTA_LESSONS[li].words;\n          if (pos < candidates.length) {\n            reviewWords.push(candidates[pos]);\n            cursors[li]++;\n            advanced = true;\n          }\n        }\n        if (!advanced) break;\n      }\n    }\n\n    out[`mukta-${lesson.lessonNum}`] = {\n      id: `mukta-${lesson.lessonNum}`,\n      sectionId: \"s9\",\n      kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n      title: `Mukta words — round ${lesson.lessonNum}`,\n      exercises: muktaLessonExercises(lesson.words, reviewWords),\n    };\n  });\n\n  out[\"check-mukta\"] = {\n    id: \"check-mukta\",\n    sectionId: \"s9\",\n    kind: \"check\",\n    title: \"Mukta words check\",\n    exercises: muktaCheckExercises(),\n  };\n\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = {\n  ...buildLetterLessons(),\n  ...buildMuktaLessons(),\n};"
}

650	const ALL_MUKTA_WORDS: MuktaWord[] = MUKTA_LESSONS.flatMap((l) => l.words);
651	
652	/**
653	 * Distractor selection: pick N other words/meanings from the full pool,
654	 * seed-shuffled by exercise id so different exercises get different
655	 * 3-distractor sets (rather than the same 3 every time).
656	 */
657	function distractorsFromPool<T>(
658	  correct: T,
659	  pool: T[],
660	  seed: string,
661	  n: number,
662	): T[] {
663	  const others = pool.filter((x) => x !== correct);
664	  let h = 2166136261;
665	  for (let i = 0; i < seed.length; i++) {
666	    h = ((h ^ seed.charCodeAt(i)) * 16777619) >>> 0;
667	  }
668	  const shuffled = [...others];
669	  for (let i = shuffled.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
670	    h = (h * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0;
671	    const j = h % (i + 1);
672	    [shuffled[i], shuffled[j]] = [shuffled[j], shuffled[i]];
673	  }
674	  return shuffled.slice(0, n);
675	}
676	
677	/**
678	 * One mukta-word lesson: 2 exercises per new word (word→meaning and
679	 * audio→word, alternating), plus 1 review per previous word (meaning→word).
680	 */
681	function muktaLessonExercises(
682	  newWords: MuktaWord[],
683	  reviewWords: MuktaWord[],
684	): Exercise[] {
685	  const meaningPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.meaning);
686	  const wordPool = ALL_MUKTA_WORDS.map((w) => w.word);
687	  const out: Exercise[] = [];
688	
689	  newWords.forEach((w, i) => {
690	    // Alternate which "first" exercise we use to vary the lesson flow.
691	    const startWithAudio = i % 2 === 0;
692	    const audioId = `mukta-${w.word}-audio`;
693	    const meaningId = `mukta-${w.word}-meaning`;
694	    const audioEx: Exercise = {
695	      id: audioId,
696	      kind: "audio-pick-word",
697	      audioForWord: w.word,
698	      options: [w.word, ...distractorsFromPool(w.word, wordPool, audioId, 3)],
699	    };
700	    const meaningEx: Exercise = {
701	      id: meaningId,
702	      kind: "word-pick-meaning",
703	      word: w.word,
704	      correctMeaning: w.meaning,
705	      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.meaning, meaningPool, meaningId, 3),
706	    };
707	    if (startWithAudio) out.push(audioEx, meaningEx);
708	    else out.push(meaningEx, audioEx);
709	  });

"use client";

// Small audio playback button. Fetches MP3 from /api/tts (which caches
// every distinct word in R2, so repeats are instant) and plays it. Used
// across all exercise types that need audio.

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

export default function AudioButton({
  word,
  label,
  autoPlay = false,
  size = "md",
}: {
  word: string;       // Gurmukhi text to pronounce — passed to /api/tts
  label?: string;     // visible label (defaults to word if not given)
  autoPlay?: boolean; // play once on mount
  size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg";
}) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<"idle" | "loading" | "playing">("idle");
  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);
  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(word)}`;

  function play() {
    if (audioRef.current) {
      audioRef.current.pause();
      audioRef.current.currentTime = 0;
    }
    setState("loading");
    const audio = new Audio(url);
    audioRef.current = audio;
    audio.onplaying = () => setState("playing");
    audio.onended = () => setState("idle");
    audio.onerror = () => setState("idle");
    audio.play().catch(() => setState("idle"));
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    if (autoPlay) {
      const t = setTimeout(play, 200);
      return () => clearTimeout(t);
    }
    // we intentionally only autoplay once on mount; subsequent renders
    // don't retrigger.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  const sz =
    size === "sm" ? "h-8 w-8 text-sm"
    : size === "lg" ? "h-14 w-14 text-2xl"

1	// Small helper to look up letter metadata (name in Punjabi for TTS, ISO
2	// romanization for display) from our existing CURRICULUM data without
3	// duplicating it into the v1.1 catalog. The v1.1 catalog only knows
4	// which letter character each exercise is about; this resolves the
5	// details when the exercise renders.
6	
7	import { CURRICULUM } from "@/data/curriculum";
8	import type { LetterLesson, NuktaGroupLesson } from "@/data/curriculum";
9	
10	interface LetterInfo {
11	  char: string;
12	  name_pa: string;        // Punjabi name, e.g. "ਸੱਸਾ" — used for TTS audio
13	  name_iso: string;       // romanized name, e.g. "sassā"
14	  ipa: string;            // phonetic value, e.g. "sə"
15	}
16	
17	// Build a lookup index once at module load. Indexes both top-level
18	// Painti letters and the 5 nukta letters (which live inside a single
19	// NUKTA_GROUP entry in CURRICULUM, not as their own top-level lessons).
20	const INDEX: Record<string, LetterInfo> = (() => {
21	  const out: Record<string, LetterInfo> = {};
22	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
23	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
24	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
25	      out[l.char] = {
26	        char: l.char,
27	        name_pa: l.name_pa,
28	        name_iso: l.name_iso,
29	        ipa: l.ipa,
30	      };
31	    } else if (lesson.kind === "nukta-group") {
32	      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {
33	        out[nl.char] = {
34	          char: nl.char,
35	          name_pa: nl.name_pa,
36	          name_iso: nl.name_iso,
37	          ipa: nl.ipa,
38	        };
39	      }
40	    }
41	  }
42	  return out;
43	})();
44	
45	/**
46	 * Look up a letter's metadata by its Gurmukhi character. Returns null
47	 * if the character isn't in the curriculum yet (caller should treat as
48	 * a graceful skip rather than crash).
49	 */
50	export function lookupLetter(char: string): LetterInfo | null {
51	  return INDEX[char] ?? null;
52	}
53	
54	// TTS prompt overrides per letter. The canonical letter-name (name_pa
55	// in CURRICULUM) is what's shown to the user; this map decides what's
56	// actually *sent* to /api/tts for audio playback. Use only when Chirp's
57	// pronunciation of the canonical name is poor enough to mislead a
58	// learner. Visible label stays canonical; audio is whatever sounds right.
59	//
60	// Every entry here MUST have its prewarmed MP3 in R2 — run
61	// `tsx scripts/prewarm-words.ts <override-value>` after adding/changing
62	// an entry, since /api/tts is cache-only.
63	const AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES: Record<string, string> = {
64	  // Chirp 3 only pronounces ੜ correctly in word-medial position (no
65	  // real Punjabi word starts with it, so the model has no training data
66	  // for word-initial ੜ). Workaround: synthesize a leading-word + ੜਾੜਾ
67	  // construction (ਨਾੜਾੜਾ) where the flaps land mid-word, then trim
68	  // the leading "ਨਾ" syllable with ffmpeg. What's left is just ੜਾੜਾ
69	  // with both flaps preserved.
70	  //
71	  // The cached MP3 lives under the key "ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed" in R2; produced
72	  // by scripts/trim-audio.ts. Edit the trim amount + re-run that script
73	  // if the cut needs adjustment (current: ਨਾੜਾੜਾ at 0.3s).
74	  "ੜ": "ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed",
75	};
76	
77	/**
78	 * What to send to /api/tts when playing the audio for a letter. Falls
79	 * back to the canonical name_pa, then to the character itself.
80	 */
81	export function audioWordForLetter(char: string): string {
82	  if (char in AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES) return AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES[char];
83	  return INDEX[char]?.name_pa ?? char;
84	}
85

1	// Synthesize a "leading word + target syllables" string, then trim the
2	// leading part to extract just the syllables we care about. Useful for
3	// letters/sounds that Chirp can only pronounce correctly in word-medial
4	// position (e.g. ੜ — no real Punjabi word starts with it).
5	//
6	// Usage:
7	//   tsx scripts/trim-audio.ts <source-word> <target-cache-key> <trim-start-sec>
8	//
9	// Writes the trimmed MP3 to R2 under <target-cache-key> so /api/tts
10	// can serve it (the cache-only route looks up by exact key).
11	import path from "node:path";
12	import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
13	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, unlinkSync } from "node:fs";
14	
15	const env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), ".env.local"), "utf8");
16	for (const line of env.split("\n")) {
17	  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);
18	  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];
19	}
20	
21	import { synthesize, VOICE_NAME } from "@/lib/google-tts";
22	import { getCachedAudio, putCachedAudio } from "@/lib/audio-cache";
23	
24	const args = process.argv.slice(2);
25	if (args.length !== 3) {
26	  console.error("usage: tsx scripts/trim-audio.ts <source-word> <target-key> <trim-start-sec>");
27	  process.exit(1);
28	}
29	const [sourceWord, targetKey, trimStartStr] = args;
30	const trimStart = parseFloat(trimStartStr);
31	
32	async function ffmpegProbeDuration(file: string): Promise<number> {
33	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
34	    const p = spawn("ffprobe", [
35	      "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
36	      "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", file,
37	    ]);
38	    let out = "";
39	    p.stdout.on("data", (d) => (out += d.toString()));
40	    p.on("close", (code) => code === 0 ? resolve(parseFloat(out.trim())) : reject(new Error(`ffprobe exit ${code}`)));
41	  });
42	}
43	
44	async function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number) {
45	  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
46	    const proc = spawn("ffmpeg", [
47	      "-y",
48	      "-i", inFile,
49	      "-ss", String(startSec),
50	      "-af", "afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025", // 25ms fade in so the cut doesn't pop
51	      "-acodec", "libmp3lame",
52	      "-q:a", "5",
53	      outFile,
54	    ]);
55	    let stderr = "";
56	    proc.stderr.on("data", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));
57	    proc.on("close", (code) =>
58	      code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exit ${code}\n${stderr.slice(-400)}`)),
59	    );
60	  });
61	}
62	
63	async function main() {
64	  // Use the cached source if there is one, so the trim is from the same
65	  // recording the user is hearing in the reference page / when fetched
66	  // via dev-fetch-audio. Without this every run gets a fresh TTS
67	  // generation that may differ slightly from the cached source.
68	  let sourceMp3: Buffer;
69	  const cached = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, sourceWord);
70	  if (cached) {
71	    sourceMp3 = Buffer.from(cached.buffer);
72	    console.log(`Using cached source: "${sourceWord}" (${sourceMp3.length}B)`);
73	  } else {
74	    console.log(`Synthesizing fresh: "${sourceWord}"`);
75	    sourceMp3 = await synthesize(sourceWord);
76	    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, sourceWord, sourceMp3);
77	    console.log(`  cached: ${sourceMp3.length}B`);
78	  }
79	
80	  const inFile = "/tmp/akhar-trim-in.mp3";
81	  const outFile = "/tmp/akhar-trim-out.mp3";
82	  writeFileSync(inFile, sourceMp3);
83	
84	  const sourceDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(inFile);
85	  console.log(`  duration: ${sourceDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);
86	  if (trimStart >= sourceDuration) {
87	    console.error(`trim-start ${trimStart}s >= source duration ${sourceDuration}s`);
88	    process.exit(1);
89	  }
90	
91	  console.log(`Trimming first ${trimStart}s …`);
92	  await ffmpegTrim(inFile, outFile, trimStart);
93	  const trimmed = readFileSync(outFile);
94	  const trimmedDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(outFile);
95	  console.log(`  trimmed: ${trimmed.length}B, ${trimmedDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);
96	
97	  await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, targetKey, trimmed);
98	  console.log(`✅ Uploaded as cache key: "${targetKey}"`);
99	
100	  unlinkSync(inFile);
101	  unlinkSync(outFile);
102	}
103	
104	main().catch((e) => {
105	  console.error(e);
106	  process.exit(1);
107	});
108	
```

When Chirp pronounces a word badly\n// in isolation (often because of sentence-initial prosody, nukta marks,\n// or addhak), we generate a cleaner version by synthesizing the word\n// inside a carrier phrase and trimming the leading carrier off\n// (scripts/trim-audio.ts), then cache the trimmed MP3 in R2 under a\n// special key. This map routes the canonical word to that key so\n// callers can keep using the natural Gurmukhi string everywhere.\n//\n// Every override value MUST have a prewarmed MP3 in R2.\n// Letter-level overrides live in lib/course/letter-lookup.ts.\n\nconst WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES: Record<string, string> = {\n  // populated per-word as we triage /debug/audio\n};\n\n/**\n * Resolve the actual /api/tts cache key for a Gurmukhi word. Falls back\n * to the word itself when there's no override.\n */\nexport function audioKeyForWord(word: string): string {\n  return WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES[word] ?? word;\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "async function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number, durationSec?: number) {\n  const args = [\n    \"-y\",\n    \"-i\", inFile,\n    \"-ss\", String(startSec),\n  ];\n  if (durationSec !== undefined) args.push(\"-t\", String(durationSec));\n  args.push(\n    \"-af\", \"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025\", // 25ms fade in so the cut doesn't pop\n    \"-acodec\", \"libmp3lame\",\n    \"-q:a\", \"5\",\n    outFile,\n  );\n  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n    const proc = spawn(\"ffmpeg\", args);\n    let stderr = \"\";\n    proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n    proc.on(\"close\", (code) =>\n      code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exit ${code}\\n${stderr.slice(-400)}`)),\n    );\n  });\n}"
}

1	// QA page: every audio prompt the course plays, in one scrollable list.
2	// Tap each ► to hear the cached R2 MP3 that /api/tts serves. Use this to
3	// catch bad Chirp pronunciations and decide which words/letters need
4	// AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES (see lib/course/letter-lookup.ts) or trimmed
5	// reconstructions (see scripts/trim-audio.ts).
6	
7	import { CURRICULUM, type LetterLesson, type NuktaGroupLesson, type ExampleWord } from "@/data/curriculum";
8	import { audioWordForLetter } from "@/lib/course/letter-lookup";
9	import { audioKeyForWord, OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES } from "@/lib/audio-overrides";
10	import { MUKTA_LESSONS } from "@/data/curriculum-v1.1";
11	import AudioButton from "@/app/course/[lessonId]/AudioButton";
12	
13	interface Row {
14	  display: string;       // what to show as the big Gurmukhi label
15	  audioWord: string;     // what's actually sent to /api/tts
16	  subtitle?: string;     // iso / meaning / etc
17	}
18	
19	function lettersRows(): Row[] {
20	  const out: Row[] = [];
21	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
22	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
23	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
24	      out.push({
25	        display: `${l.char}  ·  ${l.name_pa}`,
26	        audioWord: audioWordForLetter(l.char),
27	        subtitle: `${l.name_iso} · /${l.ipa}/`,
28	      });
29	    } else if (lesson.kind === "nukta-group") {
30	      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {
31	        out.push({
32	          display: `${nl.char}  ·  ${nl.name_pa}`,
33	          audioWord: audioWordForLetter(nl.char),
34	          subtitle: `${nl.name_iso} · /${nl.ipa}/ (nukta)`,
35	        });
36	      }
37	    }
38	  }
39	  return out;
40	}
41	
42	function exampleRows(): Row[] {
43	  const seen = new Set<string>();
44	  const out: Row[] = [];
45	  const collect = (examples: ExampleWord[], origin: string) => {
46	    for (const ex of examples) {
47	      if (seen.has(ex.pa)) continue;
48	      seen.add(ex.pa);
49	      out.push({
50	        display: ex.pa,
51	        audioWord: audioKeyForWord(ex.pa),
52	        subtitle: `${ex.iso} — ${ex.en}${ex.emoji ? `  ${ex.emoji}` : ""}  · from ${origin}`,
53	      });
54	    }
55	  };
56	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
57	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
58	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
59	      collect(l.examples, l.char);
60	    } else if (lesson.kind === "nukta-group") {
61	      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {
62	        collect(nl.examples, `${nl.char} (nukta)`);
63	      }
64	    }
65	  }
66	  return out;
67	}
68	
69	function carrierRows(): Row[] {
70	  return Object.entries(OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES).map(([word, carrier]) => ({
71	    display: carrier,
72	    audioWord: carrier,
73	    subtitle: `raw source for ${word} (this is what gets trimmed)`,
74	  }));
75	}
76	
77	function muktaRows(): Row[] {
78	  return MUKTA_LESSONS.flatMap((lesson) =>
79	    lesson.words.map((w) => ({
80	      display: `${w.word}${w.emoji ? `  ${w.emoji}` : ""}`,
81	      audioWord: audioKeyForWord(w.word),
82	      subtitle: `${w.meaning} · §9 L${lesson.lessonNum}`,
83	    })),
84	  );
85	}
86	
87	function Section({ title, count, rows }: { title: string; count: number; rows: Row[] }) {
88	  return (
89	    <section className="mt-10">
90	      <h2 className="font-serif text-xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">
91	        {title}{" "}
92	        <span className="text-sm font-normal text-zinc-500">({count})</span>
93	      </h2>
94	      <ul className="mt-3 divide-y divide-zinc-200 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 bg-white dark:divide-zinc-800 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950">
95	        {rows.map((r, i) => (
96	          <li key={`${r.audioWord}-${i}`} className="flex items-center gap-4 px-4 py-3">
97	            <AudioButton word={r.audioWord} size="md" label={`Play ${r.audioWord}`} />
98	            <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
99	              <div className="font-serif text-2xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">
100	                {r.display}
101	              </div>
102	              {r.subtitle && (
103	                <div className="mt-0.5 text-xs text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400">
104	                  {r.subtitle}
105	                </div>
106	              )}
107	            </div>
108	            <code className="hidden shrink-0 truncate font-mono text-xs text-zinc-400 sm:block">
109	              {r.audioWord}
110	            </code>
111	          </li>
112	        ))}
113	      </ul>
114	    </section>
115	  );
116	}
117	
118	export default function DebugAudioPage() {
119	  const letters = lettersRows();
120	  const examples = exampleRows();
121	  const mukta = muktaRows();
122	  const carriers = carrierRows();
123

126	      <header>

128	        <h1 className="mt-1 font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">

132	          Every sound the course plays. The big label shows what the learner
133	          sees; the small code on the right shows the exact string sent to
134	          <code className="mx-1 rounded bg-zinc-100 px-1 py-0.5 font-mono text-[11px] dark:bg-zinc-900">/api/tts</code>
135	          (so override-keyed prompts like <code className="font-mono">ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed</code> are visible).
136	        </p>
137	        <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-zinc-500">
138	          Total: {letters.length + examples.length + mukta.length} prompts.
139	        </p>
140	      </header>
141	
142	      <Section title="Letter names" count={letters.length} rows={letters} />
143	      <Section title="Letter example words" count={examples.length} rows={examples} />
144	      <Section title="Mukta words (§9)" count={mukta.length} rows={mukta} />
145	      <Section title="Raw carriers (uncropped)" count={carriers.length} rows={carriers} />
146	    </main>
147	  );

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/debug/audio/actions.ts",
  "content": "\"use server\";\n\n// Toggle verification status for an audio cache key. RLS on\n// audio_verifications enforces that only the admin email can write to\n// this table, so the action is safe to call from the client without an\n// extra check here — Postgres returns an error if a non-admin tries.\n\nimport { revalidatePath } from \"next/cache\";\nimport { serverClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { isAdmin } from \"@/lib/auth/admin\";\n\nexport async function toggleAudioVerification(\n  audioKey: string,\n  currentlyVerified: boolean,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  // Belt-and-braces admin check in addition to RLS, so non-admins fail\n  // fast and get a clear error rather than a Postgres permission rejection.\n  if (!(await isAdmin(supabase))) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"not an admin\" };\n  }\n\n  if (currentlyVerified) {\n    const { error } = await supabase\n      .from(\"audio_verifications\")\n      .delete()\n      .eq(\"audio_key\", audioKey);\n    if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };\n  } else {\n    const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n    const { error } = await supabase\n      .from(\"audio_verifications\")\n      .upsert({ audio_key: audioKey, verified_by: user!.id });\n    if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };\n  }\n\n  revalidatePath(\"/debug/audio\");\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/debug/audio/VerifyButton.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Toggle button for marking an audio cache key as verified. Optimistic:\n// flips the local state immediately so QA-clicks don't have to wait for\n// a round-trip; if the server action fails we revert and surface the\n// error. The server action also revalidatePath()s so other tabs see\n// the new state next time they refresh.\n\nimport { useState, useTransition } from \"react\";\nimport { toggleAudioVerification } from \"./actions\";\n\nexport default function VerifyButton({\n  audioKey,\n  initialVerified,\n}: {\n  audioKey: string;\n  initialVerified: boolean;\n}) {\n  const [verified, setVerified] = useState(initialVerified);\n  const [pending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n  const [err, setErr] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  function onClick() {\n    setErr(null);\n    const next = !verified;\n    setVerified(next);\n    startTransition(async () => {\n      const res = await toggleAudioVerification(audioKey, verified);\n      if (!res.ok) {\n        setVerified(verified); // revert\n        setErr(res.error ?? \"failed\");\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      onClick={onClick}\n      disabled={pending}\n      title={verified ? \"Verified — click to unverify\" : \"Unverified — click to verify\"}\n      className={\n        \"shrink-0 rounded-full px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium transition \" +\n        (verified\n          ? \"bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700 hover:bg-emerald-200 dark:bg-emerald-950 dark:text-emerald-300 dark:hover:bg-emerald-900\"\n          : \"bg-zinc-100 text-zinc-500 hover:bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\") +\n        (pending ? \" opacity-50\" : \"\") +\n        (err ? \" ring-1 ring-red-500\" : \"\")\n      }\n      aria-label={verified ? \"Verified\" : \"Not verified\"}\n    >\n      {verified ? \"✓ verified\" : \"○ unverified\"}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n"
}

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/trim-audio.ts",
  "old_string": "async function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number, durationSec?: number) {",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Run ffmpeg's silencedetect filter and return the list of detected\n * silence intervals (in seconds). noise threshold and minimum duration\n * are tuned for typical Chirp inter-word pauses (~150ms, ~-30dB).\n */\nasync function detectSilences(inFile: string): Promise<{ start: number; end: number }[]> {\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const proc = spawn(\"ffmpeg\", [\n      \"-i\", inFile,\n      \"-af\", \"silencedetect=noise=-30dB:d=0.05\",\n      \"-f\", \"null\",\n      \"-\",\n    ]);\n    let stderr = \"\";\n    proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n    proc.on(\"close\", (code) => {\n      if (code !== 0) return reject(new Error(`ffmpeg silencedetect exit ${code}`));\n      const intervals: { start: number; end: number }[] = [];\n      let currentStart: number | null = null;\n      for (const line of stderr.split(\"\\n\")) {\n        const sm = line.match(/silence_start:\\s*([\\d.]+)/);\n        const em = line.match(/silence_end:\\s*([\\d.]+)/);\n        if (sm) currentStart = parseFloat(sm[1]);\n        else if (em && currentStart !== null) {\n          intervals.push({ start: currentStart, end: parseFloat(em[1]) });\n          currentStart = null;\n        }\n      }\n      resolve(intervals);\n    });\n  });\n}\n\nasync function ffmpegTrim(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number, durationSec?: number) {"
}

  "old_string": "  const sourceDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(inFile);\n  console.log(`  duration: ${sourceDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);\n  if (trimStart >= sourceDuration) {\n    console.error(`trim-start ${trimStart}s >= source duration ${sourceDuration}s`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  const keepDuration = trimEnd > 0 ? sourceDuration - trimStart - trimEnd : undefined;\n  if (keepDuration !== undefined && keepDuration <= 0) {\n    console.error(`trim-start + trim-end (${trimStart}+${trimEnd}s) >= duration (${sourceDuration}s)`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  console.log(\n    keepDuration !== undefined\n      ? `Trimming first ${trimStart}s and last ${trimEnd}s (keeping ${keepDuration.toFixed(3)}s) …`\n      : `Trimming first ${trimStart}s …`,\n  );\n  await ffmpegTrim(inFile, outFile, trimStart, keepDuration);",
  "new_string": "  const sourceDuration = await ffmpegProbeDuration(inFile);\n  console.log(`  duration: ${sourceDuration.toFixed(3)}s`);\n\n  // If either side asks for auto, run silencedetect once and pick the\n  // appropriate gap. Inter-word silences (carrier ↔ target) show up as\n  // intervals strictly inside the audio; we skip any silence that starts\n  // at t=0 (leading pad) or runs to the end (trailing pad), since cutting\n  // at those would leave the carrier intact.\n  let effectiveStart = trimStart;\n  let effectiveEnd = trimEnd;\n  if (autoStart || autoEnd) {\n    const sil = await detectSilences(inFile);\n    const interior = sil.filter((s) => s.start > 0.05 && s.end < sourceDuration - 0.02);\n    console.log(`  silences detected (interior): ${interior.length}`);\n    interior.forEach((s, i) =>\n      console.log(`    [${i}] ${s.start.toFixed(3)}s → ${s.end.toFixed(3)}s (${(s.end - s.start).toFixed(3)}s)`),\n    );\n    if (autoStart) {\n      if (interior.length === 0) {\n        console.error(\"auto trim-start: no interior silence found — fall back to a numeric value\");\n        process.exit(1);\n      }\n      // Cut through the FIRST interior gap → start of word 2.\n      effectiveStart = interior[0].end;\n      console.log(`  auto trim-start → ${effectiveStart.toFixed(3)}s`);\n    }\n    if (autoEnd) {\n      if (interior.length === 0) {\n        console.error(\"auto trim-end: no interior silence found — fall back to a numeric value\");\n        process.exit(1);\n      }\n      // Cut at the START of the LAST interior gap → end of the target word.\n      // Need at least 2 interior gaps for a bookend trim; with only 1 the\n      // same gap can't serve as both start and end.\n      const lastGap = interior[interior.length - 1];\n      if (autoStart && interior.length < 2) {\n        console.error(\"auto trim-end: bookend needs ≥2 interior silences\");\n        process.exit(1);\n      }\n      effectiveEnd = sourceDuration - lastGap.start;\n      console.log(`  auto trim-end → ${effectiveEnd.toFixed(3)}s (from last silence at ${lastGap.start.toFixed(3)}s)`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (effectiveStart >= sourceDuration) {\n    console.error(`trim-start ${effectiveStart}s >= source duration ${sourceDuration}s`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  const keepDuration = effectiveEnd > 0 ? sourceDuration - effectiveStart - effectiveEnd : undefined;\n  if (keepDuration !== undefined && keepDuration <= 0) {\n    console.error(`trim-start + trim-end (${effectiveStart}+${effectiveEnd}s) >= duration (${sourceDuration}s)`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  console.log(\n    keepDuration !== undefined\n      ? `Trimming first ${effectiveStart.toFixed(3)}s and last ${effectiveEnd.toFixed(3)}s (keeping ${keepDuration.toFixed(3)}s) …`\n      : `Trimming first ${effectiveStart.toFixed(3)}s …`,\n  );\n  await ffmpegTrim(inFile, outFile, effectiveStart, keepDuration);"

import { getCachedAudio } from "@/lib/audio-cache";
import { VOICE_NAME } from "@/lib/google-tts";

export const runtime = "nodejs";

// Cache-only TTS route.
//
// Audio is generated server-side ahead of time by scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts.
// This route does NOT synthesize on demand — that decision avoids surprise
// GCP bills from bots and keeps hover latency predictable. On a cache miss
// the route returns 404 and the UI hides the play button gracefully.
export async function GET(request: Request) {
  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
  const word = searchParams.get("word");
  if (!word) {
    return Response.json({ error: "missing 'word' query param" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  const cached = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, word);
  if (!cached) {
    return Response.json({ error: "no cached audio" }, { status: 404 });
  }
  return new Response(new Uint8Array(cached.buffer), {
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "audio/mpeg",
      "Content-Length": String(cached.bytes),
      "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable",
    },
  });
}
```

> AGENT

Found it — `/api/tts` returns `Cache-Control: immutable, max-age=31536000`. Browser caches for a year. That's why retrims don't show. Building three things in one push:

  "replace_all": false,

  "old_string": "  revalidatePath(\"/debug/audio\");\n  return { ok: true };\n}",
  "new_string": "  revalidatePath(\"/debug/audio\");\n  return { ok: true };\n}\n\n/**\n * Force-resynth an audio key against Chirp and overwrite the R2 cache.\n * Use when a cached take sounds bad and you want a fresh roll of the dice.\n * If `sourceKey` is given, it's the carrier phrase to resynth instead (the\n * caller is then expected to retrim it separately).\n */\nexport async function regenerateAudio(audioKey: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  if (!(await isAdmin(supabase))) return { ok: false, error: \"not an admin\" };\n\n  try {\n    const mp3 = await synthesize(audioKey);\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, audioKey, mp3);\n    revalidatePath(\"/debug/audio\");\n    return { ok: true };\n  } catch (e) {\n    const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);\n    return { ok: false, error: msg };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Re-trim an existing source recording into a new (or replacement) cache\n * entry. Requires system ffmpeg (works locally; Vercel Lambda has no\n * ffmpeg binary so this server action only works on `npm run dev`).\n */\nexport async function retrimAudio(\n  sourceKey: string,\n  targetKey: string,\n  startSec: number,\n  endSec: number,\n): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {\n  const supabase = await serverClient();\n  if (!(await isAdmin(supabase))) return { ok: false, error: \"not an admin\" };\n\n  const source = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, sourceKey);\n  if (!source) return { ok: false, error: `source \"${sourceKey}\" not in R2 cache` };\n\n  const stamp = Date.now();\n  const inFile = path.join(tmpdir(), `akhar-trim-in-${stamp}.mp3`);\n  const outFile = path.join(tmpdir(), `akhar-trim-out-${stamp}.mp3`);\n  writeFileSync(inFile, Buffer.from(source.buffer));\n\n  const duration = endSec - startSec;\n  if (duration <= 0) {\n    unlinkSync(inFile);\n    return { ok: false, error: \"endSec must be > startSec\" };\n  }\n\n  try {\n    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n      const proc = spawn(\"ffmpeg\", [\n        \"-y\",\n        \"-i\", inFile,\n        \"-ss\", String(startSec),\n        \"-t\", String(duration),\n        \"-af\", \"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025\",\n        \"-acodec\", \"libmp3lame\",\n        \"-q:a\", \"5\",\n        outFile,\n      ]);\n      let stderr = \"\";\n      proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n      proc.on(\"error\", (err) => reject(err));\n      proc.on(\"close\", (code) =>\n        code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg exit ${code}: ${stderr.slice(-200)}`)),\n      );\n    });\n    const trimmed = readFileSync(outFile);\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, targetKey, trimmed);\n    unlinkSync(inFile);\n    unlinkSync(outFile);\n    revalidatePath(\"/debug/audio\");\n    return { ok: true };\n  } catch (e) {\n    try { unlinkSync(inFile); } catch {}\n    try { unlinkSync(outFile); } catch {}\n    const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);\n    // ffmpeg ENOENT means binary missing (Vercel) — translate to clearer error.\n    if (msg.includes(\"ENOENT\")) return { ok: false, error: \"ffmpeg not available — run /debug/audio locally to edit trims\" };\n    return { ok: false, error: msg };\n  }\n}"
}
