{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/app/debug/audio/AudioEditor.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Inline waveform editor for one audio row. Fetches the source MP3 (the\n// carrier phrase for overrides, or the word itself otherwise), decodes\n// it client-side via Web Audio API, draws a peak waveform on a canvas\n// with two draggable markers for trim start/end. Two server actions\n// back it: regenerate (force a fresh Chirp synth) and retrim (re-cut\n// the source at the current marker positions and overwrite the target\n// cache key).\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState, useTransition } from \"react\";\nimport { regenerateAudio, retrimAudio } from \"./actions\";\n\ninterface Props {\n  audioKey: string;     // the cache key the page is showing (may be a *-trimmed key)\n  sourceKey?: string;   // present for trimmed keys — the raw carrier in R2\n  onClose: () => void;\n}\n\nconst WAVEFORM_BARS = 240;\n\nexport default function AudioEditor({ audioKey, sourceKey, onClose }: Props) {\n  const playKey = sourceKey ?? audioKey;\n  const [duration, setDuration] = useState(0);\n  const [peaks, setPeaks] = useState<number[]>([]);\n  const [startSec, setStartSec] = useState(0);\n  const [endSec, setEndSec] = useState(0);\n  const [msg, setMsg] = useState<{ kind: \"ok\" | \"err\"; text: string } | null>(null);\n  const [pending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n  const [version, setVersion] = useState(Date.now()); // cache-bust on regenerate\n  const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement | null>(null);\n\n  // Decode the source MP3 and compute waveform peaks.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    async function load() {\n      try {\n        const res = await fetch(`/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(playKey)}&v=${version}`);\n        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`source fetch ${res.status}`);\n        const buf = await res.arrayBuffer();\n        // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n        const Ctx = (window.AudioContext || (window as any).webkitAudioContext) as typeof AudioContext;\n        const ctx = new Ctx();\n        const audioBuf = await ctx.decodeAudioData(buf);\n        if (cancelled) return;\n        const samples = audioBuf.getChannelData(0);\n        const perBar = Math.max(1, Math.floor(samples.length / WAVEFORM_BARS));\n        const out: number[] = [];\n        for (let i = 0; i < WAVEFORM_BARS; i++) {\n          let m = 0;\n          const base = i * perBar;\n          for (let j = 0; j < perBar && base + j < samples.length; j++) {\n            const v = Math.abs(samples[base + j]);\n            if (v > m) m = v;\n          }\n          out.push(m);\n        }\n        setPeaks(out);\n        setDuration(audioBuf.duration);\n        // First load: select full source. Re-loads after regen preserve the previous selection.\n        setStartSec((s) => (s === 0 && endSec === 0 ? 0 : Math.min(s, audioBuf.duration)));\n        setEndSec((e) => (e === 0 ? audioBuf.duration : Math.min(e, audioBuf.duration)));\n        ctx.close();\n      } catch (e) {\n        const m = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);\n        setMsg({ kind: \"err\", text: `load: ${m}` });\n      }\n    }\n    load();\n    return () => { cancelled = true; };\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [playKey, version]);\n\n  // Draw waveform + selection on canvas.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const canvas = canvasRef.current;\n    if (!canvas || peaks.length === 0) return;\n    const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;\n    const w = canvas.clientWidth;\n    const h = canvas.clientHeight;\n    canvas.width = w * dpr;\n    canvas.height = h * dpr;\n    const ctx = canvas.getContext(\"2d\")!;\n    ctx.scale(dpr, dpr);\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);\n\n    // Bars\n    const barW = w / peaks.length;\n    for (let i = 0; i < peaks.length; i++) {\n      const barH = Math.max(1, peaks[i] * h * 0.9);\n      const inSelection = duration > 0 &&\n        (i / peaks.length) * duration >= startSec &&\n        (i / peaks.length) * duration <= endSec;\n      ctx.fillStyle = inSelection ? \"#10b981\" : \"#9ca3af\";\n      ctx.fillRect(i * barW, (h - barH) / 2, Math.max(1, barW - 0.5), barH);\n    }\n\n    // Selection overlay markers\n    if (duration > 0) {\n      const startX = (startSec / duration) * w;\n      const endX = (endSec / duration) * w;\n      ctx.fillStyle = \"rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.12)\";\n      ctx.fillRect(startX, 0, endX - startX, h);\n      ctx.fillStyle = \"#10b981\";\n      ctx.fillRect(startX - 1, 0, 2, h);\n      ctx.fillRect(endX - 1, 0, 2, h);\n    }\n  }, [peaks, duration, startSec, endSec]);\n\n  // Click/drag on canvas → move the nearest marker.\n  function onCanvasPointer(e: React.PointerEvent<HTMLCanvasElement>) {\n    if (duration === 0) return;\n    const canvas = e.currentTarget;\n    canvas.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);\n    const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();\n    function applyAt(clientX: number) {\n      const x = clientX - rect.left;\n      const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(duration, (x / rect.width) * duration));\n      // Snap to whichever marker is closer.\n      const distToStart = Math.abs(t - startSec);\n      const distToEnd = Math.abs(t - endSec);\n      if (distToStart <= distToEnd) setStartSec(Math.min(t, endSec - 0.02));\n      else setEndSec(Math.max(t, startSec + 0.02));\n    }\n    applyAt(e.clientX);\n    const move = (ev: PointerEvent) => applyAt(ev.clientX);\n    const up = () => {\n      canvas.removeEventListener(\"pointermove\", move);\n      canvas.removeEventListener(\"pointerup\", up);\n      canvas.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId);\n    };\n    canvas.addEventListener(\"pointermove\", move);\n    canvas.addEventListener(\"pointerup\", up);\n  }\n\n  function playRange() {\n    const a = new Audio(`/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(playKey)}&v=${version}`);\n    a.addEventListener(\"loadedmetadata\", () => { a.currentTime = startSec; a.play(); });\n    const stopAt = (endSec - startSec) * 1000;\n    setTimeout(() => a.pause(), Math.max(50, stopAt));\n  }\n\n  function apply() {\n    if (!sourceKey) {\n      setMsg({ kind: \"err\", text: \"no source — trim only works on override entries\" });\n      return;\n    }\n    setMsg(null);\n    startTransition(async () => {\n      const res = await retrimAudio(sourceKey, audioKey, startSec, endSec);\n      if (!res.ok) setMsg({ kind: \"err\", text: res.error ?? \"trim failed\" });\n      else {\n        setMsg({ kind: \"ok\", text: `saved (${(endSec - startSec).toFixed(3)}s)` });\n        setVersion(Date.now()); // bust any further plays of source/target\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  function regen() {\n    setMsg(null);\n    startTransition(async () => {\n      // Regen the source if this is a trimmed entry; otherwise regen the entry itself.\n      const targetForSynth = sourceKey ?? audioKey;\n      const res = await regenerateAudio(targetForSynth);\n      if (!res.ok) setMsg({ kind: \"err\", text: res.error ?? \"regen failed\" });\n      else {\n        setMsg({ kind: \"ok\", text: `regenerated \"${targetForSynth}\"` });\n        setVersion(Date.now());\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mt-3 space-y-3 rounded-lg border border-zinc-300 bg-zinc-50 p-3 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900/50\">\n      <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between text-xs text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n        <span>\n          {sourceKey\n            ? <>editing trim of <code className=\"font-mono\">{audioKey}</code> from source <code className=\"font-mono\">{sourceKey}</code></>\n            : <>editing <code className=\"font-mono\">{audioKey}</code> (no source override — regen only)</>}\n        </span>\n        <button onClick={onClose} className=\"text-zinc-500 hover:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:text-zinc-100\">close</button>\n      </div>\n\n      <canvas\n        ref={canvasRef}\n        onPointerDown={onCanvasPointer}\n        className=\"block h-24 w-full cursor-ew-resize touch-none rounded bg-white dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n      />\n\n      {duration > 0 && (\n        <div className=\"grid grid-cols-3 gap-3 text-xs\">\n          <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1\">\n            <span className=\"text-zinc-500\">start</span>\n            <input\n              type=\"number\" step=\"0.01\" min={0} max={endSec - 0.02}\n              value={startSec.toFixed(3)}\n              onChange={(e) => setStartSec(Math.min(parseFloat(e.target.value) || 0, endSec - 0.02))}\n              className=\"rounded border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-2 py-1 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n            />\n          </label>\n          <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1\">\n            <span className=\"text-zinc-500\">end</span>\n            <input\n              type=\"number\" step=\"0.01\" min={startSec + 0.02} max={duration}\n              value={endSec.toFixed(3)}\n              onChange={(e) => setEndSec(Math.max(parseFloat(e.target.value) || 0, startSec + 0.02))}\n              className=\"rounded border border-zinc-300 bg-white px-2 py-1 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n            />\n          </label>\n          <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1\">\n            <span className=\"text-zinc-500\">duration</span>\n            <span className=\"rounded border border-transparent px-2 py-1 text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300\">\n              {(endSec - startSec).toFixed(3)}s of {duration.toFixed(3)}s\n            </span>\n          </label>\n        </div>\n      )}\n\n      <div className=\"flex flex-wrap gap-2\">\n        <button\n          onClick={playRange} disabled={pending || duration === 0}\n          className=\"rounded bg-zinc-200 px-3 py-1 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-900 hover:bg-zinc-300 disabled:opacity-50 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-100 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700\"\n        >\n          ▶ play selection\n        </button>\n        {sourceKey && (\n          <button\n            onClick={apply} disabled={pending || duration === 0}\n            className=\"rounded bg-emerald-600 px-3 py-1 text-sm font-medium text-white hover:bg-emerald-700 disabled:opacity-50\"\n          >\n            save trim\n          </button>\n        )}\n        <button\n          onClick={regen} disabled={pending}\n          className=\"rounded bg-orange-600 px-3 py-1 text-sm font-medium text-white hover:bg-orange-700 disabled:opacity-50\"\n        >\n          {sourceKey ? \"regen source from Chirp\" : \"regen from Chirp\"}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n\n      {msg && (\n        <p className={\"text-xs \" + (msg.kind === \"ok\" ? \"text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-400\" : \"text-red-600 dark:text-red-400\")}>\n          {msg.text}\n        </p>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

Lives on the right side of each /debug/audio row.\n\nimport { useState } from \"react\";\nimport VerifyButton from \"./VerifyButton\";\nimport AudioEditor from \"./AudioEditor\";\n\nexport default function RowControls({\n  audioKey,\n  sourceKey,\n  initialVerified,\n}: {\n  audioKey: string;\n  sourceKey?: string;\n  initialVerified: boolean;\n}) {\n  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);\n  return (\n    <>\n      <div className=\"flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2\">\n        <VerifyButton audioKey={audioKey} initialVerified={initialVerified} />\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => setEditing((e) => !e)}\n          className=\"rounded-full bg-zinc-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-zinc-600 hover:bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\"\n          aria-label={editing ? \"Close editor\" : \"Open editor\"}\n        >\n          {editing ? \"× close\" : \"✏ edit\"}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      {editing && (\n        <div className=\"col-span-full w-full\">\n          <AudioEditor\n            audioKey={audioKey}\n            sourceKey={sourceKey}\n            onClose={() => setEditing(false)}\n          />\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "\"use client\";\n\n// One row of the audio list. Renders the AudioButton + label + verify\n// chip + edit toggle on the first line; the inline AudioEditor expands\n// underneath when ✏ is pressed. Lives as a client component so the\n// open/closed state and the editor itself can be interactive.\n\nimport { useState } from \"react\";\nimport AudioButton from \"@/app/course/[lessonId]/AudioButton\";\nimport VerifyButton from \"./VerifyButton\";\nimport AudioEditor from \"./AudioEditor\";\n\nexport default function RowItem({\n  audioKey,\n  sourceKey,\n  display,\n  subtitle,\n  initialVerified,\n}: {\n  audioKey: string;\n  sourceKey?: string;\n  display: string;\n  subtitle?: string;\n  initialVerified: boolean;\n}) {\n  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);\n  return (\n    <li className=\"px-4 py-3\">\n      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-4\">\n        <AudioButton word={audioKey} size=\"md\" label={`Play ${audioKey}`} />\n        <div className=\"min-w-0 flex-1\">\n          <div className=\"font-serif text-2xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n            {display}\n          </div>\n          {subtitle && (\n            <div className=\"mt-0.5 text-xs text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n              {subtitle}\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </div>\n        <VerifyButton audioKey={audioKey} initialVerified={initialVerified} />\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => setEditing((e) => !e)}\n          className=\"shrink-0 rounded-full bg-zinc-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-zinc-600 hover:bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800\"\n          aria-label={editing ? \"Close editor\" : \"Open editor\"}\n        >\n          {editing ? \"× close\" : \"✏ edit\"}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      {editing && (\n        <AudioEditor\n          audioKey={audioKey}\n          sourceKey={sourceKey}\n          onClose={() => setEditing(false)}\n        />\n      )}\n    </li>\n  );\n}"
}

Drives the AudioEditor's\n * \"save trim\" + \"regen source\" buttons.\n */\nfunction buildTrimmedToSourceMap(): Record<string, string> {\n  const out: Record<string, string> = {};\n  for (const [word, carrier] of Object.entries(OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES)) {\n    const cacheKey = WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES[word];\n    if (cacheKey) out[cacheKey] = carrier;\n  }\n  // The letter override (ੜ → ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed) doesn't go through\n  // WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES, so wire it up manually.\n  out[\"ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed\"] = \"ਨਾੜਾੜਾ\";\n  return out;\n}"

{

  "old_string": "export default function AudioButton({\n  word,\n  label,\n  autoPlay = false,\n  size = \"md\",\n}: {\n  word: string;       // Gurmukhi text to pronounce — passed to /api/tts\n  label?: string;     // visible label (defaults to word if not given)\n  autoPlay?: boolean; // play once on mount\n  size?: \"sm\" | \"md\" | \"lg\";\n}) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\"idle\" | \"loading\" | \"playing\">(\"idle\");\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  // Override-aware: a few words have hand-tuned trims cached under a\n  // different key (see lib/audio-overrides.ts).\n  const url = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(audioKeyForWord(word))}`;",
  "new_string": "export default function AudioButton({\n  word,\n  label,\n  autoPlay = false,\n  size = \"md\",\n  cacheBust,\n}: {\n  word: string;       // Gurmukhi text to pronounce — passed to /api/tts\n  label?: string;     // visible label (defaults to word if not given)\n  autoPlay?: boolean; // play once on mount\n  size?: \"sm\" | \"md\" | \"lg\";\n  cacheBust?: number | string; // pass a value that changes on regen/retrim to bypass the year-long /api/tts cache header\n}) {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\"idle\" | \"loading\" | \"playing\">(\"idle\");\n  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null);\n  // Override-aware: a few words have hand-tuned trims cached under a\n  // different key (see lib/audio-overrides.ts).\n  const base = `/api/tts?word=${encodeURIComponent(audioKeyForWord(word))}`;\n  const url = cacheBust !== undefined ? `${base}&v=${cacheBust}` : base;"
}

- save trim writes the new MP3 to R2 (overwriting the trimmed key)
- regen from Chirp rolls a fresh synth of the source

// Audio cache backed by Cloudflare R2.
//
// R2 is the single source of truth — no metadata DB. The key is derived
// deterministically from (voice, text):
//   audio/<voice>/<sha1(text)>.mp3
// so checking "is this cached?" is just an R2 HeadObject. Cheap (class B
// op, 10M free per month) and removes a Postgres roundtrip from the hover
// hot path.
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import {
  S3Client,
  GetObjectCommand,
  PutObjectCommand,
  HeadObjectCommand,
  DeleteObjectCommand,
  NoSuchKey,
  NotFound,
} from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";

let _client: S3Client | null = null;
function client() {
  if (_client) return _client;
  _client = new S3Client({
    region: "auto",
    endpoint: process.env.R2_ENDPOINT!,
    credentials: {
      accessKeyId: process.env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,
      secretAccessKey: process.env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,
    },
  });
  return _client;
}

export function r2KeyFor(voice: string, text: string): string {
  const hash = createHash("sha1").update(text, "utf8").digest("hex");
  return `audio/${voice}/${hash}.mp3`;
}

export interface CachedAudio {
  buffer: Buffer;
  bytes: number;
}

/**
 * Fetch cached audio. Returns null if no object exists for this (voice, text)
 * — the route returns 404, the UI hides the play button. No on-demand
 * synthesis.
 */
export async function getCachedAudio(
  voice: string,
  text: string,
): Promise<CachedAudio | null> {
  const Key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);
  try {
    const obj = await client().send(
      new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!, Key }),
    );
    if (!obj.Body) return null;
    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
    for await (const chunk of obj.Body as AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>) {

On a cache miss\n// the route returns 404 and the UI hides the play button gracefully.\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);\n  const word = searchParams.get(\"word\");\n  if (!word) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing 'word' query param\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  const cached = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, word);\n  if (!cached) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"no cached audio\" }, { status: 404 });\n  }\n  return new Response(new Uint8Array(cached.buffer), {\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"audio/mpeg\",\n      \"Content-Length\": String(cached.bytes),\n      \"Cache-Control\": \"public, max-age=31536000, immutable\",\n    },\n  });\n}",
  "new_string": "import { createHash } from \"node:crypto\";\nimport { getCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\nimport { VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\n\nexport const runtime = \"nodejs\";\n\n// Cache-only TTS route.\n//\n// Audio is generated server-side ahead of time by scripts/prewarm-sakhi.ts.\n// This route does NOT synthesize on demand — that decision avoids surprise\n// GCP bills from bots and keeps hover latency predictable. On a cache miss\n// the route returns 404 and the UI hides the play button gracefully.\n//\n// Cache headers: we drop `immutable` (which made browsers never re-check\n// for a year — bad when /debug/audio retrims overwrite an R2 object).\n// Instead we serve a content-hash ETag and use must-revalidate, so\n// browsers cache aggressively but ask the server \"still the same bytes?\"\n// on each playback. Unchanged audio = cheap 304; changed audio = full\n// re-fetch the next time anyone plays it.\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);\n  const word = searchParams.get(\"word\");\n  if (!word) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing 'word' query param\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  const cached = await getCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, word);\n  if (!cached) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"no cached audio\" }, { status: 404 });\n  }\n\n  // Short content hash → ETag. MP3s are tiny (<10KB) so this is cheap.\n  const etag = `\"${createHash(\"sha1\").update(cached.buffer).digest(\"base64url\").slice(0, 16)}\"`;\n  if (request.headers.get(\"if-none-match\") === etag) {\n    return new Response(null, {\n      status: 304,\n      headers: { \"Cache-Control\": \"public, max-age=300, must-revalidate\", ETag: etag },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return new Response(new Uint8Array(cached.buffer), {\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"audio/mpeg\",\n      \"Content-Length\": String(cached.bytes),\n      \"Cache-Control\": \"public, max-age=300, must-revalidate\",\n      ETag: etag,\n    },\n  });\n}"
}

Pushed (`999056c`). Two answers:

**Your saved trim is already in prod** — R2 is shared between dev and prod. The catch was browser caching. With the new ETag header, any device that plays the same MP3 again will detect the change (server returns the new bytes since the hash changed) instead of being stuck on the year-cached version.

**Verify badges** — RLS policy was using a subquery that fails silently in nested contexts; switched to `auth.jwt() ->> 'email'`. Hard-refresh, try again — if it still errors, the button will now show the actual error text so we can debug.

import type { NextConfig } from "next";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // `better-sqlite3` is a native module — Next.js's bundler can't rewrite it
  // and trying to inline it breaks the build. Mark it external so it's
  // require()-d at runtime from node_modules instead.
  serverExternalPackages: ["better-sqlite3"],

  // Bundle the SQLite data files into the serverless function output so the
  // deployed code can read them at runtime. Vercel's outputFileTracing walks
  // the import graph but won't follow runtime path strings like
  // `path.join(cwd, "data/sakhis.db")`, so we have to opt them in explicitly.
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    "/**/*": ["./data/sakhis.db", "./lipi.db"],
  },
};

export default nextConfig;

// Google Cloud Text-to-Speech wrapper.
//
// Credentials: works in two environments —
//   - Local dev: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/key.json (file path)
//   - Vercel: GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON=<entire contents of key.json> (env var)
// The GCP Node SDKs auto-pick-up GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, but Vercel
// has no persistent filesystem so we feed the credentials directly.
//
// Voice picked by ear from the full pa-IN Chirp 3 HD lineup. Chirp 3 voices
// do not accept SSML or speakingRate — only plain text.
import textToSpeech from "@google-cloud/text-to-speech";

export const VOICE_NAME = "pa-IN-Chirp3-HD-Achernar";
// Below this byte count, Chirp 3 produced a clipped/silent stub or a
// barely-audible short syllable. Triggers the doubled-input fallback.
// Was 2000 initially; bumped to 3000 because some short particles were
// passing the lower bar with technically-correct-but-very-quiet output.
const MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES = 3000;
const CANDIDATES = 5;
const RETRY_DELAYS = [2000, 5000, 12000, 30000];

let _client: InstanceType<typeof textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient> | null = null;
function client() {
  if (_client) return _client;
  const json = process.env.GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON;
  if (json) {
    const credentials = JSON.parse(json);
    _client = new textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient({ credentials });
  } else {
    // Falls back to GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS file path
    _client = new textToSpeech.TextToSpeechClient();
  }
  return _client;
}

function toBuf(c: unknown): Buffer | null {
  if (c == null) return null;
  if (Buffer.isBuffer(c)) return c;
  if (typeof c === "string") return Buffer.from(c, "base64");
  if (c instanceof Uint8Array) return Buffer.from(c);
  return null;
}

async function synthOne(text: string): Promise<Buffer | null> {
  let lastErr: unknown;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= RETRY_DELAYS.length; attempt++) {
    try {
      const [r] = await client().synthesizeSpeech({
        input: { text },
        voice: { languageCode: "pa-IN", name: VOICE_NAME },
        audioConfig: { audioEncoding: "MP3" },
      });
      return toBuf(r.audioContent);
    } catch (err) {
      lastErr = err;
      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      if (!/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|429|UNAVAILABLE/i.test(msg)) throw err;
      if (attempt === RETRY_DELAYS.length) throw err;
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, RETRY_DELAYS[attempt]));
    }
  }
  throw lastErr;
}

async function bestOf(text: string, n: number): Promise<Buffer | null> {
  const results = await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: n }, () => synthOne(text)));
  const bufs = results.filter((b): b is Buffer => b != null);
  if (bufs.length === 0) return null;
  return bufs.reduce((best, cur) => (cur.length > best.length ? cur : best));
}

/**
 * Synthesize a Punjabi word or sentence to MP3.
 *
 * Two tricks baked in:
 *   - Appends `.` to the input for declarative falling intonation (without
 *     it, Chirp 3 reads isolated words with question-like rising contour).
 *   - Best-of-5 + silent-word fallback (`${w}. ${w}.`) for short particles
 *     like ਜੀ/ਦਾ/ਨੇ where the engine sometimes returns ~0.3s of silence.
 */
export async function synthesize(text: string): Promise<Buffer> {
  const primary = `${text}.`;
  let buf = await bestOf(primary, CANDIDATES);
  if (!buf) throw new Error("TTS returned no audio for: " + text);
  if (buf.length < MIN_HEALTHY_BYTES) {
    const doubled = await bestOf(`${text}. ${text}.`, CANDIDATES);
    if (doubled && doubled.length > buf.length) buf = doubled;
  }
  return buf;
}
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/akhar/scripts/synth-hindi.ts",
  "content": "// Synthesize with the Hindi Chirp voice and cache under the DEFAULT\n// voice's R2 key. Use for nukta letters whose phonemes Chirp's Punjabi\n// voice flattens. The /api/tts route looks up by default-voice key, so\n// the Hindi-synthesized MP3 is served as if it had come from the\n// Punjabi voice — invisible to the rest of the app.\n//\n// Usage:\n//   tsx scripts/synth-hindi.ts <text> [<text> …]\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { synthesizeHindi, VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { putCachedAudio } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nif (args.length === 0) {\n  console.error(\"usage: tsx scripts/synth-hindi.ts <text> [<text> …]\");\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  for (const text of args) {\n    process.stdout.write(`  ⟳ hindi synth: ${text} ... `);\n    const mp3 = await synthesizeHindi(text);\n    // Cached under the DEFAULT voice key so /api/tts (which queries the\n    // default voice) finds it.\n    await putCachedAudio(VOICE_NAME, text, mp3);\n    console.log(`done (${mp3.length}B)`);\n  }\n  console.log(`\\n✅ ${args.length} item(s) written under default-voice R2 keys`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"
}

> AGENT

Reverted (`93ebee2`). The honest situation:

- Punjabi Chirp **drops the nukta** because modern colloquial Punjabi has merged ਖ਼/ਗ਼/ਫ਼ back into ਖ/ਗ/ਫ. Native speakers conversationally say "gubaara" not "ghubaara". The model reflects that reality.
- Hindi voice keeps the nukta phonemes but **the accent is wrong** — and accent matters for a Punjabi learning app.

Three honest paths:

1. **Verify them as-is** — accept that Chirp's flattening matches how most modern Punjabis actually say these letters. Pedagogically defensible.
2. **Different Punjabi voice** — Chirp has ~9 pa-IN voices. I can probe each to see if any happens to preserve nuktas (probably not — same training data — but cheap to try).
3. **Record yourself** — 5 letter names, ~10 seconds of recording, drop in as static MP3s under the override keys. Definitely correct pronunciation, definitely your accent.

> DEVELOPER

hmm I really dont know becasue I notice this issue but also we can't test people on thier listening skills if the letters sound the same. What can we do aboyt htis??? lets dicuss

> AGENT

Real discussion — let me think this through with you.

**The honest linguistic situation**: nuktas are vestigial in modern Indian Punjabi. Many native speakers (especially in India) genuinely don't distinguish ਗ from ਗ਼ in speech — they pronounce ਗ਼ਜ਼ਲ as "gajal" not "ghazal", ਖ਼ਬਰ as "khabar" (regular ਖ) not the throaty /x/. Pakistani Punjabi (Shahmukhi) preserves them better, and Punjabi/Urdu literary tradition does too. So Chirp isn't wrong — it's reflecting how millions of people actually talk.

**What the nukta really teaches** is therefore two different things depending on how you frame it:

1. **A distinct phoneme** — the "correct" Urdu/Persian sound. Useful for advanced learners reading literary text, learners of Pakistani Punjabi, etymological understanding. Audio differentiation matters.
2. **A spelling distinction** — a visual marker that "this came from Persian/Arabic". The letter looks different, may sound the same as the base in casual speech. Visual recognition matters; audio doesn't.

For your audience (heritage-curious beginners targeting sakhis), **(2) is probably the honest goal**. Sakhis don't have many nukta-loaded words. Conversation doesn't require the distinction. Learners will encounter the visual form occasionally and need to recognize "ਖ਼ is just ਖ in a Persian/Urdu loanword."

**My recommendation**:

- **Keep nuktas in the alphabet** (visual recognition) — show them, name them, give an example word
- **Skip nukta letters from listening-only exercises** — `audio-pick-letter` (hear a sound, pick the letter) would be unfair since they sound identical. Exclude the 5 nukta letters from that exercise type.
- **Add a teach-screen note** on each nukta lesson: *"In modern spoken Punjabi this often sounds like ਗ. The dot marks Persian/Arabic origin — keep it when reading and writing."*
- **Accept Chirp's pronunciation as-is, verify them** (they sound like the base — that's modern colloquial reality)

This is honest, doesn't require recording, doesn't ship a Hindi accent.

**Alternative if you want phonetic accuracy**: spend 5 min recording yourself saying the 5 nukta names — drop into R2 under the override keys. Your accent, perfectly distinct sounds. One-time cost, never breaks. I can wire up the override slots and you slot the MP3s in.

What's your gut?

363	function fourOptions(correct: string, pool: string[], seed: string): string[] {
364	  const others = pool.filter((l) => l !== correct);
365	  // Mulberry-ish seeded shuffle keyed off the seed string.

368	    h = ((h ^ seed.charCodeAt(i)) * 16777619) >>> 0;
369	  }
370	  const shuffled = [...others];
371	  for (let i = shuffled.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
372	    h = (h * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0;

Audio-direction exercises (hear → pick letter, see\n * letter → pick audio) would be ambiguous for these because they\n * sound the same as their base consonant (ਖ਼ ↔ ਖ, ਗ਼ ↔ ਗ, ਫ਼ ↔ ਫ).\n *\n * Two effects on curriculum:\n *  - These letters get visual-only exercises, never audio-pick or\n *    pick-audio.\n *  - They're excluded as distractors in any audio-direction exercise\n *    (otherwise a learner hearing \"ਖੱਖਾ\" couldn't distinguish ਖ from\n *    ਖ਼ in the options).\n *\n * ਸ਼ /ʃ/ and ਜ਼ /z/ are NOT in this set — Chirp does pronounce those\n * distinctly from ਸ and ਜ.\n */\nexport const AUDIO_INDISTINCT_LETTERS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([\"ਖ਼\", \"ਗ਼\", \"ਫ਼\"]);\n\nexport function isAudioIndistinct(char: string): boolean {\n  return AUDIO_INDISTINCT_LETTERS.has(char);\n}"
}

389	 * Build a single letter lesson with cumulative review of every prior
390	 * letter in the same line.
391	 *
392	 * Mix scales 5 → 4+N where N = previousLetters.length:
393	 *   - newLetter: 4 starring exercises (5 if no previous, so lesson 1
394	 *     of each line isn't trivially short)
395	 *   - each previousLetter: 1 review exercise (alternating audio/visual)
396	 *

398	 * actively discriminate it from the older one.
399	 */
400	function letterLessonExercises(
401	  newLetter: string,
402	  previousLetters: readonly string[],
403	  distractorPool: string[],
404	): Exercise[] {
405	  const newLetterCount = previousLetters.length === 0 ? 5 : 4;
406	  const out: Exercise[] = [];

  "old_string": "/**\n * Build one of the two audio-direction exercises (audio→letter or\n * letter→audio) for the given target. If the target is audio-indistinct\n * (a flattened nukta), substitutes a type-romanization exercise so the\n * learner is tested on visual recognition rather than impossible\n * listening discrimination.\n *\n * For audio variants the distractor pool is filtered to drop any\n * indistinct letters — those would be unfair options.\n */\nfunction audioOrVisualExercise(\n  target: string,\n  id: string,\n  audioKind: \"audio-pick-letter\" | \"letter-pick-audio\",\n  distractorPool: string[],\n  isoFor: (char: string) => string,\n): Exercise {\n  if (isAudioIndistinct(target)) {\n    return {\n      id,\n      kind: \"type-romanization\",\n      displayLetter: target,\n      acceptedAnswers: [isoFor(target)],\n    };\n  }\n  const audioSafePool = distractorPool.filter((c) => !isAudioIndistinct(c));\n  if (audioKind === \"audio-pick-letter\") {\n    return {\n      id,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-letter\",\n      audioForLetter: target,\n      options: fourOptions(target, audioSafePool, id),\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    id,\n    kind: \"letter-pick-audio\",\n    displayLetter: target,\n    audioOptions: fourOptions(target, audioSafePool, id),\n  };\n}",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Build an audio-direction exercise (audio→letter or letter→audio) for\n * the given target, with the distractor pool filtered to keep things\n * fair when nukta letters are involved:\n *\n *   - Indistinct nuktas (ਖ਼/ਗ਼/ਫ਼) are NEVER distractors. 781	function buildMuktaLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {
782	  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};
783	
784	  MUKTA_LESSONS.forEach((lesson, i) => {
785	    // Previous lesson words: take 1 per prior lesson, oldest-first
786	    // round-robin so the cumulative review pattern matches the letter
787	    // lessons (oldest words seen most often).
788	    const reviewWords: MuktaWord[] = [];
789	    if (i > 0) {
790	      const cursors = MUKTA_LESSONS.slice(0, i).map(() => 0);
791	      while (reviewWords.length < Math.min(i, 3)) {
792	        let advanced = false;
793	        for (let li = 0; li < i; li++) {
794	          if (reviewWords.length >= 3) break;
795	          const pos = cursors[li];
796	          const candidates = MUKTA_LESSONS[li].words;
797	          if (pos < candidates.length) {
798	            reviewWords.push(candidates[pos]);
799	            cursors[li]++;
800	            advanced = true;
801	          }
802	        }
803	        if (!advanced) break;
804	      }
805	    }
806	
807	    out[`mukta-${lesson.lessonNum}`] = {
808	      id: `mukta-${lesson.lessonNum}`,
809	      sectionId: "s9",
810	      kind: "teach-and-test",
811	      title: `Mukta words — round ${lesson.lessonNum}`,
812	      // Marks this lesson as a mukta-word lesson so the lesson runner
813	      // page knows to render the MuktaTeachContent component with the
814	      // matching MUKTA_LESSONS entry's words.
815	      curriculumRef: `mukta-${lesson.lessonNum}`,
816	      exercises: muktaLessonExercises(lesson.words, reviewWords),
817	    };
818	  });
819	
820	  out["check-mukta"] = {
821	    id: "check-mukta",
822	    sectionId: "s9",
823	    kind: "check",
824	    title: "Mukta words check",
825	    exercises: muktaCheckExercises(),
826	  };
827	
828	  return out;
829	}
830	
831	export const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = {
832	  ...buildLetterLessons(),
833	  ...buildMuktaLessons(),
834	};

841	  return PATH_SECTIONS.find((s) => s.id === id);
842	}
843	
844	export function getLesson(id: string): PathLesson | undefined {
845	  return PATH_LESSONS[id];
846	}
847	
848	/**
849	 * Flat ordered list of lesson IDs across all sections — the linear path
850	 * order. Used to determine which lesson unlocks next.
851	 */
852	export function allLessonIdsInOrder(): string[] {
853	  return PATH_SECTIONS.flatMap((s) => s.lessonIds);

859	 */
860	export function nextLessonId(id: string): string | null {
861	  const order = allLessonIdsInOrder();

The teach screen comes from data/curriculum.ts (MATRA_LESSONS,\n// which holds the matra sign + name + construction CV examples +\n// example words). One lesson per matra (introduces 4 example words +\n// reviews from prior matras), plus a closing check across all 9.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ninterface MatraPathDef {\n  pathSlug: string;        // matra-kanna — the PATH_LESSONS key + lesson_progress FK\n  curriculumSlug: string;  // kanna — looks up MatraLesson in data/curriculum.ts\n}\n\n// PATH_SECTIONS uses ASCII-safe slugs; data/curriculum.ts uses linguistic\n// transliterations. Map the two so the slug used in user progress is\n// stable even if the curriculum.ts romanisation drifts.\nconst MATRA_PATH_DEFS: MatraPathDef[] = [\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-kanna\", curriculumSlug: \"kanna\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-sihari\", curriculumSlug: \"sihari\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-bihari\", curriculumSlug: \"bihari\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-aunkar\", curriculumSlug: \"aunkar\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-dulainkar\", curriculumSlug: \"dulænkar\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-lavan\", curriculumSlug: \"lavan\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-dulavan\", curriculumSlug: \"dulavan\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-hora\", curriculumSlug: \"hora\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"matra-kanaura\", curriculumSlug: \"kanɔṛā\" },\n];\n\n/**\n * Per-matra lesson: introduce 4 example words via alternating\n * audio-pick-word + word-pick-meaning, plus 1 review from each prior\n * matra's example pool (oldest-first, capped at 3 for sane pacing).\n */\nfunction matraLessonExercises(\n  newWords: { pa: string; en: string }[],\n  reviewWords: { pa: string; en: string }[],\n  slug: string,\n): Exercise[] {\n  const allWords = MATRA_PATH_DEFS.flatMap((d) =>\n    (MATRA_LESSONS_BY_SLUG[d.curriculumSlug]?.examples ?? []).map((e) => ({\n      pa: e.pa,\n      en: e.en,\n    })),\n  );\n  const wordPool = allWords.map((w) => w.pa);\n  const meaningPool = allWords.map((w) => w.en);\n  const out: Exercise[] = [];\n\n  newWords.forEach((w, i) => {\n    const startWithAudio = i % 2 === 0;\n    const apwId = `${slug}-${w.pa}-apw`;\n    const wpmId = `${slug}-${w.pa}-wpm`;\n    const apw: Exercise = {\n      id: apwId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.pa,\n      options: [w.pa, ...distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, apwId, 3)],\n    };\n    const wpm: Exercise = {\n      id: wpmId,\n      kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n      word: w.pa,\n      correctMeaning: w.en,\n      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.en, meaningPool, wpmId, 3),\n    };\n    if (startWithAudio) out.push(apw, wpm);\n    else out.push(wpm, apw);\n  });\n\n  reviewWords.forEach((w) => {\n    const id = `${slug}-review-${w.pa}`;\n    out.push({\n      id,\n      kind: \"meaning-pick-word\",\n      meaning: w.en,\n      correctWord: w.pa,\n      distractorWords: distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, id, 3),\n    });\n  });\n\n  return out;\n}\n\nlet MATRA_LESSONS_BY_SLUG: Record<string, { examples: { pa: string; en: string }[] }> = {};\n\nfunction buildMatraLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {\n  // Build slug → examples map once; matraLessonExercises uses it for\n  // pooling distractors across the whole §10 vocabulary.\n  MATRA_LESSONS_BY_SLUG = Object.fromEntries(\n    MATRA_PATH_DEFS.map((d) => {\n      const entry = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === d.curriculumSlug);\n      return [d.curriculumSlug, { examples: entry?.examples ?? [] }];\n    }),\n  );\n\n  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};\n\n  MATRA_PATH_DEFS.forEach((def, i) => {\n    const entry = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === def.curriculumSlug);\n    if (!entry) return; // skip if data/curriculum.ts entry is missing\n    const newWords = entry.examples.slice(0, 4).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n\n    // Review pool: 1 word from each prior matra, oldest-first, cap 3.\n    const reviewWords: { pa: string; en: string }[] = [];\n    if (i > 0) {\n      const cursors = MATRA_PATH_DEFS.slice(0, i).map(() => 0);\n      while (reviewWords.length < Math.min(i, 3)) {\n        let advanced = false;\n        for (let li = 0; li < i; li++) {\n          if (reviewWords.length >= 3) break;\n          const pos = cursors[li];\n          const prior = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === MATRA_PATH_DEFS[li].curriculumSlug);\n          const candidates = prior?.examples ?? [];\n          if (pos < candidates.length) {\n            reviewWords.push({ pa: candidates[pos].pa, en: candidates[pos].en });\n            cursors[li]++;\n            advanced = true;\n          }\n        }\n        if (!advanced) break;\n      }\n    }\n\n    out[def.pathSlug] = {\n      id: def.pathSlug,\n      sectionId: \"s10\",\n      kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n      title: `${entry.name_pa} — ${entry.sound_iso}`,\n      curriculumRef: `matra-${def.curriculumSlug}`,\n      exercises: matraLessonExercises(newWords, reviewWords, def.pathSlug),\n    };\n  });\n\n  // Closing check: 1 audio-pick-word + 1 word-pick-meaning per matra,\n  // shuffled order so it's not 9-on-9 blocks.\n  const checkExercises: Exercise[] = [];\n  const allNewWords = MATRA_PATH_DEFS.flatMap((d) => {\n    const entry = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === d.curriculumSlug);\n    return (entry?.examples.slice(0, 4) ?? []).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n  });\n  const wordPool = allNewWords.map((w) => w.pa);\n  const meaningPool = allNewWords.map((w) => w.en);\n  MATRA_PATH_DEFS.forEach((def) => {\n    const entry = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === def.curriculumSlug);\n    const w = entry?.examples[0];\n    if (!w) return;\n    const apwId = `check-matras-${w.pa}-apw`;\n    const wpmId = `check-matras-${w.pa}-wpm`;\n    checkExercises.push({\n      id: apwId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.pa,\n      options: [w.pa, ...distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, apwId, 3)],\n    });\n    checkExercises.push({\n      id: wpmId,\n      kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n      word: w.pa,\n      correctMeaning: w.en,\n      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.en, meaningPool, wpmId, 3),\n    });\n  });\n\n  out[\"check-matras\"] = {\n    id: \"check-matras\",\n    sectionId: \"s10\",\n    kind: \"check\",\n    title: \"Matras check\",\n    exercises: checkExercises,\n  };\n\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = {\n  ...buildLetterLessons(),\n  ...buildMuktaLessons(),\n  ...buildMatraLessons(),\n};"
}

1	// QA page: every audio prompt the course plays, in one scrollable list.
2	// Tap each ► to hear the cached R2 MP3 that /api/tts serves. Use this to
3	// catch bad Chirp pronunciations and decide which words/letters need
4	// AUDIO_PROMPT_OVERRIDES (see lib/course/letter-lookup.ts) or trimmed
5	// reconstructions (see scripts/trim-audio.ts).
6	
7	import { notFound } from "next/navigation";
8	import { CURRICULUM, type LetterLesson, type NuktaGroupLesson, type ExampleWord } from "@/data/curriculum";
9	import { audioWordForLetter } from "@/lib/course/letter-lookup";
10	import { audioKeyForWord, OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES, WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES } from "@/lib/audio-overrides";
11	import { MUKTA_LESSONS } from "@/data/curriculum-v1.1";
12	import { serverClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
13	import { isAdmin } from "@/lib/auth/admin";
14	import RowItem from "./RowItem";
15	
16	// Static-regen would freeze this page until next deploy; we iterate on
17	// it constantly during audio QA, so opt into dynamic rendering.
18	export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
19	
20	interface Row {
21	  display: string;       // what to show as the big Gurmukhi label
22	  audioWord: string;     // what's actually sent to /api/tts
23	  subtitle?: string;     // iso / meaning / etc
24	  sourceKey?: string;    // for *-trimmed entries: the carrier the trim was cut from
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Reverse-lookup map: for each TRIMMED cache key (e.g. "ਸਨ-trimmed"),
29	 * which carrier phrase in R2 is it cut from? Built by composing the
30	 * two override maps in lib/audio-overrides.ts. Drives the AudioEditor's
31	 * "save trim" + "regen source" buttons.
32	 */
33	function buildTrimmedToSourceMap(): Record<string, string> {
34	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
35	  for (const [word, carrier] of Object.entries(OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES)) {
36	    const cacheKey = WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES[word];
37	    if (cacheKey) out[cacheKey] = carrier;
38	  }
39	  // Letter overrides (lib/course/letter-lookup.ts) don't go through
40	  // WORD_AUDIO_OVERRIDES; wire each carrier source up manually here so
41	  // the editor knows what to load + retrim from.
42	  out["ੜਾੜਾ-trimmed"] = "ਨਾੜਾੜਾ";
43	  return out;
44	}
45	
46	function lettersRows(trimmedToSource: Record<string, string>): Row[] {
47	  const out: Row[] = [];
48	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
49	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
50	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
51	      const key = audioWordForLetter(l.char);
52	      out.push({
53	        display: `${l.char}  ·  ${l.name_pa}`,
54	        audioWord: key,
55	        subtitle: `${l.name_iso} · /${l.ipa}/`,
56	        sourceKey: trimmedToSource[key],
57	      });
58	    } else if (lesson.kind === "nukta-group") {
59	      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {
60	        const key = audioWordForLetter(nl.char);
61	        out.push({
62	          display: `${nl.char}  ·  ${nl.name_pa}`,
63	          audioWord: key,
64	          subtitle: `${nl.name_iso} · /${nl.ipa}/ (nukta)`,
65	          sourceKey: trimmedToSource[key],
66	        });
67	      }
68	    }
69	  }
70	  return out;
71	}
72	
73	function exampleRows(trimmedToSource: Record<string, string>): Row[] {
74	  const seen = new Set<string>();
75	  const out: Row[] = [];
76	  const collect = (examples: ExampleWord[], origin: string) => {
77	    for (const ex of examples) {
78	      if (seen.has(ex.pa)) continue;
79	      seen.add(ex.pa);
80	      const key = audioKeyForWord(ex.pa);
81	      out.push({
82	        display: ex.pa,
83	        audioWord: key,
84	        subtitle: `${ex.iso} — ${ex.en}${ex.emoji ? `  ${ex.emoji}` : ""}  · from ${origin}`,
85	        sourceKey: trimmedToSource[key],
86	      });
87	    }
88	  };
89	  for (const lesson of CURRICULUM) {
90	    if (lesson.kind === "letter") {
91	      const l = lesson as LetterLesson;
92	      collect(l.examples, l.char);
93	    } else if (lesson.kind === "nukta-group") {
94	      for (const nl of (lesson as NuktaGroupLesson).letters) {
95	        collect(nl.examples, `${nl.char} (nukta)`);
96	      }
97	    }
98	  }
99	  return out;
100	}
101	
102	function carrierRows(): Row[] {
103	  return Object.entries(OVERRIDE_DEBUG_SOURCES).map(([word, carrier]) => ({
104	    display: carrier,
105	    audioWord: carrier,
106	    subtitle: `raw source for ${word} (this is what gets trimmed)`,
107	  }));
108	}
109	
110	function muktaRows(trimmedToSource: Record<string, string>): Row[] {
111	  return MUKTA_LESSONS.flatMap((lesson) =>
112	    lesson.words.map((w) => {
113	      const key = audioKeyForWord(w.word);
114	      return {
115	        display: `${w.word}${w.emoji ? `  ${w.emoji}` : ""}`,
116	        audioWord: key,
117	        subtitle: `${w.meaning} · §9 L${lesson.lessonNum}`,
118	        sourceKey: trimmedToSource[key],
119	      };
120	    }),

160	export default async function DebugAudioPage() {
161	  const supabase = await serverClient();
162	  // 404 (not 401/redirect) so the page doesn't even reveal its existence
163	  // to non-admin users. Treat it as if the route doesn't exist.

166	  const trimmedToSource = buildTrimmedToSourceMap();

172	  // One query for the whole page; the table is small and the page is
173	  // admin-only so we don't need to scope by section.
174	  const { data: verifiedRows } = await supabase
175	    .from("audio_verifications")
176	    .select("audio_key");
177	  const verifiedSet = new Set((verifiedRows ?? []).map((r) => r.audio_key as string));
178	
179	  const total = letters.length + examples.length + mukta.length + carriers.length;
180	  const verifiedTotal = [letters, examples, mukta, carriers]
181	    .flat()
182	    .filter((r) => verifiedSet.has(r.audioWord)).length;

184	  return (

188	        <h1 className="mt-1 font-serif text-3xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">

192	          Every sound the course plays. Click ► to listen, then mark each
193	          one verified once it sounds correct. New prompts default to

198	        </p>

200	
201	      <Section title="Letter names" count={letters.length} rows={letters} verifiedSet={verifiedSet} />
202	      <Section title="Letter example words" count={examples.length} rows={examples} verifiedSet={verifiedSet} />
203	      <Section title="Mukta words (§9)" count={mukta.length} rows={mukta} verifiedSet={verifiedSet} />
204	      <Section title="Raw carriers (uncropped)" count={carriers.length} rows={carriers} verifiedSet={verifiedSet} />
205	    </main>

okay so I have verified a lot the issue is that a lot of the audio clips have a lot of dead space before them, is there any way we can address this???

> AGENT

Yeah this is a real Chirp issue — it tacks ~200-500ms of dead air on the front. Two-pronged fix: (1) bake leading-silence trim into the synthesis pipeline so all future audio is clean, (2) a batch script to walk every cached MP3 in R2 and trim what's already there.

  "content": "// Shared leading-silence trimmer. Chirp 3 reliably tacks 200-500ms of\n// dead air on the start of every clip it produces, which feels laggy\n// in a tap-to-play UI. We run silencedetect to find the leading\n// silence interval, then ffmpeg to cut it off (preserving a small\n// onset pad so we don't clip the first phoneme).\n//\n// Used by:\n//   - lib/google-tts.ts synthesize() — in the synthesis hot path so all\n//     newly cached audio is already tight.\n//   - scripts/trim-cache-leading-silence.ts — batch over existing R2\n//     cache to clean up everything that was cached before this landed.\n//\n// Requires ffmpeg. On Vercel we lean on @ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg's\n// bundled binary; locally the system ffmpeg works fine. Set\n// FFMPEG_PATH if you need to override.\n\nimport { spawn } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport { writeFile, readFile, unlink, mkdtemp } from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport { tmpdir } from \"node:os\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport ffmpegInstaller from \"@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg\";\n\nconst FFMPEG_BIN = process.env.FFMPEG_PATH || ffmpegInstaller.path || \"ffmpeg\";\n\n// 80ms preserved before the detected speech onset — the silence\n// threshold catches the natural attack of a phoneme as silence, so\n// trimming exactly at silence_end would clip the consonant onset.\nconst LEADING_PAD_SEC = 0.08;\n\n// Minimum amount of leading silence worth cutting. Below this it's\n// effectively just the file's own header padding; trimming saves bytes\n// but not perceptual time, and risks clipping a soft onset.\nconst MIN_LEADING_SILENCE_SEC = 0.05;\n\ninterface SilenceInterval { start: number; end: number }\n\n/**\n * Detect silence intervals in an MP3 buffer using ffmpeg's silencedetect\n * filter. -25dB threshold matches scripts/trim-audio.ts so the batch\n * trim and the synthesis trim use the same boundary definition.\n */\nasync function detectSilences(inFile: string): Promise<SilenceInterval[]> {\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const proc = spawn(FFMPEG_BIN, [\n      \"-i\", inFile,\n      \"-af\", \"silencedetect=noise=-25dB:d=0.05\",\n      \"-f\", \"null\", \"-\",\n    ]);\n    let stderr = \"\";\n    proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n    proc.on(\"error\", (e) => reject(e));\n    proc.on(\"close\", (code) => {\n      if (code !== 0) return reject(new Error(`ffmpeg silencedetect exit ${code}`));\n      const intervals: SilenceInterval[] = [];\n      let currentStart: number | null = null;\n      for (const line of stderr.split(\"\\n\")) {\n        const sm = line.match(/silence_start:\\s*([\\d.]+)/);\n        const em = line.match(/silence_end:\\s*([\\d.]+)/);\n        if (sm) currentStart = parseFloat(sm[1]);\n        else if (em && currentStart !== null) {\n          intervals.push({ start: currentStart, end: parseFloat(em[1]) });\n          currentStart = null;\n        }\n      }\n      resolve(intervals);\n    });\n  });\n}\n\nasync function ffmpegSeekTo(inFile: string, outFile: string, startSec: number) {\n  return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n    const proc = spawn(FFMPEG_BIN, [\n      \"-y\",\n      \"-ss\", String(startSec),\n      \"-i\", inFile,\n      // 25ms fade-in so the cut doesn't pop\n      \"-af\", \"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025\",\n      \"-acodec\", \"libmp3lame\",\n      \"-q:a\", \"5\",\n      outFile,\n    ]);\n    let stderr = \"\";\n    proc.stderr.on(\"data\", (d) => (stderr += d.toString()));\n    proc.on(\"error\", (e) => reject(e));\n    proc.on(\"close\", (code) =>\n      code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg trim exit ${code}: ${stderr.slice(-200)}`)),\n    );\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Trim leading silence from an MP3 buffer and return the result.\n * Returns the original buffer unchanged when:\n *   - no leading silence was detected, or\n *   - the leading silence is short enough (<50ms) that cutting wouldn't\n *     help, or\n *   - ffmpeg fails for any reason (we never want a silence-trim error\n *     to break the audio pipeline).\n */\nexport async function trimLeadingSilence(mp3: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {\n  let dir: string | null = null;\n  try {\n    dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), \"akhar-leadtrim-\"));\n    const inFile = path.join(dir, \"in.mp3\");\n    const outFile = path.join(dir, \"out.mp3\");\n    await writeFile(inFile, mp3);\n    const silences = await detectSilences(inFile);\n    // Leading silence = the first interval that starts at (or near) t=0.\n    const lead = silences.find((s) => s.start <= 0.05);\n    if (!lead) return mp3;\n    const trimAmount = lead.end - LEADING_PAD_SEC;\n    if (trimAmount < MIN_LEADING_SILENCE_SEC) return mp3;\n    await ffmpegSeekTo(inFile, outFile, trimAmount);\n    const trimmed = await readFile(outFile);\n    return trimmed;\n  } catch (e) {\n    // Soft-fail: log + return original. We never want this to break\n    // the synthesis path or the batch script.\n    console.warn(\"trimLeadingSilence: falling back to untrimmed\", e instanceof Error ? e.message : e);\n    return mp3;\n  } finally {\n    if (dir) {\n      await Promise.allSettled([\n        unlink(path.join(dir, \"in.mp3\")),\n        unlink(path.join(dir, \"out.mp3\")),\n      ]);\n    }\n  }\n}\n"
}

> DEVELOPER

woah woah but you can't jsut blindy trim by a set amoubt!!!! what is your strategy???

> AGENT

Sorry — let me lay out the strategy before doing anything destructive. **Not** a fixed amount.

**Per-clip silence detection:**
1. Pipe the MP3 into `ffmpeg silencedetect=noise=-25dB:d=0.05` — same threshold + duration we've used successfully for the carrier trims (ਉਹ ਸਨ। auto-trimmed cleanly with this).
2. Find the FIRST silence interval whose `silence_start ≤ 0.05s` — that's *the leading dead air* specifically, not interior pauses.
3. Cut at `silence_end - 80ms pad` so we keep a small pre-onset buffer (preserves the phoneme attack — same pad value the carrier-trims use).

**Safety bailouts (the buffer is returned unchanged in any of these cases):**
- No silence interval found that starts at t≈0 → already tight, leave it
- Leading silence shorter than 50ms → not perceptually worth cutting, risk of clipping onset
- ffmpeg fails for any reason → soft-fail, log warning, return original (never break the pipeline)

**Where it applies:**
- In `synthesize()` after Chirp returns, before R2 cache write — so future audio is always tight
- In a batch script over the existing R2 cache (the part I hadn't written yet) — this is the risky bit

**Honest caveats** about the batch:
- Threshold `-25dB` matches what worked for our carrier trims, but it's an empirical tune — soft-onset words (e.g. a word starting with /h/) might briefly read as silence past t=0 and trigger an over-cut. The 80ms pad protects most cases but not all.
- Idempotent if you re-run (already-tight clips bail at bailout #1)
- One-way operation — original R2 bytes are overwritten

**Two checkpoints I want from you before running the batch:**

1. The 80ms onset pad — tighter (50ms = snappier but more clip risk) or looser (120ms = safer but less snappy)?
2. Want a dry-run first that just reports "would-trim N clips by X ms each" so you can spot-check before committing?

Used when re-synthesising a known-bad cached entry. */\nexport async function deleteCachedAudio(voice: string, text: string): Promise<void> {\n  const Key = r2KeyFor(voice, text);\n  await client().send(\n    new DeleteObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!, Key }),\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * List every R2 key under audio/<voice>/. The text-of-origin isn't\n * recoverable from the sha1-hash key, so this is mainly useful for\n * bulk operations (batch trimming, audit, migration) where we just\n * need to walk every object regardless of its source string.\n */\nexport async function listCachedAudioKeys(voice: string): Promise<string[]> {\n  const Prefix = `audio/${voice}/`;\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  let token: string | undefined;\n  do {\n    const res = await client().send(\n      new ListObjectsV2Command({\n        Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!,\n        Prefix,\n        ContinuationToken: token,\n      }),\n    );\n    for (const obj of res.Contents ?? []) {\n      if (obj.Key) out.push(obj.Key);\n    }\n    token = res.IsTruncated ? res.NextContinuationToken : undefined;\n  } while (token);\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Fetch by raw R2 key (vs the (voice, text) variant). Used by the bulk\n * scripts that walk listCachedAudioKeys() — they have keys, not texts.\n */\nexport async function getCachedAudioByKey(key: string): Promise<CachedAudio | null> {\n  try {\n    const obj = await client().send(\n      new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!, Key: key }),\n    );\n    if (!obj.Body) return null;\n    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];\n    for await (const chunk of obj.Body as AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>) {\n      chunks.push(chunk);\n    }\n    const buffer = Buffer.concat(chunks);\n    return { buffer, bytes: buffer.length };\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof NoSuchKey || err instanceof NotFound) return null;\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Put by raw R2 key, used by the bulk batch trim script. */\nexport async function putCachedAudioByKey(key: string, mp3: Buffer): Promise<void> {\n  await client().send(\n    new PutObjectCommand({\n      Bucket: process.env.R2_BUCKET!,\n      Key: key,\n      Body: mp3,\n      ContentType: \"audio/mpeg\",\n    }),\n  );\n}"

{

  "content": "// READ-ONLY audit of leading-silence in the R2 audio cache. Walks every\n// object under audio/<voice>/, downloads it, runs ffmpeg silencedetect,\n// and reports what a real batch trim WOULD change. Touches nothing in\n// R2 — safe to run any time.\n//\n// Output: per-row \"lead end | trim amount | decision\", then a summary:\n//   - total objects scanned\n//   - how many would be trimmed\n//   - distribution of leading silence (median, p90, max)\n//   - top 20 offenders\n//\n// Usage:\n//   tsx scripts/dry-run-trim-leading-silence.ts            # default voice\n//   tsx scripts/dry-run-trim-leading-silence.ts --limit 50 # sample only N keys (for fast iteration)\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport { listCachedAudioKeys, getCachedAudioByKey } from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\nimport { analyzeLeadingSilence } from \"@/lib/audio-trim\";\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst limitFlag = args.indexOf(\"--limit\");\nconst LIMIT = limitFlag >= 0 ? parseInt(args[limitFlag + 1], 10) : Infinity;\nconst CONCURRENCY = 8;\n\ninterface Row {\n  key: string;\n  bytes: number;\n  leadEndSec: number | null;\n  wouldTrim: boolean;\n  reason: string;\n}\n\nfunction median(xs: number[]): number {\n  if (xs.length === 0) return 0;\n  const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const mid = Math.floor(s.length / 2);\n  return s.length % 2 ? s[mid] : (s[mid - 1] + s[mid]) / 2;\n}\nfunction percentile(xs: number[], p: number): number {\n  if (xs.length === 0) return 0;\n  const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const idx = Math.min(s.length - 1, Math.floor(p * s.length));\n  return s[idx];\n}\n\nasync function processKey(key: string): Promise<Row | null> {\n  const cached = await getCachedAudioByKey(key);\n  if (!cached) return null;\n  const analysis = await analyzeLeadingSilence(cached.buffer);\n  return {\n    key,\n    bytes: cached.bytes,\n    leadEndSec: analysis.leadEndSec,\n    wouldTrim: analysis.wouldTrim,\n    reason: analysis.reason,\n  };\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  console.log(`Listing R2 keys under audio/${VOICE_NAME}/ …`);\n  let keys = await listCachedAudioKeys(VOICE_NAME);\n  console.log(`  found ${keys.length} objects`);\n  if (Number.isFinite(LIMIT) && keys.length > LIMIT) {\n    keys = keys.slice(0, LIMIT);\n    console.log(`  sampling first ${LIMIT}`);\n  }\n\n  const rows: Row[] = [];\n  // Crude N-at-a-time worker — keeps R2 + ffmpeg busy without hammering.\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker() {\n    while (true) {\n      const i = cursor++;\n      if (i >= keys.length) return;\n      const r = await processKey(keys[i]);\n      if (r) rows.push(r);\n      if ((rows.length % 25) === 0) {\n        process.stdout.write(`\\r  scanned ${rows.length}/${keys.length}`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: CONCURRENCY }, () => worker()));\n  process.stdout.write(\"\\n\");\n\n  const wouldTrim = rows.filter((r) => r.wouldTrim);\n  const leadSeconds = rows\n    .map((r) => r.leadEndSec)\n    .filter((x): x is number => x !== null);\n  const trimSeconds = wouldTrim.map((r) => (r.leadEndSec ?? 0) - 0.08);\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Summary ===\");\n  console.log(`Scanned objects:       ${rows.length}`);\n  console.log(`Would trim:            ${wouldTrim.length} (${((wouldTrim.length / rows.length) * 100).toFixed(1)}%)`);\n  console.log(`Skipped (no lead):     ${rows.filter((r) => r.reason === \"no-leading-silence\").length}`);\n  console.log(`Skipped (<50ms lead):  ${rows.filter((r) => r.reason === \"below-min\").length}`);\n  console.log(`Errors:                ${rows.filter((r) => r.reason === \"error\").length}`);\n  if (leadSeconds.length > 0) {\n    console.log(\"\");\n    console.log(\"Leading silence (seconds) across ALL scanned clips:\");\n    console.log(`  median:   ${median(leadSeconds).toFixed(3)}`);\n    console.log(`  p90:      ${percentile(leadSeconds, 0.9).toFixed(3)}`);\n    console.log(`  max:      ${Math.max(...leadSeconds).toFixed(3)}`);\n  }\n  if (trimSeconds.length > 0) {\n    console.log(\"\");\n    console.log(\"Trim amount (seconds) for clips we WOULD trim:\");\n    console.log(`  median:   ${median(trimSeconds).toFixed(3)}`);\n    console.log(`  p90:      ${percentile(trimSeconds, 0.9).toFixed(3)}`);\n    console.log(`  max:      ${Math.max(...trimSeconds).toFixed(3)}`);\n    console.log(`  total reclaimable: ${trimSeconds.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0).toFixed(2)}s across ${wouldTrim.length} clips`);\n  }\n\n  console.log(\"\\n=== Top 20 offenders (longest leading silence) ===\");\n  const sorted = [...wouldTrim].sort((a, b) => (b.leadEndSec ?? 0) - (a.leadEndSec ?? 0));\n  for (const r of sorted.slice(0, 20)) {\n    const shortKey = r.key.split(\"/\").pop()?.slice(0, 16) ?? r.key;\n    console.log(`  ${shortKey} … ${(r.leadEndSec ?? 0).toFixed(3)}s lead → cut at ${(((r.leadEndSec ?? 0) - 0.08)).toFixed(3)}s  (${r.bytes}B)`);\n  }\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"
}

process.exit(1); });\n"

  "content": "// Real batch — walks every R2 object under audio/<voice>/, trims leading\n// silence in-place using the same trimLeadingSilence() helper that the\n// synthesis pipeline now uses. Idempotent: re-running on already-tight\n// clips bails at the silence-detect step and does NOT re-encode.\n//\n// Reports a final summary + per-clip \"trimmed/skipped/error\" tally.\n// Errors are logged but never abort the run.\n//\n// Usage:\n//   tsx scripts/trim-cache-leading-silence.ts\n//   tsx scripts/trim-cache-leading-silence.ts --limit 100   # cap for safety\n//   tsx scripts/trim-cache-leading-silence.ts --concurrency 4\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\n\nconst env = readFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), \".env.local\"), \"utf8\");\nfor (const line of env.split(\"\\n\")) {\n  const m = line.match(/^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/);\n  if (m) process.env[m[1]] = m[2];\n}\n\nimport { VOICE_NAME } from \"@/lib/google-tts\";\nimport {\n  listCachedAudioKeys,\n  getCachedAudioByKey,\n  putCachedAudioByKey,\n} from \"@/lib/audio-cache\";\nimport { trimLeadingSilence } from \"@/lib/audio-trim\";\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nfunction flag(name: string, def?: number): number | undefined {\n  const i = args.indexOf(name);\n  if (i < 0) return def;\n  return parseInt(args[i + 1], 10);\n}\nconst LIMIT = flag(\"--limit\") ?? Infinity;\nconst CONCURRENCY = flag(\"--concurrency\") ?? 8;\n\ninterface Tally {\n  trimmed: number;\n  unchanged: number;\n  errors: number;\n  bytesBefore: number;\n  bytesAfter: number;\n}\n\nasync function processKey(key: string, tally: Tally): Promise<string> {\n  try {\n    const cached = await getCachedAudioByKey(key);\n    if (!cached) { tally.errors++; return \"error: not in r2\"; }\n    const trimmed = await trimLeadingSilence(cached.buffer);\n    // trimLeadingSilence returns the SAME buffer reference when it\n    // decides not to trim — cheap identity check, no expensive compare.\n    if (trimmed === cached.buffer) {\n      tally.unchanged++;\n      tally.bytesBefore += cached.bytes;\n      tally.bytesAfter += cached.bytes;\n      return `skip (already tight, ${cached.bytes}B)`;\n    }\n    await putCachedAudioByKey(key, trimmed);\n    tally.trimmed++;\n    tally.bytesBefore += cached.bytes;\n    tally.bytesAfter += trimmed.length;\n    return `trimmed ${cached.bytes}B → ${trimmed.length}B (saved ${cached.bytes - trimmed.length}B)`;\n  } catch (e) {\n    tally.errors++;\n    const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);\n    return `error: ${msg}`;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  console.log(`Listing R2 keys under audio/${VOICE_NAME}/ …`);\n  let keys = await listCachedAudioKeys(VOICE_NAME);\n  console.log(`  found ${keys.length} objects`);\n  if (Number.isFinite(LIMIT) && keys.length > LIMIT) {\n    keys = keys.slice(0, LIMIT);\n    console.log(`  limiting to first ${LIMIT}`);\n  }\n\n  const tally: Tally = { trimmed: 0, unchanged: 0, errors: 0, bytesBefore: 0, bytesAfter: 0 };\n  let cursor = 0;\n\n  async function worker() {\n    while (true) {\n      const i = cursor++;\n      if (i >= keys.length) return;\n      const result = await processKey(keys[i], tally);\n      const done = tally.trimmed + tally.unchanged + tally.errors;\n      if (done % 25 === 0 || result.startsWith(\"error\")) {\n        process.stdout.write(`\\r[${done}/${keys.length}] trimmed:${tally.trimmed} unchanged:${tally.unchanged} errors:${tally.errors}    `);\n        if (result.startsWith(\"error\")) process.stdout.write(`\\n  ${keys[i].split(\"/\").pop()?.slice(0, 16)} ${result}\\n`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  const startTime = Date.now();\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: CONCURRENCY }, () => worker()));\n  const elapsedSec = (Date.now() - startTime) / 1000;\n  process.stdout.write(\"\\n\\n\");\n\n  const savedBytes = tally.bytesBefore - tally.bytesAfter;\n  console.log(\"=== Done ===\");\n  console.log(`  Trimmed:     ${tally.trimmed}`);\n  console.log(`  Unchanged:   ${tally.unchanged}`);\n  console.log(`  Errors:      ${tally.errors}`);\n  console.log(`  Total time:  ${elapsedSec.toFixed(1)}s (${(keys.length / elapsedSec).toFixed(1)} clips/sec)`);\n  console.log(`  Bytes:       ${(tally.bytesBefore / 1024).toFixed(0)}KB → ${(tally.bytesAfter / 1024).toFixed(0)}KB (${(savedBytes / 1024).toFixed(0)}KB saved)`);\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"
}

  "content": "\"use client\";\n\n// Teach screen for §11 diacritic lessons (adhikk, tippi, bindi).\n// Renders the diacritic mark in isolation (on a ◌ base), name + iso,\n// a prose explainer of what it changes about pronunciation, and the\n// 4 new example words this round drills.\n\nimport AudioButton from \"./AudioButton\";\nimport type { ConceptLesson } from \"@/data/curriculum\";\n\nexport function DiacriticTeachContent({\n  diacritic,\n  introducedWords,\n}: {\n  diacritic: ConceptLesson;\n  introducedWords: readonly { pa: string; en: string; emoji?: string }[];\n}) {\n  return (\n    <div className=\"space-y-6\">\n      <div className=\"text-center\">\n        <div className=\"font-serif text-7xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n          <span className=\"opacity-30\">◌</span>\n          <span>{diacritic.symbol}</span>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"mt-3\">\n          <div className=\"font-serif text-xl text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n            {diacritic.name_pa}\n          </div>\n          <div className=\"font-mono text-sm text-zinc-500\">{diacritic.name_iso}</div>\n        </div>\n        <p className=\"mt-3 text-sm text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400\">\n          {diacritic.description_en}\n        </p>\n      </div>\n\n      {introducedWords.length > 0 && (\n        <div>\n          <h3 className=\"mb-3 text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-zinc-500\">\n            New words this round\n          </h3>\n          <ul className=\"grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2\">\n            {introducedWords.map((w) => (\n              <li\n                key={w.pa}\n                className=\"flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg border border-zinc-200 bg-white px-3 py-2 dark:border-zinc-800 dark:bg-zinc-950\"\n              >\n                <AudioButton word={w.pa} size=\"sm\" label={`Play ${w.pa}`} />\n                <div className=\"flex-1\">\n                  <div className=\"font-serif text-lg text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50\">\n                    {w.pa}\n                  </div>\n                  <div className=\"text-xs text-zinc-500\">{w.en}</div>\n                </div>\n                {w.emoji && <div className=\"text-xl\" aria-hidden>{w.emoji}</div>}\n              </li>\n            ))}\n          </ul>\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// §11 Diacritics — adhikk (ੱ), tippi (ੰ), bindi (ਂ). Each modifies how\n// the adjacent letter/vowel sounds. Source data is CONCEPT_LESSONS in\n// data/curriculum.ts (same pattern as §10 matras: that file is the\n// content table; this file just wires the lesson catalog + exercises).\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ninterface DiacriticPathDef {\n  pathSlug: string;\n  curriculumSlug: string;\n}\n\nconst DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS: DiacriticPathDef[] = [\n  { pathSlug: \"diacritic-addhak\", curriculumSlug: \"adhikk\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"diacritic-tippi\", curriculumSlug: \"tippi\" },\n  { pathSlug: \"diacritic-bindi\", curriculumSlug: \"bindi\" },\n];\n\nfunction diacriticLessonExercises(\n  newWords: { pa: string; en: string }[],\n  reviewWords: { pa: string; en: string }[],\n  slug: string,\n): Exercise[] {\n  // Pool across the full §11 vocab + §10 matras so distractors come\n  // from a meaningful neighbourhood — every word a learner has met\n  // recently is fair game as a distractor.\n  const matraWords = MATRA_PATH_DEFS.flatMap((d) => {\n    const entry = MATRA_LESSONS.find((m) => m.slug === d.curriculumSlug);\n    return (entry?.examples.slice(0, 4) ?? []).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n  });\n  const diacriticWords = DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS.flatMap((d) => {\n    const entry = CONCEPT_LESSONS.find((c) => c.slug === d.curriculumSlug);\n    return (entry?.examples.slice(0, 4) ?? []).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n  });\n  const allWords = [...matraWords, ...diacriticWords];\n  const wordPool = allWords.map((w) => w.pa);\n  const meaningPool = allWords.map((w) => w.en);\n\n  const out: Exercise[] = [];\n  newWords.forEach((w, i) => {\n    const startWithAudio = i % 2 === 0;\n    const apwId = `${slug}-${w.pa}-apw`;\n    const wpmId = `${slug}-${w.pa}-wpm`;\n    const apw: Exercise = {\n      id: apwId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.pa,\n      options: [w.pa, ...distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, apwId, 3)],\n    };\n    const wpm: Exercise = {\n      id: wpmId,\n      kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n      word: w.pa,\n      correctMeaning: w.en,\n      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.en, meaningPool, wpmId, 3),\n    };\n    if (startWithAudio) out.push(apw, wpm);\n    else out.push(wpm, apw);\n  });\n\n  reviewWords.forEach((w) => {\n    const id = `${slug}-review-${w.pa}`;\n    out.push({\n      id,\n      kind: \"meaning-pick-word\",\n      meaning: w.en,\n      correctWord: w.pa,\n      distractorWords: distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, id, 3),\n    });\n  });\n\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction buildDiacriticLessons(): Record<string, PathLesson> {\n  const out: Record<string, PathLesson> = {};\n  DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS.forEach((def, i) => {\n    const entry = CONCEPT_LESSONS.find((c) => c.slug === def.curriculumSlug);\n    if (!entry) return;\n    const newWords = entry.examples.slice(0, 4).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n\n    // Review pool: 1 word from each prior diacritic, oldest-first, cap 3.\n    const reviewWords: { pa: string; en: string }[] = [];\n    if (i > 0) {\n      const cursors = DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS.slice(0, i).map(() => 0);\n      while (reviewWords.length < Math.min(i, 3)) {\n        let advanced = false;\n        for (let li = 0; li < i; li++) {\n          if (reviewWords.length >= 3) break;\n          const pos = cursors[li];\n          const prior = CONCEPT_LESSONS.find((c) => c.slug === DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS[li].curriculumSlug);\n          const candidates = prior?.examples ?? [];\n          if (pos < candidates.length) {\n            reviewWords.push({ pa: candidates[pos].pa, en: candidates[pos].en });\n            cursors[li]++;\n            advanced = true;\n          }\n        }\n        if (!advanced) break;\n      }\n    }\n\n    out[def.pathSlug] = {\n      id: def.pathSlug,\n      sectionId: \"s11\",\n      kind: \"teach-and-test\",\n      title: `${entry.name_pa} ${entry.symbol}`,\n      curriculumRef: `diacritic-${def.curriculumSlug}`,\n      exercises: diacriticLessonExercises(newWords, reviewWords, def.pathSlug),\n    };\n  });\n\n  // Closing check: 1 audio-pick-word + 1 word-pick-meaning per diacritic.\n  const checkExercises: Exercise[] = [];\n  const allDiacriticWords = DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS.flatMap((d) => {\n    const entry = CONCEPT_LESSONS.find((c) => c.slug === d.curriculumSlug);\n    return (entry?.examples.slice(0, 4) ?? []).map((e) => ({ pa: e.pa, en: e.en }));\n  });\n  const wordPool = allDiacriticWords.map((w) => w.pa);\n  const meaningPool = allDiacriticWords.map((w) => w.en);\n  DIACRITIC_PATH_DEFS.forEach((def) => {\n    const entry = CONCEPT_LESSONS.find((c) => c.slug === def.curriculumSlug);\n    const w = entry?.examples[0];\n    if (!w) return;\n    const apwId = `check-diacritics-${w.pa}-apw`;\n    const wpmId = `check-diacritics-${w.pa}-wpm`;\n    checkExercises.push({\n      id: apwId,\n      kind: \"audio-pick-word\",\n      audioForWord: w.pa,\n      options: [w.pa, ...distractorsFromPool(w.pa, wordPool, apwId, 3)],\n    });\n    checkExercises.push({\n      id: wpmId,\n      kind: \"word-pick-meaning\",\n      word: w.pa,\n      correctMeaning: w.en,\n      distractorMeanings: distractorsFromPool(w.en, meaningPool, wpmId, 3),\n    });\n  });\n\n  out[\"check-diacritics\"] = {\n    id: \"check-diacritics\",\n    sectionId: \"s11\",\n    kind: \"check\",\n    title: \"Diacritics check\",\n    exercises: checkExercises,\n  };\n\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport const PATH_LESSONS: Record<string, PathLesson> = {\n  ...buildLetterLessons(),\n  ...buildMuktaLessons(),\n  ...buildMatraLessons(),\n  ...buildDiacriticLessons(),\n};"
}
